![Android Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20Studio-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![OCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/OCR-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![yolov11](https://img.shields.io/badge/yolov11-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### 🛠️ Challenges We Ran Into

Building **SmartVendor AI** for real-world retail environments presented several tough engineering hurdles:

#### 1. Specular Glare & Letter Distortion on Reflective Foil Packaging
* **The Hurdle**: Real Kirana store items (like *Maggi* yellow foil, *Snickers* wrappers, and *Lays* chips bags) reflect bright overhead lights. This created specular whiteout glare on camera frames, causing the OCR engine to extract garbled or duplicated letter noise (e.g., reading `"maazza"` instead of `"maaza"`).
* **How We Solved It**: We engineered a custom YUV frame processor in Kotlin (`OcrScannerManager`) that calculates pixel luminance ($Y$) and filters out whiteout glare spots ($Y > 235$) before sampling colors. We also added a regular expression character compressor (`replace(Regex("(.)\\1+"), "$1")`) to normalize glare-duplicated letters back into clean text before candidate evaluation.

#### 2. Phonetic & Visual Brand Cross-Match Confusion (*Maggi* vs. *Maaza*, *Soya Sticks* vs. *Snickers*)
* **The Hurdle**: Short FMCG brand names with overlapping letter counts produced high Levenshtein fuzzy similarity scores under fast camera motion. Scanning a *Maggi* packet would occasionally misidentify as *Maaza*, while *Soya Sticks* would cross-match with *Snickers*.
* **How We Solved It**: We created a multi-layered verification engine combining an explicit **Anti-Confusion Guard Matrix** (hard-blocking known negative brand pairs) with a **Packaging Color Classifier** (YUV $\rightarrow$ HSV hue mapping: Yellow for *Maggi*, Blue for *Oreo*, Red for *KitKat*). This ensured a +20% score boost on correct packaging colors while immediately dropping conflicting pairs.

#### 3. Camera Scanner Re-Triggering & User Interaction Ergonomics
* **The Hurdle**: When a vendor tapped **Add to Bill**, holding the packet in front of the lens while putting it into a customer's bag caused the camera to continuously spam duplicate item cards. Conversely, tapping **Cancel** on a misread item caused the camera to freeze up.
* **How We Solved It**: We built a dual-state interaction engine in `ScanViewModel`:
  - **Add to Bill**: Triggers a **5-second duplicate suppression cooldown** for that item ID.
  - **Cancel**: Records the rejected candidate in an ignored set and **instantly displays candidate #2 (the next highest-ranked alternative recommendation)** without interrupting the live camera stream.

#### 4. Cold-Start Camera & ML Native Binary Latency
* **The Hurdle**: Initializing Google ML Kit C++ native libraries and fetching store inventory from the database on first camera render caused a noticeable 2.8-second cold-start lag.
* **How We Solved It**: Implemented an application-level pre-warming pipeline (`SmartVendorApplication.kt`) that asynchronously pre-loads inventory products into an in-memory RAM cache (`InventoryCache`) and executes a dummy 0ms ML Kit initialization pass on app startup, dropping startup latency down to **under 0.4 seconds**.

# 📖 Overview

SmartVendor AI is an AI-powered retail assistant that converts any Android smartphone into a complete Point of Sale (POS) system.

Instead of relying on expensive barcode scanners and dedicated billing hardware, SmartVendor AI uses Computer Vision and Artificial Intelligence to recognize products directly through the phone's camera, automatically generate bills, update inventory, analyze sales, and recommend future stock requirements.

Designed especially for:

- Kirana Stores
- Grocery Shops
- Bakeries
- Medical Stores
- Small Retail Businesses

---

# 🎯 Problem Statement

Millions of small retailers still rely on:

- Manual billing
- Paper notebooks
- Expensive POS systems
- Barcode scanners
- Manual inventory tracking

These methods are slow, error-prone, and difficult to manage.

SmartVendor AI provides an affordable AI-powered alternative using only a smartphone.

SmartVendor AI replaces traditional billing systems with AI-powered product recognition.

**Challenges we ran into**

Orchestrating an end-to-end AI agent that can predict, monitor, pay, and book flights without any manual intervention.

**The problem it solves**

Flight prices change constantly, forcing travelers to repeatedly check fares and guess the best time to book. This process is time-consuming, uncertain, and often results in overpaying or missing the lowest fare.

Anton solves this by turning flight booking into an autonomous experience. Users simply provide their travel details and preferences, authorize a one-time payment mandate through Prava, and Anton takes over. It continuously monitors fares, predicts the best booking opportunity using historical pricing data, and automatically books the ticket when the price drops. This saves time, reduces booking anxiety, and helps travelers secure better prices without any manual effort.

**The problem it solves**

1. Orycon (Event Management System)

Orycon is a centralized hub designed to eliminate the "spreadsheet chaos" often found in college societies. Society admins and student leads can use it to manage the entire lifecycle of an event from brainstorming in the Idea Box and recruiting teams via the Hiring Portal, to real time execution with QR based automated attendance. It makes existing tasks significantly safer and more efficient by unifying scattered workflows (like WhatsApp coordination or manual Excel tracking) into a single, role-based dashboard. This ensures that institutional knowledge is preserved for future batches through automated Content Documentation, while the Social Media Scheduler ensures consistent community engagement without the risk of manual posting errors.

2. Keploy Blog Website

The Keploy Blog serves as a vital educational resource for developers navigating the world of AI powered test automation. People use it to access deep-dive technical tutorials, case studies, and product updates. This project makes the existing platform "faster and friendlier" by optimizing Core Web Vitals and refining the UI/UX for high-performance reading. By migrating to a more robust TypeScript architecture and improving the search/navigation logic, we make information discovery nearly instantaneous. For contributors, it streamlines the writing process through clearer documentation and a lightweight asset pipeline, ensuring that the blog remains a high speed, reliable source of truth that reflects Keploy’s own standard of technical excellence.

3. TranscribeIt

TranscribeIt is a powerful accessibility tool that converts video content and live streams into interactive, searchable, and diarized transcripts. It is primarily used by the hard of hearing community, researchers, and students who need to navigate long form video content efficiently. It makes existing tasks easier by providing word level timestamps and speaker identification, allowing users to jump directly to specific parts of a video rather than scrubbing through hours of footage. By integrating robust ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) pipelines and offering exports in Markdown, PDF, and JSON, it turns passive video watching into an active data retrieval process, ensuring that digital content is inclusive, WCAG compliant, and accessible to everyone.

**The problem it solves**

RD_Voicify lets you clone any voice straight from a YouTube Video (5-10sec) URL just paste the link, type your text, and get it spoken back in that exact voice within seconds. Powered by XTTS v2 neural cloning and Demucs vocal isolation, it automatically strips background noise from the video, clones the voice with AI, and runs it through a humanizer DSP chain so the output sounds natural, not robotic. No audio downloads, no manual setup just a URL and your words.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdle was getting clean voice extraction from YouTube audio when we fed raw YouTube audio directly into XTTS v2, the model kept picking up background music and noise as part of the voice signature, making the cloned output sound muddy and inconsistent.

**The problem it solves**

Bridging the Gap Between Abstract Theory and Practical Application in C Programming and Logic Building.

Learning low-level languages like C is often perceived as dry, intimidating, and overly abstract. Beginners struggle to visualize how concepts like pointers, memory management, and control structures translate into real-world systems. Traditional learning methods—textbooks and command-line compilers—often lack engagement and immediate, meaningful feedback, leading to high drop-out rates among new students.

How Code Chronicles Helps
Code Chronicles: The C Expedition transforms the learning experience into an immersive sci-fi strategy game. It provides a platform where code isn't just text on a screen—it is the tool used to survive and explore.

Key Use Cases:

Gamified Education: Students and hobbyists use it to learn C syntax and logic by writing code to control a lunar rover, repair planetary systems, and solve environmental puzzles.
Visualizing Logic: Instead of debugging invisible variables, users see their code execute in a 3D environment. A for loop failure might mean the rover runs out of fuel, while a pointer error might cause a system overload, making abstract failures concrete and understandable.
Safe Experimentation: It offers a zero-setup, sandboxed web environment where learners can experiment with low-level code without the complex process of setting up local compilers or the risk of crashing their own systems.
Benefits:

Makes Learning "Stick": By tying technical concepts to a narrative (e.g., "Use pointers to reroute power to life support"), users retain information better than through rote memorization.
Lowers Barriers to Entry: Being browser-based, it eliminates the "environment setup hell" that discourages many first-time C programmers.
Instant Feedback Loop: The game provides real-time validation and visual simulation results, allowing users to iterate and correct their logic instantly.

**Challenges we ran into**

Fighting Browser's Autoplay Policy
One of the most frustrating polish issues was getting the immersive background ambience to play reliably. Modern browsers block audio playback that isn't triggered by a user interaction (like a click) to prevent spammy ads.

The Hurdle: The game would often load in silence, breaking the intended atmospheric immersion of being stranded in space.
The Solution: I implemented a "User Interaction Fallback" system in the
AudioProvider. The game attempts to autoplay on load, but simultaneously attaches global event listeners for click and keydown events. As soon as the player interacts with the page in any way, the audio engine initializes and fades in, ensuring compliance with browser policies while still delivering the experience as early as possible.

Synchronizing Game State with Next.js Hydration
Since the game tracks player stats (credits, unlocked levels) using localStorage, I ran into "hydration mismatch" errors. Next.js renders the initial HTML on the server (where localStorage doesn't exist), but the client re-renders with the saved data.
The Hurdle: The screen would flash or React would throw errors because the server-rendered HTML (Level 1) didn't match the client-rendered state (Level 5).
The Solution: I utilized useEffect hooks and a mounted state variable to ensure that any component relying on persistent data only renders after the client has fully hydrated. This prevents the "fouc" (flash of unstyled content) and ensures the UI remains stable during load.

Bridging C Code with Visual Logic
Connecting the "Code Editor" (text) to the "3D Simulation" (visual output) was architecturally complex.
The Hurdle was that how do you translate a simple C for loop into a complex animation of a rover moving across a terrain?
As a Solution, I built an intermediate "Simulation Layer." Instead of running the C code directly in the browser (which is unsafe and difficult), the code is sent to a server-side handler that analyzes the logic and returns a "sequence of events" JSON. The frontend then behaves like a movie player, reading this sequence to trigger specific animations (e.g., MOVE_FORWARD, TURN_LEFT) in the Three.js scene, decoupling the code execution from the rendering.

These were 3 major Challenges we ran into so we have structure our problems and solution is Topic(Hurdle and Solution) manner.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

The Gemini API acts as the intelligence engine of our platform, powering both mentorship and performance insights.

Our project integrates Gemini in two key features:

ARIA – The AI Mentor (/api/chat)
Powered by Gemini Flash, ARIA is an in-character AI mentor that guides students through C programming in an engaging sci-fi persona. It explains concepts, provides hints, and helps learners solve problems through dynamic conversations, making coding guidance interactive rather than static.

AI Performance Analysis (/api/analysis)
Using Gemini’s structured JSON generation, our system analyzes player statistics stored in Supabase to generate personalized insights such as skill assessments, strengths, improvement areas, and progress predictions.

Together, these features transform raw gameplay data and questions into a personalized, AI-driven learning experience. 🚀

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

The ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech API powers the voice of ARIA, bringing our AI mentor to life through natural, expressive speech.

Our /api/tts route integrates with ElevenLabs to convert ARIA’s responses into high-quality voice audio, creating an immersive spoken-dialogue experience inside the game.

To ensure reliability, the system also includes automatic voice-ID fallback logic, guaranteeing that ARIA can always respond with audio even if the primary voice configuration fails.

This transforms the AI mentor from simple text responses into a fully interactive voice-driven guide. 🎙️🚀

**Best Use of Vultr**

Our project is fully optimized for cloud deployment on Vultr, ensuring a reliable and scalable hosting environment.

It includes a dedicated DEPLOYMENT.md Vultr Deployment Guide, a Dockerfile for containerized setup, and a PM2 ecosystem configuration for efficient process management.

Together, these components enable smooth, production-ready deployment on a Vultr VPS with minimal configuration. 🚀

## 🔥 Key Features

- **Real-time voice interview** using **Google Gemini Live** (brain + TTS).
- **Lifelike avatar**: Tavus primary + Beyond Presence automatic fallback via **LiveKit** streaming.
- **Résumé Analyzer**: upload PDF → AI extracts skills/projects → asks personalized questions.
- **GitHub Analyzer**: paste GitHub URL → parser reads repos/README → asks repo/project-specific questions.
- **Stateful interview flow**: normal → resume mode → github mode → resumes normal flow seamlessly.
- **Pluggable avatar**: option to run local open-source talking-head (Ditto / LivePortrait) when self-hosting.
- **Extensible**: future integration for **local emotion & tone analysis** (MediaPipe + OpenSMILE).

---

## 🔍 Problem It Solves

- Students often prepare with static Q&A or videos — not realistic recruiter interactions.  
- Generic mock interview platforms don’t adapt to a candidate’s actual résumé or code.  
- Paid avatar services (Tavus) can stop mid-session due to credits, breaking the experience.

**PracterViews** addresses these by providing:
- Adaptive, résumé- and GitHub-aware questioning.
- Real-time voice + visual interviewer presence.
- Automatic avatar fallback so interviews never stop.

---

## 🧰 Tech Stack

- **AI / Brain:** Google Gemini Live (responses + audio)  
- **Backend:** Python — FastAPI, async WebSocket handlers  
- **Real-time media:** LiveKit (WebRTC)  
- **Avatars:** Tavus (primary), Beyond Presence (fallback) — optional local Ditto/LivePortrait  
- **Frontend:** React (LiveKit SDK), React Dropzone for uploads  
- **Parsing / Tools:** PyMuPDF (PDF), GitHub REST API, Whisper (optional local STT)  
- **Local emotion/tone (planned):** MediaPipe + OpenSMILE / pyannote

# The Problem It Solves



### 🎯Mock interviews feel fake — real interviews are personal

Most students practice using:

- ❌ Generic question banks  
- ❌ Random YouTube videos  
- ❌ Static MCQ-based mock tests  
- ❌ Chatbots that do not adapt  
- ❌ Platforms that ignore your résumé and GitHub  

These tools fail to replicate an **actual recruiter** who:

- Reads your resume  
- Analyzes your projects  
- Asks personalized questions  
- Evaluates how you speak  
- Responds to your answers  
- Follows up intelligently  

### 🔥 Our Solution

We built a **real-time AI Interviewer** that feels like a *human recruiter*:

- 🎙️ **Live voice conversation** powered by Gemini  
- 🧑‍💼 **Realistic AI avatar** with Tavus (with Beyond Presence fallback)  
- 📄 **Résumé Analyzer** — upload your resume, get personalized questions

Students gain:

- Realistic interview experience  
- Personalized technical questions  
- Confidence in communication  
- Exposure to real recruiter behavior  
- In-depth project-based questioning  

This transforms mock interviews into **real, human-like interview simulations.**

# 🛠️ Challenges I Ran Into


### ⚠️ **1. Tavus Avatar Credits Running Out**
Tavus consumes credits quickly, causing interviews to crash mid-session.

#### 💡 Solution  
A **smart fallback**:  
If Tavus fails → automatically switch to **Beyond Presence** without interrupting the interview.

---

### ⚠️ **2. Managing Multi-Mode Interview Flow**
Interview had different states:

- Normal questions  
- Resume questions  
- GitHub questions  
- Returning back to normal mode  

Unmanaged flow → mixed/random questions.

#### 💡 Solution  
We built a **state machine**:

normal → resume_mode → normal → github_mode → normal

yaml
Copy code

This makes the AI behave exactly like a structured professional interviewer.

---

### ⚠️ **3. Parsing Complex Résumés**
PDF résumés often had:

- Multi-column layouts  
- Scanned images  
- Unextractable text  

#### 💡 Solution  
A **hybrid PDF parser**:

- 📝 Local text extraction  
- 🤖 Fallback to Gemini Document AI for OCR & parsing  

Guarantees reliable résumé understanding.

---

### ⚠️ **4. Inconsistent GitHub Repositories**
Common problems:

- Empty repos  
- No README  
- Dead projects  
- Too many repos  

#### 💡 Solution  

Filtering by:
- Recency  
- README existence  
- Language relevance  
- Project quality  

Then summarizing repos before sending to AI.

---

### ⚠️ **5. Keeping the AI in Interviewer Mode**
LLMs naturally:

- Over-explain  
- Act like teachers  
- Break character  

#### 💡 Solution  
A **strict system prompt** enforcing recruiter behavior:

- Ask one question at a time  
- Never explain concepts  
- Never break character  
- Natural follow-ups only  

---

### ⚠️ **6. Real-Time Avatar + Audio Sync**
Gemini → Avatar → LiveKit syncing was difficult at first.

#### 💡 Solution  
Used:

- Buffered audio streams  
- Async response handling  
- Retry & auto-fallback logic  

Now it's smooth & real-time.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Noir](https://img.shields.io/badge/Noir-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### What problem Onyx solves

The core problem is simple:

> Zcash gives you strong privacy, but there is **no credibly backed, stable “money layer”** on top of it.

Right now ZEC looks scary to most normal people:

- “What even is Zcash?”
- “The price chart looks like a nuke.”
- “It is private, so it must be risky.”
- “I cannot park savings in something that can drop 40% in a month.”

They are not completely wrong. ZEC is volatile and “just hold ZEC” is not a great savings story. On the other side:

- Dollar stablecoins (USDC, USDT, etc.) live on **fully transparent chains**, so every balance and transfer is traceable.
- “Algo stables” often rely on circular, reflexive tokenomics that blow up under stress.
- There is **no Zcash-native, private stablecoin** that feels conservative and boring enough to be real money.

Onyx is designed to fill that gap.

---

### Our approach: a \$100 floor and explicit risk separation

Onyx introduces **USDO**, a ZEC-backed stablecoin that lives privately on **Aztec**.  
The key design choice is a **conservative ZEC floor price** and a split between “safe” value and “risky” value.

1. The protocol picks a conservative **floor price** for ZEC, for example  
   \`P_f = \$100 per ZEC\`.
2. When ZEC trades above that (say \`P_m = \$350\`), the protocol **only treats the first \$100 as stable collateral** for USDO.
3. The extra \$250 of value is not assumed to be safe. It is pushed into:
   - a **surplus / bond token** called **xUSDO**, and  
   - a buffer called the **Volatility Absorption Pool (VAP)**.

So if ZEC is at \$350 and you deposit 1 ZEC:

- You mint roughly **100 USDO** (plus a small protocol-defined bonus).
- You receive **xUSDO** that represents the extra volatile value.
- Some of the surplus is routed to VAP and protocol fees.

If ZEC “nukes” down toward \$100 or below:

- The system only promised the floor part.  
  USDO is still backed by at least \$100 of ZEC per ZEC used at mint.
- The pain is **absorbed by xUSDO holders and protocol buffers**, not by USDO holders.
- There is no magical algorithm pretending \$350 is still “there” when it is not.

If ZEC rallies higher, xUSDO and a time-based redemption curve allow risk takers to share upside, while USDO stays pegged close to \$1.

In other words, Onyx takes the “what if Zcash nukes?” question and bakes the answer directly into the math instead of hoping it never happens.

---

### What people can actually use it for

- **ZEC holders who do not want to sell**  
  Borrow USDO against ZEC at a conservative floor instead of dumping into a CEX. Keep long-term ZEC exposure but unlock stable liquidity.

- **Privacy-focused users**  
  Hold a dollar-like asset (USDO) that lives in **Aztec’s private state**, instead of fully transparent L1s where their entire financial history is on-chain.

- **Builders in the privacy DeFi stack (Aztec dapps, Boreal projects, etc.)**  
  Plug a **native private stablecoin** into lending, DEXs, payments and payroll without bolting on a centralized USDC bridge.

Onyx does not claim ZEC is risk-free or magically backed. It just makes the risk **explicit and priced**:

- USDO is backed at the conservative floor price.
- xUSDO and VAP take the “nuke or moon” volatility.

---
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9d08f3373eb94b8092a2829fb4a1d071/eb9dbe4e-22b9-4f22-b5be-549c40f45a46.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Onyx came with several challenges because designing a private ZEC-backed stablecoin that actually works required solving real economic, cryptographic, and cross-chain problems. One of the biggest challenges was taking the simple idea of a $100 ZEC floor and turning it into a real mathematical model. The idea sounds easy: the first $100 of ZEC value is “safe collateral,” and anything above that is volatile surplus. But when you try to implement it, you quickly realize you need a three-zone pricing system so the protocol behaves correctly whether ZEC is pumping or nuking. That led to defining three regimes based on the market price P_m relative to the $100 floor P_f and the threshold price P_t. In Zone 1 (high confidence), USDO is minted using the floor price and the surplus becomes xUSDO. In Zone 2 (caution), USDO is discounted based on how close ZEC is to the floor, and surplus is taxed harder. In Zone 3 (emergency), the protocol ignores the floor entirely and uses the real market price with a haircut, while minting zero xUSDO. On top of this, we had to enforce a global solvency rule so total reserves multiplied by the floor always covers the entire USDO supply. Getting all of this mathematically consistent, conservative, and still reasonable for users took a lot of iteration.
Another challenge was dealing with the classic “Zcash nukes” and “ZEC isn’t backed by anything” concerns. Instead of pretending ZEC is safe, Onyx directly separates the stable and volatile parts of ZEC’s value. USDO holders only rely on the stable floor value, not the full spot price. All volatility above the floor is absorbed by xUSDO and the volatility absorption pool. This lets the system stay solvent even if ZEC drops from $350 down to $100 or lower without breaking the stablecoin. It also creates a clean narrative: the system only trusts the floor price and explicitly labels everything above it as risk.
Another big challenge was architecting the protocol inside Aztec’s private environment. Unlike Ethereum, Aztec does not expose balances publicly; everything is stored as private notes. Ownership checks, vault accounting, redemptions, and liquidations all require zk proofs instead of simple address checks. Only aggregated vault totals and supply numbers can be public. This required re-thinking every system component as a Noir circuit. Even designing how a user “owns” a vault position required planning for private note ownership proofs, private state transitions, and ensuring no user data leaks .

**General Bounty**

Onyx sits directly in the “privacy as a building block for new digital societies” narrative. A credibly backed, private stablecoin is one of the core primitives you need for startup communities, network states, and off-grid economies. USDO gives those communities a way to store and move value privately using Zcash, while still having programmable behavior on Aztec, which fits well with Network School’s focus on zk-identity, zk-census, and sovereign tooling.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Onyx provides the ZEC-backed, privacy-native stablecoin; Axelar provides the routing to other chains. Together, USDO can become a cross-chain asset that originates from Zcash, is minted privately on Aztec, and then is bridged via Axelar to EVM or Cosmos DeFi. That enables private ZEC collateral to back positions on other chains, which is exactly the “cross-chain private DeFi” story Axelar is looking for.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

Onyx is almost a direct answer to the Aztec bounty: a Zcash-backed stablecoin designed specifically to live as a private asset on Aztec. Minting, transfers, redemptions, and even liquidations happen in private state using Noir, and USDO is meant to be the default “money” for private Aztec apps. It demonstrates how to plug ZEC privacy into Aztec’s programmable privacy for actual payments and everyday value transfer, not just speculation.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

Once USDO exists as a ZEC-backed stablecoin on Aztec, it opens the door to creative flows into the Cosmos world via Osmosis. A natural direction is a private-to-public bridge where users mint USDO privately, then selectively move it into liquidity pools or payment rails on Osmosis without leaking their original Zcash identities, possibly combining shielded memos and structured flows. That is a non-obvious but powerful “privacy meets Cosmos DeFi” use case.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Onyx can use Helius infra to extend USDO into the Solana ecosystem as a wrapped asset while keeping the ZEC-backed, Aztec-minted origin private. Helius gives indexing, RPC and webhook tools to track bridged USDO and build Solana-side DeFi integrations, like stable pools or lending markets that are ultimately backed by ZEC held in a private vault. That ties Zcash privacy, Aztec’s private logic, and Solana’s high performance trading together.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

Onyx is directly focused on bringing serious DeFi to Zcash in a way that respects the shielded pool. It designs a conservative, floor-based stablecoin backed by ZEC and deploys the logic on a privacy L2, but the economic value, risk model, and UX are all centered around ZEC holders. USDO and xUSDO become the base primitives for private lending, private trading, and capital markets that actually originate from Zcash instead of bypassing it.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

Onyx fits Unstoppable’s goals by giving wallets a privacy-native stablecoin they can integrate alongside normal chains. A future integration could let Unstoppable users hold ZEC, mint USDO, and see those balances and flows without revealing their full activity graph publicly. USDO can then be wired into private swap flows or cross-chain DEX aggregation while keeping the core collateral and transaction history shielded.

**Cross-Chain Privacy Solutions**

Onyx can use NEAR intents to let ZEC and USDO holders orchestrate actions on other chains using a natural language or agentic experience, while the underlying collateral and minting logic stay private. For example, a user could hold ZEC, mint USDO, and then “tell” an agent to deploy that value into DeFi on NEAR or elsewhere via intents, all while their original Zcash identity and vault remain shielded. That is a strong private payments and orchestration story.

**General Bounty**

Onyx is a core building block for private payments in the Zcash ecosystem: it takes volatile ZEC and turns it into a stable medium of exchange that still respects privacy. With Tachyon’s general bounty support, Onyx can harden the bridge, refine the Aztec integration, and build simple payment flows so users can actually send and receive USDO like money instead of just treating ZEC as a speculative asset. It squarely advances private payments on top of Zcash.

**Private Payments & Transactions**

Onyx fits the Star Fun bounty as a novel private payment rail: USDO gives people a stable, ZEC-backed unit they can spend while keeping identities shielded. It can power private point of sale, remittance flows, or creator payments where the source value comes from Zcash but the day to day behavior looks like using a normal stablecoin. That kind of “real world but still private” payment use case is exactly what this track is asking to showcase.

Ser Pepe

### ProofFund

> Agentic grants, verified by markets.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Web3 grants are often subjective, slow, and lack accountability for developers after funds are released. Our platform solves this by turning public goods funding into a data-driven, market-based process.

When a developer applies for a grant, an AI agent evaluates their past on-chain history using Sourcify to generate a trust score. Based on this score and the proposal, the AI generates strict on-chain KPIs and opens decision markets tied directly to specific funding chunks.

Crucially, the developer does not receive all the money at once. Instead, traders bet with real capital on whether the developer will hit their milestones, and these market bets dictate when the money is released. If the market bets "YES" (approves the project), the first chunk of funding is unlocked immediately to start development. After a 14-day development window, smart contracts automatically verify if the on-chain KPIs were met. If the developer delivers, the market resolves, the final chunk of funding is released to the developer, and the winning traders claim their payouts. This ensures funders only pay for proven, measurable results, governed entirely by market consensus.

**Challenges we ran into**

System Scale vs. Hackathon Timeline: The project architecture required building four distinct systems from scratch: a BigQuery ML pipeline, a Python AI agent, Layer-2 smart contracts, and a React frontend. Completing the end-to-end integration of all four within 48 hours exceeded the time limit.

Middleware Integration: The Solidity contracts (Decision Market, Treasury, KPIVerifier) are fully written and deployed. However, building the Python middleware (web3.py) for the AI agent to securely manage keys, sign transactions, and handle testnet block times required more development hours than we had left.

Demo Execution: To prove the concept works, we prioritized the core logic. We kept the Sourcify ML pipeline running live, but temporarily shifted the smart contract execution math (pricing and pool state changes) into the frontend. This allowed us to demonstrate the exact market mechanics without relying on incomplete middleware.

**Sourcify Bounty**

The key idea is to turn Sourcify’s verified contract dataset into an automated due-diligence layer for Web3 venture and grant decisions.

The system uses Sourcify data to answer concrete due‑diligence questions about each developer wallet: Are the contracts fully verified on Sourcify? What functionality is exposed through the ABI? Is the project relying on standard patterns and libraries or on unusual custom logic? Is the code upgradeable through proxies? Are there known dangerous patterns in the source that should trigger human review?

Using BigQuery is important because it allows contracts to be analyzed in context. Instead of inspecting a single address via an ad‑hoc API call, the service queries Sourcify’s public tables for all verified deployments of a wallet across supported EVM chains and compares them against the wider corpus of verified contracts (e.g., by chain, verification quality, and metadata). This makes the resulting reliability score more objective and evidence‑based.

The output of this stage is a structured, machine‑readable audit result that downstream agents and UIs can turn into human‑friendly reports for investors, grant programs, and hackathon judges. It highlights technical risks, summarizes positive credibility signals, and provides a normalized score with a categorical recommendation (APPROVE, REVIEW, or REJECT) for each developer wallet.

This is a meaningful use of Sourcify because its verified source code, bytecode, ABI, compiler metadata, and storage layouts are treated as the primary ground truth for the technical assessment. Without this dataset, the system would not be able to perform reliable, reproducible smart‑contract due diligence at scale.

**Best Agentic Venture**

Web3 grants are often subjective, slow, and lack accountability for developers after funds are released. Our platform solves this by turning public goods funding into a data-driven, market-based process.

When a developer applies for a grant, an AI agent evaluates their past on-chain history using Sourcify to generate a trust score. Based on this score and the proposal, the agent researches the developer's GitHub activity and proposal viability to generate strict on-chain KPIs. It then autonomously deploys isolated smart contracts (a prediction market and a KPI verifier) directly from its own wallet, with no human approval required.

The developer does not receive all the money at once. Instead, traders bet with real capital on whether the developer will hit their milestones, and these market bets dictate when the money is released. If the market bets "YES" (approves the project), the first chunk of funding is unlocked immediately to start development, and our smart contracts automatically mint a dedicated ENS subdomain (e.g., `project.prooffund.eth`) to the developer's wallet as an on-chain badge of trust. After a designated development window, smart contracts automatically verify if the on-chain KPIs were met. If the developer delivers, the market resolves, the final chunk of funding is released to the developer, and the winning traders claim their payouts. This ensures funders only pay for proven, measurable results, governed entirely by market consensus.

**Best ENS Integration for AI Agents**

Our platform is an AI-driven grant market where developers must pass a strict reputation audit and win a public prediction market vote to receive funding. To make this earned reputation visible across Web3, we integrated programmatic ENS issuance directly into the grant lifecycle.

When a prediction market approves a grant, our smart contracts automatically mint a dedicated ENS subdomain (e.g., projectname.prooffund.eth) to the developer's wallet via the Sepolia NameWrapper. Throughout the 14-day development window, our AI agent continuously monitors on-chain metrics and updates the ENS Text Records with live state data—such as current KPI progress, funding tranches, and trust scores. In Web3, reputation is fragmented. It proves to users and investors that this specific developer has passed a AI audit and is actively delivering, adding deep, dynamic utility to the ENS ecosystem.

### JustDM
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/justdm-fd80) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/daiwikmh/DM) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://justdms.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/cnS7xoC8B-4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Justdm turns the reel you shared into a purchase

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**JUSTDM**

Right now, a shared product reel is a dead end. Someone saves or shares and then:

There's no price, no size, no stock check — just a video.
Later it's buried in chat history, and you don't remember which reel it was.
If you actually want to buy it: screenshot, guess the brand, search manually, maybe land on the wrong color, then create a new account on some retailer's site and type your card number in for a single purchase you'll never make again there.

The moment of wanting something dies in the gap between seeing it and buying it. justdm closes that gap.

What Justdm Does

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/a024c01d-fadf-4f52-a9c3-f9751e67067d.png)Screenshot 2026-08-03 at 1.23.59 AM

Turns a sent reel into a priced, buyable item automatically.
The product is identified and matched against live retailer inventory the moment it's shared. 

Gives shared intent a memory.
No more "didn't we send that jacket last week?" Every item you've sent or received sits on a dashboard with a price next to it, for as long as you want it there.

Removes the re-entry tax on buying.
No new retailer account. No re-typing a card number for a one-off purchase. Approve with the passkey already on your phone, and it's done.

Makes casual buying safer than typing your real card into a new site.
Every purchase runs on a one-time card locked to that merchant and that exact amount, enforced by Visa's network. A $40 approval at one store can't be reused or misused anywhere else — unlike handing a new site your actual card number.

Who It's For

Anyone in the constant cycle of sending "look at this" reels with friends or saves it in their saved option which is most Instagram DM traffic already. If you're someone who sees something, wants it, and then either loses track of it or has to do real work to go get it, Justdm removes everything after "I want it" except approving the purchase.

**Challenges we ran into**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/070e78c1-acd4-4b22-bc01-d09b3ad45fb3.png)Screenshot 2026-08-02 at 11.53.31 PM

"Payment Failed."

For a long stretch, every checkout died at the same place.
The cause was, When you open a payment session you tell the network who the merchant is, and we were handing it the full product link the deep URL with the product path and all the tracking junk stapled to the end. The network wants the plain storefront address and nothing else. One wrong character breaks full merchant's checkouts, and the error it produces tells you nothing about why. We fixed it by validating and normalizing that identifier in one place, so no part of the app can send a malformed one ever again.

**Browser Harness for Merchant Checkouts**

Minting a card turned out to be the easy half. Prava hands you a working one-time card and then stops.

Buying something means driving a real merchant's checkout: a storefront we don't control, that has never heard of us, with its own layout, its own quirks, its own captchas. We built a browser harness to do it — an automated browser that opens the product page, adds to cart, fills the address, and types in the minted card like a customer would. Storefronts customize their checkouts heavily, so anything written for one shop broke on the next. We eventually made two decisions that saved it: narrow the harness to a few checkout platform that's standardized enough to automate reliably.

I also hardcoded India at the start for Address so that was pretty wrong.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/5e4ab97d-e2a0-418a-9722-8bb3b51e4cce.png)

Justdm turns a DM into a checkout powered by Visa.

Every day, millions of product reels get sent in Instagram DMs and just... die there. justdm intercepts that moment and completes it: the reel becomes a real, priced item, and when you approve the buy, we mint a one-time virtual card through Prava that's locked to that exact merchant and exact amount enforced directly by Visa's network,  Visa's own infra is the safety net.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/ea6639b6-c84e-4f7f-a5cb-9563188dbbbc.png)Screenshot 2026-08-03 at 1.03.36 AM

JustDM is more than a shopping bookmarklet: it's the first product to close the loop from social intent → Visa-secured payment, entirely inside the conversation where the intent already existed. DMs stop being where purchases go to die and become where they start and finish social commerce with VISA underneath it.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Justdm turns the reel you already shared into a purchase.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/ab62c540-2f58-4869-af3c-f7baf2bdd4bf.png)

Instagram users share product reels in DMs constantly then the intent disappears into chat history. 
Justdm intercepts that moment: send us a reel (via IG DM, WhatsApp, or your OS share sheet), we identify the product, and it lands on your us as a real, priced, buyable item instead of a dead link. 

Tap to buy: approve with your device passkey, and justdm mints a one-time-use virtual card scoped to that exact merchant and amount,

Retailers pay justdm to be surfaced and ranked in that discoverability layer: We are the first paid channel for demand that starts as a social reel, not a search query.

Check out our video the live link is only going to work for insta ids in our beta test, please share your insta ids so we can approve them via meta console.

**OpenAI**

***Justdm** turns the reel you already saved into a purchase.*

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/84869ca1-21a2-4c8f-b27e-a6216f92c56d.png)

The problem: a reel or DM is unstructured — a video, a caption, maybe a product tag if you're lucky. Nothing a shopping engine can act on.

Justdm's resolver takes a reel keyframe/image and its caption and turns them into a structured product signal brand, product type, color, material, and a clean search query using multimodal, function-call-style extraction built on the OpenAI API interface. 

This structured-extraction layer builds the stack for ucp merchant for us. Once a reel becomes a structured product signal, it can be matched against live merchant inventory, priced, sized, and dropped into a dashboard as something buyable instead of dying in your DMs as a link nobody follows up on. Solve the extraction problem well, and everything downstream, discoverability, merchant placement, checkout becomes possible. BTW We use gpt 4.1

**Best Agentic User Experience**

*The biggest unlock for is that the product start at a simple DM which millions of people use daily.*

I would say the user doesn't even understand when the checkout occured after minting card that how fast the ux is for us and also for us:
The hardest problem in agentic products isn't the agent — it's trust. People can't see it working. Most agentic UX fails one of two ways: it hides everything (a black box, no visibility) or it exposes everything (a chat window that implies infinite capability, then breaks). justdm avoids both.

No new interaction to learn. The trigger is a DM — something the user already does. No "prompt the agent" moment.

The agent's work is visible, not chat-shaped. Every reel becomes a card on a dashboard, not a conversation turn. Each card shows its real state — working, exact match, similar match, or unreadable — so the user knows what's happening without reading a wall of text.

One approval moment, not constant negotiation. Discovery, pricing, and session setup happen silently. The only thing handed back to a human is a passkey tap to authorize spend — the one decision that shouldn't be automated. Nothing else.

Degrades honestly instead of pretending. If an item isn't buyable yet, the card says "view at merchant" — not a fake checkout button. The UI never claims capability the agent doesn't have.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/d93a1f7f-1e5b-40b2-aaa7-73610359a8ea.png)Screenshot 2026-08-03 at 1.23.59 AM
Justdm is an AI agent that turns unstructured intent a video someone sent in a DM into a completed purchase. A human approves the one decision i.e spending real money. Everything else is the agent's job.

That's the core of agentic commerce: an agent handles discovery and execution.

For us
A multimodal model reads the reel's keyframe and caption, extracts a structured product signal brand, type, material, search query.

No human types a search query.

Payment Is Agent-Initiated, Network-Enforced
Justdm opens a Prava session and mints a one-time virtual card scoped to the exact merchant and amount the agent determined.

A passkey confirmation is the one moment a person acts.
Before it: finding the product, pricing it, opening the session — the agent's job.
After it: settling the transaction — the agent's job.
Agents that discover and transact, with network-level guardrails standing in for the trust a human would otherwise have to extend by hand.
Even the merchant checkout is autonomous check out our video at: https://youtu.be/cnS7xoC8B-4

**The problem it solves**

This project is a basic** single-player FPS game prototype **made in Unity within a limited time frame (≈44 hours).

Our main goals for this project is to demonstrate core FPS mechanics, create an immersive war-zone experience with realistic environments, weapon handling,  and interesting storyline to keep player attached through the missions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Major Challanges Faced

 1) Hardware Limitations (Low-End Devices)

One of the major challenges in this project was developing the game on low-end devices. Due to limited system performance, game development became more difficult.
The system struggled to handle large maps, detailed textures, and multiple characters at the same time.
Lag and slow performance made testing and fixing errors time-consuming.
High-quality graphics features like advanced lighting and shadows could not be fully used.
Even with these limitations, the project was optimized as much as possible to achieve acceptable performance.

2) Map Design & Environment

Creating a believable battlefield environment presented several difficulties.
Achieving a realistic feel using terrain tools
Correct selection and blending of map textures
Designing trenches, uneven surfaces, and war-zone layouts
Performance optimization while maintaining visual quality

3) Enemy Movement

Enemy behavior was the most complex part of the project.
Gun Pointing Direction:
Aligning enemy weapons correctly toward the player during combat was difficult.
Animation Transitions:
Smooth transitions between idle, walk, attack, and death animations were challenging to implement.
Navigation Agent Issues:
Unity’s NavMesh Agent did not work correctly on the uneven battlefield terrain.
As a workaround, manual movement logic was attempted, but achieving natural enemy movement remained difficult.

**Open Track**

We idealised this idea ourselves irrespective of the Problem-statements of the Partners of Merge Conflict.

### BLOOP
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bloop-a116) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Poorvikab/Bloop) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://kiro-bloop.hashnode.dev/how-kiro-helped-evolve-ai-build-bloop) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/1Ne5ScYR7sQ?si=8WTahExXgGU_dyHm) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hackxios%202K25-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackxios2k25.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Where Concepts BLOOP Into Clarity

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Manim](https://img.shields.io/badge/Manim-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAST%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Bloop addresses the **gap between how STEM subjects** are taught and how they are actually understood. While science and mathematics rely heavily on visualization, structure, and practice, most existing tools remain text‑centric, static, or disconnected from real learning goals like exams and time constraints. This leads to shallow understanding, poor retention, and inefficient preparation. Bloop **reframes learning as a visual, adaptive, and goal‑oriented process**, helping learners move from **confusion to clarity**, from randomness to structure, and from **passive study to active mastery** within the constraints they actually face.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge while building Bloop was the **video generation pipeline occasionally breaking** due to the complexity of chaining multiple stages—LLM reasoning, visual code generation, rendering, and final video stitching. Failures were often non‑deterministic: a single scene could fail to render due to malformed code, timeout, or library‑level issues, causing the entire pipeline to break.

To address this, **Kiro helped us re‑architect the pipeline** into isolated, scene‑level units instead of treating video generation as an all‑or‑nothing process. We introduced looped retry mechanisms for failure‑prone stages and added graceful fallbacks, if a specific video scene failed even after 3 retries, the system would skip that scene and continue assembling the rest of the video. 
This ensured that users still received a usable explanation rather than a complete failure, significantly improving the robustness and reliability of the overall pipeline.

**Best Innovation**

Bloop fits the Best Innovation track because it **rethinks how STEM learning systems are built**, not just what they deliver. Instead of treating learning as text consumption or static videos,

> Private cross-chain bridge over Zcash to Starknet

![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cargo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cargo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cairo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cairo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Circom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Circom-333333?style=flat-square) ![StarkNet](https://img.shields.io/badge/StarkNet-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zcash](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zcash-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

- **Privacy-Preserving Transfers:** Unlike traditional bridges that expose "User A bridged 100 ZEC" on-chain, ZCLAIM uses Zcash's shielded notes and homomorphic value commitments. The bridge verifies validity without learning amounts, true financial privacy across chains.

   -  **Trustless Custody**: No centralized custodian holds your assets. Multiple independent vaults lock ZEC, each posting 150% collateral. If a vault misbehaves, users claim collateral directly. No single point of failure.

  - **Cryptographic Proof of Locking:** Zero-knowledge proofs (πZKMint/πZKBurn) prove notes exist in Zcash's Merkle tree, are addressed to the correct vault, and have matching value commitments, all without revealing actual values.

 - **On-Chain Zcash Verification:** The RelaySystem contract maintains Zcash block headers with PoW verification and Sapling commitment roots, enabling trustless verification of Zcash state on Starknet.

 - **Challenge-Response Security**: Vaults can challenge bad encryption by revealing shared secrets, with malicious users losing deposits.

 - **Composable Private DeFi**: wZEC on Starknet enables private trading on DEXs, private collateral in lending, and anonymous DAO participation, extending Zcash privacy into DeFi.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Cairo 2.8 Compiler Issues:** The Cairo compiler panicked when enabling multiple modules with cross-dependencies. Fixed by restructuring the module hierarchy, inlining crypto functions, and adding required Default/Copy traits to storage enums.

 - **Fixed-Size Array Limitations:** Cairo doesn't support 2D array indexing like Rust. The BLAKE2b sigma permutation table had to be reimplemented as an if-else lookup function instead of sigma.at(round).at(index).

 - **Zcash Cryptography in Cairo:** Zcash uses BLAKE2b-256, Equihash PoW, and SHA256d—none native to Cairo. Pure implementations would be gas-prohibitive. Solution: use circom circuits for heavy crypto off-chain, verify ZK proofs on-chain.

 - **Storage Constraints:** Cairo contracts can't store dynamic arrays. Created separate MintTransferStorage structs without Array<felt252> fields for persistence.

  - **RPC Deprecation:** Starknet public RPC endpoints (BlastAPI) became unreliable, requiring migration to Alchemy/Infura with API keys.

**Private DeFi & Trading**

private cross chain bridging of funds

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Tomato Bag integrates Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) through Prava to deliver a secure, agentic payment experience. From meal planning to checkout, the AI handles the complete commerce flow, requiring only a single user approval.

* **Scalable Agent Harness** – Our custom harness manages Codex execution, tool orchestration, memory, and sandboxed environments, making it easy to extend Tomato Bag with additional MCPs and autonomous capabilities in the future.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem We Solve

Generic fitness apps prescribe the same programme regardless of how the user's body is performing on a given day. A user who slept poorly, is under physiological stress, or has an elevated resting heart rate is pushed through the same high-intensity session as they would be on their best day. This is both ineffective and risky.

Solofit addresses this with three principles:

- **Measure, don't assume** -  Biometric state is captured objectively, not self-reported.
- **Reason, don't template** - AI generates plans from scratch based on current data, not static presets.
- **Adapt, don't repeat** - Every scan is a new input; every plan is a fresh output.

---

**Challenges we ran into**

Implimenting presgae SDK into React Native App but we nailed It

**Best Use of MongoDB**

MongoDB atlas and compass for social media community page database to share PRs and other achievements between user communities along with leader board for bragging rights

**Best Use of Presage SDK**

Fitness readiness is a physiological question, not a subjective one. Blood pressure, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, and respiratory rate are the same metrics sports scientists use to assess athlete recovery. Traditionally, measuring these required dedicated hardware - chest straps, pulse oximeters, or clinical-grade monitors.

Presage SmartSpectra solves this using **remote photoplethysmography (rPPG)**: the camera captures subtle colour changes in facial skin caused by blood flow, and signal processing extracts cardiovascular and respiratory metrics from that optical signal alone. No hardware. No wearable. Just the phone camera the user already has.

We evaluated several alternatives:

| Alternative | Why We Did Not Use It |
|---|---|
| Apple HealthKit / Google Fit | Passive aggregation only; requires wearable for real-time vitals |
| Heart rate from GPS watch | Requires separate hardware; not universally accessible |
| Manual self-reporting | Subjective, inconsistent, not medically meaningful |
| Generic camera HR apps | No REST API; no clinical-grade signal processing pipeline |

Presage was the only solution that provided a **REST API for rPPG-based biometric extraction** that works with standard phone cameras in a controlled environment, making it the only viable path to a hardware-free, objective readiness measurement system.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

Custom exercises and diet plan generation along with guided tips to deal with ailments if any while exercising

**The problem it solves**

Farmers face many challenges that affect their productivity and income. Crop diseases, unpredictable weather conditions, poor irrigation planning, and lack of timely agricultural guidance often lead to reduced crop yield and financial losses. Many farmers also struggle to identify plant diseases early or choose the most suitable crops for their soil and climate. In addition, access to accurate market price information is limited, making it difficult for farmers to sell their produce at the right time and get fair value.

Another major challenge is the limited availability of easy-to-use digital tools designed specifically for rural farmers. Many existing solutions are complex or not available in local languages, which makes them difficult to adopt.

Karsakah AI aims to address these problems by providing farmers with simple, accessible, and data-driven support. Through AI-based crop disease detection, weather insights, crop recommendations, and market information, the platform helps farmers make smarter decisions and improve their overall farming outcomes. 🌾

**Challenges we ran into**

While developing **Karsakah AI**, several challenges were encountered. One of the main challenges was understanding the real needs of farmers and designing a platform that is simple enough for people who may not be familiar with digital technology. Ensuring that the interface is easy to use, with minimal text and clear features, required careful planning.

Another challenge was integrating multiple data sources such as weather data, agricultural information, and market prices into one platform. Collecting reliable datasets and connecting APIs efficiently took significant effort. Additionally, implementing AI-based crop disease detection required finding suitable datasets and training models that can provide accurate results.

Balancing technical complexity with usability was also a key challenge. The goal was to build a powerful system while keeping it accessible and practical for farmers in rural areas. 🌾

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into**
One of the biggest technical hurdles I faced while building this project was a persistent database connection error after deploying the Next.js app to Vercel.
The Bug
After deployment, the app started throwing this error on every request that needed to fetch user progress data:

**Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND db.bclxmxvffswramiifjmt.supabase.co
    at async o.queryWithCache...
    [cause]: Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND ...**

The query was trying to connect to Supabase using a direct PostgreSQL connection, but it kept failing with a DNS resolution error.

**Root Cause Discovery**

I initially thought it was a credentials issue or that the Supabase project had paused. After checking the dashboard and logs, I noticed the connection string was using the **Direct connection:**

postgresql://postgres:[PASSWORD]@db.bclxmxvffswramiifjmt.supabase.co:5432/postgres

When I opened the Supabase dashboard, I saw a clear warning: "Not IPv4 compatible" with a note saying "Use Session Pooler if on an IPv4 network".

This was the key insight — Supabase’s direct database connections are now IPv6-only in most regions, while Vercel (and most serverless platforms) still primarily operate on IPv4. The hostname simply couldn’t be resolved from the Vercel runtime.

**How I Solved It**

I switched from the Direct connection to Supabase’s Transaction Pooler (the recommended option for serverless applications):

Went back to the Supabase Dashboard → Connect page.
Changed the connection method from "Direct connection" to "Transaction Pooler".
Copied the new connection string (using port 6543).
Updated the DATABASE_URL environment variable in Vercel.
Redeployed the application.

I also added ?pgbouncer=true to the connection string (since I’m using Drizzle ORM) for better compatibility with the pooler.

**Outcome**
The error disappeared immediately after the new deployment. The app now connects reliably, and performance is actually better because of connection pooling.

**Key Takeaway**
This experience taught me how important it is to read platform-specific warnings (the "Not IPv4 compatible" banner) and to always use the correct connection method for serverless environments. What looked like a mysterious DNS error was actually a common mismatch between modern database hosting and serverless infrastructure.

> Smart Detection. Smart Isolation. Smart Grid

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Relay Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/Relay%20Module-333333?style=flat-square) ![ESP-32 WiFi Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/ESP--32%20WiFi%20Module-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sensors](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sensors-333333?style=flat-square) ![LCD Screen](https://img.shields.io/badge/LCD%20Screen-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The **GridSense** system continuously monitors voltage, current, and temperature of all three phases in real time. Under **normal operating conditions, the relays remain in a closed state**, allowing power flow, and the corresponding LED indicators glow, providing instant visual confirmation of healthy phases.

When a fault is detected in any phase:
 - The affected phase relay is automatically opened (isolated)

The corresponding **LED turns OFF**, **indicating a fault condition**
- The faulty phase is safely disconnected from the system

At the same time, the system implements an intelligent load transfer mechanism with phase priority **(Phase A → Phase B → Phase C)**. If the currently active phase becomes faulty, the load is automatically transferred to the next healthy phase, ensuring continuous power supply without manual intervention.

Once the fault condition is removed, the system continuously monitors the phase and, after a 5-second stability delay, automatically restores the relay to the closed state and turns the LED ON again, confirming that the phase has returned to a healthy condition.

This approach prevents:
- total power failure 
- protects electrical equipment
- improves system reliability  
- enhances safety by isolating only the faulty phase instead of shutting down the   entire system.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Challenges I Ran Into :
 
1.Handling Multiple Fault Conditions :-      
      Managing voltage, current, and temperature faults across three phases simultaneously was challenging. Initial logic caused incorrect isolation when multiple faults occurred together. This was solved by implementing phase-wise fault flags and independent decision logic

2.Safe Relay Switching and Load Transfer :-
   Instant switching between phases caused unstable relay behavior and unsafe transitions. A short safety delay was added between relay OFF and ON operations to ensure proper isolation before load transfer.

3.Reliable Auto-Recovery Mechanism :-
    Immediate reconnection after fault clearance led to relay chattering. This was resolved by adding a time-based recovery delay so a phase reconnects only after remaining stable for a fixed duration.

4.Clear System Status Indication :-
     Displaying real-time phase health and relay status clearly was difficult during rapid changes. Synchronizing LEDs, LCD messages, and serial output provided clear and reliable system feedback.

5.Dashboard Integration with Simulation :-
    Direct data access from the Wokwi simulator was not available. This was overcome by sending real-time data to a cloud IoT platform using standard HTTP communication, similar to real ESP32 deployments.

- How We Got Over These Challenges :

We addressed these challenges by breaking the system into phase-wise independent logic, allowing each phase to be monitored, isolated, and recovered without affecting the others. Safety delays and time-based recovery mechanisms were added to ensure stable relay operation and prevent false switching.
To improve clarity and debugging, we synchronized relay states with LEDs, LCD output, and serial monitoring. For dashboard integration, we adopted a cloud-based IoT communication approach, making the system scalable, reliable, and close to real-world smart grid implementations.

**The problem it solves**

## ❗ The Problem It Solves

Modern education platforms often focus only on content delivery, lacking **personalization, engagement, mentorship, and real-world career direction**. Students struggle with low motivation, unclear progress tracking, limited guidance, and isolation during learning.

**EduMentor solves these challenges by combining AI, gamification, and human mentorship into one unified platform.**

### 🧠 Key Problems Addressed

- **Low Engagement in Learning**  
  Traditional learning feels repetitive and boring, leading to dropouts and poor consistency.

- **One-Size-Fits-All Education**  
  Most platforms ignore individual strengths, weaknesses, and learning pace.

- **Lack of Mentorship & Guidance**  
  Students often don’t know whom to ask for help or how to get expert guidance.

- **Unclear Progress & Motivation**  
  Learners lack visibility into their growth, achievements, and learning consistency.

- **Poor Collaboration & Communication**  
  Learning in isolation reduces understanding, confidence, and problem-solving skills.

### ✅ How EduMentor Makes It Better

- 🎮 **Gamifies Learning** with XP, badges, streaks, challenges, and leaderboards to keep students motivated.
- 🤖 **Personalizes Learning Paths** using AI-driven recommendations based on performance and behavior.
- 👨‍🏫 **Connects Students with Expert Mentors** through a secure mentor marketplace and 1-on-1 sessions.
- 📊 **Tracks Progress Visually** using dashboards, analytics, and achievement systems.
- 💬 **Enables Real-Time Collaboration** through peer chats, study groups, and mentor communication.
- 🔐 **Ensures Secure & Role-Based Access** for students, mentors, and admins.

### 🎯 What People Can Use EduMentor For

- Students can **learn smarter, stay consistent, and grow faster**
- Mentors can **share expertise and earn through structured guidance**
- Learners can **collaborate, compete, and improve together**
- Institutions can **offer a modern, engaging, and scalable learning ecosystem**

➡️ **In short:** EduMentor transforms education from passive content consumption into an **engaging, guided, and personalized learning experience**.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

Building **EduMentor** was an exciting but challenging journey. While developing a feature-rich, scalable platform, I encountered several technical and design hurdles. Below are the key challenges and how I overcame them:

### ⚙️ Handling Complex State & User Roles
With multiple user roles (Students, Mentors, Admins), managing access control and UI rendering became complex.

**Solution:**  
I implemented role-based route protection and conditional rendering using Next.js middleware and centralized auth context, ensuring secure and clean role separation.

---

### 🔄 Real-Time Chat Synchronization Issues
Maintaining real-time message updates without duplication or delay was initially unstable.

**Solution:**  
I optimized Socket.io event handling, added unique message IDs, and implemented proper cleanup of socket listeners to prevent memory leaks and duplicate messages.

---

### 🎮 Gamification Logic & Consistency
Keeping XP, badges, streaks, and leaderboards in sync across sessions was tricky, especially with edge cases like missed days or partial progress.

**Solution:**  
I designed a centralized gamification service with clear rules and atomic updates, ensuring consistency even during refreshes or reconnects.

---

### 🤖 AI Recommendation Accuracy
Early AI recommendations felt generic and repetitive due to limited user interaction data.

**Solution:**  
I refined the recommendation logic by combining multiple signals—course completion, quiz scores, time spent, and interests—resulting in more relevant suggestions over time.

---

### 🎨 UI Performance & Animations
Heavy animations and interactive components initially caused performance drops on low-end devices.

**Solution:**  
I optimized animations using Framer Motion best practices, lazy-loaded heavy components, and minimized unnecessary re-renders.

---

### 🔐 Authentication Edge Cases
Handling session persistence, redirects, and protected routes led to unexpected login loops.

**Solution:**  
I standardized authentication flow using NextAuth, carefully managed callback URLs, and added fallback states to prevent broken navigation.

---

### 🧩 Component Reusability & Scaling
As features grew, maintaining consistency across UI components became harder.

**Solution:**  
I created a reusable design system using Radix UI and custom components, making the UI scalable and easy to maintain.

---

### 🏁 Key Takeaway
Each challenge helped improve the architecture and overall quality of EduMentor. Solving these issues strengthened my understanding of **scalable system design, real-time applications, and user-focused development**.

➡️ Challenges weren’t roadblocks — they were **learning milestones**.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**DrawRush 🎨**
A real-time multiplayer drawing and guessing game built with Next.js, Node.js, and Socket.io. Players take turns drawing while others guess the word, similar to Pictionary.

**Features**
**Real-time Multiplayer Gaming**: Play with friends using WebSocket connections
**Drawing Board**: Interactive canvas for drawing with real-time synchronization
**Chat**: Integrated message communication using Socket.io
**Game Lobby**: Room creation and player management
**Score Tracking**: Points awarded for drawing and correct guesses
**Word Hints**: AI-powered hints using Cohere AI
**Responsive Design**: Mobile-friendly interface with Tailwind CSS
**Toast Notifications**: User feedback with react-hot-toast

**Tech Stack**
**Frontend**
**Framework**: Next.js 16.1.2 with React 19.2.3
**Real-time Communication**: Socket.io Client
**UI Library**: Lucide React (icons)
**Styling**: Tailwind CSS 4
**Notifications**: react-hot-toast
**Avatar Generation**: DiceBear

**Backend**
**Runtime**: Node.js
**Framework**: Express.js
**Real-time Communication**: Socket.io
**AI Integration**: Cohere AI (for hints)
**Utilities**: UUID, CORS, dotenv

**Gameplay**
**Create a Room**: Enter your name and click "Create Room" to generate a room code
**Join a Room**: Share the room code with friends or enter it to join
**Game Flow**:  
One player is designated as the drawer
The drawer sees a word and has limited time to draw it
Other players guess what's being drawn
Points are awarded based on correct guesses and drawing
Players take turns as the drawer
**Game Settings**: Room host has the right to modify the game settings in game lobby.
