## 🎯 Problem

Kolkata suburban railways carry **40 lakh passengers daily** across 458 stations and 1,501 km of track. Yet:

- 70%+ of crimes go **unreported**
- No real-time crowd safety information exists
- Women commuters have no dedicated safety layer
- Police have no data-driven patrol intelligence

---

## 💡 Solution — 4 Pillars

|---|---|
| **Crowd Intelligence** | SAFE / CAUTION / AVOID badges per train, powered by Neo4j + Random Forest ML |
| **Nirbhoy Sathi Bot** | Multilingual (EN/HI/BN) AI complaint assistant — auto-generates GRP FIR forms |
| **Police Intelligence Dashboard** | Crime hotspots, hourly patterns, patrol recommendations *(coming soon)* |
| **Women's Safety Layer** | SOS button, live location sharing, safe arrival timer *(coming soon)* |

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

**1. erail.in blocked direct scraping**
The API rejected requests without browser headers. Fixed by copying real Chrome headers (User-Agent, Referer) to mimic a real browser request.


**2. Neo4j showing morning trains from Howrah as GREEN**
Our crowd distribution rules weren't accounting for trains *departing* from city stations — only trains arriving. Fixed by adding `is_from_city` logic so 7–10am Howrah departures are correctly marked RED.

**3. IndentationError crashing FastAPI on every edit**
Manually adding code to `main.py` kept breaking Python indentation. Fixed by always replacing the entire file instead of patching individual lines.

**4. Groq LLaMA3 hallucinating IPC sections**
The model was inventing fake law sections with confidence. Fixed using RAG — IPC sections are now always retrieved from ChromaDB, never generated by the LLM.

**Open Innovation**

## How KolkataRail Fits Open Innovation

Open Innovation means solving real public problems using technology that is 
accessible, scalable, and community-driven. KolkataRail does exactly that.

**1. Solving a Problem Nobody Has Solved Yet**  
Indian Railways carries 23 million passengers daily but has zero public 
crowd-safety intelligence. No app, no API, no data exists. We built the 
first AI-powered crowd safety layer for Kolkata suburban trains from scratch.

**2. Open Data + Open Architecture**  
Our train data is scraped from publicly available erail.in timetables. 
Our graph database, ML model, and API are all open and extensible — any 
developer can plug in new train lines, cities, or safety features on top.

**3. Community-Powered Intelligence**  
The system gets smarter with every commuter report. Each RED/YELLOW/GREEN 
submission from a real passenger improves future predictions — turning 40 
lakh daily commuters into a distributed safety sensor network.

**4. Inclusive by Design**  
Nirbhoy Sathi works in Bengali, Hindi, and English — because a safety 
system that only works in English excludes the majority of its users. 
Language should never be a barrier to reporting a crime.

**5. Scalable Beyond Kolkata**  
The same architecture works for any Indian city — Mumbai, Chennai, Delhi. 
Swap the train data, reseed Neo4j, retrain the model. The core system 
requires no structural changes to scale nationally.

**The problem it solves**

MedAI solves this by acting as an intelligent first layer of medical triage. It analyzes symptoms in real time, assesses severity, and guides users toward appropriate care and specialist consultation. By transforming unstructured symptom descriptions into structured medical insights, MedAI reduces uncertainty, prevents unnecessary hospital visits, and ensures timely medical intervention when needed.

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, we faced several technical and design challenges.
One major challenge was implementing real-time voice processing with low latency. Converting speech to text, processing it through AI models, and generating responses quickly required careful optimization and API handling.
Another challenge was ensuring medically responsible outputs. Since healthcare is sensitive, we had to structure prompts carefully to avoid direct diagnosis claims and instead provide severity-based guidance and specialist recommendations.
Integrating multiple components — voice processing, symptom analysis, severity assessment, doctor availability, and appointment booking — into a seamless workflow was also complex. We overcame this by modularizing the architecture and clearly defining data flow between each layer.
Through iterative testing and UI refinement, we improved response accuracy, user clarity, and overall system reliability.

**Grand Prize**

MedAI directly addresses challenges in early symptom detection, medical triage, and healthcare accessibility. By providing AI-powered real-time symptom analysis and severity assessment, it improves decision-making at the entry point of healthcare. It reduces unnecessary hospital visits and ensures critical cases are prioritized.

### FWakeFi
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fwakefi-42cd) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/nihaparkashuni-del/FWakefi) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://f-wakefi-atfh.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/VWPFIrGJVgw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHDenver%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethdenver2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> An alarm that stakes and wakes

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every alarm app on the planet has the same fatal flaw: zero consequences for ignoring it.

You set an alarm. You snooze it. You feel guilty for 5 minutes. Nothing happens. The app still gives you a badge tomorrow. There's no real cost to failing — so the brain learns to ignore it.

Behavioral economics calls this the commitment problem: humans consistently intend to do things tomorrow that they resist doing when tomorrow arrives. The solution  proven by decades of research is credible pre-commitment: locking in a real cost before the moment of weakness arrives.

Traditional accountability apps can't do this because they're just software. They can threaten, but they can't enforce.

WakeFi can. Because it uses the blockchain.

What People Can Use It For
⏰ Wake-Up With Real Stakes
Stake HBAR before you sleep. If you wake up and answer a crypto news quiz within 15 minutes of your alarm — your stake is safely returned. If you sleep through, snooze, or ignore it — Hedera Consensus automatically executes the burn, even if your phone is off.

Proving Discipline On-Chain
Every successful wake-up is a verifiable event: a ScheduleDeleteTransaction on the Hedera ledger. You get an actual on-chain record of your consistency, not just a local streak badge.

Morning Crypto Briefing
The quiz pulls a live crypto news article every morning (via CryptoCompare). You don't just wake up, you wake up informed. The question tests whether you actually read it, not just whether you're physically present.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest blocker was discovering that Hedera's ScheduleCreateTransaction does not auto-execute by default  you must explicitly call setWaitForExpiry(true), which is buried in the SDK docs with minimal examples. Without it, the schedule just expires silently and nothing burns. We found this after debugging why scheduled transactions were creating successfully but never executing.

A second critical bug: the Hedera SDK silently rejected our private key because it was ECDSA but being parsed as ED25519 the default. This produced a cryptic signing failure with no useful error message; we isolated it by running a raw Node.js reproduction script against the testnet until the signing algorithm mismatch surfaced.

**Use of AI tools and agents**

WakeFi was built using Cursor (AI-powered IDE) with Antigravity as the primary agentic assistant running inside it.
It handled the full development loop autonomously reading and writing source files, running terminal commands, debugging Hedera SDK errors, executing test scripts against testnet, capturing browser screenshots to verify UI, and pushing commits to GitHub. It maintained context across the entire overnight build session without losing the thread of the architecture. Gemini 3.0 generated the alarm clock splash screen asset (alarm.png). Using all these the system design, architecture decisions, and prompt engineering was done.

**Futurllama**

WakeFi combines behavioral psychology, AI-generated quizzes, and blockchain automation exactly.  built a loss-aversion alarm clock on blockchain before. It's frontier tech with a real use case.

**On-Chain Automation with Hedera Schedule Service**

When a user arms their WakeFi alarm, the app creates a ScheduleCreateTransaction that will automatically transfer their staked HBAR to the burn address at exactly 15 minutes after wake time. No server executes this  the Hedera ledger does it autonomously. The app can be closed, the phone can go offline  the burn still happens. If the user wakes up and passes the quiz, a ScheduleDeleteTransaction cancels the burn. This is a real-world automation use case where the blockchain replaces human willpower enforcement

**“No Solidity Allowed” - Hedera SDKs Only**

WakeFi is built entirely using the Hedera JavaScript SDK — no Solidity, no EVM, no smart contracts of any kind. Every on-chain action uses native Hedera transaction types. ScheduleCreateTransaction creates the burn, ScheduleDeleteTransaction cancels it. The entire product logic lives in hederaService.js using only @hashgraph/sdk. This is a real consumer app — not a demo — that proves Hedera's native SDK is powerful enough to build production products without touching the EVM

### Kira
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kira-2875) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SudhanPlayz/Kira) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-finance-hub.replit.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI for Indian shopkeepers: udhaar, SMS & voice, EN

![Expo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Expo-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Drizzle](https://img.shields.io/badge/Drizzle-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node-333333?style=flat-square) ![react-native](https://img.shields.io/badge/react--native-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anthropic](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anthropic-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Small shopkeepers across India manage udhaar (customer credit), supplier dues, and daily cashflow using notebooks or memory. They receive transaction clues from SMS, UPI alerts, and informal messages in Hinglish or Hindi but have no simple way to log these, track who owes what, or get actionable advice without complex software.

**Kira solves this by:**

1. **Multiple input modes** — (a) **Paste or type** messages (e.g. "Ravi ko 500 udhaar diya", "2k aaya from Amit"); (b) **Incoming SMS**: on-device SMS reader sends raw text to the API; Claude parses and stores pending items; user confirms or dismisses from Home/Alerts to create transactions. (c) **Voice**: tap-to-speak in Add Transaction; recording is sent to OpenAI Whisper (Hindi/English), transcript is fed into the same AI parser.

2. **Structured parsing** — Claude parses with a strict JSON schema (type, amount, party_name, confidence, optional clarification_suggestion). Low-confidence parses prompt the user to confirm before saving.

3. **Customer & supplier intelligence** — Customers tracked with pending udhaar and total business; suppliers with pending dues. AI assesses customer risk (credit suggestion) and supplier payment priority (negotiation tips). Results stored with lastAssessedAt / lastAnalyzedAt.

4. **Cashflow & recommendations** — Cashflow analysis (7-day/30-day projections, stability, warnings, suggestions) is persisted. An **orchestrator** can call tools (recent transactions, dashboard summary, customers, suppliers, pending recommendations, cashflow, customer transactions) to gather context, then outputs up to 3 recommendations (collect_payment, pay_supplier, reduce_credit, extend_credit, cashflow_warning, general_advice) and optional agent_decisions (approve/reject per contributing agent), stored in agent logs.

5. **India-first** — Bilingual UI and AI (English + Hindi/Devanagari). Expo app (Web, iOS, Android); Replit-ready backend with batch rate limiting and SSE for batch analysis.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Parsing informal Indian language** — We use Claude with a strict JSON schema and confidence + clarification_suggestion for ambiguous input. Parser accepts Hinglish variants (udhar/udhaar, 2k/aaya/diya) and run-on sentences.

**Orchestrator with tools** — The orchestrator can call 7 read-only tools (transactions, dashboard, customers, suppliers, recommendations, cashflow, customer transactions). We use the AI SDK (generateText, stepCountIs(5)) with Anthropic; if tooling fails (e.g. baseURL/404), we fall back to context-only and structured parse. Agent decisions (approve/reject per agent) are logged in metadata.

**Incoming SMS flow** — On-device SMS reader posts rawText to /api/incoming-sms; we parse and store as pending. User confirms (create transaction + update customer/supplier) or dismisses. Home and Alerts show pending SMS with Add/Dismiss; unread count includes pending SMS.

**Voice input** — expo-av recording → base64 → OpenAI Whisper (gpt-4o-mini-transcribe) with language hi/en → transcript into message field, then same parser. Handles permissions and recording state in the app.

**Persistence and batch** — Cashflow analyses stored in DB; orchestrator tool get_cashflow reads latest. Batch analysis (all customers/suppliers + cashflow + orchestrator) uses concurrency limits and retries; progress streamed via SSE.

**Hackathon Prizes**

Kira is built for **Build India**: Indian small businesses and shopkeepers, **Claude** for Hinglish/UPI parsing and multi-agent orchestration (with tool use for live business context), **Replit**-ready Express + Neon Postgres.

It addresses **India-first** (udhaar, supplier dues, bilingual), **language diversity** (SMS + voice + text in Hindi/English, Devanagari outputs), **on-ground realities** (mobile-first, SMS ingestion, voice input, simple UX, actionable recommendations). We ship a working app: paste/SMS/voice → parse → transactions; customers/suppliers with AI risk and negotiation tips; persisted cashflow; tooled orchestrator with agent decisions; batch analysis over SSE.

Team **Flaze** -- [Prajan Bala](https://github.com/NotWrench), [Sudharson A R](https://github.com/SudhanPlayz)

### REagent
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/reagent-the-autonomous-ai-agent-for-binary-analysis-e945) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/criticic/reagent) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/dgbO6TMoox8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomous AI Agent for Binary Analysis

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anthropic](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anthropic-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cybersecurity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cybersecurity-333333?style=flat-square) ![claude](https://img.shields.io/badge/claude-333333?style=flat-square) ![litellm](https://img.shields.io/badge/litellm-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI-Agent](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI--Agent-333333?style=flat-square) ![Textual](https://img.shields.io/badge/Textual-333333?style=flat-square) ![reverse-engineering](https://img.shields.io/badge/reverse--engineering-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**AI Can Build — But It Can't Break.** Every developer has Claude Code and Codex CLI for *writing* software, but *finding vulnerabilities* in compiled binaries remains entirely manual. As AI-assisted development ships code faster, the attack surface grows exponentially. We need agentic AI on defense too.

**The talent gap is real.** Fewer than 10,000 capable reverse engineers exist globally at $300K+/year. India is digitizing critical infrastructure — UPI, Aadhaar, DigiLocker — but lacks the RE workforce to audit the binaries powering it.

**Existing tools are passive.** IDA Pro costs $2K+/year. Ghidra is free but purely passive. Neither can run a binary, set breakpoints, or verify a hypothesis autonomously.

**REagent** takes a binary + goal and autonomously: (1) runs the binary to observe behavior, (2) triages metadata and security features, (3) decompiles and traces cross-references, (4) launches GDB/LLDB to set breakpoints, read registers, inspect memory, and *prove* hypotheses, (5) reports verified findings with evidence chains.

The key innovation: the **Autonomous Verification Loop**. Static analysis *proposes* hypotheses, dynamic analysis *confirms or rejects* them by executing code. No unverified claims. Built with a multi-agent architecture (6,500+ lines, 26 tools), three-tier context management, D-Mail context time-travel, managed PTY system, and a real-time TUI — all powered by Claude Sonnet + Haiku.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Context Explosion:** A single GDB session dumps thousands of lines. We built three-tier context management: tool-level truncation (2000 lines/50KB), pruning old results into stubs, and LLM-based compaction with Claude Haiku that summarizes history while keeping recent messages verbatim.

**Agent Drift:** After 20 steps on a wrong path, the agent's context is polluted and it can't pivot. We built D-Mail (Context Time-Travel): the agent sends knowledge back to a past checkpoint, context reverts, and it restarts with hindsight. Implemented via a `BackToTheFuture` exception that reverts the JSONL context store.

**Making Debuggers Agent-Compatible:** GDB/LLDB expect human interaction. We built a managed PTY system with process group isolation (`os.setpgrp`), ANSI stripping, 50K-line thread-safe rolling buffers, and prompt-based command/response matching. This makes debuggers reliably drivable by an LLM.

**GDB vs LLDB Abstraction:** macOS ships LLDB, Linux ships GDB with different syntax. We built a translation map that auto-detects the debugger and transparently converts operations. The agent never knows which debugger runs.

**Decompiler Fallback:** Not every system has rz-ghidra. Our decompile tool chains: `pdg` → `pdc` → `pdsf+pdf`. The agent always gets useful output.

**Decoupling Agent from UI:** A typed Wire Protocol with 15 event types lets CLI and TUI subscribe to the same agent stream.

**Hackathon Prizes**

**Claude at the Core:** Two-model architecture — Claude Sonnet for reasoning (orchestration, code comprehension, hypothesis formation, script generation) + Claude Haiku for context compaction. Extended thinking support with signature round-tripping. Demonstrates sophisticated, production-grade use of Anthropic's model lineup.

**India Relevance:** India is digitizing critical infrastructure at unprecedented scale — UPI, Aadhaar, DigiLocker, CoWIN. The compiled binaries powering this infrastructure need security auditing, but the RE talent pool is tiny and expensive. REagent democratizes capability previously locked behind $2K+/year tools (IDA Pro) and rare human expertise. India's growing CTF community and cybersecurity workforce gets a force multiplier.

**Novel Innovation:**
- The only AI system that *proves* findings via runtime debugger verification
- D-Mail: context time-travel to escape agent drift — a novel solution to a fundamental problem in long-running agent tasks
- Progressive skill loading: on-demand domain reference loading instead of prompt stuffing
- Wire protocol: clean architectural separation enabling CLI + TUI + future web UI from the same agent core

**Why This Exists:** Born from years of competitive CTF reverse engineering and cybersecurity work at IIT (BHU). The security side of software needs the same AI tooling that the development side already has.

Team **cynikal inc** -- [Sagnik Mandal](https://github.com/criticic/)

> Resell. Donate. Make an Impact.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many people want to sell or donate usable items, but existing platforms are often unsafe, untrusted, and confusing. Users don’t know the right price, worry about fake buyers or sellers, and donating items usually involves unclear processes and no proof of impact.

This platform makes reselling and donating simple, safe, and transparent. AI helps users set fair prices, detect basic product condition, and flag suspicious activity. Secure login, verified profiles, in-app chat, and escrow payments reduce scams and misuse.

It also allows users to donate items directly to verified NGOs, with doorstep pickup, delivery tracking, and auto-generated donation certificates. This removes middlemen and ensures items reach the right people.

Overall, the platform helps users reuse items responsibly, avoid fraud, and contribute to social good in an easy and reliable way.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge we faced was building and tuning the AI-based price estimation and description generation. Initially, the AI outputs were inconsistent, prices were sometimes too high or too low, and generated descriptions did not always match the product condition. We fixed this by adding validation logic, limiting AI outputs to safe ranges, and allowing users to review and edit AI-generated suggestions before publishing a listing.

Another challenge was creating a simple UI for different user roles. Sellers, buyers, and NGOs all need different information, and showing everything on one screen made the design confusing. We solved this by separating dashboards and keeping the layout minimal, with clear navigation and consistent design components.

**Sustainable Development Goals**

This project aligns with multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by promoting responsible consumption, social welfare, and sustainable communities. By enabling people to resell and donate usable items instead of discarding them, the platform directly supports SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, reducing waste and encouraging reuse.

The direct donation feature connects users with verified NGOs, helping essential goods reach people in need, which contributes to SDG 1: No Poverty and SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities. Doorstep pickup and transparent delivery ensure fair and efficient distribution of resources.

Additionally, by reducing unnecessary purchases and encouraging reuse, the platform helps lower environmental impact, supporting SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities and SDG 13: Climate Action.

**Open Innovation**

This project aligns with the Open Innovation track by rethinking how technology can be used to solve everyday problems in a more inclusive and impactful way. Instead of treating resale and donation as separate systems, the platform combines AI-assisted resale, direct NGO donations, and secure logistics into a single solution.

The solution is scalable, adaptable, and not limited to a single domain, making it suitable for multiple use cases such as community reuse, disaster relief support, and NGO resource distribution. This flexibility and problem-driven innovation make it a strong fit for the Open Innovation track.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vocalguard-ab92) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/harshitag20/VocalGuard) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackTU%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacktu7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Tracking speech changes for early neurological

![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-333333?style=flat-square) ![LibROSA](https://img.shields.io/badge/LibROSA-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![pydub](https://img.shields.io/badge/pydub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

VocalGuard is a speech based early screening and monitoring tool designed to identify meaningful changes in voice patterns associated with neurological conditions such as Parkinson’s disease. It is intended for screening support and monitoring, not medical diagnosis.

Primary Uses

1.Early screening support: Detects statistically significant deviations in speech that may appear before visible motor symptoms, helping flag individuals who may benefit from early clinical evaluation.

2.Longitudinal monitoring: Tracks how a person’s speech changes over time relative to their own baseline, making it useful for monitoring disease progression after diagnosis.

3.Treatment and therapy feedback: Helps observe whether speech patterns stabilize or improve following medication changes or speech therapy.

4.Research and academic use: Provides a lightweight, explainable prototype for studying speech-related neurological changes and feature-level behavior.

How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer

1.Objective assessment: Reduces reliance on subjective listening by providing measurable, repeatable acoustic feature analysis.

2.Personalized comparison: Compares speech against an individual’s own baseline instead of a generic population model, reducing bias.

3.Non invasive and low cost: Requires only a microphone or audio file, with no specialized hardware.

Explainable results: Visualizes feature wise deviations, making it clear which aspects of speech are changing.

Ethically safer: Avoids disease classification and diagnostic claims, focusing instead on deviation detection and screening support.

Overall, VocalGuard complements clinical workflows by enabling accessible, continuous, and explainable speech monitoring, especially in settings where frequent specialist evaluation is not feasible.

**Challenges we ran into**

false positive cases, background noises, breaks in voice records

### CodeBuddy
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/codebuddy-6dc0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/arnavag9545-star/CodeBuddy) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/NqhgElGthbw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Where coding meets collabaration

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Monaco Editor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Monaco%20Editor-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

It does not take an experienced coder even a second to recall the number of instances where he wished he could collaborate real time with his other colleagues. The usual process of uploading into GitHub and then collaborating upon the files from there is a long one, hence we came up with the idea of CodeBuddy. CodeBuddy provides a platform that allows coders from all around the world to work real time with each other. It allows the users a shared code editor and a working space which even extends to a Canvas. These additions allow the users to not only code but also, if need arises, explain it using the canvas to others. The coded files can then be downloaded and stored quite easily for everyone. The most optimal use cases are those where a teacher needs to teach the students. Instead of using multiple platforms for all these functionalities, we have combined them into a single platform CodeBuddy.

**Challenges we ran into**

The project consisted mainly of 3 components. The front end work of Code editor and Canvas and the backend work of syncing them through websockets. The major challenge which persisted throughout the project was real time syncing of the canvas. While the code editor and it’s functionalities were somewhat easily integrated, integrating Canvas with the backend was very tough and ran into constant problems. To improve the overall UI, we decided to incorporate the whole setting up of DataBase, something which we were not acquainted with and hence it constantly required us debugging. Specifically coming to DataBase, we decided to implement Persistence and Data Restoration for late joiners, which again was quite hard to implement and required us constantly banging our heads against the walls for them to be integrated successfully.

**Open Track**

Our solution caters to a wide range of people

**Fresher's Track**

We are but a bunch of freshers, in our voyage of dev.

Team **TeamRocket** -- [Arnav Agarwal](https://github.com/arnavag9545-star), Kapil Kulkarni, Vedant Chaudhary

> A tricky Card Game

![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

DRIVE LINK FOR DEMO VIDEO!!!!!!!!

Description / Overview
MindF*ck is multiplayer card game where players compete to maintain the lowest sum value of all cards in their hand. The game combines strategy, memeory retention, and decision-making in a competitive real-time environment.

Players can create or join rooms, and all game actions are synced across devices.The player can make strategic decisions or can just do fun random actions to make the game more interesting.

**Challenges we ran into**

Known Issues
UI responsiveness may vary on larger devices
Game state recovery if app closes mid-game is limited
Scope
A login page with phone number and OTP or with Email and passkey
Sharing of code is not possible yet.We wanted to at least be able to copy the code and then paste it on the respective messanging platforms.
We wanted to have a range of 3-8 players with flexible players in the game. The game could start whenever there were sufficient players.
Timer per player for quick decisions
End game logic was different. Whenever a player called end game, a last round was to be commenced. After each player gets a last turn and the turn of the end game initiator came again, that;s when the game was to end
We wanted to add a feature of quick swap and throwing of cards. Which means that whenever a player had the same valued card as on the pile, they can quickly add it to the pile so as to reduce cards and hence their sum. Another interesting feature was that we can throw the card of another player if we know it is the same as that as the last card of the pile and we can give them a bad card of ours
New deck recycling. Whenever deck got empty, cards from the pile reshuffle and form a new pile
Power logic issues
We can't see all cards of every player in the end. Hence, we cannot know our sum as well as the sum of players who did not win

### Vaahan
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vahaan-4193) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/arihantjain-14/Vaahan) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/t6J2xFb2MeA) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/t6J2xFb2MeA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Smart Public Transport for Small Cities.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In many small and semi-urban cities, public transport systems are poorly digitized. 
Passengers often face confusion around ticket pricing, route availability, and lack 
any incentive to prefer buses over private vehicles.

Vaahan solves this by providing a simple and structured public transport platform.

### How people can use it:
- Passengers can book buses for intercity and intracity travel from a single platform  
- Ticket prices are calculated automatically based on distance, removing manual guesswork  
- Users earn carbon points for choosing public transport, which can be reused as discounts  
- Drivers can digitally register their buses, add schedules, and manage routes easily  

### How it makes travel easier and safer:
- Reduces confusion by showing clear pricing and rewards before booking  
- Encourages eco-friendly travel through carbon point incentives  
- Digitizes bus and schedule management for better organization  
- Lays the foundation for future safety and accessibility features like SOS, live tracking, PWD concessions, and ride feedback systems  

Overall, Vaahan simplifies public transport usage while promoting sustainable and  responsible travel habits.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was designing two different flows in the same project: one for drivers and one for passengers; without mixing up the logic and data.

Initially, managing bus registration, schedules, and passenger bookings together was confusing and caused issues in data handling. We solved this by clearly separating driver-related and passenger-related components, which made the system easier to manage and debug.

Another challenge was implementing distance-based pricing along with carbon points. 
We fixed this by refining the calculation logic step by step and testing it with different routes and distances.

We also faced issues while managing environment variables and backend configuration, which initially caused the application to fail during deployment. This was resolved by properly using '.env' files and ensuring sensitive data was not pushed to GitHub.

These challenges helped us improve the project structure and build a more stable and scalable system within the hackathon time limit.

### CivicFix
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/civicfix-83a5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/kartikjoshi7/civicfix-hackathon) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://civicfix-frontend-nykz.onrender.com/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/yz4CjxI1xGw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI-powered smart city issue reporting & resolution

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Maps API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Maps%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML/CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML/CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

- **Eliminates Fake Reports:** AI filters out spam, duplicates, and AI-generated submissions, reducing invalid reports by 60–70% and saving hundreds of staff hours every month.

- **One-Tap Reporting for Citizens:** A single photo auto-detects issue type, severity, and GPS location — cutting report time from minutes to under 10 seconds and increasing successful submissions by 2–3×.
 
- **Smart Priority for Dangerous Issues:** A 1–10 severity score fast-tracks life-threatening hazards (electric poles, flooding, open manholes), reducing emergency response time by 40–50%.
 
- **Faster City Operations:** Live heatmaps and AI-recommended actions reduce issue triage from hours to under 5 minutes and overall resolution time by 50%+.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **AI Content Spoofing:** Early versions accepted almost any image. I fixed this by building a Gemini 2.0 Flash–based “authenticity gate” that rejects AI-generated, irrelevant, or suspicious images before they reach the database.

- **reCAPTCHA Domain Errors:** Deploying on Render caused “Invalid domain for site key” failures. Solved by properly whitelisting dynamic .onrender.com subdomains in Google Admin Console.

- **Location Not Actionable for Authorities:** Raw GPS coordinates were useless for officials. Added reverse geocoding to convert them into recognizable local areas (e.g., Vasad, Rajupura).

- **Abuse Prevention at Scale:** Implemented a 5-reports/day limit per user. The tricky part was real-time enforcement, solved by syncing Firestore counts directly into React state to instantly disable submissions.

> Guarding Your Digital World

![CSS3​](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3​-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square) ![Responsive design techniques](https://img.shields.io/badge/Responsive%20design%20techniques-333333?style=flat-square) ![Browser API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Browser%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

People can use this project to improve their digital privacy and stay safe from cyber threats such as phishing, data misuse, and unsafe online activities. It helps users understand basic cybersecurity practices in a simple and user-friendly way without requiring technical knowledge.

This project makes existing tasks easier by combining awareness, guidance, and security features into a single platform instead of using multiple tools and resources. Users can quickly access tips, learn how to protect their personal data, and follow safe online practices from one place.

It also makes tasks safer by encouraging** *privacy-focused behavior, reducing the risk of human error, and helping users avoid common online threats.*** Overall, the project simplifies cybersecurity for everyday users and helps them navigate the digital world with more confidence and protection.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building this project, we faced several challenges related to functionality and design. One major issue was making the navigation between different screens work properly. At first, the buttons were not responding correctly and some screens were not loading as expected. This happened due to errors in JavaScript event handling and incorrect element references. We fixed this by debugging the code using browser developer tools and correcting the logic for screen switching.

Another challenge was making the interface look like a mobile application instead of a normal website. Initially, the layout was not responsive and did not fit well on different screen sizes. We solved this by using mobile-first CSS styling and adjusting the layout with flexible design techniques.

We also faced issues with form validation where the contact form allowed empty or incorrect inputs. This was resolved by adding proper input checks and improving error handling in **JavaScript.**

Performance was another hurdle when adding animations and transitions, as some animations caused lag and visual glitches. We overcame this by simplifying the animations and optimizing the code for smoother performance.
Overall, these challenges helped us improve our debugging skills, understand responsive design better, and build a more stable and user-friendly cybersecurity application.

### ABHA-View
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/abhaview-f16b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/samarth-verma-dev/ABHA-VIEW.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=BMdrFAZz8vYeIBJw&v=q-APBoRfwww&feature=youtu.be) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Secure access + Clear history = Better care.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Healthcare data today is fragmented across multiple hospitals and laboratories, making it difficult for doctors to access a patient’s complete medical history during a consultation. This often leads to:

- Incomplete or inaccurate diagnosis
- Over-reliance on patient memory
- Repeated tests and delayed treatment
- Privacy risks when records are shared informally

Our system solves this by enabling secure, consent-based, temporary access to a patient’s ABHA-linked medical records.

How It Helps / Use Cases

Doctors can view a single, chronological medical history pulled from multiple hospitals and labs in real time.

How It Helps / Use Cases:

1.  Patients maintain full control through device-based biometric authentication and OTP-verified consent.
2. - Verified records from trusted providers are clearly marked, improving clinical trust and decision-making.
3. - Critical information such as allergies or past conditions can be identified even if the patient is unaware.
4. - Medical data exists only during the consultation; once the visit ends, encryption keys are destroyed, ensuring the data is rendered unreadable.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Partial & Inconsistent Data Availability**
**Challenge:**

-  Not all hospitals consistently link medical records to ABHA IDs.
-  Some records may be missing, delayed, or available only as PDFs.

**How we handled it:
Designed the system to work with partial data.**

1. Clearly displayed data completeness indicators (e.g., records fetched from 3/5 providers).
2. Avoided assuming a “complete medical history”.

**No Central Medical Data Storage
Challenge:**

- ABHA does not store medical records; data remains distributed across hospitals. 
- Real-time data fetching depends on external systems.

**It was tempting to “solve everything,” including hospital compliance and data standardization.
How we addressed it:**
Clearly declared hospital-side compliance and uploads as out of scope
Focused strictly on:
- Doctor usability
- Privacy
- Safe clinical viewing
Note-
A major challenge during this project was the nature of the data itself. Since health records are government-owned, highly confidential, and protected by strict privacy and security regulations, we could not access real patient data or live systems. This limited our ability to test the solution with actual records and forced us to rely on assumptions, mock data, and publicly available specifications. While this constraint ensured ethical and legal compliance, it also highlighted the real-world barriers involved in working with sensitive government health information.

![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase MLKit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20MLKit-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, many students are confused about what to study or which career to choose, and they only know a few traditional options. There are career tests and counselling services, but they are often boring, expensive or not accessible for school and college students, so most students never use them regularly. FuturePath solves this by turning career and skill discovery into a gamified quiz experience with XP, levels, streaks and leaderboards, so students actually enjoy exploring different fields. Based on their quiz performance and interests, the platform gives them personalised hints about domains that might fit them better, helping them save time and move from “confused” to “clear next steps”.**********

**Challenges we ran into**

### Firebase integration & module loading bug

While building FuturePath, one big hurdle was integrating Firebase (Firestore) with my vanilla HTML/JS quiz. I switched my scripts to `type="module"` to use `import` for the Firebase SDK, but after that the quiz stopped working: questions were not random, the timer and XP bar were not updating, and nothing obvious was failing.

At first there were no clear errors in the console, which made debugging confusing. I eventually realized the issue was how I was loading the modules and how the files were referenced. The browser could not find the correct `firebase-init.js` file via the relative path, so the import silently failed and the rest of the logic never ran properly.

To fix it, I:
- Opened DevTools and carefully checked the Network and Console tabs.
- Verified the folder structure and corrected the import paths (for example, `import { db } from './firebase-init.js';` vs `./js/firebase-init.js`).
- Made sure my `<script type="module" src="js/quiz.js"></script>` was at the bottom of the HTML and that Firebase SDK URLs were correct.

Once I fixed the module paths and script tags, the quiz logic (random questions, timer, XP/levels) started working as expected, and Firebase logging worked reliably. This taught me to always double-check module paths and use the browser console/network tab instead of guessing.

**Duality AI — Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation**

FuturePath is an AI‑powered, gamified learning platform that prepares students for real‑world AI challenges like the Duality track at DUHacks. It uses interactive quizzes, projects and career guidance to teach concepts such as synthetic data, digital twin simulations and robust model training for applications like off‑road autonomous driving. By turning complex topics like semantic segmentation and simulator‑based training into simple, game‑like missions, FuturePath helps more students gain the mindset and skills needed to work on Duality‑style Falcon simulation problems in the future.

### DocuMind-AI

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Markdown](https://img.shields.io/badge/Markdown-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![GOOGLE GEMINI API](https://img.shields.io/badge/GOOGLE%20GEMINI%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🧠 The Problem: Information Overload
In today's digital age, students and professionals are drowning in PDFs—textbooks, research papers, legal contracts, and documentation.

Reading is slow: Manually scanning hundreds of pages to find one specific answer is inefficient.

Retention is low: Passive reading often leads to forgetting key details quickly.

Privacy is compromised: Most AI tools require users to create accounts and upload sensitive documents to the developer's database, creating a massive risk for data leaks.

💡 The Solution: DocuMind
DocuMind transforms static documents into an interactive "Neural Interface." It solves these problems by allowing users to chat with their data directly in the browser.

🚀 Key Features & Benefits:
Instant Comprehension: Instead of reading 100 pages, just ask: "What are the key findings of this paper?" or "Summarize the legal obligations." The AI extracts the exact answer in seconds.

Active Learning (Auto-Quiz): DocuMind doesn't just summarize; it teaches. It automatically generates interactive quizzes from your document to test your knowledge and improve retention using "Active Recall" principles.

"Zero-Storage" Privacy: We utilize a transient architecture. Unlike typical apps that store user uploads in a database, DocuMind streams text directly to the secure Gemini API for processing. We hold zero records of your documents on our servers—once you close the tab, the data is gone.

Universal Accessibility: Whether you are a medical student cramming for exams or a developer reading complex documentation, DocuMind turns dense text into a simple conversation.

In short: We turn "Reading" into "Knowing."

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ 1. Taming the "Chatty" AI (JSON Parsing Errors)
One of the biggest hurdles was getting the Gemini API to return strictly structured JSON for the Quiz generation.

The Bug: The AI often wrapped the JSON response in Markdown code blocks (json ... ) or added conversational filler text like "Here is your quiz!" before the data. This caused my JSON.parse() function to crash the app.

The Fix: I implemented a robust "Sanitization Pipeline." I wrote a regex function to strip out Markdown backticks and extraneous text before parsing. I also refined the system prompt to strictly enforce "Output ONLY raw JSON," significantly reducing parse errors.

📄 2. The "Zero Backend" Constraint
Building a truly serverless, privacy-first app meant I couldn't rely on Python/Node.js servers to process PDFs.

The Hurdle: Parsing complex PDFs entirely in the browser is resource-intensive and tricky with large files.

The Fix: I utilized pdf.js to render and extract text client-side. This keeps the user's data 100% private (it never leaves their tab) but required careful handling of asynchronous text extraction to prevent the UI from freezing during large uploads.

📱 3. Responsive "Glassmorphism"
My "Neural Glass" UI looked great on desktop but broke completely on mobile devices.

The Bug: The sidebar and chat window tried to squeeze side-by-side on phone screens, making the text unreadable.

The Fix: I used Tailwind's responsive prefixes (md:flex-row, flex-col) to re-architect the layout. On mobile, the sidebar now collapses or stacks gracefully, ensuring the "futuristic" vibe works on any screen size.

**The problem it solves**

## What Problem Does This Project Solve?

**TalkToMe** is a full-stack application that provides accessible, AI-powered emotional support and mental wellness tools. It helps users manage emotions, reflect on their mental state, and build healthier habits in a safe, supportive, and private environment.

---

### What Can People Use It For?

- **Emotional Support Chat:**  
  Chat with an empathetic AI assistant ("Talktome") to talk through feelings, receive encouragement, and get helpful self-care suggestions.

- **Mood Tracking & Emotional Analysis:**  
  Analyze messages to detect emotional trends and become more aware of mental health over time.

- **Crisis Detection:**  
  Detect signs of crisis in conversations and provide immediate resources or alerts, making it safer for users in distress.

- **Journaling:**  
  Save conversations or personal notes to a private journal for self-reflection and growth.

- **Breathing & Meditation Exercises:**  
  Use built-in guided exercises to manage stress and anxiety.

- **Personalized Experience:**  
  Onboarding and user profiles allow the app to tailor support and suggestions to each individual.

---

### How Does It Make Tasks Easier or Safer?

- **Always Available:**  
  Access support anytime, without waiting for appointments.

- **Privacy & Anonymity:**  
  Private conversations reduce stigma or fear of judgment.

- **Early Intervention:**  
  Mood tracking and crisis detection encourage seeking professional help when needed.

- **Accessible Self-Help:**  
  Journaling, mood tracking, and breathing exercises are all integrated in one place.

---

> **Disclaimer:**  
> TalkToME provides emotional support, but it is **not a substitute for therapy or professional mental health care**. If you are experiencing a crisis or have a severe mental health condition, please seek help from a licensed professional.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Multi-Environment Configuration and Deployment Consistency

One of the most intricate challenges was architecting a configuration system that would reliably propagate environment variables and secrets across local, staging, and production environments. The frontend (Vite) and backend (FastAPI) each had their own requirements for environment variable exposure, and subtle differences in how variables were loaded led to elusive bugs—such as the frontend silently failing to fetch the correct API endpoint, or the backend using stale credentials. To address this, we implemented a layered configuration strategy:  
- **Centralized .env Management:** We created environment-specific `.env` files and a validation script to ensure all required variables were present before build or deployment.
- **CI/CD Integration:** Our CI/CD pipelines were enhanced to inject secrets securely, validate environment consistency, and fail fast if any configuration drift was detected.
- **Runtime Diagnostics:** We added runtime checks and logging to both frontend and backend, surfacing misconfigurations early in the deployment process.

### 2. Robust CORS and Authentication Across Dynamic Origins

Supporting secure communication between the frontend and backend, especially with preview deployments and custom domains, introduced a web of CORS and authentication challenges.  
- **Dynamic Origin Whitelisting:** We built middleware to dynamically validate request origins against an allowlist that could be updated without redeploying the backend.
- **Token Propagation:** Ensuring authentication tokens were securely stored, refreshed, and transmitted across both HTTP and WebSocket connections required careful handling to avoid race conditions and token leakage.
- **Automated Security Audits:** We integrated automated security scanning tools into our pipeline to detect CORS misconfigurations and potential vulnerabilities in authentication flows.

### 3. Real-Time NLP Processing and Scalability

Delivering real-time emotion analysis and crisis detection at scale required a hybrid architecture:
- **Asynchronous Task Queues:** We offloaded heavy NLP computations to background workers using task queues, allowing the chat UI to remain responsive.
- **Model Versioning and Rollback:** To support continuous improvement of our emotion and crisis detection models, we implemented a model registry with versioning and rollback capabilities, enabling safe experimentation and rapid iteration.
- **Resource Monitoring:** We set up distributed tracing and resource monitoring to detect bottlenecks and auto-scale processing nodes based on load.

### 4. Crisis Detection: Ethical, Legal, and Technical Complexity

Building a responsible crisis detection system went far beyond technical implementation:
- **Ethical Review:** We convened an advisory group including mental health professionals and ethicists to review our detection criteria, escalation protocols, and user privacy safeguards.
- **User Feedback Loop:** A mechanism was built for users to provide feedback on false positives/negatives, which was then used to retrain and fine-tune the detection models.
- **Legal Compliance:** We conducted a legal review to ensure compliance with data protection laws (GDPR, HIPAA where applicable), especially regarding sensitive user data and automated interventions.

### 5. Advanced UI/UX: Accessibility, Internationalization, and Personalization

Creating an inclusive, accessible, and personalized user experience presented its own set of hurdles:
- **Accessibility Audits:** We used automated and manual accessibility testing to uncover issues with screen reader compatibility, keyboard navigation, and color contrast, leading to several rounds of refactoring.
- **Internationalization (i18n):** To support a global user base, we abstracted all user-facing text and built a translation management workflow, including right-to-left language support and locale-aware formatting.
- **Adaptive Personalization:** We implemented a user profiling system that dynamically adjusted suggestions, tone, and interface elements based on user preferences and behavioral analytics, while maintaining strict privacy controls.

---

Overcoming these multifaceted challenges required not only technical expertise but also cross-disciplinary collaboration, rigorous testing, and a deep commitment to ethical and user-centered design. Each obstacle forced us to innovate and ultimately resulted in a more resilient, secure, and empathetic platform.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Render](https://img.shields.io/badge/Render-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves 

Monitoring vessel activity inside Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) using satellite data is complex and time-consuming. Raw SAR satellite images do not directly indicate whether a detected vessel is legitimate, broadcasting AIS, or potentially suspicious. Manually inspecting satellite imagery, correlating it with AIS information, and extracting usable insights is inefficient and does not scale.

This project addresses that gap by converting SAR satellite imagery and related data into structured, machine-readable outputs through an automated pipeline.

### How marine officials can use this system
- They can simply choose any region over the map.
- Process SAR satellite images to automatically detect vessel candidates
- Identify which detected vessels are located inside Marine Protected Areas
- Determine whether each detected vessel is broadcasting AIS or operating without AIS
- Review vessel detections through structured JSON reports rather than raw imagery
- Access cropped vessel and sea image patches for further verification or analysis

### How it makes operational monitoring easier
- Reduces the need for manual inspection of raw satellite radar images
- Automatically highlights vessels that may require further attention due to missing AIS signals
- Converts complex geospatial and image data into consistent, machine-readable reports
- Enables faster triage by separating AIS-active vessels from AIS-dark candidates

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges & Learnings

### 1. Real-time SAR data access
Most satellite data platforms returned **401/403 authorization errors** when attempting programmatic access.  
As a workaround, **Copernicus Data Space** was used. However, SAR data downloads take approximately **5 minutes per scene** due to:
- Large file sizes
- Limited local compute resources

This constrained rapid experimentation and near–real-time processing.

---

### 2. Real-time deployment limits
End-to-end real-time deployment proved infeasible on free-tier infrastructure due to:
- Heavy computational requirements of SAR processing
- GenAI API quota limitations

As a result, a **lightweight demonstrative deployment** was created to showcase the pipeline and system capabilities rather than full real-time execution.

---

### 3. LSTM-based behavior modeling
Initial behavior modeling attempts used **LSTM architectures**, which require **dense temporal time-series data**.  
Since SAR imagery is **spatially sparse and temporally discontinuous**, this approach was unsuitable.

The behavior analysis was redesigned to leverage:
- Spatial vessel patterns
- Fleet formations
- Vessel proximity and clustering inside MPAs

This resulted in more reliable and interpretable behavior signals.

---

### 4. CNN data imbalance
Early CNN training used mostly **ship-only image patches**, leading to:
- Overconfident predictions
- Poor generalization on real SAR scenes

To address this, **synthetic sea-only patches** were generated and added to the dataset, improving:
- Class balance (ship vs. non-ship)
- Model confidence calibration
- Detection robustness

**Best Innovation**

- This system catches illegal fishing ships that turn off their tracking devices to hide in protected ocean zones.

- Ships disable their transponders to fish illegally where it's banned, exploiting the fact that current monitoring only works if vessels cooperate.

- This project uses satellite radar to physically see ships on the water regardless of whether they're broadcasting their position — they can't hide from physics.

- The innovation is in how it works:
  - Instead of relying purely on black-box AI, it grounds detections in radar physics first for explainability.
  - It then validates detections using clustering and neural networks.
  - Every detection traces back to specific measurements that can hold up in court.
- It focuses only on protected zones to stay cost-effective.
- It automatically generates intelligence reports that enforcement agencies can act on immediately.
- While most AI/ML projects target saturated domains like medical, FinTech, or EdTech, this tackles an underserved frontier — environmental enforcement — where sophisticated AI/ML solutions are desperately needed but rarely applied.

- The brilliance lies in solving a genuine environmental crisis with elegant engineering — combining satellite technology, multiple AI techniques, and practical deployment thinking into something agencies can actually afford to use at scale.

**AWS**

## Why Ghost Hunter Fits the AWS Track

- Built using an AI-assisted development workflow powered by Kiro, which acted as an engineering co-pilot across ideation, system design, coding, debugging, and optimization.

- Kiro was actively used to design the end-to-end pipeline, breaking a complex maritime surveillance problem into scalable, cloud-ready stages.

- Code generation and refactoring were accelerated with Kiro, enabling rapid iteration, modular scripts, and clean orchestration under tight hackathon timelines.

- Kiro helped identify and fix failure points early, such as incomplete data, missing detections, and edge cases, improving overall system reliability.

- AI-assisted development enabled faster delivery without sacrificing correctness, demonstrating how Kiro can meaningfully improve real-world engineering productivity.

- The final system showcases how Kiro can be used not just for coding, but for end-to-end system thinking, making complex solutions easier to build and maintain on AWS-based infrastructure.

**The problem it solves**

The problem SoilSathi solves
The Problem SoilSathi Solves

Agriculture today faces a range of challenges, including declining soil health, unidentified plant diseases, limited access to expert knowledge, and inefficient farm management practices. Farmers and gardeners often rely on manual observation, costly laboratory testing, or trial-and-error approaches. This results in:

Reduced crop yield due to untreated soil and undetected plant issues

High input costs from improper use of fertilizers, pesticides, and water

Limited knowledge-sharing between farmers and communities

Difficulty in accessing modern agricultural services such as drones and e-commerce platforms

Lack of engaging and accessible educational tools for children, beginners, and the elderly

How SoilSathi Helps

SoilSathi is designed to make agriculture smarter, safer, and more accessible by combining artificial intelligence, real-time monitoring, and community-driven features.

Key Ways It Simplifies and Improves Tasks

Real-Time Soil Health Monitoring
Provides instant soil analysis and actionable recommendations, reducing the need for external testing and enabling timely decision-making.

AI-Powered Plant Disease Detection
Identifies plant diseases through simple photo capture and suggests treatments, preventing crop loss and improving productivity.

Role-Specific Dashboards
Farmers and gardeners have access to tailored dashboards that simplify complex data into practical insights.

Drone Services Integration
Offers aerial monitoring, spraying, and surveillance, improving efficiency while reducing manual labor and safety risks.

Educational Platform
Provides interactive learning tools such as games, AR exploration, and structured content for children, beginners, and elderly learners.

Community Features
Connects users for knowledge sharing, fostering collaboration and collective problem-solving.

Integrated E-commerce Marketplace
Delivers direct access to seeds, fertilizers, tools, and equipment with secure payment options and reliable order tracking.

Impact

For Farmers: Increases yield, reduces costs, and ensures better crop health through timely interventions.

For Gardeners: Simplifies plant care and provides expert guidance at home.

For Learners: Makes agricultural knowledge accessible and engaging through structured educational content.

For Communities: Creates a collaborative platform for exchanging agricultural practices and insights.

In summary, SoilSathi bridges the gap between traditional farming methods and modern, AI-driven solutions, making agriculture more efficient, sustainable, and accessible.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into
Challenges I Ran Into

While building SoilSathi, several technical and design-related challenges arose:

AI Model Integration for Disease Detection
Challenge: Training and integrating an AI model that could accurately identify plant diseases from images was difficult due to limited datasets and varying image quality from mobile devices.

Solution: I overcame this by using transfer learning with pre-trained vision models and augmenting the dataset with synthetic images. This improved accuracy while keeping the model lightweight enough to run on mobile devices.

Performance Optimization in React Native
Challenge: The app initially faced performance issues, especially when handling camera features and rendering AR content.

Solution: I optimized rendering using React Native’s memoization techniques and offloaded heavy computations to background tasks. Additionally, I used Expo’s optimized libraries for camera and AR integration.

Offline Functionality for Farmers in Rural Areas
Challenge: Many target users, especially farmers, may not always have reliable internet connectivity.

Solution: I implemented offline data caching with AsyncStorage so users could still access soil health tips, saved analyses, and educational content without internet access. Data automatically syncs when connectivity is restored.

Designing for Multiple User Types
Challenge: Creating a single application that caters to farmers, gardeners, and children required distinct user experiences without overwhelming the interface.

Solution: I solved this by building role-specific dashboards (Farmer Dashboard, Gardener Dashboard, Kids Education Hub) with tailored features and simplified navigation for each user type.

Complex Navigation and State Management
Challenge: Managing navigation between multiple feature sets (dashboards, education, e-commerce, drone services) was complex.

Solution: I standardized navigation using React Navigation 6 and applied the Context API for consistent global state management across different modules.

Outcome

By addressing these challenges, I ensured that SoilSathi is not only technically robust and user-friendly, but also accessible to diverse users in both urban and rural contexts. These solutions helped transform the initial concept into a scalable and practical application.

Modern surveillance relies on manual monitoring that is slow, error-prone, and unable to 
interpret subtle behavioral or audio cues. In crowded public spaces, this leads to missed 
suspicious actions, delayed detection of dangerous objects, and poor anticipation of escalating 
threats, ultimately compromising safety. There is a need for an intelligent, software-only system 
that can automatically analyze video and audio feeds, understand behavior in context, detect 
anomalies, and deliver timely, reasoned alerts to support faster and more reliable decision
making.

**Solution:-**
The solution is an AI-driven security intelligence engine that processes video and audio feeds in real time to 
automatically detect suspicious behaviour, abnormal actions, dangerous objects, and audio anomalies. Using 
advanced computer vision and sound classification models, the system interprets human posture, identifies 
potential threats, performs crowd analysis, and predicts escalation risks. It then generates clear alerts with 
contextual reasoning, allowing security teams to respond faster and more accurately without relying on manual 
monitoring. This software-only platform enhances public safety by transforming raw surveillance data into 
actionable intelligence.

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🧨 **MAJOR CHALLENGES WE RAN INTO WHILE BUILDING HAWKEYE**

---

# 🟥 **1. Multimodal Fusion Is Extremely Hard**

Combining **vision**, **audio**, and **motion** into one unified risk score was a major challenge because:

* Each stream runs at different frame rates
* Each model outputs different formats
* Synchronizing features across time is tricky
* Contradiction handling (e.g., scream without visible panic) had to be solved manually

This became one of the biggest engineering puzzles.

---

# 🟦 **2. Maintaining Real-Time Performance**

Running YOLO, pose estimation, optical flow, audio analysis, and UI rendering **simultaneously** pushed our hardware to its limits.

Challenges included:

* GPU memory spikes
* FPS drops
* Latency between modules
* Race conditions in shared buffers

Making the system run smoothly in real time required intense optimization.

---

# 🟩 **3. Building the Replay Buffer (TimeWarp) Without Lag**

Recording:

* previous 5 seconds
* current frame
* next 5 seconds

…all while still processing live video, was surprisingly difficult.

Problems:

* Memory leaks
* Dropped frames
* Buffer overflow
* Sync mismatches with audio & pose

This took careful engineering to get right.

---

# 🟨 **4. Designing a Transparent Explainability Layer**

Generating:

* heatmaps
* motion vectors
* audio spike graphs
* LLM-based narratives

…in real time was challenging because explainability normally happens **offline**, not during live inference.

We had to build a pipeline that could visualize *why* the AI reacted without slowing everything down.

---

# 🟧 **5. Creating the Plugin Architecture**

This was one of the hardest engineering tasks.

We had to figure out:

* how plugins register themselves
* how to load/unload modules without restarting the backend
* safe sandboxing
* plugin → fusion API compatibility

Building a dynamic ecosystem in 24–36 hours is not trivial.

---

# 🟪 **6. Aligning 6 Independent Modules Without Overlap**

With six members working in parallel:

* avoiding merging conflicts
* keeping architectures flexible
* unifying naming conventions
* designing common data formats

…became a serious coordination challenge.

We solved it with clean module boundaries and stream simulators.

---

# 🟫 **7. Handling False Positives & Noise**

Because real-life footage is messy:

* background chatter
* sudden light changes
* occlusions
* thermal noise
* irregular motion

All produced accidental triggers.

We had to tune the risk thresholds and contradiction rules carefully to avoid chaos.

---

# 🟰 **8. Balancing Ethics & Functionality**

We built face-blur, no-storage mode, and transparency logs — but ensuring these didn't break performance was tough.

Ethical constraints sometimes conflicted with technical demands.

---

# 🌀 **Integrating Everything Into One Dashboard Without Crashes**

The UI had to juggle:

* overlays
* risk timeline
* incident logs
* replay video
* plugin marketplace
* settings

This caused:

* framerate drops
* backend overload
* occasional UI freezes

A LOT of debugging went into this.
