### Marvel Shield
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/marvel-shield-1fd7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AstronomerAKabhi/MarvelShield.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/9edwCQ0VU9o) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> See every threat before it strikes and patch it up

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

New web applications are constantly being threatened by various attacks like SQL injection, XSS, command injection, and path traversal, among others.
Traditional WAFs have a set of predefined rules, which are not enough to keep up with new emerging trends and patterns of attacks.
MarvelShield provides the following features to heal the gateway and protect the application from attacks:
🔍 Detects attacks in real time – all requests are behaviorally analyzed, and suspicious payloads are traced and sent to the AI engine powered
by Google Gemini.
🧠 AI diagnoses and patches automatically – brain.py analyzes the attack traces and provides precise regex-based patches with confidence
scores, all done automatically without any human intervention.
⚡ Blocks future attacks instantly – once the patches are deployed, all future requests matching the pattern are automatically blocked
in microseconds.
📊 Provides complete visibility and awareness – a dashboard provides all the information about the requests, attacks, AI diagnosis, patches,
and the attacker with a timeline of the threats.
- 🌐 Extends the security to the browser, where a Chrome/Edge extension stores active patches locally, caching them, and monitors outgoing requests for suspicious behavior before they even leave the user’s browser.

  It converts passive infrastructure into an active, self-defending security layer, bringing enterprise-grade threat response to the table for any developer running a web service.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Permanent Ban" simulation deadlock The toughest bug: after the first attack simulation, 127.0.0.1 gets permanently banned in Redis. Since
  stop.sh never cleared the ip_blocklist key, every subsequent simulation run had all requests IP-banned before brain.py could create a trace — meaning
  zero AI diagnoses, zero patches, and a completely silent dashboard. It looked like the AI wasn't working when it simply never got a chance to run. Fixed
  by flushing ip_blocklist, attacker_profiles:*, and bw:* keys at the start of each simulation run.

  2. The extension banning itself The browser extension polled /api/patches every 30 seconds for live data — but this went through the full WAF
  middleware. Since 127.0.0.1 was the source, those polling requests counted toward the behavioral rate-limiter and eventually triggered a self-ban. Fixed
  by adding a MANAGEMENT_PATHS bypass in the middleware that skips all security checks for internal health/stats/patch endpoints.

  3. Chrome MV3 Service Worker + Socket.IO incompatibility MV3 service workers can't maintain persistent WebSocket connections (they are terminated when
  idle). This made real-time Socket.IO integration impossible for the extension. Had to redesign to use REST polling with parallel /api/patches and
  /api/stats fetches, storing results in chrome.storage.local.

  4. Silent chrome.tabs.create() failure The "Open Dashboard" button in the extension did nothing for a long time. No error in the console. Root cause:
  chrome.tabs.create() requires the "tabs" permission explicitly declared in manifest.json — missing it causes a silent no-op rather than an exception.

  5. Dashboard stats inconsistency (Total=0, Blocked=8) IP-banned requests return early in the middleware before publishing the incoming Socket.IO event,
  so the dashboard's total-requests counter never incremented for them. The blocked count kept rising while total stayed at zero. Fixed by incrementing
  stats.total on the frontend whenever a block event with reason === 'ip_banned' arrives.

  6. WebSocket reliability over WSL2 All services run inside WSL2 but the dashboard is accessed from Windows Chrome. Raw WebSocket connections were
  dropping intermittently. Solved by configuring Socket.IO to start with HTTP long-polling first and upgrade to WebSocket only after the connection is
  stable (transports: ['polling', 'websocket']).

Team **Marvel Night Riders** -- [Himanshu Ranjan](https://github.com/himanshukumarranjan3-code), [Kanishkar Y](https://github.com/kanishkar08-star), [Abhishek Purushotham](https://github.com/AstronomerAKabhi), [ajay prasad](https://github.com/ajaycode7904)

![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MTCNN](https://img.shields.io/badge/MTCNN-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn library](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn%20library-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Deepfake Crisis Is Real

Over **500,000 deepfake videos** were shared online in 2023 alone.
Manipulated media is being weaponized for misinformation, financial 
fraud, identity theft, and reputational damage — and it is 
accelerating. The human eye **cannot reliably detect** modern 
AI-generated deepfakes.

**Existing solutions are expensive, cloud-dependent, and inaccessible 
to most people and organizations.**

---

## DeepGuard Changes That

DeepGuard is an enterprise-grade deepfake detection platform that 
brings **state-of-the-art AI directly to your machine** — no cloud 
dependency, no data exposure, no compromise.

### 🎯 What It Enables

**For Organizations**
- Verify video authenticity in legal proceedings and investigations
- Protect executives from impersonation in video communications
- Screen media content before publication or broadcast

**For Individuals**
- Detect manipulated videos circulating on social media instantly
- Confirm the identity of participants in live video calls
- Protect yourself from video-based fraud and scams

---

## How It Works

DeepGuard uses a **ResNeXt50 + LSTM deep learning pipeline** that 
analyzes spatial and temporal inconsistencies across video frames —
the same subtle artifacts that reveal a deepfake but are invisible 
to the human eye.

| Detection Mode | Use Case |
|----------------|----------|
| 📤 Video Upload | Analyze any stored video file |
| 📷 Live Camera | Real-time detection during video calls |
| 🖥️ Screen Capture | Monitor any live video stream |
| 🔌 Browser Extension | Detect on YouTube, Twitter, any website |

---

## Why DeepGuard Stands Apart

✅ **93.6% accuracy** — trained on FaceForensics++ benchmark dataset  
✅ **100% local processing** — your videos never leave your device  
✅ **Real-time analysis** — results in seconds, not minutes  
✅ **No subscription, no API key, no cloud** — fully self-contained

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. 🧠 Model Weight Availability
The pretrained ResNeXt50 + LSTM weights were not publicly available
in the original research repository. We had to architect a **fallback 
inference pipeline** that gracefully degrades to demo mode when weights 
are unavailable, while keeping the full inference pipeline intact and 
ready to plug in trained weights — ensuring the application remains 
fully functional and demonstrable at all times.

---

## 2. ⚡ Real-Time Frame Analysis Latency
Running deep learning inference on every webcam frame caused 
significant lag, making the live detection unusable. We solved this 
by implementing **asynchronous frame capture** — decoupling the webcam 
feed from the inference pipeline so the video stream runs smoothly 
while analysis happens in the background at configurable intervals 
(1s / 2s / 3s), giving users control over the accuracy vs. performance 
tradeoff.

---

## 3. 🎭 Face Detection in Varied Conditions
MTCNN face detection was failing on low-light webcam feeds and 
angled faces, causing false "no face detected" results. We resolved 
this by **tuning detection thresholds** and adding a confidence 
fallback — if the primary detection fails, the system retries with 
relaxed parameters before declaring no face found.

---

## 4. 🔒 CSRF Token Handling in AJAX Requests
Live detection frames are sent to the Django backend via fetch() 
API calls, which were being blocked by Django's CSRF middleware. 
We implemented **proper CSRF token injection** into all AJAX request 
headers by reading the token from cookies, maintaining full security 
without disabling protection.

---

## 5. 🎨 UI Consistency Across Detection Modes
Building four distinct detection interfaces (upload, live, screen, 
extension) while maintaining a consistent enterprise design system 
was challenging. We solved this by building a **centralized theme.css** 
design token system — a single source of truth for colors, typography, 
spacing, and component styles — ensuring every page feels like part 
of the same product.

**The problem it solves**

# 🛡️ The Problem It Solves

## 🚨 The Growing Threat of Ransomware

Ransomware attacks encrypt user files within seconds and demand payment for recovery.  
Traditional antivirus solutions often rely on known signatures, which means:

- New ransomware variants go undetected
- Detection happens after significant damage
- Recovery becomes costly or impossible

By the time users notice something is wrong, their files are already encrypted.

---

## 🔍 What This Project Solves

Our system provides **real-time behavioral ransomware detection and elimination**, focusing on *how* a process behaves rather than what it is called.

Instead of waiting for known malware signatures, the system:

- Monitors rapid file modifications
- Tracks suspicious extension changes
- Detects abnormal entropy spikes (encryption behavior)
- Analyzes activity across multiple directories
- Calculates a real-time risk score
- Automatically blocks or terminates suspicious processes

This allows early intervention — often before large-scale encryption completes.

---

## 🧠 Who Can Use It

### 👨‍💻 Developers
- Protect development environments from malicious scripts
- Prevent build systems or dependency attacks from causing file damage
- Monitor unexpected file churn during runtime

### 🏢 Small Businesses
- Safeguard sensitive documents without expensive enterprise security systems
- Add an additional defensive layer beyond traditional antivirus

### 🎓 Students & Personal Users
- Protect assignments, research, and personal data
- Detect suspicious behavior caused by unknown downloads or cracked software

### 🔐 Security Researchers
- Study ransomware-like patterns safely
- Test behavioral detection models in controlled environments

---

## ⚡ How It Makes Tasks Safer

Traditional security tools react after detection.

This system:
- Detects abnormal behavior in real time
- Reduces false positives through multi-factor scoring
- Prevents encryption spread across directories
- Adds automated containment measures
- Improves response time from minutes to seconds

It transforms ransomware defense from reactive to proactive.

---

## 🌍 Why It Matters

Ransomware does not announce itself.  
It works silently, quickly, and aggressively.

This project introduces:

- Behavioral intelligence
- Sliding window monitoring
- Context-aware risk scoring
- Automated threat neutralization

It shifts security from static signature scanning to adaptive, real-time protection.

---

# 💡 In Simple Terms

Instead of asking:

“Is this file malicious?”

We ask:

“Is this process behaving like ransomware?”

And if the answer crosses a defined risk threshold —  
we act before the damage becomes irreversible.

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🚧 Challenges We Faced

## 1️⃣ Event Explosion from `watchdog`

### The Problem
When monitoring file activity in real time, a single file save triggered multiple events.  
One modification could generate 3–5 `modified` events instantly.

This inflated our event counts and falsely increased the risk score.

### Why It Happened
Modern editors don’t simply edit a file. They often:
- Create temporary files  
- Replace the original file  
- Trigger metadata updates  

This results in multiple filesystem events for a single user action.

### How We Solved It
We implemented a **sliding time window buffer using `deque()`**:
- Tracked only events within the last 5 seconds  
- Filtered duplicate rapid events for the same file  
- Ignored directory-level noise  

This stabilized event counts and shifted detection to behavior-based analysis instead of raw event counting.

---

## 2️⃣ False Positives During Normal Usage

### The Problem
Operations like:
- `npm install`
- Extracting ZIP files
- Compiling large projects  

Generated behavior similar to ransomware:
- Hundreds of file modifications  
- Multiple directories affected  
- High file churn  

The system initially flagged these as suspicious.

### How We Solved It
We transitioned from single-metric detection to **multi-factor behavioral scoring**, including:

- File modification frequency  
- Extension change tracking  
- Entropy analysis  
- Unique directory spread  
- Process identification  

Instead of triggering alerts based on one signal, we introduced a **risk score threshold system**, significantly reducing false positives.

---

## 3️⃣ Detecting Encryption via Entropy

### The Problem
Encrypted files typically have high entropy. However:
- Compressed files  
- Media files  
- Certain binary formats  

Also exhibit high entropy, leading to unreliable detection if used alone.

### How We Solved It
- Calculated entropy only on recently modified files  
- Combined entropy spikes with extension change detection  
- Treated entropy as a contributing signal rather than a standalone trigger  

This improved accuracy while maintaining performance.

---

## 4️⃣ Safe Ransomware Simulation for Testing

### The Problem
We needed to test ransomware-like behavior without executing real malware.

### How We Solved It
We developed a controlled Python simulation script that:
- Rapidly modified files  
- Renamed file extensions  
- Increased file entropy artificially  

This allowed safe and repeatable testing of detection mechanisms.

---

## 5️⃣ Real-Time Process Blocking

### The Problem
Detecting ransomware is one challenge.  
Stopping it instantly without disrupting legitimate processes is another.

### How We Solved It
- Identified suspicious parent processes  
- Verified risk score thresholds before taking action  
- Implemented careful process termination and firewall rule enforcement  

This ensured effective elimination while preserving system stability.

---

# 💡 Key Learnings

- Single metrics are unreliable in real-world detection  
- Behavioral patterns provide stronger signals than raw event counts  
- Real-time systems must balance speed, accuracy, and system safety  
- Context-aware scoring dramatically reduces false positives  

Ransomware detection is not about counting events.  
It is about understanding behavior over time.

**The problem it solves**

# ArchSentinel Enterprise: Proactive Architecture Threat Simulator

## Inspiration
In modern Cloud Security, the gap between architecture design and security validation is dangerously wide. Teams build complex cloud networks but typically rely on reactive tools—like vulnerability scanners or penetration tests—to find critical flaws *after* deployment. We wanted to shift security completely left. Our goal was to build a platform allowing architects to visually model their networks, inject real-world configurations, and use cutting-edge AI to simulate devastating, CVE-driven cyberattacks before a single line of infrastructure code is deployed.

## What it does (The problem it solves)
ArchSentinel Enterprise introduces **architecture-level security governance**.

It transforms static diagrams into live, hackable threat models, allowing organizations to:
* **Visually Model Infrastructure:** Drag-and-drop configurable virtual components (WAFs, Load Balancers, Web Servers, Databases, SIEMs) onto an interactive canvas to construct multi-directional network topologies.
* **Auto-Discover Cloud Assets:** Connect directly to AWS to ingest and visualize live, production EC2, RDS, and ELB topographies.
* **Inject Real-World Context:** Use AI to dynamically enrich generic components with specific, vulnerable software versions (e.g., Apache 2.4.49, Windows Server 2012 R2), mapping them to real-world threat intelligence.
* **Simulate AI-Driven Zero-Day Attacks:** Unleash a sophisticated AI threat modeler (powered by Google Gemini) that analyzes the exact topology, attempts to bypass misconfigurations, and streams a live, phase-by-phase kill chain animation directly on the canvas.
* **Generate SOC-Grade Reports:** Instantly produce comprehensive PDF compliance reports featuring Risk Radar charts, Attack Heatmaps, financial impact projections, and actionable remediation steps.
* **1-Click Auto-Remediation:** Intelligently apply missing security controls (like WAF enforcement or encryption-at-rest) directly to the architecture to instantly patch the simulated vulnerabilities.

## How we built it
* **Frontend UI & Visualization:** Built with **Next.js 14**, **React Flow** (for the highly interactive, custom-node canvas), and **Tailwind CSS** to create a stunning, glassmorphic dark-mode interface.
* **Backend Security:** Leveraged **Next.js App Router API** routes secured strictly by **Clerk** (JWT sessions) and **Zod** (schema validation) to implement Zero Trust access and prevent Denial of Wallet attacks on our LLM APIs.
* **AI Engine:** Integrated **Google Gemini** as the core reasoning engine. We engineered complex system prompts to force the LLM to respect strict physical network boundaries (e.g., offline nodes cannot be hacked, attacks must stop at active firewalls) and exploit real CVEs over generic attacks.
* **Cloud Discovery:** Utilized the **AWS SDK (v3)** to securely query cloud environments and map massive datasets to our visual standard.
* **Reporting Output:** Used **jsPDF** and **Recharts** to dynamically render Canvas-based data visualizations into downloadable enterprise PDF reports.

## Challenges we ran into
* **Hallucination Control in AI Threat Simulation:** LLMs frequently attempt to "magic" their way through firewalls in text generation. We had to build strict rule-based prompt engineering paired with rigid frontend graph traversal logic to ensure the AI's "kill chain" respected the physical reality of the network edges and node power states (e.g. `isActive: false`).
* **Complex Graph State Management:** Synchronizing the React Flow state with the AI's streaming attack phases—handling highlighting, node disabling, and CSS filtering concurrently without overwriting offline states—required deep React hook memoization and custom Node overrides.

## Accomplishments that we're proud of
* Engineering the **AI Threat Modeler** to genuinely understand structural network topology (e.g., realizing it cannot laterally pivot to an internal database if the external WAF blocks the initial payload).
* Building the **Automated AWS Discovery** feature, smoothly transitioning ArchSentinel from a theoretical design space into a live Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) utility.
* Creating an interface that is not only highly technical but intensely visually engaging—the animated, pulsing attack phases make abstract security concepts immediately tangible.

## What's next for ArchSentinel
* **Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Export:** Generating secure, ready-to-deploy Terraform or AWS CloudFormation templates directly from the patched, successful visual architecture.
* **Multi-Cloud Support:** Expanding real-time discovery and simulation to Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environments.
* **CI/CD Pipeline Integration:** Running headless, automated architecture simulations as GitHub Actions to block vulnerable infrastructure designs from ever reaching production.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Hallucination Control in AI Threat Simulation
**The Hurdle:** Large Language Models naturally want to succeed at the tasks given to them. During early testing, the Gemini engine would routinely "magic" its way through active firewalls or laterally pivot to nodes that were physically physically disconnected or powered off (`isActive: false`), breaking the realism of the simulation.
**The Fix:** We had to implement rigid, rule-based prompt engineering. We built a system that actively injects the graph topology into the prompt, mapping strict physical network boundaries. We enforced "CRITICAL RULES" at the system level: if a node is offline, it cannot be hacked; if an active WAF sits in front of a web server, the attack kill chain *must* stop there and register as "BLOCKED" rather than hallucinating a bypass sequence. 

### 2. Complex Graph State Management
**The Hurdle:** Architecting the drag-and-drop canvas using React Flow was straightforward until we had to synchronize it with the streaming AI attack phases. As the AI evaluated the network, we needed to highlight nodes red, pulse attacker nodes, and fade out uncompromised infrastructure—all simultaneously and sequentially.
**The Fix:** The state manipulation was constantly overwriting the default styles of the nodes (e.g., turning a powered-off, grayscale node permanently red). We resolved this by creating a highly memoized React Hook architecture and custom Node overrides ([ArchNode.tsx](cci:7://file:///c:/Users/White%20Devil/Music/MAIN%20PROJECT%20HACKATHON%20IEM/Research/web/src/app/dashboard/architect/ArchNode.tsx:0:0-0:0)). This allowed us to apply localized CSS filtering animations strictly to targeted node IDs during the "kill chain" sequence, ensuring that once the animation finished, the nodes instantly reverted to their correct, underlying power states.

### 3. Multi-Directional Topology Connections
**The Hurdle:** By default, React Flow nodes assume a linear flow (one input on top, one output on the bottom). Real-world cloud architectures are multi-directional meshes where a single Load Balancer might output to five identical EC2 instances while simultaneously receiving traffic from multiple external sources.
**The Fix:** We had to strip out the native React Flow default components and build entirely custom nodes that expose 360-degree connection handles (Target and Source ports on all four axes). We then mathematically mapped these multi-directional edges into an adjacency list payload that the Gemini model could parse perfectly for lateral movement simulations.

### 4. Securing Backend LLM APIs from "Denial of Wallet"
**The Hurdle:** Our core feature relies on querying the Gemini AI API sequentially. If our frontend endpoints were left fully public, malicious users could script automated requests against Next.js, draining our LLM quotas and resulting in massive, unexpected cloud bills.
**The Fix:** We wrapped our Next.js App Router API in strict security controls. We implemented Clerk's edge-level JWT middleware to explicitly block any unauthenticated IP from reaching the backend server logic. Furthermore, we implemented Zod schema validation to drop any arbitrary or malformed `nodeData` payloads, preventing automated prompt injection attacks against our AI inference engine.

**Best Beginners' Team**

### Why ArchSentinel fits the "Best Beginners' Team" Track

Our team entered this hackathon with a foundational understanding of web development, but ArchSentinel pushed us completely out of our comfort zone into uncharted territory. We believe our project perfectly embodies the spirit of the Beginners' Track because of the sheer volume of advanced concepts we had to learn and synthesize within the time limit.

As a beginner team, we tackled three massive domains simultaneously:

1. **Complex Interactive UI:** We had never touched advanced graph visualization libraries before. Learning how to manipulate `React Flow` to create a drag-and-drop, multi-directional network canvas—complete with animated edges and custom nodes—was a huge technical leap for us.
2. **Applied Artificial Intelligence:** Instead of just building a simple chat wrapper, we learned how to engineer complex, rule-based prompts using the `Google Gemini` API. We taught the model to act as a Threat Intelligence Engine, forcing it to read JSON graph structures and simulate mathematically restricted lateral movement across our visual canvas.
3. **Cybersecurity & Cloud Native Architecture:** We dived deep into OWASP principles, CVEs, and cloud architecture. We learned how to securely handle authentication using `Clerk` middleware and input validation using `Zod` to defend our own backend against the very vulnerabilities our app simulates. We even learned how to integrate the live `AWS SDK` to pull real-world Cloud asset data.

ArchSentinel wasn't just a project we built; it was an intensive bootcamp where we transformed from coding beginners into full-stack architects capable of integrating AI, Cloud Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity principles into a single, cohesive enterprise product.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Access to reliable, immediate healthcare guidance remains a major challenge—especially for individuals far from hospitals, facing long wait times, or unsure whether their symptoms require urgent care. Many people rely on scattered online sources, often encountering misinformation, panic-driven content, or unverified advice.
**ArogyaSetu** bridges this gap by offering a centralized, AI-powered healthcare ecosystem that delivers structured, context-aware medical assistance in real time.

1. Delayed Initial Diagnosis

People often struggle to decide whether to ignore, monitor, or seek treatment for symptoms. Minor issues are neglected, while harmless ones cause anxiety.
The AI Symptom Checker analyzes inputs and provides urgency-based risk assessment, guiding users toward informed action.

2. Limited Access to Diagnostic Insights

Interpreting X-rays or skin conditions typically requires specialist appointments and time.
ArogyaSetu’s AI image analysis tools provide preliminary insights within seconds—supporting early awareness before professional consultation.

3.Poor Health Data Organization

Health metrics, prescriptions, and reports are often scattered, leading to missed medications and fragmented care.
The integrated dashboard and medication manager centralize health tracking in one privacy-focused interface.

4. Low Awareness of Government Healthcare Schemes

Complex eligibility rules and scattered portals prevent many citizens from accessing benefits.
The AI-powered Scheme Finder analyzes demographic inputs and identifies relevant active schemes.

5.Emergency Preparedness Gaps

During emergencies, valuable time is lost searching for first aid or nearby clinics.
ArogyaSetu provides instant SOS access, a searchable first-aid knowledge base, and real-time clinic location support.

**In essence, ArogyaSetu reduces healthcare uncertainty—bringing clarity, structure, and early decision support into one intelligent platform.**

**Challenges we ran into**

While building **ArogyaSetu**, the biggest challenge was turning powerful AI responses into something clear, structured, and medically responsible. Initially, the AI outputs were long and unstructured, which could confuse users, so we redesigned the prompts to enforce risk levels, next steps, and disclaimers in a consistent format. Handling image uploads and validation for X-rays and dermatology scans also caused API errors due to file size and format issues, which we fixed by implementing strict frontend validation and cleaner request handling. Another serious concern was AI hallucination in a medical context, so we carefully framed outputs as informational guidance rather than diagnoses and added visible safety warnings. Overall, the hardest part wasn’t just integration — it was ensuring the system remained accurate, safe, and ethically responsible while still being intelligent and usable.

**Gemini API**

ArogyaSetu is fundamentally powered by the Gemini API, not as a side feature but as the core intelligence layer across the entire platform. Every major module — the AI Symptom Checker, X-Ray Analysis Tool, AI Dermatologist, and Government Scheme Finder — runs on Gemini’s multi-modal capabilities (text + image reasoning).

For symptom analysis, we use Gemini for contextual medical reasoning with structured prompt engineering to generate risk-level classification, possible causes, and next-step guidance. For X-ray and dermatology scans, we leverage Gemini’s vision understanding capabilities to analyze uploaded medical images and generate medically contextual insights. The scheme eligibility assistant uses Gemini to parse demographic inputs and match them intelligently against structured policy logic.

What makes our implementation strong is not just API usage — it’s how we engineered it. We built layered prompts, response structuring, urgency tagging, and safety framing on top of Gemini’s generative outputs to make it reliable in a healthcare setting. The frontend dynamically parses and formats Gemini’s responses into structured UI blocks, ensuring clarity and usability.

Gemini is not an add-on in our system — it is the decision-making engine behind the product. Without Gemini’s reasoning and multi-modal intelligence, ArogyaSetu would not function. That is why this project is a direct and meaningful implementation of the Gemini API track.

**The problem it solves**

We developed a user-friendly application named ApnaPG, designed to simplify and modernize the process of finding suitable Paying Guest (PG) accommodations according to individual preferences. In today’s fast-moving world, especially in metro cities like Kolkata and other major educational and job hubs, students and working professionals often struggle to find reliable, affordable, and comfortable PG options that match their specific needs. ApnaPG provides a complete digital solution to this problem by offering a smart search platform where users can filter accommodations based on location, budget, food availability, room type (single, double, triple sharing), amenities (Wi-Fi, AC, laundry, security, parking, etc.), and gender preference. The app ensures transparency by displaying detailed property information, real photos, pricing details, and genuine user reviews, helping users make informed decisions without physically visiting multiple places. Additionally, ApnaPG allows direct communication between users and PG owners, reducing the involvement of brokers and saving both time and money. With its easy-to-use interface, secure data handling, and preference-based recommendation system, ApnaPG aims to create a seamless, trustworthy, and efficient platform that connects tenants with the most suitable PG accommodations, ultimately making the house-hunting experience simple, reliable, and stress-free

UI/UX Design Complexity – Designing a simple, attractive, and user-friendly interface.
Database Management – Storing and managing large amounts of PG data efficiently.
Real-Time Availability Updates – Keeping room availability and rent updated instantly.
User Authentication – Implementing secure login and registration systems.
Data Security – Protecting user information from hacking and data breaches.
Payment Gateway Integration – Integrating secure and reliable online payment systems.
Server & Hosting Issues – Handling high traffic and maintaining website uptime.
Cross-Platform Compatibility – Ensuring the app works smoothly on different devices and browsers.
Testing & Debugging – Finding and fixing errors before launching.
Scalability – Designing the system to handle future growth and more users.
Maintenance & Updates – Regularly updating features and fixing technical issues.

**The problem it solves**

Birthday & surprise gifts – Photos that play hidden personal videos when scanned.

 Proposals & love messages – Emotional private video reveals.

 College merch & event posters – Fest posters, T-shirts, yearbooks that come alive.

Brand marketing – Product packaging or flyers that show demo videos instantly.

 Real estate & brochures – Printed image → instant property walkthrough.

 Art & exhibitions – Paintings that explain themselves through video.

How it makes things better:

Turns static print into interactive experience

Reduces need for long manuals or links

Makes offline marketing measurable (scan tracking)

Keeps content semi-private (only works with the sticker)

Creates emotional, memorable moments

In simple words:
It connects physical objects with digital storytelling.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major hurdle was image tracking instability with MindAR.

Some uploaded images (plain backgrounds, low contrast, blurry photos) were not getting detected properly, so the AR video either flickered or didn’t trigger at all.

How we solved it:

Added image quality validation before upload (checking contrast & feature points).

Displayed a warning if the image was too plain.

Recommended users upload high-detail images (textures, edges, patterns).

Optimized video loading to start only after stable detection.

Result:
Tracking became smoother, more stable, and user experience improved significantly.

**The problem it solves**

Job seekers today apply to dozens or even hundreds of roles without understanding whether their resume matches industry requirements, which skills they are missing, or why they are getting rejected. Most candidates rely on guesswork, generic resume templates, and unstructured interview preparation, while companies use data-driven screening systems and ATS filters. This mismatch creates wasted effort, repeated rejections, and slow career growth because applicants lack real-time, personalized feedback on resume quality, skill gaps, interview readiness, and market demand. The core problem is the absence of an integrated, data-backed system that objectively evaluates a candidate’s profile against current industry standards and provides clear, actionable direction for improvement.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was building a system that delivers meaningful, personalized insights rather than generic AI responses. Parsing resumes accurately across different formats, extracting structured data, and ensuring consistent skill mapping to industry requirements required careful handling of edge cases. Another major difficulty was aligning resume analysis, interview simulation, and market insights into a single coherent workflow without overwhelming the user interface. We also had to balance performance and responsiveness while integrating AI models, since generating detailed analysis can be resource-intensive. Ensuring the feedback felt actionable, accurate, and trustworthy—rather than vague or repetitive—was a constant technical and design challenge throughout development.

### OptiEngine
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/optiengine-d87f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gauravnetes/OptiEngne) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Dy448wYpBE3_lFloHlAwn2qg1Vt8QOLX/view) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Diversion%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://diversion2k26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem Statement**

The problem **OptiEngine** solves is not that AI writes bad code. It's that AI writes code without knowing your organization. Every engineering team has accumulated years of hard-won decisions — which libraries to use, how to handle auth, when to paginate, how to protect sensitive data. These decisions live in ADRs nobody reads, in senior engineers' heads, and in PR review comments that arrive after the damage is done. When a junior developer opens Cursor or Claude and types a prompt, the AI is extraordinarily capable — but completely blind to your organization's standards. 

**It doesn't know you mandated React Query over useEffect.**
**It doesn't know your sales data needs a 5-minute staleTime.**
**It doesn't know revenue figures need a PermissionGate.**
**It generates code that is technically correct and organizationally wrong.**

The result is a review cycle where senior engineers spend 45 minutes per PR catching violations that should never have been written. 

For a team of 8, that's 1,200+ minutes of senior review time per week — not reviewing logic, not improving architecture — just enforcing known standards that the AI didn't know existed.OptiEngine makes organizational coding standards machine-executable. 

It sits between the developer's prompt and the code generator as an MCP server, intercepts every prompt, retrieves the 3-5 most semantically relevant rules from a domain-isolated vector database, rewrites the prompt with those rules as hard mandatory requirements, and hands the enhanced prompt to the AI. 

**The developer typed regular prompt. The AI receives a enhanced prompt mentioning engineering specifications followed across the organization. The code comes out compliant on the first generation.**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1557475782ba4536ad3daab59a2db469/d07c76f8-37ad-40b7-bf08-cf835c6effed.png)




**What it does -- Feature List**

**Semantic RAG Pipeline**
Rules are stored as embeddings in ChromaDB using all-MiniLM-L6-v2. When a developer writes a prompt, the system queries both the global collection and the domain-specific collection in parallel, ranks candidates by cosine distance, and retrieves only the rules semantically relevant to that specific prompt. A developer asking about inventory hooks gets PermissionGate and ErrorBoundary rules. They never see JWT signing rules or AI streaming rules — those live in different collections.

**Domain Isolation**
Each team operates in a hard-isolated ChromaDB collection — guidelines_web, guidelines_backend, guidelines_ai. There is no metadata filtering that can be bypassed. A Web developer's prompt physically cannot retrieve Backend rules. This mirrors how real organizations work — the React team doesn't need to know bcrypt cost factors.

**MCP Integration**
The enhancement pipeline runs as a FastMCP server connected to Cursor via stdio. Every prompt the developer writes in Agent mode is intercepted by enhance_development_prompt before any code is generated. The interception is invisible to the developer — they type naturally, the tool fires automatically, and the enhanced prompt is what the LLM sees.

**ADR Auto-Ingestion**
Tech Leads paste any Architecture Decision Record into the control plane. Groq reads the document and extracts 5-15 atomic, enforceable rules automatically. The Staff Engineer reviews, edits, approves or skips rules individually, then ingests with one click. Rules are live in ChromaDB immediately — the next developer prompt fires them with no restart required.

**Prompt Injection Defense**
All user inputs are sanitized through a regex-based pattern detector before reaching the RAG pipeline. Attempts to override instructions, inject roles, or bypass rules are redacted and logged as security warnings. The system returns HTTP 422 with PROMPT_INJECTION_DETECTED rather than silently passing the flagged prompt.

**Graceful Degradation**
If Groq fails, the system appends raw rule text as structured directives rather than blocking the request. If ChromaDB returns zero matches, the original prompt passes through with a loud warning: DEGRADED MODE — MUST be reviewed by senior engineer before merge. Failures are never silent.

**Live Demo Dashboard**
A Next.js dashboard hits the live backend in real time — showing which rules fired for any prompt, their exact semantic distances from ChromaDB, the before and after prompt transformation, and side-by-side code generated from the raw prompt versus the enhanced prompt using the same model.


![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1557475782ba4536ad3daab59a2db469/59bb3007-4586-4c8e-917c-eab435ffa074.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. The Relevance Threshold Problem**
The hardest calibration problem in the entire system. Set RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD too low and only highly specific rules fire — a developer asking about "sales data" might not trigger the "use cursor pagination" rule even though they should. Set it too high and every prompt retrieves 15 loosely-related rules, bloating the enhanced prompt with irrelevant directives that confuse the LLM.
The solution was switching from Euclidean distance to cosine similarity in ChromaDB by setting hnsw:space=cosine on collection creation, then logging all candidate distances on every retrieval call. This let us empirically observe that related rules cluster between 0.35–0.75, loosely related rules sit between 0.75–1.0, and truly irrelevant rules are above 1.0. Setting the threshold at 1.0 and taking the top 5 candidates gave the right balance — specific enough to be useful, broad enough to catch non-obvious relationships like "inventory stock" triggering "PermissionGate for sensitive data."

**2. The Venv Path Corruption Bug**
The project folder was renamed mid-development from OptiEngne to OptiEngine — one missing letter. The virtual environment had the old path hardcoded in every launcher script inside .venv/Scripts/. Every attempt to run Python, pip, or uvicorn failed with ENOENT — the executable existed but the path inside it pointed to a folder that no longer existed. Cursor's MCP spawn also failed with ENOENT for the same reason — it was trying to launch the old Python path.
The fix was deleting the entire .venv directory and rebuilding it from scratch. Three hours were lost to this before identifying the root cause by diffing the path strings character by character.

**3. Groq Model Decommission Mid-Build**
llama3-8b-8192 was deprecated by Groq during active development. The model returned HTTP 400 with model_decommissioned after working correctly for weeks. The retry logic in prompt_builder.py made this worse — it retried twice, both failed, then fell back to raw rule injection. The fallback worked but stripped the Groq synthesis quality from the enhancement, making enhanced prompts look like raw bullet lists instead of coherent engineering specifications.
Fix was a one-line model name change to llama-3.1-8b-instant. The lesson was that model names should be environment variables, not string literals — a change that's now in the codebase.

**4. The Contaminated Blind Test**
When testing "MCP off versus MCP on" to demonstrate the difference, the MCP-off results looked nearly identical to MCP-on results. The reason: the MCP-on generation had already created useSalesData.js with React Query, staleTime, and Zod in the project. When MCP was disabled for the comparison run, Cursor's codebase indexer read those existing files and mirrored the patterns — not because it followed the rules, but because it copied what was already there.
This required redesigning the test to use a feature the codebase had no existing example of — an inventory hook instead of a sales hook. Without a prior implementation to mirror, Cursor fell back to raw LLM knowledge and generated Python instead of TypeScript, with no React Query, no Zod, and no role checks. The contrast became undeniable.

**5. Browser CORS Blocking Direct LLM API Calls**
The demo dashboard was designed to call the Anthropic API directly from the browser to generate side-by-side code comparisons. This failed with a CORS error — Anthropic blocks browser-origin requests by design, and exposing the API key client-side is a security violation regardless.
The fix was a Next.js API route at /api/generate that proxies the generation call server-side. The browser calls its own origin, the Next.js server holds the API key in .env.local, and the key is never exposed to the client. Switching from the Anthropic SDK to Groq for generation also simplified the integration since the same GROQ_API_KEY already present in the environment could be reused.

**6. The "Just Use a JSON File" Objection**
Not a technical challenge but a product challenge that required rethinking the demo entirely. During testing, the MCP-off generation with guidelines.json present in the project produced code nearly as good as the MCP-on generation. This appeared to invalidate the core value proposition.
The resolution was understanding and articulating three distinct failure modes of the JSON file approach that only appear at scale: context window saturation with 200+ rules, inconsistent rule weighting by the LLM across different prompts, and the absence of any organizational control or audit trail. The demo was redesigned to remove guidelines.json entirely from the project, making OptiEngine the only source of standards knowledge and the contrast clean and honest.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem MeritMap Solves

Every year, **billions of dollars in scholarships go unclaimed** — not because students are ineligible, but because they never find out about them. The process of discovering, evaluating, and applying for scholarships is broken:

- **Information is scattered** across thousands of institutional websites, government portals, and NGO pages — each with different formats, deadlines, and eligibility criteria.
- **Keyword searches fail** students who don't know the exact terminology (e.g., searching "financial aid for engineering" misses scholarships labelled "grants for STEM undergraduates").
- **Eligibility is hard to self-assess** — students waste hours applying for scholarships they don't qualify for, or miss "near-miss" opportunities where they fall just slightly short.
- **Entrance exams and olympiads are equally opaque** — students preparing for competitive exams have no single place to discover which exams they qualify for, when they're held, or how to benchmark their performance.
- **Application forms are tedious** — re-entering the same academic details across dozens of forms burns time and leads to errors.

---

## What MeritMap Does

MeritMap is an **AI-powered academic opportunity platform** that replaces guesswork with intelligent, personalized guidance:

### 🎓 Smart Scholarship Discovery
Match against **1,100+ global scholarships** using a neural recommendation engine that understands your academic profile — percentage, board, stream, income bracket, category, and more — not just a keyword filter.

### 🔍 Semantic Search
Find scholarships by *meaning*, not exact words. Ask "scholarship for a low-income girl studying medicine in India" and get relevant results — the same way a human advisor would interpret your query.

### ✅ Instant Eligibility Checking
Upload or enter your marksheet via OCR and the eligibility engine instantly classifies every scholarship as **Eligible**, **Near Miss**, or **Recommended** — so you know exactly where to focus effort and what to improve for future cycles.

### 📝 Exam & Olympiad Matching
Discover entrance exams and olympiads you actually qualify for, with suitability scores and performance predictions powered by a CatBoost model trained on historical olympiad data.

### 🔔 Deadline Notifications & Bookmarks
Never miss a closing date. Save opportunities, get push notifications, and track your application pipeline from a single dashboard.

### 🧩 Browser Extension
The MeritMap Chrome extension brings AI-matched scholarship alerts and **one-click auto-fill** to any application form on the web — eliminating the repetitive data-entry that causes applicants to abandon forms mid-way.

---

In short, MeritMap compresses what used to be weeks of manual research, eligibility cross-checking, and form-filling into a **few minutes of guided, AI-assisted discovery** — making access to educational funding faster, fairer, and more transparent for every student.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

---

## 1. Keras Custom Model Serialization Breaking on Load

The neural models (`ScholarshipRecommender`, `ExamRecommender`, `SiameseTextMatcher`) use subclassed `tf.keras.Model` architectures. When we tried to reload them with `keras.models.load_model()`, Keras threw errors because it couldn't reconstruct the custom classes from the saved `.keras` file.

**Fix:** Every custom model class had to be decorated with `@keras_standalone.saving.register_keras_serializable()` and implement a `get_config()` method that serializes all constructor arguments. The loading call also had to explicitly pass `custom_objects={"ScholarshipRecommender": ScholarshipRecommender, ...}`. This was a subtle but hard-to-debug failure since the save step succeeded silently while the load step crashed.

---

## 2. TensorFlow Optional Import Without Breaking the Entire Backend

We wanted the backend's data and auth endpoints to stay live even if TensorFlow wasn't installed (e.g. on a lightweight deployment or during local testing without GPU). A bare `import tensorflow` at the top of `model_service.py` would kill the entire FastAPI process on import failure.

**Fix:** Wrapped every TF import in a `try/except`, set a `TF_AVAILABLE` flag, and guarded all inference code behind that flag. All five model classes similarly used fault-tolerant imports in `model/__init__.py`. This meant scholarship data endpoints, profile endpoints, and auth all worked independently of whether the ML stack was present.

---

## 3. OCR Confidence Too Low on Real Marksheets

Tesseract OCR produced wildly inconsistent results on scanned marksheets — especially printed-on-colored-paper state board certificates. Percentage values were misread, subject names were garbled, and confidence scores hovered below the acceptance threshold.

**Fix:** Built a retry pipeline in `ocr_service/main.py` that re-runs OCR with progressively different Tesseract PSM (Page Segmentation Mode) flags (`--psm 6`, `--psm 7`, `--psm 8`) on each retry. Before each retry, the image is preprocessed with OpenCV: converted to grayscale and binarized with Otsu thresholding. The best-confidence result across all attempts is returned. A confidence floor of `0.30` was set as the minimum for a result to be considered valid, with a `needsReview` flag surfaced to the user when it falls below `0.60`.

---

## 4. Neural Score Degradation on Sparse Student Profiles

When users skipped optional profile fields (income, category, stream), the neural recommender's input vectors had many zeros, causing it to output near-uniform scores across all scholarships — effectively ranking them randomly. Users with incomplete profiles got worse results than the rule-based fallback.

**Fix:** Implemented a hybrid scoring pipeline: the heuristic eligibility scorer runs in parallel with the neural model and the two scores are **blended** (70% neural + 30% rule-based for exams; similar logic for scholarships). When the neural model's output variance is too low (all scores clustered), the system automatically falls back to the full rule-based ranking. This made cold-start profiles usable immediately.

---

## 5. Auth0 Token Not Available to the Chrome Extension

The browser extension needed the user's Auth0 access token to call `GET /api/user/profile` and auto-fill forms. But extensions cannot access `localStorage` of a web page directly from a background service worker — only content scripts can.

**Fix:** Wrote `token_capture.js` as a content script that runs only on the MeritMap frontend origin. It reads the Auth0 SPA-JS token from `localStorage` (key prefix `@@auth0spajs@@`), then uses `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` to pass it to the background worker, which stores it in `chrome.storage.local`. The capture runs on page load, after a 1.5 s delay (to wait for SPA hydration), and again at 4 s. It also listens to the `storage` event so it auto-refreshes when Auth0 silently renews the token.

---

## 6. Dual Database Sync (SQLite ↔ Appwrite) Getting Out of Sync

The backend uses SQLite as the primary fast-read store and Appwrite as the cloud persistence layer. In practice, profile writes made directly to Appwrite (e.g. from the OCR Appwrite Function) weren't reflected in SQLite, causing the `/api/profile` endpoint to return stale data.

**Fix:** Added a read-through cache pattern: on every `GET /api/profile` request, if SQLite returns nothing, the backend calls Appwrite, writes the result back to SQLite, then returns it. This self-healing backfill means the two stores converge even if a write only reached one of them. Appwrite deprecation warnings from the Python SDK were also suppressed globally to prevent log noise masking real errors.

---

## 7. Vite Proxy Mismatch for Olympiad Routes

The frontend used a Vite dev proxy to forward `/api/*` to `localhost:8000`. However, the olympiad endpoints were registered at `/olympiad/*` and `/olympiads/*` (without the `/api` prefix) on the FastAPI backend. API

**ElevenLabs**

# How ScholarSync Uses ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs was used to produce the **AI-generated voiceover narration** for the ScholarSync demo video submitted for Diversion 2k26.

---

## What We Used It For

Creating a polished demo video requires a clear, professional voice explaining the product. Instead of recording a manual voiceover, we used **ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech** to generate the narration — giving the video a consistent, high-quality voice throughout.

---

## Why ElevenLabs

| Need | How ElevenLabs Solved It |
|---|---|
| Professional narration without a recording setup | AI voice generation from plain text script |
| Consistent tone across the entire video | Same voice, same style, no retakes |
| Fast iteration | Changing a line means editing the script, not re-recording |
| Natural-sounding speech | ElevenLabs voices sound human, not robotic |

---

## How It Worked

1. **Wrote the video script** — covering the problem statement, the one-time profile setup, AI recommendations, and the browser extension autofill demo.
2. **Pasted the script into ElevenLabs** and selected a natural-sounding voice.
3. **Generated the audio** and downloaded it as an MP3.
4. **Synced the voiceover** with the screen recording of ScholarSync in the video editor.

The final YouTube video uses this ElevenLabs-generated voice as the sole narration track.

---

## Why This Matters for the Judges

- The demo video clearly communicates the USP without relying on a human presenter being on camera.
- It demonstrates practical use of an AI audio tool as part of the product delivery pipeline — not just the core app, but the presentation layer too.
- ElevenLabs made it possible to produce a submission-quality video within hackathon time constraints.

---

## Summary

> ElevenLabs powered the voice of ScholarSync's demo video — turning a written pitch script into a professional AI narration that walks judges through the product end-to-end.

**Auth0**

# How MeritMap Uses Auth0

Auth0 is the **identity backbone** of MeritMap. Every user-facing feature that stores, personalises, or secures data runs through Auth0 — from the initial login on the React frontend, through JWT verification on the FastAPI backend, to the Chrome extension auto-filling forms on third-party scholarship websites.

---

## 1. SPA Authentication (`@auth0/auth0-react`)

The React frontend integrates Auth0 via the `@auth0/auth0-react` SDK, configured in `frontend/src/auth/auth0-config.js`:

```js
{
  domain:   'scholarsync.us.auth0.com',
  clientId: '<SPA client id>',
  authorizationParams: {
    audience: 'https://scholarsync-api',
    scope:    'openid profile email',
  },
  cacheLocation:    'localstorage',  // persists session across page refreshes
  useRefreshTokens: true,            // silent renewal — no login prompt loop
}
```

Users click **Sign In** in the Navbar, are redirected to Auth0's hosted login page, and return with an RS256-signed access token and an `id_token` containing their name, email, and profile picture. The `isAuthenticated` and `user` objects from `useAuth0()` are consumed throughout every page and component.

---

## 2. Backend JWT Verification (`python-jose` + JWKS)

Every protected API endpoint in the FastAPI backend uses a `get_current_user` dependency (`backend/auth.py`) that:

1. Extracts the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
2. Fetches (and caches in-process) Auth0's public JWKS from `https://scholarsync.us.auth0.com/.well-known/jwks.json`.
3. Matches the JWT `kid` header to the correct public key.
4. Verifies the RS256 signature, audience, issuer, and expiry with `python-jose`.
5. Returns the decoded payload — including the `sub` claim (Auth0 user ID) used as the primary key for all user data.

```python
payload = jwt.decode(
    token,
    rsa_key,
    algorithms=["RS256"],
    audience=AUTH0_AUDIENCE,
    issuer=f"https://{AUTH0_DOMAIN}/",
)
```

If the token is missing, forged, or expired, the endpoint returns HTTP 401. All scholarship recommendation, profile, exam, olympiad, bookmark, and notification endpoints are protected this way.

---

## 3. Login Sync — Auth0 `/userinfo` → SQLite + Appwrite

On every login, the frontend calls `POST /api/auth/sync` (authenticated). The backend then calls Auth0's `/userinfo` endpoint with the user's access token to retrieve the canonical `email`, `name`, and `picture` fields, then upserts them into both:

- **SQLite** — fast local read store keyed on `auth0_user_id` (`sub`)
- **Appwrite** — cloud persistence layer, also keyed on the Auth0 `sub`

This means the Auth0 identity is the single source of truth for who the user is, while MeritMap's own databases store the extended academic profile attached to that identity.

---

## 4. Auth0 Management API — Bidirectional Name Sync

When a user updates their display name in the MeritMap profile editor, the backend calls the **Auth0 Management API** (`PATCH /api/v2/users/{id}`) to write the new name back to their Auth0 profile. This keeps the Auth0 identity and the application profile in sync, so the name shown in Auth0's dashboard and in the JWT `name` claim matches what the user set in MeritMap.

```python
await client.patch(
    f"https://{AUTH0_DOMAIN}/api/v2/users/{encoded_id}",
    json={"name": name},
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {mgmt_token}"},
)
```

An in-memory M2M token cache avoids repeated Management API token requests.

---

## 5. `useApi()` Hook — Every API Call is Authenticated

The custom `useApi()` hook (`frontend/src/hooks/useApi.js`) calls `getAccessTokenSilently()` before every request, silently renewing the token if it has expired. This means:

- All scholarship recommendations are user-specific and scoped to the authenticated identity.
- Profile saves, bookmark writes, exam saves, and olympiad predictions all carry a valid token — no anonymous mutations are permitted.
- Token expiry is transparent to the user; they are never prompted to re-login during normal usage.

---

## 6. Chrome Extension — Token Relay from Auth0 SPA

The MeritMap Chrome extension needs the user's access token to call `GET /api/user/profile` and auto-fill scholarship forms on external websites. Because extension background service workers cannot read web page `localStorage`, the token relay works as follows:

1. **`token_capture.js`** runs as a content script exclusively on the MeritMap origin.
2. It reads the Auth0 SPA-JS token from `localStorage` (key prefix `@@auth0spajs@@`) — the same storage location used by the `@auth0/auth0-spa-js` SDK.
3. It forwards the token to the background worker via `chrome.runtime.sendMessage`.
4. The background worker stores it in `chrome.storage.local` and uses it to call the backend profile endpoint on demand.
5. It also listens to `window.storage` events so silent token renewals by Auth0 are automatically captured.

The token is **only ever sent to the MeritMap API origin** — never to the third-party scholarship sites wh

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Modern cloud accounts often accumulate unused or forgotten infrastructure over time. These resources continue to generate costs even though they provide no real value. This phenomenon—commonly referred to as “cloud waste” or “zombie resources”—is common in environments using platforms like Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure.

Typical causes include:

Developers spinning up test infrastructure and forgetting to remove it.

Temporary resources created during deployments or experiments.

Backup snapshots and storage volumes left unattached.

Idle compute instances that remain running.

Because cloud billing is usage-based, even small unused resources can quietly cost thousands of dollars per year across an organization.

How This Project Helps

Your system acts as an automated cloud waste auditor that scans infrastructure and identifies resources that are likely unnecessary or underutilized.

Instead of manually checking dozens of dashboards, teams get a single visual interface that highlights waste instantly.

1. Detect Hidden Cloud Waste

The platform scans cloud infrastructure and flags resources that are likely unnecessary.

Examples include:

Idle compute instances

Unattached storage volumes

Orphaned IP addresses

Old backup snapshots

Each flagged resource includes:

Why it was detected

Confidence score

Estimated monthly cost impact

This turns invisible waste into clear, actionable insights.

2. Reduce Cloud Costs

One of the biggest benefits is direct cost savings.

For example, if a company has:

10 idle compute instances

5 unused storage volumes

3 unused IP addresses

The system may reveal hundreds or thousands of dollars in monthly waste.

Teams can immediately see:

Total potential savings

Cost per zombie resource

Which regions waste the most money

3. Make Cloud Infrastructure Safer

Blindly deleting cloud resources can break systems.

This project prevents that by showing dependency awareness, such as:

Whether a volume is attached to a server

Whether a snapshot is linked to backups

Whether an IP address is used by networking rules

This helps engineers avoid accidentally deleting critical infrastructure.

4. Replace Manual Cloud Audits

Without a tool like this, engineers often need to manually:

Check compute utilization

Inspect storage attachments

Review snapshots

Track network allocations

Estimate costs

This can take hours or days.

Your system reduces that to a few seconds of automated analysis.

5. Provide Visual Infrastructure Insight

Instead of large tables of resources, the project introduces a visual “Waste Map”.

This makes it easy to understand:

Cloud Account
   ├── Region
   │     ├── EC2 Instances
   │     ├── Storage Volumes
   │     └── Snapshots

Resources are color-coded:

🟢 Healthy resources

🟡 Zombie resources

🔴 Risky resources with dependencies

This makes infrastructure health immediately understandable.

Real-World Use Cases
Startups

Startups often experiment with infrastructure quickly. This tool helps them avoid wasting budget on forgotten resources.

DevOps Teams

DevOps engineers can run the tool as a regular infrastructure audit.

FinOps (Cloud Cost Management)

Finance and engineering teams can collaborate using this tool to optimize cloud spending.

Educational / Learning Environments
Students learning cloud platforms often leave resources running accidentally. This system helps identify and clean them safely.

This project helps organizations automatically detect, explain, and safely clean up unused cloud infrastructure—saving money, improving visibility, and reducing operational risk.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Accessing Real AWS Production Data
Getting real AWS infrastructure data for testing was difficult. Production AWS environments require strict security, and obtaining IAM credentials with read-only permissions is not straightforward without proper organizational access. Because of this, we had to design a mock cloud environment that simulates AWS resources such as IAM roles, compute instances, and storage services to test our zombie detection system.

2. First-Time Working with AWS SDK
This was our first time integrating the AWS SDK into a project. Understanding authentication, resource listing APIs, and service-specific configurations took significant time. We had to learn how AWS services expose metadata and how to securely fetch resource details for analysis.

3. Gemini API Rate Limit During AI Testing
While building the AI-powered cleanup recommendation system, we faced limitations with the Gemini API, which allowed only 20 requests per day on the free tier. This made rapid testing and iteration difficult. To overcome this, we implemented local testing with cached responses and structured prompts to minimize API calls while still validating the AI workflow.

**Gemini API**

Our project Graveyard, Cloud Zombie Exorcism helps developers detect and remove unused cloud resources (we call them Cloud Zombies) that silently increase infrastructure cost. And we used the Gemini API as the intelligence layer of the system.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/945dc10028c84f70a1d1ee378587a839/2ff5b680-eb33-4b75-8205-3dce7c45be86.jpeg)

when our system detects inactive resources, we send the resource metadata to the Gemini API. Gemini analyzes the context and automatically generates safe cleanup scripts and remediation commands

> Intelligent Market Maker

![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AlphaFlow (IntelliMM) democratizes institutional-grade high-frequency trading (HFT) infrastructure. Currently, the "HFT Gap" prevents 99% of traders from competing with billion-dollar firms like Citadel or Jane Street due to three massive barriers:


- Information Asymmetry: Large firms use Order Flow Imbalance (OFI) to predict price moves seconds before they happen. AlphaFlow provides a research-validated OFI engine with a 0.137–0.172 correlation, giving smaller players the same "predictive lens."


- The Complexity of Execution: Trading isn't just about buying low and selling high; it's about managing inventory and avoiding "toxic flow." Our Deep Reinforcement Learning (SAC/PPO) agents automate this, beating classical trading models by 277% in efficiency.


- The "Latency Tax": In HFT, being 1 millisecond slow means losing the trade. We built a Global Latency Optimizer that uses Dijkstra’s algorithm and speed-of-light modeling across 23 exchanges to tell users exactly where to co-locate their servers, reducing latency by 60%.


In short: It turns a "PhD-level" infrastructure problem into a plug-and-play "Operating System" for algorithmic trading.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdle was the "Simulation-to-Reality" Gap—ensuring that an AI trained on historical data wouldn't "blow up" when it hit the live Binance Testnet.

- The Bug: During early backtesting, the RL agent showed "god-like" profits because it assumed it could execute trades instantly at the mid-price. When moved to a live WebSocket stream, the agent failed because it didn't account for Network Jitter and Order Book Fading (where liquidity disappears as soon as you try to hit it).

- The Fix: I had to rewrite the Gymnasium Environment to be "Latency-Aware." I injected stochastic delays into the training loop to mimic real-world network lag and implemented a Microprice Midpoint calculation instead of a simple Last Traded Price.


The Result: This "adversarial training" forced the agent to become more conservative and realistic. When we finally deployed to the Binance Testnet, the agent transitioned seamlessly, executing 297 orders and generating $361.82 in profit in just 10 minutes without crashing.

**Grand Prize**

**AlphaFlow is a textbook example of Open Innovation because it takes proprietary, "black-box" technologies used by Wall Street elite and rebuilds them into an accessible, modular framework for the broader developer community.**

- Democratizing Proprietary Tech: We are taking "Speed-of-Light" routing and "Order Flow Alpha"—concepts usually guarded by strict NDAs in hedge funds—and providing an integrated stack that any quantitative researcher can use.


- Cross-Domain Synthesis: This project doesn't just innovate in "Finance." It bridges Geospatial Mapping (C++/OpenGL), Advanced Robotics Math (Reinforcement Learning), and Big Data Engineering. By combining these unrelated fields, we’ve created a new tool for market stability.


- Modular Extensibility: Our architecture is designed for others to build upon. A developer can swap out our SAC agent for their own model, or add a new exchange to our Latency Optimizer, making it a "Community OS" for the future of decentralized and centralized finance.

**The problem it solves**

## Mamaset — Emotionally intelligent AI parenting companion

**Mamaset** is an emotionally intelligent AI parenting companion designed for the user-owned internet. Today, parents generate vast amounts of family data—memories, developmental notes, school milestones, and behavioral insights—but most of it is trapped inside fragmented, centralized apps. Mamaset changes this by giving families a proactive AI assistant that helps reduce parental mental load while ensuring the knowledge and memories they create remain portable and user-controlled.

Built as a conversational agent (Telegram + OpenClaw) with a modular tool layer, Mamaset helps parents stay ahead of their child’s needs by recommending age-appropriate books and videos, surfacing local classes and school deadlines, and capturing meaningful family moments for future memory books. The system uses a hybrid architecture: real-time interactions are handled through a modern AI agent stack, while long-term memories can be anchored to decentralized storage (e.g., IPFS via Pinata), enabling verifiable, portable family archives. In future iterations, Mamaset plans to incorporate privacy-preserving models such as **Venice AI** to further strengthen user-controlled, private AI support for families.

Mamaset’s core innovation is shifting parenting support from reactive search to proactive, personalized guidance while aligning with user ownership principles. Instead of extracting value from family data, the assistant is designed to work on behalf of the parent, building a family-controlled intelligence layer that can evolve into wallet-linked identity, milestone NFTs, and portable developmental records.

By combining emotionally aware AI with user-owned data infrastructure, Mamaset demonstrates how the next generation of consumer apps can bring mainstream families into the user-owned internet—starting with one of the most universal human experiences: raising children.
