> Autonomous AI that plans, executes, and learns

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Orchestrator](https://img.shields.io/badge/Orchestrator-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Autonomous AI Project Manager addresses the growing complexity of modern software development by eliminating the need for manual coordination across planning, execution, review, and documentation. Instead of developers and product teams spending valuable time managing tasks, this system accepts a single project goal and autonomously converts it into a complete execution pipeline using intelligent AI agents. The Planner agent decomposes goals into structured tasks, the Executor carries out those tasks, the Critic continuously evaluates results for quality, and the Memory component learns from past executions to improve future performance. Every action is transparently logged, fully traceable, and stored in a persistent database, providing real-time visibility and accountability. By automating repetitive decision-making, reducing human error, and enabling self-improving workflows, this platform significantly accelerates project delivery while allowing humans to focus on creativity, strategy, and innovation rather than operational overhead.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges during development was designing a reliable autonomous execution loop where multiple AI agents (Planner, Executor, Critic, and Orchestrator) interact without breaking data consistency. Initially, database errors occurred due to schema mismatches when logs and task statuses evolved during development, especially when adding new fields like execution status and agent metadata. This was resolved by carefully aligning SQLAlchemy models with the actual PostgreSQL schema and recreating tables to avoid hidden inconsistencies. Another significant hurdle was integrating the Gemini LLM API, where incorrect model naming and missing API configuration caused runtime failures. By isolating the LLM layer, validating API keys early, and testing LLM calls independently before wiring them into the agent pipeline, the issue was resolved. Finally, handling long-running AI execution inside FastAPI endpoints required careful orchestration to ensure the API remained responsive, which was addressed by structuring the orchestration logic cleanly and committing database state incrementally. These challenges ultimately strengthened the system’s reliability and architectural clarity.

### SignFlow
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/signflow-aba2) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/KDsyd7BzeiA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Translating hands into voices

![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Unity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Camera](https://img.shields.io/badge/Camera-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mediapipe](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mediapipe-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

There are many deaf people around the **world** who find it hard to **understand or talk to others**, especially when it comes to things like TV shows, speeches, or normal conversations. Most people don’t know sign language, which makes communication even harder.

To help with this, I made **an app that can change spoken language into sign language and also sign language into text**. This makes it easy for deaf and hearing people to talk and understand each other without needing anyone in between.

The app makes communication **simple and clear**. It helps deaf people understand what others are saying and also helps others learn how to communicate with them. The main aim is to make talking and understanding easier for everyone using technology.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was understanding sign language itself. Sign language is not the same everywhere and Indian Sign Language has its own rules and signs. Finding correct and trusted learning resources took a lot of time.

Another major challenge was training the machine learning model. At first the model was not accurate. It confused similar hand signs especially when lighting was bad or the camera angle was wrong. I had to adjust the dataset and test the model again and again to improve accuracy.

Camera detection issues were also a problem. Sometimes the hand was not detected properly because of background noise skin color variations or fast hand movements. Using MediaPipe and OpenCV helped but tuning them correctly was difficult.

Creating sign animations in Unity was another challenge. Making the hand movements look natural and matching them correctly with words required patience and multiple corrections.

There were also technical issues like bugs errors crashes and performance problems when combining Python and Unity. Making both parts work smoothly together took a lot of debugging and testing.

Lastly lack of real-world testing was a challenge. Since not many people around me use sign language daily it was difficult to test the app with real deaf users at every stage. Visiting Sanjay School was helpful, but more testing is still needed.

Uses real time computer vision to segment hand gestures from complex backgrounds and convert them into meaningful semantic output aligning with visual perception and scene understanding goals of this track

Ensures **consistent validation rules**
Reduces **human errors and oversight**
Improves **trust in digital invoice documents**

The system is designed to be **extensible toward decentralized verification,** where document hashes or validation proofs can be anchored for tamper-resistant verification in the future.

Finance and accounting teams
Small and medium businesses handling large volumes of invoices
Organizations aiming to automate document verification workflows
Platforms that require reliable invoice quality checks before processing payments

**Challenges we ran into**

**Inconsistent invoice layouts:**
Invoices from different vendors had varying structures, making fixed-position extraction unreliable.
**Solution:** Used keyword-based and pattern-driven extraction to handle layout variations.

**Missing or ambiguous fields:**
Some invoices lacked clear labels or complete data, causing validation errors.
**Solution:** Implemented smart validation rules with graceful fallbacks and clear error flags instead of hard failures.

**PDF extraction inconsistencies:**
Encoding issues and hidden characters affected text parsing.
**Solution:** Normalized extracted text and added logging to debug and stabilize the extraction pipeline.

### Stem OS
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/stem-os-706b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Jilpatel18/Stem-OS.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://stem-os.web.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Sehb__Yn6Mg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Play.Learn.Evolve.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This platform replaces anxiety-inducing tests with action-packed mini-games. It serves as a "Gym for the Brain" that translates gameplay data into actionable career guidance.

1. For Students: "Gamified Self-Discovery"
Discover Hidden Strengths: A student playing the "Logic Mover" game isn't just solving a puzzle; they are proving they have the algorithmic thinking required for Software Engineering.
Stress-Free Assessment: It removes the pressure of "Pass/Fail." If you fail a level, you just retry. This "safe to fail" environment encourages experimentation, which is the heart of the scientific method.
Contextual Learning: Instead of just getting a high score, the system tells them: "Great pattern recognition! This is a core skill for Forensic Science and Cryptography."

2. For Educators & Counselors: "Data-Driven Insights"
Beyond Grades: Helps teachers identify students who may not participate in class but possess high innate potential in specific areas (e.g., a quiet student with exceptional 3D spatial visualization).
Career Guidance: Provides an automated, unbiased starting point for career counseling conversations based on actual performance metrics rather than just interest surveys.

3. Making STEM "Easier" & "Safer"
Instant Feedback Loop: Unlike an exam where results take weeks, students see their cognitive metrics (Reaction Time in ms, Accuracy %) immediately.
Low-Stakes Environment: It provides a safe digital playground to practice critical skills. Fumbling a "virtual surgery" game is a much safer way to learn hand-eye coordination than in a real lab!
Accessibility: Complex concepts (like trajectories in Physics) are simplified into intuitive gameplay mechanics (like the Gravity Catch game), lowering the barrier to entry for difficult subjects.

**Challenges we ran into**

🐛 Challenges I ran into
1. The "Sandbox" Problem: Connecting Games to Data
The Hurdle: Each game (like Gravity Catch or Memory Matrix) runs as a standalone HTML5 application. The challenge was: How do we get the precise score and reaction time from inside the iframe game back to the main React application securely?
The Fix: I implemented a robust window.postMessage communication system. The game sends an event (GAME_OVER) with payload data (score, accuracy), and the parent React component has an event listener waiting for specifically formatted messages to trigger the API call to save progress.

2. Bridging the Gap: AI vs. Deterministic Logic
The Hurdle: Relying solely on Generative AI for career matching created inconsistent results—running the same profile twice could yield different career paths. Plus, relying on an external API could make the app slow or fragile if the internet connection dropped.
The Fix: I built a Hybrid Recommendation Engine. The system first runs a "Rule-Based" analysis (hard-coded logic mapping Geometry skills to Architecture). The AI is then treated as an enhancement layer—it only runs if available to add "flavor text" and deeper insights. If the AI service is down or slow, the user still gets their immediate, rule-based result without waiting.

3. Database "Emoji" Support
The Hurdle: I wanted the UI to be fun and youthful, using Emojis 🚀 stored directly in the database for game icons and user avatars. However, the standard MySQL charset kept breaking or turning them into ???? symbols.
The Fix: I had to explicitly configure the database schema to use utf8mb4 (which supports 4-byte characters like emojis) instead of the standard utf8. This required carefully updating the connection strings and table definitions in schema.sql.

4. Normalizing "Skill" Data
The Hurdle: Different games produce different ranges of scores (Reaction time is in milliseconds where lower is better; Memory score is an integer where higher is better). Comparing them directly on a leaderboard was impossible.
The Fix: I created a DifficultyScaler utility class. It normalizes raw inputs into a standard 0-100 "Skill Score" using weighted algorithms, allowing us to compare a user's Reflexes against another user's Pattern Recognition fairly.

No personal information or login is required, making the system secure and user-friendly.

**5. Learning and Educational Use**
Students and developers can use it to understand how content-based recommendation systems work in real-world applications.

**6. Future Scope and Expansion**
The project can be extended to playlist generation, mood-based recommendations, and integration with music streaming platforms.

**Challenges we ran into**

Bug / Hurdle Faced During Development

One major hurdle we faced was handling song name selection and recommendation errors. Initially, when a user selected a song that was not properly indexed in the dataset, the application would crash due to an index error while accessing the similarity matrix.

To solve this, we carefully ensured that the selected song name always matched an existing entry in the dataset by using a controlled dropdown menu instead of free text input. This guaranteed valid indexing and prevented runtime errors.

Another challenge was managing the large similarity matrix (35k × 35k), which could be slow to load and memory-intensive. We overcame this by precomputing the cosine similarity matrix once and storing it using Pickle, allowing the application to load recommendations quickly without recomputing similarities each time.

These fixes made the system more stable, faster, and suitable for real-time use in a web application.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Managing shared expenses in groups such as trips, shared flats, college events, or friend outings is often confusing and inefficient. People rely on manual calculations, repetitive data entry, and informal communication, which leads to errors, duplicate expenses, unclear balances, and delayed settlements. As the number of participants and transactions increases, keeping track of who owes whom becomes difficult and prone to misunderstandings.

---

## How the Solution Helps

This application simplifies and automates group expense management by combining reliable expense-splitting logic with intelligent assistance.

### What People Can Use It For
- Splitting expenses fairly among friends, roommates, or trip groups  
- Tracking who paid, who owes, and how much  
- Settling balances with minimal transactions  
- Viewing complete expense history for transparency  

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier
- **Reduces manual entry** by allowing users to add expenses using natural language or bill scanning  
- **Automatically calculates balances and settlements**, eliminating calculation errors  
- **Provides clear insights** into spending patterns and imbalances  
- **Works offline-first**, ensuring reliability even without internet access  

### Why It Is Safer and More Reliable
- Core calculations are handled locally using deterministic logic  
- AI is used only as an assistive layer for parsing input and generating insights  
- User data is processed with a privacy-first approach, sharing only minimal, summarized context with AI  

---

Overall, the solution transforms a tedious and error-prone process into a **clear, efficient, and stress-free experience for managing shared expenses**.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

Building a full-featured expense-splitting application with AI assistance involved several technical and design challenges.

### 1. Balancing Core Logic with AI Integration
One of the main challenges was deciding how much responsibility to assign to AI. Relying on AI for calculations could lead to incorrect balances and unpredictable behavior.

**How it was solved:**
- All expense calculations, balance tracking, and settlements were implemented using deterministic local logic.
- AI was restricted to assistive tasks such as parsing user input, generating insights, and explaining settlements.
- This separation ensured reliability, consistency, and easier debugging.

---

### 2. Handling Natural Language Expense Inputs
Interpreting user-written expense descriptions in different formats and phrasings was challenging, as users often describe the same expense in many ways.

**How it was solved:**
- Structured prompts were designed to extract only essential information (amount, participants, split type).
- The parsed data was always shown to the user for confirmation before saving the expense.
- Manual entry was kept as a fallback in case AI parsing failed.

---

### 3. Preventing Duplicate and Inconsistent Expenses
During testing, similar expenses were sometimes added multiple times, causing incorrect balances.

**How it was solved:**
- Rule-based checks were added to detect suspicious duplicates based on amount, date, and payer.
- AI was used only to validate and explain potential duplicates, not to block them automatically.
- Final control was always given to the user.

---

### 4. Designing an Offline-First Experience
Ensuring the app worked smoothly without internet access while still supporting AI features was a challenge.

**How it was solved:**
- Core features such as group management, expense entry, and balance calculations were designed to work fully offline.
- AI features were made optional and triggered only when an internet connection was available.
- Clear fallback flows were implemented when AI services were unavailable.

---

### 5. Managing UI Complexity Without Overwhelming Users
With many features and screens, keeping the interface simple and intuitive was difficult.

**How it was solved:**
- A clear navigation structure was defined early in the design phase.
- Advanced features were introduced progressively instead of all at once.
- Consistent UI patterns and empty states were used to guide users naturally.

---

Overall, these challenges helped shape a more reliable, user-friendly, and production-ready application by focusing on clear separation of responsibilities, privacy, and usability.

> Beyond blind trust: Cross-examine every commitment

![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Cloud Platform (GCP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Cloud%20Platform%20(GCP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![gemini](https://img.shields.io/badge/gemini-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google ADK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20ADK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In global commerce, the primary obstacle isn't a lack of data, but the presence of **contradictory and adversarial information**. Current procurement and planning decisions rely heavily on supplier-provided delivery guarantees and static historical averages—sources that are often structurally biased toward optimism.

**ARBITER** solves the **"Optimism Bias"** in supply chain commitments by replacing blind trust with **Adversarial Consensus**.

#### **Core Value Proposition**

* **Challenges Unreliable Commitments:** Supplier on-time delivery performance often deviates from promised levels by **20–40%**. ARBITER cross-examines these claims in real-time.
* **Synthesizes Conflicting Signals:** Instead of averaging data and suppressing critical minority risks—like a localized port strike or an emerging storm surge—ARBITER preserves and analyzes these contradictions.
* **Provides Probabilistic Transparency:** It converts conflicting agent outputs into a **Risk-Adjusted Confidence Score**, allowing decision-makers to act on probability rather than hope.
* **Facilitates Proactive Contingency:** By identifying the specific root cause of disagreement (e.g., seasonal port congestion), ARBITER empowers firms to deploy pre-planned Plan B strategies *before* a failure occurs.

---

### **B2B Applications & Operational Impact**

As a **B2B-first application**, ARBITER integrates directly into the executive decision-making loop, making existing logistics tasks significantly safer and more efficient:

1. **Procurement & Sourcing:** Managers can use the platform to vet new suppliers by running "Adversarial Stress Tests" against their promised transit times.
2. **Inventory Management:** CFOs can better plan buffer stocks based on probabilistic confidence levels rather than binary "On-Time/Delayed" estimates.
3. **Logistics Monitoring:** Operations teams can monitor high-value shipments using real-time telemetry from the **Logistics** and **Weather** agents to identify "Black Swan" events as they develop.

---

### **Multi-Domain Scalability**

While demonstrated here for maritime logistics, the **adversarial multi-agent logic** is a universal framework applicable to any high-stakes domain where data is volatile:

* **AgriTech:** Challenging crop yield promises by debating soil sensor data against climate forecasts and market demand volatility.
* **FinTech:** Cross-examining loan risk by pitting internal credit audits against macro-economic sentiment and real-time market fluctuations.
* **HealthTech:** Resolving diagnostic contradictions by cross-referencing patient symptoms with clinical lab results and drug interaction databases.

---

### **The Technical Foundation**

* **Orchestration:** Built on the **Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)** to manage the sequential "Round Table" logic and shared session state.
* **Reasoning Engine:** Powered by **Gemini 2.0 Flash**, enabling high-speed processing of structured metrics and unstructured web intelligence.
* **Fact Grounding:** Real-time data ingestion via **SerpApi** (Google Search) and **Open-Meteo** (Weather Telemetry) ensures every agent assertion is backed by a verifiable source.

**Challenges we ran into**

The primary hurdle was mastering the **Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)** for the first time. Managing the shared session.state was critical to ensure the **Extraction Specialist** could pass structured data to downstream agents without losing context. I overcame this by implementing a **SequentialAgent** wrapper that effectively turned each agent’s output into a "growing file" of evidence for the next.

Achieving a genuine **"Round Table" conversation** feel required deep prompt engineering to preventcontext drift. I utilized ADK’s built-in session management to maintain a continuous conversational memory. This allowed the **Skeptic Agent** to specifically identify "Optimism Bias" in the data provided by previous agents, transforming a robotic sequence into a live adversarial debate.

The final challenge was developing a **Next.js UI** that visually represented this backend complexity. To provide a real-time experience, I used **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** to stream agent reasoning character-by-character. I then utilized **Framer Motion** and trigonometry to build a circular "Adversarial Arena" where visual tracers and grounded citations from **SerpApi** gave users the feeling of watching a live, data-backed discussion.

> Heal Without Fear

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### **The problem it solves**

Mental health support today faces two massive walls: **fear** and **access**.

We realized that even when people *want* help, they often don't seek it because they are afraid of being judged or leaving a digital paper trail. On top of that, professional therapy is expensive and often has long waiting lists. If you're having a panic attack at 3 AM, you can't just "book an appointment."

**Swaraksha** (which means "Self-Protection") bridges this gap by offering **immediate, anonymous, and judgment-free support.**

* **It removes the fear of entry:** By eliminating logins and emails, we created a **"Zero-Knowledge"** system. Users can start healing the second they open the page, knowing their identity is **completely protected**.
* **It acts as a "Therapeutic Jarvis":** Sometimes, typing is too hard when you're overwhelmed. Our **voice-enabled AI** allows users to just *speak* to a supportive companion that listens and responds instantly, making support feel like a **natural conversation** rather than a clinical intake form.
* **It empowers self-regulation:** We moved beyond just "chatting" to include **active coping mechanisms**. Whether it's "popping" a stressful thought in our mini-game, tracking mood trends to build self-awareness, or finding a nearby park to cool down, Swaraksha gives users **tangible tools** to manage their own mental state before it escalates.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Latency Bottlenecks in Voice Conversational Flow**

* **The Technical Hurdle:** Our initial prototype relied on standard CPU-based inference, resulting in a **Time-To-First-Token (TTFT)** of ~3-4 seconds. In a text-based chat, this is acceptable latency. However, in a full-duplex voice interface, this delay caused "turn-taking" errors where users would speak over the AI, breaking the conversational state.
* **The Solution:** We migrated our inference pipeline to **Groq’s LPU (Language Processing Unit)** architecture. This reduced our TTFT to **<300ms**, allowing us to process Speech-to-Text and generate LLM responses in near real-time, effectively solving the synchronization issues in the voice loop.

**2. Architecting "Zero-Knowledge" Persistence**

* **The Technical Hurdle:** We needed to maintain **conversational context** and **mood analytics** (PostgreSQL relational data) without linking it to a user identity (Auth tables). The challenge was creating a persistent session that survives browser refreshes but leaves no PII (Personally Identifiable Information) on our servers.
* **The Solution:** We implemented a **client-side session generation strategy**. instead of a server-issued cookie, the frontend generates a cryptographically secure UUID upon first load and stores it in `localStorage`. The backend treats this UUID as an ephemeral key to associate vector memory and mood logs, validating the session existence without ever requiring an authentication handshake or email linkage.

**3. Mitigating Non-Deterministic LLM Output in Crisis Scenarios**

* **The Technical Hurdle:** LLMs are inherently probabilistic. Relying on a prompt system instruction (e.g., "If user is sad, help them") was insufficient for high-stakes crisis scenarios (e.g., self-harm ideation), where the model might hallucinate metaphors instead of providing helpline numbers.
* **The Solution:** We built a **deterministic middleware interceptor** (`crisisService.js`) that sits upstream of the AI service. This service runs input payloads against a weighted keyword and regex pattern matcher. If a threshold is breached, the request is **short-circuited** bypassing the LLM entirely to return a hard-coded, clinically safe JSON response containing local emergency resources. This ensures safety is algorithmic, not probabilistic.

**4. Managing Global State for "Fluid" Transitions**

* **The Technical Hurdle:** We wanted the app to feel like a native SPA (Single Page Application) with zero layout shifts, but our heavy use of graphical assets (charts, animations) caused render blocking during route changes.
* **The Solution:** We utilized **React Query** for aggressive pre-fetching of session data and **Framer Motion’s** `AnimatePresence` to handle component unmounting lifecycles. We wrapped the router outlet in a motion component that manages the exit/entry animations of the DOM tree, ensuring the UI thread remains unblocked even while fetching new chat contexts.

That frustration led to *'AI Scholarship Finder'* — a platform that instantly tells students which scholarships they’re eligible for and why. No guesswork, no false hopes.
Students can even experiment with a what-if tool to see how changes in CGPA or income affect eligibility.

It turns a stressful, time-consuming process into something clear and actionable.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Eligibility logic complexity: Handling CGPA, income, category, gender, state, and minority rules together initially caused incorrect matches. I fixed this by enforcing all mandatory conditions and restructuring the eligibility engine.

- Backend deployment issues: Python version conflicts and dependency incompatibilities broke deployments. I resolved this by locking the backend to Python 3.11 and cleaning dependencies.

- Frontend routing & CORS problems: Page refreshes caused 404 errors and API calls failed due to CORS restrictions. I fixed routing configuration and properly whitelisted frontend URLs.

- Service integration bugs: Mismatched function signatures between eligibility, scoring, and explanation services caused runtime errors. I refactored all services to follow consistent interfaces.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

StockEx democratizes professional-grade stock analysis by solving critical challenges faced by individual investors in the Indian market:

### 🎯 **Making Sense of Information Overload**
With thousands of stocks on NSE/BSE and endless news streams, investors struggle to analyze data effectively. StockEx consolidates technical charts, fundamental metrics, news sentiment, and sector trends into one unified AI-powered recommendation.

### 💰 **Reducing Expensive Advisory Costs**
Professional investment advisory services can cost ₹10,000-50,000+ annually. StockEx provides institutional-quality analysis powered by 8 specialized AI agents at a fraction of the cost—making expert-level insights accessible to everyone.

### ⚖️ **Eliminating Single-Perspective Bias**
Most investors rely on either technical OR fundamental analysis. StockEx's multi-agent system evaluates stocks from 8 different perspectives simultaneously—technical patterns, financial health, market sentiment, ESG factors, momentum signals, sector dynamics, risk metrics, and valuation—ensuring well-rounded decisions.

### ⏱️ **Saving Hours of Research Time**
What takes analysts hours—screening financial statements, calculating ratios, analyzing charts, reading news—StockEx does in seconds. Get comprehensive reports instantly for any NSE/BSE stock.

### 🎚️ **Personalizing Investment Strategy**
Not all investors think alike. Day traders need different insights than long-term value investors. StockEx lets you customize agent weights to match your investment style—prioritize momentum for trading or fundamentals for value investing.

### 🌐 **Breaking Language Barriers**
With Hindi support alongside English, StockEx makes sophisticated investment analysis accessible to millions of non-English speakers in India, truly democratizing financial literacy.

### 👥 **Building an Informed Community**
The integrated discussion forum and portfolio tracking help investors learn from each other, monitor their investments, and make collaborative decisions—moving beyond isolated, emotion-driven trading.

### 🔒 **Ensuring Security & Privacy**
With Google OAuth authentication and Firebase security, your investment data and portfolio information remain protected while you get personalized insights based on your holdings.

---

**Perfect for:** First-time investors learning the ropes, experienced traders seeking validation, working professionals without time for deep research, NRIs tracking Indian markets from abroad, and anyone looking to make data-driven investment decisions in the Indian stock market.

**Real-World Impact:** Whether you're deciding between mutual funds or individual stocks, evaluating a hot IPO, rebalancing your portfolio, or simply learning about investing—StockEx provides the multi-dimensional analysis that previously only institutional investors could access.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

Building StockEx presented several technical and data-related hurdles that required creative problem-solving and persistence:

### 📊 **Finding Reliable Indian Market Data Sources**
**The Challenge:** Unlike US markets where Yahoo Finance and Alpha Vantage provide comprehensive APIs, Indian stock data (NSE/BSE) is fragmented and inconsistent. Official NSE APIs require lengthy approvals, and free alternatives often have rate limits or missing data.

**The Solution:** After testing multiple libraries ('nsepy', 'nsetools', 'jugaad-data'), I settled on a hybrid approach:
- Used 'yfinance' with '.NS' suffix for NSE stocks (e.g., 'RELIANCE.NS')
- Implemented fallback mechanisms to handle data gaps
- Built custom scrapers for real-time sentiment data from financial news sites
- Added caching layers to reduce API calls and improve performance

**Key Learning:** Always have fallback data sources—if one API fails, the system gracefully degrades rather than crashes.

---

### 🤖 **Selecting the Right AI Model for Financial Analysis**
**The Challenge:** Initially explored fine-tuning models from Hugging Face (FinBERT, RoBERTa-financial) for sentiment analysis, but faced issues:
- Most models were trained on US financial data, not Indian market terminology
- Fine-tuning required expensive GPU resources and labeled Indian stock data
- Deployment size constraints on Hugging Face Spaces

**The Solution:** 
- Switched to Google Gemini API for its superior reasoning capabilities and context understanding
- Designed specialized system prompts for each of the 8 AI agents (Technical Analyst, Fundamental Analyst, etc.)
- Used prompt engineering to adapt the model to Indian market nuances (NSE/BSE terminology, Indian company naming conventions)
- Implemented agent coordination logic to synthesize recommendations from multiple perspectives

**Why It Worked:** Gemini's large context window allowed feeding comprehensive stock data, and its reasoning abilities produced more nuanced analysis than fine-tuned smaller models.

---

### 🔐 **Firebase Authentication Integration with FastAPI**
**The Challenge:** Integrating Google OAuth through Firebase with a FastAPI backend and React frontend created several issues:
- CORS errors between frontend and backend
- JWT token validation and refresh logic
- Securely storing Firebase service account credentials in Hugging Face Spaces

**The Solution:**
- Implemented proper CORS middleware in FastAPI with specific origins
- Created a custom JWT middleware to verify Firebase tokens on protected routes
- Used Hugging Face Spaces Secrets to securely store 'FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT' JSON
- Built a token refresh mechanism in the React frontend to maintain sessions

---

### 📈 **Real-Time Chart Rendering Performance**
**The Challenge:** Rendering interactive candlestick charts with multiple technical indicators (RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands) caused significant lag, especially on mobile devices.

**The Solution:**
- Switched from heavy charting libraries to lightweight 'recharts'
- Implemented data downsampling for longer time periods (show weekly data instead of daily for 1-year view)
- Used React 'memo' and 'useMemo' to prevent unnecessary re-renders
- Lazy-loaded chart components only when users click on the "Charts" tab

---

### 🌐 **Multi-Language Support (English & Hindi)**
**The Challenge:** Supporting Hindi required more than just UI translation:
- Stock names needed transliteration (Reliance Industries → रिलायंस इंडस्ट्रीज)
- AI responses needed to be in Hindi when language was switched
- Number formatting differs in Indian numbering system (lakhs/crores vs millions/billions)

**The Solution:**
- Used 'i18next' for UI translations
- Modified AI prompts to respond in Hindi when user language preference is set
- Created custom number formatting utilities for Indian numbering (₹1,50,000 vs ₹150,000)
- Stored language preference in Firebase user profiles

---

### 💾 **Managing Agent Recommendations Consistency**
**The Challenge:** With 8 different AI agents analyzing the same stock, recommendations sometimes conflicted wildly (one agent says "Strong Buy", another says "Sell"), confusing users.

**The Solution:**
- Implemented a weighted voting system where users can adjust agent importance
- Created a "consensus score" algorithm that considers confidence levels from each agent
- Added transparency by showing individual agent reasoning, not just final recommendation
- Built a conflict resolution system that flags when agents strongly disagree (signals high uncertainty)

**The problem it solves**

## Avatar: The Earth Project - Solution Brief

**The Problem**: Environmental changes like deforestation, pollution spread, and water level fluctuations often go undetected for weeks or months due to the vast areas involved and limited manual monitoring capabilities, resulting in delayed responses and irreversible ecological damage.

**Our Solution**: An AI-powered environmental monitoring platform that automatically analyzes satellite imagery to detect, classify, and alert authorities about environmental changes in near real-time.

**How It Works**:

The system continuously fetches free satellite imagery (Sentinel-2, Landsat) for monitored regions. Our ML pipeline calculates vegetation and water indices (NDVI, NDWI) and compares them across time periods to identify significant changes. When deforestation, flooding, drought, or pollution is detected, the AI classifies the severity, pinpoints the exact location, calculates the affected area, and generates actionable alerts with recommended responses.

Authorities access an intuitive dashboard featuring interactive maps, before/after comparisons, trend charts, and a prioritized alert queue—transforming complex satellite data into clear, actionable intelligence without requiring technical expertise.

**Key Impact**:

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Detection takes weeks/months | Detection within hours |
| Manual image analysis | Automated AI processing |
| Reactive response | Proactive intervention |
| Limited coverage | Scalable to any region |
| Raw data complexity | Clear visual insights |

**Bottom Line**: We bridge the gap between satellite data and ground action—enabling authorities to protect forests, manage water resources, and respond to environmental threats before they become disasters.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

 1. Satellite Data Acquisition & Processing
Accessing and processing satellite imagery proved complex—dealing with API rate limits, large file sizes (GeoTIFFs often exceeding 1GB), varying cloud cover affecting image quality, and the need to handle multiple coordinate reference systems. We mitigated this by pre-downloading demo datasets and implementing robust cloud masking algorithms.

 2. Accurate Change Detection Thresholds
Determining the right thresholds for detecting "significant" environmental changes was challenging. Too sensitive meant false alarms from seasonal variations or shadows; too lenient meant missing actual deforestation. We iteratively calibrated NDVI change thresholds (-0.2 to -0.5) using reference datasets and implemented confidence scoring to reduce false positives.

3. Real-Time Processing Performance
Processing high-resolution satellite imagery through our ML pipeline was computationally intensive, initially taking several minutes per analysis. We optimized using Numba-accelerated calculations, tiled processing for memory management, and async pipelines—bringing processing time under 60 seconds.

4. Georeferencing & Visualization
Converting pixel-based detections to accurate GPS coordinates and displaying them correctly on interactive maps required careful handling of coordinate transformations, map projections, and ensuring the before/after images were properly co-registered for valid comparisons.

 5. Time Constraints & Scope Management
With 36 hours, we had to make tough prioritization decisions—focusing on deforestation detection as our primary use case rather than building all three detection types (deforestation, water, pollution) with mediocre quality. Delivering one polished feature proved more impactful than three incomplete ones.

Know something is wrong but don’t know what action to take next.
This reactive farming approach results in massive yield losses, rising costs, and economic instability for small and marginal farmers.

🚜 The Solution: KisanMitra

KisanMitra is an AI-powered Smart Farming Android App designed specifically for Indian farmers.
It acts as a digital farming companion that closes the loop from problem detection to solution execution.

We replace guesswork with a closed-loop system that Detects, Explains, and Resolves agricultural problems in real time.

🌟 1) Our “Hero” Technologies
📸 AI Crop Doctor (Image-Based Disease Detection)

Farmers simply click or upload a photo of an infected crop.

A CNN-based ML model detects the disease instantly

AI explains the disease in simple, farmer-friendly language

No labs, no experts, no delay

🌱 Soil Intelligence & Crop Advisory

Using soil data (NPK, pH, moisture, rainfall):

Identifies soil imbalance and stress conditions

Predicts crop risk due to low rainfall and poor soil health

Recommends best crops, fertilizers, and treatments using AI

🔁 2) The Complete Economic Loop
🛒 From Diagnosis to Solution – In One App

KisanMitra doesn’t stop at identifying problems.

AI recommends the exact treatment

📈 Closing the Loop

Problem → Diagnosis → AI Recommendation → Product Access → Action

This ensures farmers are not just informed — they are empowered to act immediately.

**Challenges we ran into**

1) The “Heavyweight Model” Problem: CNNs in Rural Reality

Problem:
Our initial CNN-based crop disease model was accurate but computationally heavy, leading to slow inference and occasional failures on low-end devices and weak networks common in rural areas.

Struggle:
Uploading high-resolution crop images to the FastAPI backend often caused timeouts under poor connectivity, making the disease detection flow unreliable.

Fix:

Implemented client-side image compression and resizing
Optimized backend inference by keeping only essential preprocessing
Reduced image payload size drastically

📉 Result: Average diagnosis time dropped from 10–12 seconds to under 5 seconds, even on slow networks.

2) Schema vs AI Output Mismatch (The Silent Failure Bug)

Problem:
AI (Gemini + ML) returned rich structured data (lists for causes, treatment, prevention), but our database schema expected simple string fields.

Struggle:
This caused:

Pydantic validation errors (Expected str but got list)
Cases where APIs returned 200 OK but data was not stored
Difficult debugging due to lack of visible crashes

Fix:
We redesigned the architecture:
Persist only core facts (disease name, confidence, image path, farm ID)
Generate detailed explanations dynamically using Gemini AI when needed

🧠 This decoupled AI evolution from database design and eliminated serialization issues.

3) Lack of Real Indian Crop Disease Data

Problem:
Some crop diseases common in India had very limited labeled datasets, leading to overfitting.

Fix:

Applied data augmentation (rotation, noise, flipping)
Expanded small datasets (e.g., 40–50 images → 400–500 samples)
📊 Result: Improved generalization and stable predictions in real-world tests.

**The problem it solves**

This project is a **loan repayment optimization** backend designed to help users make informed decisions about managing debt and surplus funds. The problem it addresses is that users with one or multiple loans often lack clarity on how to repay efficiently, whether to use extra money for prepayment or investment, and when a lump-sum prepayment should be made to reduce interest costs.
It first simulates loan repayment month by month, applying interest accurately and allocating available cash using a debt avalanche strategy, which prioritizes higher-interest loans to minimize total interest paid. This provides users with a clear repayment timeline and total cost of debt.


When surplus funds are available, the system evaluates the opportunity cost by comparing the interest saved through loan prepayment with the potential returns from investing the same amount. This helps users choose the financially better option instead of relying on intuition.


Finally, if a user decides to prepay, the system analyzes different prepayment timings and identifies the month that yields the maximum interest savings. By combining these three components, the project converts complex financial trade-offs into clear, data-driven outcomes, enabling users to reduce debt efficiently and make rational financial decisions.

**The problem it solves**

## Use Cases & Benefits

**SentriAI** is designed to enhance security and reduce the need for constant manual surveillance by leveraging AI-powered computer vision. It helps organizations and individuals monitor environments more efficiently, accurately, and safely.

### 🏢 Where People Can Use SentriAI
- **Offices & Corporate Campuses** – Monitor restricted areas, detect unusual movement after working hours, and reduce reliance on 24/7 human monitoring.
- **Educational Institutions** – Improve campus safety by identifying suspicious activities in hallways, entrances, or parking areas.
- **Public Spaces** – Assist authorities in monitoring crowded areas such as malls, stations, and events for abnormal behavior.
- **Parking Lots & Residential Areas** – Detect unauthorized access, loitering, or unusual activity in real time.
- **Industrial & Restricted Zones** – Prevent trespassing and enhance safety in high-risk or restricted environments.

### 🔒 How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer
- **Automated Monitoring**  
  Eliminates the need for continuous human observation by automatically analyzing live video streams.

- **Real-Time Alerts**  
  Instantly notifies users when suspicious or abnormal behavior is detected, enabling faster response.

- **Reduced Human Error**  
  AI-driven detection minimizes missed incidents caused by fatigue or distraction.

- **Visual Evidence**  
  Highlights detected events with bounding boxes and timestamps, making incidents easier to review and verify.

- **Scalable & Cost-Effective**  
  One system can monitor multiple feeds simultaneously without increasing manpower.

### 🚀 Key Advantages
- Improves situational awareness without invasive hardware
- Assists security teams rather than replacing them
- Enables proactive response instead of reactive monitoring
- Easy to deploy using pretrained models and standard cameras

SentriAI transforms traditional surveillance systems into **intelligent, proactive security solutions**, making environments safer while reducing operational overhead.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Real-Time Video Processing Performance
Processing live video frames with object detection was initially slow and caused frame drops, especially on limited hardware.

**How I solved it:**  
I optimized the pipeline by resizing frames, skipping frames selectively, and using lightweight pretrained YOLO models. This significantly improved real-time performance without compromising detection accuracy.

---

### 2. Defining “Suspicious” or Abnormal Activity
Determining what qualifies as suspicious behavior is subjective and context-dependent, especially when using pretrained models.

**How I solved it:**  
Instead of hardcoding rules, I focused on detecting unusual motion patterns, restricted-area presence, and sudden changes in movement. This made the system flexible and suitable for multiple environments.

---

### 3. False Positives in Detection
Early versions of the system generated frequent false alerts due to normal movements being misclassified as suspicious.

**How I solved it:**  
I added confidence thresholds and temporal checks, ensuring that alerts are triggered only when abnormal behavior persists over multiple frames.

---

### 4. Integrating Backend with Frontend
Streaming real-time alerts from the FastAPI backend to the frontend dashboard required careful handling of state and timing.

**How I solved it:**  
I designed a simple alert pipeline where detections are timestamped and stored temporarily, allowing the frontend to fetch and display alerts reliably without blocking the video stream.

---

### 5. Working Within Hackathon Constraints
Due to limited time and resources, training custom models was not feasible.

**How I solved it:**  
I intentionally used pretrained models and focused on system design, integration, and real-world usability, which allowed me to deliver a functional and deployable prototype within the hackathon timeline.

---

These challenges helped me better understand real-world AI system limitations and reinforced the importance of optimization, design trade-offs, and practical decision-making.

**The problem it solves**

Students often struggle with low engagement in STEM subjects and lack of clear career direction. Traditional learning methods are static, non-interactive, and disconnected from real-world career outcomes. As a result, students may perform well academically but still feel confused about what skills they need, which careers suit them, and how to progress toward their goals.

Career guidance today is mostly generic and one-time, ignoring a student’s continuous learning progress, strengths, weaknesses, and evolving interests. This gap leads to poor career decisions, skill mismatches, and missed opportunities.

Pathfinder AI solves this problem by combining gamified STEM learning with AI-driven career guidance in a single platform. It continuously tracks student performance, analyzes skills and interests, and translates learning progress into personalized career insights. Instead of learning blindly, students clearly understand:

What they are good at

What they need to improve

Which careers match their profile

What to learn next to reach their goals

By connecting learning with career outcomes, Pathfinder AI makes education more engaging, goal-oriented, and future-ready, helping students make informed academic and career decisions with confidence.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges we faced was designing the backend architecture and integrating AI agents within the limited hackathon timeframe. Coordinating multiple AI agents (skill profiling, career matching, learning path, and guidance) required clear data flow, well-defined responsibilities, and scalable logic, which was initially complex to manage.

Another challenge was the absence of a fully implemented backend and live AI models. Since our focus was on building a strong, scalable frontend and system design, real-time AI inference and database integration could not be completed within the given time constraints.

To overcome this, we:

Designed a modular, AI-ready architecture that cleanly separates frontend, backend, and AI logic

Used mock data and simulated agent outputs to demonstrate how AI-driven decisions would work in real scenarios

Clearly defined agent responsibilities and data pipelines to ensure smooth future integration

Prioritized system design, user experience, and scalability over rushed implementation

These challenges helped us better understand real-world AI system design and ensured that Pathfinder AI is future-proof, extensible, and ready for full backend and AI deployment beyond the hackathon.

**Duality AI — Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation**

Pathfinder AI aligns with the Duality AI track by leveraging AI-driven semantic understanding and intelligent decision-making to analyze complex, real-world data and generate meaningful insights.

While Duality AI focuses on semantic scene understanding, our project applies similar AI principles to the education and career domain by semantically analyzing student learning behavior, performance patterns, skills, and interests. The system interprets this multidimensional data to segment students into skill profiles, learning stages, and career readiness levels—similar to how semantic segmentation classifies environments into meaningful regions.

Using multiple AI agents, Pathfinder AI continuously processes learning signals (quiz results, progress metrics, engagement patterns) to build adaptive student models and generate personalized learning paths and career recommendations. This mirrors Duality AI’s approach of transforming raw data into structured, actionable intelligence.

By applying AI-based segmentation, profiling, and decision-making beyond physical environments into human learning ecosystems, Pathfinder AI demonstrates how Duality AI’s core concepts can power intelligent, real-world applications in education and workforce development

## ⚡ Challenge 1: ML Inference Latency (300ms → 45ms)

**Problem:** Random Forest classification added 200-300ms per transaction.

**Solution:**
```python
# Load once at startup
model = joblib.load('fraud_model.pkl')
scaler = joblib.load('scaler.pkl')

# Optimized pipeline
features = np.array([[amount, hour, day, lat, lng, ...]])
fraud_prob = model.predict_proba(scaler.transform(features))[0][1]  # ~5ms
```

**Hybrid approach:** Rule-based fast-path for obvious cases (40%), ML for nuanced analysis (60%).  
**Result:** 85% latency reduction, 96%+ accuracy maintained.

---

## 🧊 Challenge 2: Cold Start for New Users

**Problem:** No transaction history = no behavioral baseline for fraud detection.

**Solution:** Progressive trust system
```python
if txn_count < 3:
    score = apply_global_rules(txn)  # Conservative thresholds
elif txn_count < 10:
    score = (global_rules + early_patterns) / 2  # Hybrid
else:
    z_score = (amount - avg) / std_dev  # Full profiling
```

**Impact:** 40% fewer false positives for new users, 92%+ detection rate during learning.

---

## 🌐 Challenge 3: CORS & Cross-Origin Auth

**Problem:** Vercel frontend couldn't talk to Render backend. Standard CORS failed.

**Solution:**
```python
# Backend: Explicit allowlist
ALLOWED_ORIGINS = ["http://localhost:3000", "https://*.vercel.app"]
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS, allow_credentials=True)
```

```typescript
// Frontend: Token-based (not cookies)
localStorage.setItem('admin_token', response.data.token);
api.interceptors.request.use(config => {
  config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${localStorage.getItem('admin_token')}`;
});
```

---

## 📊 Challenge 4: SSR Hydration Errors

**Problem:** Recharts/ForceGraph2D use browser APIs, causing Next.js hydration mismatches.

**Solution:**
```tsx
const ForceGraph = dynamic(() => import('react-force-graph-2d'), { 
  ssr: false,
  loading: () => <Skeleton />
});
```

Trade-off: Lost SEO for charts (acceptable for admin dashboard), gained stability.

---

## 🎨 Challenge 5: Theme Consistency

**Problem:** Hardcoded colors across 7+ pages made updates tedious.

**Solution:**
```css
/* globals.css */
:root {
  --background: #0C0E1D;
  --card: #211F36;
  --primary: #51FAAA;
}
```

```tsx
// Reusable components with CSS variables
<div className="bg-card hover:bg-card-hover border-primary">
```

**Result:** Theme changes in 5 minutes instead of 2 hours.

---

## 🔒 Challenge 6: Rate Limiting Without Redis

**Problem:** Need brute-force protection without infrastructure overhead.

**Solution:**
```python
class RateLimiter:
    attempts = defaultdict(lambda: {"count": 0, "locked_until": 0})
    
    def check(self, ip, max=5, window=60):
        if self.attempts[ip]["locked_until"] > time.time():
            return False
        self.attempts[ip]["count"] += 1
        if self.attempts[ip]["count"] > max:
            self.attempts[ip]["locked_until"] = time.time() + window
            return False
        return True
```

Works for single-server deployments. Use Redis in production for multi-server.

---

## 🔐 Challenge 7: Lightweight Auth

**Problem:** Secure admin login without NextAuth/Clerk.

**Solution:**
```python
token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)  # 256-bit
ACTIVE_TOKENS[token] = {"user": username, "expires": now + timedelta(hours=24)}
```

Security: Crypto-secure tokens, 24h expiration, rate limiting, HTTPS-only.

---

## 📱 Challenge 8: Responsive Dashboard

**Problem:** Complex layout needed to work on 390px–1920px screens.

**Solution:**
```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4">
  <StatCard />
</div>

<aside className="w-16 lg:w-64">  {/* Icons on mobile, full on desktop */}
  <span className="hidden lg:inline">Dashboard</span>
</aside>
```

Mobile-first Tailwind approach with touch-optimized buttons.

---

## 🎯 Key Learnings

1. **Pre-optimization matters** - Model warmup = 85% latency cut
2. **Progressive trust** - Balance security & UX for new users
3. **Check SSR compatibility** - Saves debugging time
4. **CSS variables scale** - Maintainable theming
5. **Simple works** - In-memory solutions for single-server apps

**Tech Stack:** FastAPI • Next.js 15 • scikit-learn • Tailwind CSS • SQLite • Recharts

### GujjuSense
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/gujjusense-3938) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ThatNocturnalCoder/GujjuSense) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Bridging Silence, Connecting Gujarat

![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mediapipe](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mediapipe-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Bridging the Regional Accessibility Gap

While assistive technology has advanced rapidly, a significant void remains for regional Indian languages. Most sign language tools today focus heavily on American Sign Language (ASL) or standardized Indian Sign Language (ISL), often overlooking the nuances of regional contexts. In Gujarat, the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) community faces a "double barrier": the general communication gap with the hearing world, and a specific lack of digital tools that support Gujarati-contextualized communication.

This isolation creates friction in education, healthcare, and daily social life. Hearing individuals often lack the means to communicate even basic ideas to DHH neighbors, while DHH individuals lack accessible, interactive, and regionally relevant resources to learn and express themselves. GujjuSense solves this by leveraging AI to create a localized, accessible, and intelligent communication ecosystem.

What People Can Use It For
GujjuSense is designed as a dual-purpose platform: an educational tool for learners and a utility tool for daily communication.

1. Interactive, AI-Powered Learning
Gamified Skill Acquisition: Unlike static videos, the app uses Computer Vision (MediaPipe) to "watch" the learner. Users can practice Gujarati Sign Language (GSL) alphabets and numbers, receiving real-time validation (e.g., "Correct! 🎉" or guidance on finger placement).

Infinite AI Tutor: Powered by Google Gemini, the "AI Tutor" breaks the limits of pre-recorded content. Users can ask for lessons on any custom topic—from "Medical emergency signs" to "Family relationships"—and the AI instantly generates a structured lesson plan with quizzes and explanations in English and Hindi.

2. Real-Time Communication Bridge ("Setu")
Text-to-Sign Translation: A hearing person can type a phrase in Gujarati (e.g., "કેમ છો" - How are you?), and the app instantly retrieves and plays the corresponding sign language animation. This is vital for interactions in shops, banks, or government offices.

Voice-to-Sign Accessibility: To make interaction even more natural, the Voice-to-Sign feature allows users to speak directly into the app. It converts spoken Gujarati audio into sign language animations in real-time, facilitating smoother conversations without the need to type.

3. Self-Correction & Practice
Live Sign Detector: The app serves as a "digital mirror" for DHH individuals and learners. By visualizing the hand skeleton and recognizing gestures on the fly, it provides a safe, judgment-free environment for users to refine their signing accuracy before engaging in real-world conversations.

How It Makes Tasks Easier & Safer
Removing Geographical Barriers: Quality sign language education is often restricted to specialized institutes in major cities. GujjuSense democratizes this, putting a personal tutor in the pocket of anyone with a smartphone, regardless of their location in Gujarat.

Empowering Emergency Communication: In medical or legal situations, clarity is critical. The instant translation features ensure that specific, urgent messages can be conveyed visually and accurately, reducing the risks associated with misinterpretation.

Building Confidence: For hearing individuals, the fear of "doing it wrong" often prevents engagement. The app’s feedback loop builds confidence, encouraging hearing people to initiate conversations and integrating the DHH community more fully into society.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
Building GujjuSense was not just about connecting APIs; it was a battle against concurrency, resource management, and the architectural complexities of running real-time AI on a mobile device. Every feature that looks seamless now—the live tracking, the instant translation—was forged through hours of debugging "invisible" errors.

Here are the most significant hurdles I overcame:

1. The "Ghost Image" Race Condition (Concurrency Nightmare)
The most grueling challenge was a catastrophic crash (java.lang.IllegalStateException: Image is already closed) that would randomly kill the app during live detection.

The Struggle: This wasn't a logic error I could see. It was a race condition deep within the GPU pipeline. The CameraX analyzer runs at 30+ frames per second, while the MediaPipe AI (running on a background thread) takes a few milliseconds to process each frame. The camera was "closing" and deleting the image frame from memory before the AI had finished looking at it. The AI would wake up to process a "ghost" image that no longer existed, causing a fatal crash.

The Fix: I had to fundamentally re-architect the image processing pipeline. Instead of passing the live reference, I implemented a defensive "Copy-First" strategy. I forced the app to convert the raw YUV camera feed into a persistent Bitmap copy on the main thread before dispatching it to the background executor. This effectively decoupled the camera's lifecycle from the AI's processing speed, stabilizing the tracking without dropping frames.

2. Dependency Hell & The "Zombie" Classes
Integrating the cutting-edge Gemini 1.5 Flash model alongside MediaPipe created a massive dependency conflict that rendered the app unbuildable for days.

The Struggle: The app compiled fine but crashed instantly upon launching the "AI Tutor" with a cryptic NoClassDefFoundError: HttpTimeout. It turned out that the Google AI SDK and Firebase libraries were fighting over different versions of the Ktor networking client. Android Studio's automated dependency resolution failed, leaving the app with missing networking classes at runtime. It felt like trying to solve a puzzle where the pieces kept changing shape.

The Fix: I had to perform a "nuclear" clean of the project and manually override Gradle's dependency tree. I explicitly forced the inclusion of specific Ktor serialization and OkHttp libraries (okhttp:4.12.0), strictly managing the transitive dependencies to ensure the AI brain could finally talk to the internet without crashing the networking layer.

3. The "Silent Corruption" of the Neural Network
Early in development, the app would crash immediately upon opening the camera with zero meaningful logs.

The Struggle: The logs pointed to generic initialization errors. I spent hours auditing the permission flows and camera hardware access. The breakthrough came when I manually audited the binary assets.

The Fix: I discovered that the hand_landmarker.task file (the "brain" of the vision system) was corrupted. It was a 4KB HTML placeholder instead of the actual 3MB binary model. This taught me a valuable lesson: never trust the download. I now have strict validation checks that verify the integrity of AI models before the app even attempts to load them.

4. Balancing Real-Time Latency vs. Accuracy
Running a Vision Model (MediaPipe) and a Large Language Model (Gemini) simultaneously on a mobile CPU is resource-intensive.

The Struggle: Initially, the UI would freeze every time the hand detector ran, dropping the app to a sluggish 5 frames per second. The "Main Thread" was choked by heavy mathematical calculations.

The Fix: I implemented a strict Threading Architecture. The "Eyes" (Vision) were moved to a dedicated SingleThreadExecutor, while the "Brain" (Gemini) was confined to Coroutine Dispatchers.IO. This ensured that the UI remained buttery smooth (60 FPS) for the user, even while the phone was performing heavy matrix calculations and network requests in the background.

### Ak-DsKit Robustness & Stability Overhaul
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/woc-2f68) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1P_ivz7dDQKAu7dR74VB3eBp-2lJlQ8iIa0Fd3dn_aUk/edit?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Making the Ak-dskit Data Science library crash-pro

![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# Making Ak-dskit "Crash-Proof" for Beginners

Currently, the **Ak-dskit** library has a high barrier to entry for new developers. The demonstration scripts—which are supposed to teach users how to use the library—frequently crash due to missing dependencies, unhandled logic errors, and strict type requirements.

My project solves these critical stability issues across three key modules:

## 1. Solves "Dependency Hell" in Data IO & Modeling
* **The Problem:** Previously, if a user tried to run the standard demos without having *every* optional library installed (like PyArrow, CatBoost, or Optuna), the scripts would crash immediately.
* **The Solution:** I implemented **"Safe Mode"** patterns using defensive `try-except` blocks. Now, if an optional library is missing, the code detects it and gracefully skips that specific feature with a friendly warning instead of crashing the entire program.

## 2. Fixes Critical Logic Bugs in EDA
* **The Problem:** The Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) module contained a logic flaw where it expected a Dictionary return type. In certain environments where the library returned a simple health score (Float), the script crashed with an `AttributeError`.
* **The Solution:** I implemented dynamic type checking (`isinstance`). The code now intelligently handles both return types, ensuring the "Health Check" report works in all environments.

## 3. Enforces Type Safety for Machine Learning
* **The Problem:** The Modeling demo was broken for classification tasks, throwing `ValueError: Unknown label type: continuous` because target variables were being treated as floats.
* **The Solution:** I refactored the data preparation pipeline to strictly enforce integer casting (`.astype(int)`), allowing Scikit-Learn classifiers to run successfully "out of the box."

### Impact
This project transforms Ak-dskit from a fragile library into a **robust, beginner-friendly tool**, ensuring that new contributors can run all 15 demos successfully on their first try.

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. Simulating "Broken" Environments
The biggest challenge was testing the "Safe Mode" features. Since my development machine had all libraries (CatBoost, Optuna, PyArrow) installed, the code always worked for me.
* **The Hurdle:** I couldn't reproduce the crashes new users were seeing.
* **The Fix:** I had to create multiple virtual environments and intentionally uninstall specific packages to trigger the `ImportError` and verify that my `try-except` blocks successfully caught the failures without crashing the script.

## 2. Debugging "Invisible" Return Types
The logic error in the EDA module (`03_eda_demo.py`) was difficult to trace because the crash was inconsistent.
* **The Hurdle:** The `demo_health_check` function would sometimes return a Dictionary (causing the script to pass) and other times a Float (causing it to fail). It wasn't immediately obvious *why* the return type was changing.
* **The Fix:** I used print-debugging to inspect the `type(report)` at runtime in different scenarios. This revealed that the core library has a fallback mechanism that returns a simple score when generation fails. I implemented `isinstance()` checks to handle this polymorphism dynamically.

## 3. Deciphering Scikit-Learn Errors
The "Unknown label type: continuous" error in the modeling demo was cryptic.
* **The Hurdle:** The data looked correct visually, but Scikit-Learn's classifiers are extremely strict about data types.
* **The Fix:** I realized that even though the numbers were whole (0, 1), they were stored as `floats` (0.0, 1.0). Explicitly casting the target variable using `.astype(int)` solved the issue instantly, teaching me the importance of strict type enforcement in ML pipelines.

### Hybrid Market Intelligence Engine (HMIE)
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/hybrid-market-intelligence-engine-hmie-c37c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Hrayasa/Hybrid-Market-Intelligence-Engine-HMIE-) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Winter%20of%20Code%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://winter-of-code-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Explaining market signals using price & sentiment

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![GRAPHVIZ](https://img.shields.io/badge/GRAPHVIZ-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rule-based Analysis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rule--based%20Analysis-333333?style=flat-square) ![Log File Analysis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Log%20File%20Analysis-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves

Retail investors often rely on isolated indicators such as price trends or basic technical signals when analyzing stocks. These indicators provide limited context and do not explain why certain movements may be happening. At the same time, qualitative signals like news sentiment are usually analyzed separately, if at all.

This project explores how price-based indicators and simple sentiment signals can be combined in a transparent and explainable way. By analysing historical price data alongside sampled news sentiment, the tool helps users understand how different signals interact rather than treating them as independent sources of information.

The goal is not prediction or profit generation, but improved interpretability. It makes market analysis easier by bringing multiple signals into a single, clearly explained workflow that can be inspected, modified, and extended.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into

One of the main challenges was keeping the analysis realistic without relying on live or paid market data sources. Many existing tools assume continuous API access, which can hide complexity and make results difficult to verify.

To address this, I designed the system to work entirely with local, well-structured datasets. This required extra care in defining clear data formats and separating real analysis logic from simulated inputs. While this reduced scope, it improved transparency and made every output reproducible.

Another challenge was combining qualitative sentiment signals with quantitative price indicators in a way that remained explainable. Instead of using complex models, I relied on simple, rule-based combinations and clearly documented how each signal influenced the final output.

**AOPS**

This project fits the AOPS track because it focuses on clear, structured reasoning rather than prediction or automation. Instead of treating market analysis as a black box, the system breaks it down into simple, well-defined steps such as numerical indicators, rule-based sentiment interpretation, and transparent decision logic.

Each part of the analysis is explicit and traceable, similar to how mathematical problems are solved step by step. This makes it easier to see how different inputs affect the outcome and to reproduce the results. The overall focus is on understanding and explanation, which aligns closely with the AOPS approach to problem solving and logical thinking.

Instead of random problem selection, AlgoDuel integrates a structured workflow focusing on 15+ curated patterns (like Sliding Window, Two Pointers).
