![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Speech API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Speech%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In today’s fast-moving digital world, many people work, study, and live in isolated environments — often spending long hours behind screens without emotional connection or support.
While virtual assistants exist, most of them feel robotic, emotionless, and disconnected from the user's mental state. They provide answers — but they don’t feel the user’s mood, stress, or energy.

As a result, people increasingly experience loneliness, lack of motivation, burnout, and emotional fatigue — especially students, remote workers, and individuals who spend a lot of time alone.

ROOMii solves this problem by creating an emotionally intelligent AI companion that doesn’t just process commands — it understands how you feel.

Everyone's individual character is saved and ROOMii is as same as YOU!! And the thing is IT changes according to people and people's Situations and Emotions!!

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c0051e54e58e4819addb4626f90d9271/8ebc2aca-c41d-412c-8d70-b5b7ec360a87.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

While building ROOMii, I ran into quite a few unexpected challenges that really pushed me to think differently. Getting real-time emotion detection to work smoothly was tough at first — the camera feed kept lagging because the model was analyzing every frame. I fixed it by caching emotions for a few seconds, which made the performance much faster. Synchronizing AI replies with voice output was another struggle; ROOMii would sometimes interrupt itself or speak over previous messages. I restructured the backend so it waits for the AI’s full response before generating audio and added a stop button to instantly cancel playback if the user speaks again. These small details made ROOMii feel more natural and human.

Another major challenge was making the 3D model expressive and responsive. The model initially faced the wrong direction, and those text-style faces like ^_^ looked odd in 3D. I fixed this by reorienting the model, adding glowing eyes that change color with mood, and introducing breathing and idle animations for realism. I also dealt with voice API limits and local audio clutter — ROOMii now auto-deletes old files and falls back to backup voices if an API fails. Balancing AI logic, live emotion tracking, and smooth visuals wasn’t easy, but seeing ROOMii respond calmly, emotionally, and in real time made it all worth it.
We are still in devlopment phase, so accuracy will be increased soonn!!!

**Best Innovation**

Its best as its solves real world problem of Isolation and Depression!!

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sensors](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sensors-333333?style=flat-square) ![MIT App Inventor](https://img.shields.io/badge/MIT%20App%20Inventor-333333?style=flat-square) ![LocationServices](https://img.shields.io/badge/LocationServices-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS Kiro](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS%20Kiro-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Road accidents often go unnoticed or are reported late, causing delays in emergency response and increasing the risk of serious injury or loss of life. In many cases, victims are unable to call for help immediately after an accident. There is a need for an automated system that can detect accidents in real time and quickly notify emergency contacts with accurate location details.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was accurately detecting accidents using mobile sensor data while avoiding false triggers during normal movement. tuning the acceleration threshold to balance sensitivity and reliability required multiple tests. Another challenge was integrating different tools, as the mobile application was built using MIT app inventor while the backend logic and frontend prototype were developed suing Kiro IDE. Managing proper version control and maintaining a clean, gradual commit history on Github within  the hackathon time limit was also challenging

**Ethereum Track**

we explored how blockchain can improve trust and transparency in emergency response systems. Accident events and alert triggers can be recorded as immutable transactions on the Ethereum blockchain. This ensures that accident reports cannot be altered or denied later, which is especially useful for insurance claims, legal verification, and emergency service audits.
Smart contracts can be used to log accident timestamps, location hashes, and alert status while preserving user privacy. This creates a decentralized and tamper-proof record of incidents. Our project demonstrates how such a system can integrate with a mobile accident detection app, making emergency data more reliable and verifiable.

**Best Innovation**

Our innovation focuses on reducing emergency response time after road accidents by enabling automatic, real-time detection without user intervention. Unlike traditional safety apps that rely on manual reporting, our solution continuously monitors sensor data to identify sudden impact events and instantly triggers alerts with live location details. By combining a lightweight mobile implementation with clearly defined backend logic, the system is simple, accessible, and practical for everyday users. This approach makes accident response faster, more reliable, and independent of the victim’s ability to request help.

**AWS**

Kiro IDE played a key role in our project by enabling structured development of backend logic and system design during the hackathon. We used Kiro IDE to design, implement, and test the accident detection algorithm and alert-handling modules in a modular way. The IDE helped us clearly separate decision-making logic from the mobile frontend, making the system more scalable and cloud-ready.
By developing backend logic in Kiro IDE, the project is well prepared for future deployment on AWS services such as Lambda for processing sensor events, SNS for alert notifications, and API Gateway for communication between the mobile app and cloud services. Kiro IDE allowed us to simulate and validate this architecture during the hackathon, aligning the project with AWS best practices.

**The problem it solves**

🌱 CropCare : Smart Crop Advisory System for Farmers
🧩 The Problem It Solves

Small and marginal farmers often make critical farming decisions based on guesswork, traditional knowledge, or advice from local vendors, which may not always be accurate or unbiased.
They usually lack access to personalized, real-time, and trustworthy agricultural advisory that considers their specific conditions such as soil type, season, and weather.

This leads to:

Poor crop selection

Overuse of fertilizers and water

Increased costs and reduced yields

Environmental damage

Difficulty accessing information due to language and literacy barriers

There is a strong need for a simple, explainable, and accessible digital solution that helps farmers make better decisions with confidence.

✅ What CropCare Is & How People Can Use It

CropCare is a smart, web-based crop advisory platform designed to help farmers make informed agricultural decisions using technology that is easy to understand and trust.

👨‍🌾 Farmers can use CropCare to:

Create a secure account and maintain their own farming profile

Enter crop, soil type, and seasonal details

Receive personalized crop and fertilizer recommendations

Get weather-aware advisories such as heat stress or irrigation suggestions

View recommendations in their preferred local language

Listen to advisories using voice support, helpful for low-literacy users

Track previous advisories to review past decisions

View indicative market prices for crops

Provide feedback to improve future recommendations

🚀 How CropCare Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer

✅ Replaces guesswork with structured, rule-based recommendations

✅ Reduces dependency on unreliable advice from third parties

✅ Improves decision-making using real-time weather context

✅ Encourages sustainable practices by avoiding overuse of inputs

✅ Increases accessibility through multilingual and voice-based support

✅ Builds trust with explainable, transparent logic instead of black-box AI

CropCare acts as a digital decision-support companion for farmers,

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/7314bec336484f22b80c83e0fd2a3f30/b85ac0a1-0101-4e6d-99fa-e0ad3faa4c4d.png) simple enough to use, yet powerful enough to make a real difference.

🌍 Why It Matters

By empowering farmers with the right information at the right time, CropCare contributes to:

Better productivity and yields

Lower input costs

Improved livelihoods

Sustainable and environmentally responsible farming

✅ In short:
CropCare helps farmers farm smarter, safer, and with confidence.
[https://cropcare-tech.netlify.app/](url)

**Challenges we ran into**

⚠️ Challenges I Ran Into (and How I Overcame Them)
1️⃣ Understanding Where Data Was Actually Being Stored

Challenge:
After implementing authentication and advisory logic using Kiro, everything appeared to work correctly, but it was initially unclear where user login data and advisory history were being stored. Since MongoDB collections are created dynamically, this caused confusion during early testing.

How I Overcame It:
I traced the data flow end-to-end, reviewed the MongoDB connection logic, and inspected the database directly using MongoDB Atlas. This helped me clearly understand how Mongoose models map to collections and how user-specific data is persisted. This improved my confidence in backend data handling.

2️⃣ Avoiding Blind API Integration

Challenge:
While integrating external APIs (such as weather data), it was tempting to directly copy API usage code. However, doing so without understanding posed a risk of security issues and unstable behavior if APIs failed.

How I Overcame It:
I slowed down the integration process, studied how APIs work conceptually, and ensured all API calls were made only from the backend with keys stored securely in environment variables. I also implemented graceful fallback responses so the application continues to function even if the API is unavailable.

3️⃣ Deployment Confusion Across Multiple Platforms

Challenge:
Understanding why the frontend and backend could not be deployed together on a single platform like Netlify or Vercel was initially confusing. Different deployment requirements for static frontends and server-based backends introduced complexity.

How I Overcame It:
Through iteration and guidance from Kiro, I learned to separate concerns properly: deploying the React frontend on Netlify and the Node.js backend on Render, while using MongoDB Atlas for the database. This clarified real-world deployment architecture and improved system stability.

4️⃣ Scoping the Project Without Over-Engineering

Challenge:
At the beginning, the idea included advanced AI features like image-based pest detection. Implementing everything within a limited hackathon timeframe risked creating an incomplete or unstable product.

How I Overcame It:
I consciously scoped the MVP to focus on a rule-based advisory engine with weather integration. Features that required higher complexity were deferred as future scope. This decision ensured the project remained complete, functional, and demo-ready.

5️⃣ Using AI Tools Thoughtfully Instead of Blindly

Challenge:
Using an AI-powered coding platform can easily lead to blindly accepting generated code without understanding it, which can cause long-term issues.

How I Overcame It:
I treated Kiro as a collaborator rather than an autopilot—asking follow-up questions, reviewing logic, and refining outputs. This approach helped me learn system design, APIs, and deployment concepts instead of just producing code.

🧠 Key Takeaway

Each challenge improved both technical understanding and engineering judgment. By combining careful planning, iterative development, and thoughtful use of AI tools, the project evolved into a stable and meaningful solution.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/7314bec336484f22b80c83e0fd2a3f30/cb612500-5225-407d-991b-8a10580fa3cd.png)

**Best Innovation**

1️⃣ Innovation in Problem Approach (Not Just Technology)

Most agri-tech solutions focus on either:

Generic advice, or

Complex black-box AI models that farmers cannot trust or understand

CropCare innovates by rethinking how intelligence should be delivered to farmers:

It prioritizes explainability over opacity

It focuses on decision support, not blind automation

It adapts advice to context (soil, crop, season, weather) rather than one-size-fits-all suggestions

This approach directly addresses trust, usability, and adoption—key challenges often ignored by traditional solutions.

2️⃣ Explainable, Rule-Based Intelligence as an Innovation

Instead of using heavy machine learning models, CropCare uses a rule-based advisory engine that:

Produces transparent and verifiable recommendations

Allows farmers (and experts) to understand why a recommendation was given

Reduces the risk of incorrect or unsafe advice in a high-stakes domain

In agriculture, where decisions impact livelihoods, explainable intelligence is itself a strong innovation.

3️⃣ Accessibility-Driven Innovation

CropCare introduces innovation through inclusive design, not just algorithms:

🌐 Multilingual support lowers language barriers

🗣️ Voice-based advisory output supports low-literacy users

📱 Simple web interface ensures usability on basic devices

By designing for accessibility first, CropCare ensures technology reaches users who are often excluded from digital solutions.

4️⃣ Thoughtful Use of AI Tools (Kiro as a Collaborator)

Innovation is also reflected in how the project was built.

Kiro IDE was used as a planning and reasoning partner, not just for code generation

The team used Kiro to:

Break down the problem into realistic phases

Make conscious scoping decisions

Iterate on architecture and logic

This demonstrates an innovative human-AI collaboration workflow, aligning with modern development practices

5️⃣ System-Level Innovation & Future Scalability

CropCare is designed as a modular, cloud-ready system:

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![BeautifulSoup](https://img.shields.io/badge/BeautifulSoup-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Online financial frauds such as phishing websites, fake banking pages, and UPI scams are increasing rapidly. Most existing systems detect fraud **after a transaction happens**, which is too late for users.

Our project solves this by providing **real-time scam detection before users enter sensitive data** like UPI PINs, OTPs, passwords, or card details.

The system analyzes:
- The website URL and domain structure
- HTML layout and form behavior
- Social-engineering patterns (urgency, fake alerts, impersonation)
- AI-based semantic intent (with safe fallback if AI is unavailable)

This proactive approach helps users avoid scams **at the browsing stage itself**, reducing financial loss and improving digital safety.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was avoiding false positives on legitimate banking websites while still catching sophisticated phishing clones.

Another challenge was handling AI reliability. External AI APIs can fail, rate-limit, or behave inconsistently, which could not be allowed to affect user safety.

We solved this by:
- Designing a rule-based and HTML-driven detection pipeline that works even without AI
- Introducing trusted domain overrides for official banking infrastructure
- Implementing safe fallback logic so AI never blindly marks a site as SAFE
- Building an in-memory cache to reduce repeated scans and API calls

Balancing accuracy, performance, and reliability within a short hackathon window was challenging but rewarding.

**Best Innovation**

This project fits the Best Innovation track by addressing online financial fraud **before damage occurs**, rather than reacting after a transaction is completed.

Unlike traditional fraud systems that operate at the bank or transaction level, our solution works directly at the **browser level**, detecting scam and phishing websites in real time before users enter sensitive information such as UPI PINs, OTPs, or passwords.

The innovation lies in combining:
- Rule-based URL and HTML structure analysis
- AI-driven semantic intent detection with safe fallback logic
- Trusted infrastructure overrides to avoid false positives
- A real-time Chrome extension for proactive user protection

This hybrid, security-first approach is both technically novel and highly practical, offering a scalable foundation for real-world fraud prevention.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem fAImer Solves: Bridging the Digital Harvest Gap

Despite being the backbone of the global economy, millions of farmers remain trapped in a cycle of **uncertainty** and **information asymmetry**. Traditional farming relies on guesswork, while modern industrial precision agriculture is often too expensive or complex for the average grower. 

**fAImer** democratizes agricultural intelligence by turning a standard smartphone into a world-class agronomist, financial advisor, and market analyst.

### 1. Eliminating the Knowledge Barrier
Farmers can lose up to **40% of their yields** to pests and diseases simply because they couldn't identify the threat in time.
* **The fAImer Solution:** Using AI-powered image analysis, farmers don't need a degree in plant pathology. They snap a photo, and our **on-device vision models** provide instant diagnosis and treatment plans.

### 2. Solving the Connectivity Crisis
Most AgriTech apps fail the moment a farmer enters a remote field with no signal. A tool that only works on 5G is useless in the heart of a farm.
* **The fAImer Solution:** Built as an **Offline-First PWA**, fAImer uses local browser storage and lightweight LLMs (like LaMini and Transformers.js). Critical farming logic and AI assistance are available in the middle of a field, **zero bars required**.

### 3. Ending Market Exploitation
Fragmented data allows middlemen to exploit farmers who are unaware of the true value of their harvest.
* **The fAImer Solution:** We provide **Real-Time Market Price transparency**. By knowing the exact rates in nearby markets (*mandis*), farmers regain their bargaining power and financial agency.

### 4. Agentic AI & Accessibility: Zero-UI Interaction
Traditional apps require navigating complex menus—a significant barrier for illiterate or tech-averse farmers.
* **The fAImer Solution:** We have implemented **Agentic AI** workflows. Instead of manually navigating to the 'Expense Tracker' or 'Crop Planner,' users simply speak their intent. 
* **Action-Oriented Intelligence:** When a farmer says, *"I just bought three bags of urea for 1200 rupees,"* our agentic layer parses the intent, categorizes the transaction, and updates the database automatically. 
* **True Accessibility:** By combining the **Web Speech API** with **Gemini’s function-calling capabilities**, fAImer transforms from a static app into an autonomous personal assistant that does the work *for* the user, requiring **zero typing and zero menu navigation.**

### 5. Financial & Operational Chaos
Managing labor, tracking fluctuating input costs, and navigating complex government subsidies is a massive administrative burden.
* **The fAImer Solution:** fAImer acts as a **Digital Farm Manager**. The **AI Expense Tracker** categorizes spending automatically, while the **Government Schemes** portal matches farmers to the subsidies they are eligible for, ensuring no financial aid is left on the table.

## What Sets fAImer Apart

While other apps are just dashboards, fAImer is an **Intelligent Ecosystem** built for the realities of the field:

* **Offline-First AI (The 'Brains'):** Uses **LaMini-Flan-T5** and **Transformers.js** for browser-based inference. Farmers get AI insights in remote areas with zero connectivity.
* **Multilingual Voice Assistant:** A hands-free, voice-activated interface supporting local Indian languages, designed for farmers who prefer speaking over typing.
* **Computer Vision Diagnostics:** Instant pest and disease detection using **Google Cloud Vision** and **local ML models**, reducing crop loss by providing immediate scientific remedies.
* **Economic Empowerment:** Live market price aggregation and a smart **Expense Tracker** with AI insights to help farmers move from "subsistence" to "profitable business."
* **Actionable Roadmap:** The **Crop Planner** doesn't just give text; it generates visual flowcharts (via Mermaid.js) so farmers can see their entire season at a glance.

*fAImer isn't just an app; it's a bridge. It bridges the gap between the lab and the field, between the market and the shed, and between high-end AI and the humble smartphone. We are moving farming from **'hope-based'** to **'data-driven'**.*

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Overcame

Building an AI-powered app for the "Last Mile" farmer presented unique technical hurdles, specifically regarding browser-based compute and memory management.

### 1. The Web Problem: Running Offline ML
The biggest hurdle was getting our offline LLM (**LaMini-Flan-T5**) and **Transformers.js** models to run reliably inside a mobile browser.
* **The Bug:** Initially, the models were either crashing the browser tab due to OOM (Out of Memory) errors or failing to load because of Service Worker timeout limits.
* **The Fix:** We implemented **Model Quantization** (converting models to 4-bit/8-bit) to reduce the memory footprint by over 60%. We also architected a **Chunked Loading Strategy** within our Service Worker to ensure the model weights were cached incrementally without hitting browser memory spikes.

### 2. Multi-Lingual Intent Parsing (Agentic Flow)
Getting the AI to accurately trigger functions (like "Add Expense") from raw voice input in different accents and languages was difficult.
* **The Bug:** The Speech-to-Text would often misinterpret agricultural jargon, leading to failed Agentic actions.
* **The Fix:** We built a **Context-Aware Prompting** layer. Before passing the transcript to the AI, we inject a "Farm-Specific Dictionary" into the system prompt. This helps the model realize that "Urea" is a category for "Expenses" and "Blight" is a "Disease Detection" query, significantly increasing our Agentic success rate.

### 3. State Syncing in a Zero-Signal Environment
Ensuring that data logged offline (like a new pest scan) didn't conflict with the database once the farmer returned to a 4G zone.
* **The Fix:** We utilized **IndexedDB** for robust local storage combined with a **Background Sync API**. This ensures that the app "retries" the upload silently in the background the moment a connection is detected, without the farmer needing to keep the app open.

**Best Innovation**

fAImer qualifies for the Best Innovation track because it reimagines agricultural technology from the ground up rather than optimizing existing assumptions. Instead of building another cloud-dependent AI tool, we engineered a connectivity-aware, bilingual intelligence system that works reliably offline on low-end mobile devices, breaking the dependency on constant internet. The platform combines computer vision for crop, weed, pest, and soil diagnostics, agentic voice-based navigation in 8 Indian languages, and a transparent marketplace layer that removes pricing opacity and middleman exploitation. We unified farm planning, laborer coordination, community-driven alerts, and government subsidy discovery into one intelligent ecosystem, solving integration gaps that traditional agri-tech ignores. Our innovation lies not only in using AI, but in making it adaptive, inclusive, and field-ready for the people who need it most, transforming fragmented rural workflows into guided intelligence that works everywhere, for everyone.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Postman](https://img.shields.io/badge/Postman-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embedded Systems](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embedded%20Systems-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most AI assistants are designed to always answer, even when the information is incomplete, outdated, or restricted.
This becomes dangerous in enterprise environments where permissions, compliance, and accuracy matter.

This project solves the problem of unsafe and uncontrolled knowledge access by introducing governance into Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

What people can use it for

Enterprise knowledge access
Safely query internal documents such as HR policies, technical documentation, or internal reports.

Role-restricted information retrieval
Ensure employees only see information they are authorized to access based on their role.

Compliance-sensitive environments
Prevent leakage of confidential or regulated information by enforcing document-level and chunk-level permissions.

Auditable AI decisions
Track who queried what, why an answer was given, or why a query was rejected.

How it makes existing workflows safer

Prevents hallucinated or unauthorized answers

Refuses to answer when information is missing or restricted

Makes AI outputs traceable, explainable, and confidence-scored

Separates knowledge governance from language model generation

Instead of behaving like a chatbot, the system acts as a controlled knowledge layer — prioritizing safety and trust over convenience.

image related to clusters :-
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/8874cdf165df4d8684ec6b82d007b9ef/972bff49-fb53-48b8-8324-1a5405eb365c.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Preventing the system from “over-answering”

One major challenge was ensuring the system did not generate answers by default.
Early versions returned responses even when retrieved context was weak or incomplete.

How I solved it:

Introduced strict pre-LLM filtering
Added rejection logic when no permitted or relevant chunks exist
Logged all rejections for auditability instead of silently failing

2. Managing permissions across documents and chunks

Applying permissions only at the document level was too coarse and unsafe.
Some documents contained sections that should be restricted even if the rest was allowed.

How I solved it:

Introduced chunk-level metadata with allowed roles
Ensured permission checks happen before passing context to the LLM
Kept governance logic in the database layer to avoid backend coupling

3. Designing auditability without breaking existing logic

Adding analytics, query logs, and confidence tracking without refactoring backend code was challenging.

How I solved it:

Designed append-only MongoDB collections for logging
Treated the database as a control plane, not just storage
Added observability without changing execution paths

4. Avoiding tight coupling between systems

Another challenge was preventing hard dependencies between MongoDB, Qdrant, and the LLM.

How I solved it:

Clearly separated responsibilities:
MongoDB → governance & audit
Qdrant → semantic retrieval
LLM → response generation
Ensured each layer can evolve independently

**Best Innovation**

Most AI assistants and RAG systems are optimized to maximize answers.
They retrieve relevant text and generate responses regardless of whether the information is appropriate, authorized, or reliable.

This project takes the opposite approach.

Instead of asking “Can the model answer this?”
it first asks “Should the system answer this?”

That shift in mindset is the core innovation.

1️⃣ Governance Comes Before Generation

Traditional RAG pipelines treat governance as an afterthought.
Here, governance is enforced before the language model is involved.

Every document is tracked with metadata, ownership, and lifecycle status

Every chunk has explicit permission rules

Unauthorized or outdated content is filtered out early

This ensures that the LLM only sees approved, role-appropriate knowledge, eliminating accidental leakage and hallucinated reasoning.

2️⃣ Refusal Is a First-Class Outcome

Most systems see failure as an error.
This project treats refusal as a correct and logged response.

If information is missing → the system refuses

If the user is unauthorized → the system refuses

Every refusal is recorded with a reason code

This creates a safer, more predictable AI system that behaves like an enterprise service — not a guessing engine.

3️⃣ Databases Act as an Intelligence Control Plane

Databases are usually passive storage layers.
In this system, MongoDB becomes an active governance layer:

It enforces access rules

Stores audit trails

Tracks document authority and freshness

Enables explainability after the fact

This decouples trust and accountability from model behavior — a pattern rarely demonstrated in hackathon projects.

4️⃣ Confidence Is Measured, Not Assumed

Most AI tools present answers with the same certainty, regardless of quality.
This project attaches a confidence score derived from:

Semantic relevance

Agreement across multiple sources

Document freshness

Users don’t just get an answer — they get context about how much the system trusts it.

5️⃣ Designed to Be Deployed, Not Just Demonstrated

Many projects work only under ideal demo conditions.
This system was intentionally designed so that:

Components are modular and replaceable

Vector search, governance, and generation are clearly separated

Operational concerns like auditability and safety are built-in

Nothing fundamental needs to be rewritten to move from demo to production.

Innovation Summary -

""The innovation isn’t smarter answers —
it’s accountable intelligence.""

This project demonstrates how AI systems can be useful without being reckless, making it a practical blueprint for the next generation of enterprise RAG systems.

**AWS**

This project is designed around scalable, governed, and secure cloud-native architecture, which aligns directly with AWS’s strengths in managed infrastructure, security, and data services.

Rather than using AWS as simple hosting, the system naturally maps to AWS as an enterprise control plane.

1️⃣ Cloud-Native, Modular Architecture

The system is composed of independent layers:

document ingestion

governance and metadata control

semantic retrieval

response generation

Each layer can scale independently, which fits AWS’s microservice-friendly architecture.

On AWS, these layers can be deployed as:

API services (EC2 / ECS / Lambda where appropriate)

Managed data services

Scalable storage and networking components

This design aligns with AWS best practices for fault isolation and horizontal scalability.

2️⃣ Security & Identity Are First-Class Concepts

AWS places heavy emphasis on identity, access control, and security by default, which mirrors the project’s core design philosophy.

The system:

Enforces role-based access to knowledge

Restricts sensitive information before processing

Logs every access decision for auditability

These concepts directly align with AWS’s shared responsibility and security model, making the project suitable for compliance-driven deployments.

3️⃣ Data Governance at Scale

The project treats databases as governance layers, not just storage.
This aligns well with AWS’s managed data services, which emphasize durability, consistency, and monitoring.

Key AWS strengths reflected here:

Reliable managed databases

Observability and logging

Automated backups and lifecycle management

The project demonstrates how structured metadata and audit trails can be enforced at cloud scale.

4️⃣ Event-Driven and Observable by Design

Every document upload, query, or rejection is an event that can be observed, logged, and analyzed.

This fits naturally into AWS’s event-driven ecosystem, where:

System behavior is observable

Failures are traceable

Performance can be monitored continuously

The architecture supports production-grade monitoring, making it suitable for long-running cloud deployments.

5️⃣ Designed for Real Enterprise Deployment

AWS is widely used in regulated and enterprise environments.
This project reflects those same needs by including:

Audit logs

Controlled access

Explainable decisions

Safe failure behavior

As a result, the project demonstrates how generative AI can be responsibly deployed on AWS, not just experimented with.

AWS Track Summary

This project showcases how AWS can be used not just to scale AI,
but to govern it.

It highlights AWS’s strengths in security, data reliability, and operational excellence, making it a strong candidate for the AWS innovation track.

     - Early disease detection using image analysis

Instead of solving just one problem, Farm-AI integrates crop recommendation, disease detection, weather awareness, multilingual support, and AI chat assistance into one unified system. This reduces dependency on multiple apps, experts, or costly tools.

Smart crop recommendation based on input conditions
AI-driven crop disease detection using image analysis
Multilingual accessibility, making technology usable for farmers from different regions
Simple web-based interface, requiring no technical knowledge

Farm-AI focuses on real-world usability, not complexity. By combining multiple agricultural decision-making tools into one platform, it empowers farmers to make faster, smarter, and more sustainable decisions, directly improving productivity and reducing losses.

**The problem it solves**

How we solve problem through our project and challenges we face

Project Introduction

Nyaay-Drishti is a web and mobile-based judicial scheduling system designed to optimize daily courtroom operations through structured, rule-based logic. The project focuses on improving the generation and management of daily cause lists by introducing deterministic scheduling and spillover handling mechanisms. Built using Flutter for the frontend and Firebase for the backend, Nyaay-Drishti aims to enhance transparency, reduce administrative delays, and improve time utilization within court proceedings without interfering in judicial decision-making.

What Problem Our Project Solves

One of the major contributors to judicial delays in India is inefficient daily case listing. Courts often schedule more cases than can realistically be heard in a single day. When hearings exceed their expected duration, cases listed later are frequently adjourned due to lack of time. This results in repeated hearing dates, long waiting hours for lawyers and litigants, and overcrowding within court premises.

Current scheduling processes are largely static and do not account for realistic courtroom constraints. Nyaay-Drishti addresses this issue by introducing a structured scheduling approach that prioritizes cases based on predefined rules and efficiently manages end-of-day spillovers. Cases that cannot be heard within court hours are automatically identified and prioritized for the next working day, reducing unnecessary adjournments and improving predictability, fairness, and overall courtroom efficiency.

Challenges Faced During the Hackathon

Designing a Reliable Priority Scheduling Algorithm
Implementing a priority-based scheduling algorithm that behaved consistently under limited court time was one of the biggest challenges. Initial versions produced incorrect prioritization and required multiple iterations and debugging.

Backend Logic Integration
Integrating backend scheduling logic with an already developed UI required careful alignment of data structures, workflows, and state updates, which increased development complexity.

Time Pressure and Coordination
Working within a 36-hour hackathon window was demanding. The two-hour extension of the submission deadline helped significantly, allowing us to stabilize the priority algorithm, fix critical issues, and submit a more complete and functional solution.

**Challenges we ran into**

While developing NyaayDrishti – App ki Adalat, one of the biggest challenges was understanding and translating the complex, real-world workflow of the Indian judicial system into a structured digital platform. The court process is not linear; it involves multiple stages, strict roles, and procedural dependencies, which made system design challenging. Another major difficulty was creating a priority-based listing algorithm that remained fair and transparent while considering factors such as case age, category, stage, vulnerable litigants, and adjournments due to court time constraints. Estimating realistic hearing durations and fitting cases into limited judicial hours without over-listing also required careful planning. Additionally, implementing role-based access so that lawyers, court masters, and judges each saw only what was relevant to them was technically demanding. On the design side, balancing a government-grade professional interface with a modern, youth-driven approach—while using priority colors effectively—was a constant challenge. Finally, building the entire system using only HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, without modern frameworks, increased development complexity but helped maintain transparency, performance, and compatibility with government systems.

**Best Innovation**

NyaayDrishti stands out as an innovation because it does not attempt to replace the judiciary, but instead augments it using data-driven decision-making. Unlike traditional court management systems that merely digitize paperwork, our platform introduces an algorithmic, transparent, and dynamic case listing mechanism that directly addresses the root problem of case pendency. By assigning a daily urgency score to every case and combining it with time-binning optimization, the system ensures that judicial time is used efficiently and predictably. The innovation lies in treating courts as intelligent queue management systems, where prioritization is based on objective parameters such as case age, stage, vulnerability, and adjournment history, rather than manual discretion alone. Our role-based dashboards further enhance this by giving each stakeholder exactly the information and controls they need, reducing friction and human error. This approach blends law, governance, and technology in a way that is practical, ethical, and scalable, making NyaayDrishti not just a digital platform, but a forward-looking model for judicial reform

**AWS**

NyaayDrishti fits strongly within the AWS track because it is designed as a scalable, data-driven public infrastructure platform that can seamlessly operate on cloud-native principles. The platform relies on continuous data ingestion, real-time priority computation, and dynamic scheduling, all of which align naturally with AWS services such as cloud databases, serverless compute, and managed APIs. Judicial systems handle large volumes of structured and unstructured data, and our architecture is built to scale horizontally as case volumes grow, making it well-suited for deployment on AWS. Features like real-time case listing updates, role-based dashboards, and secure access control reflect use cases where AWS’s reliability, availability, and security are critical, especially for government-grade systems.

Kiro IDE played a crucial role in accelerating our development throughout the hackathon. It helped us translate complex judicial workflows into clean, modular code by assisting in logic design, debugging, and rapid iteration. While implementing the priority-based listing and time-binning algorithms, Kiro’s chatbot allowed us to reason through edge cases, validate algorithmic fairness, and structure our JavaScript files efficiently without breaking existing functionality. It also helped us maintain consistency across backend APIs and frontend data flow, which is critical in a multi-role system like ours. Overall, Kiro IDE acted as a productivity multiplier, enabling us to focus more on system design and innovation rather than getting stuck on boilerplate or syntax issues, making it an essential part of delivering a complete, scalable solution within hackathon timelines.

**The problem it solves**

ARC — Smart Attendance & Conversational AI-Driven Curriculum System for Colleges
Problem Statement

Manual attendance in colleges is inefficient, prone to proxy marking, and disconnected from students’ actual learning outcomes. Existing biometric or hardware-based solutions are costly, rigid, and fail to translate attendance data into meaningful academic guidance. Students also lack continuous, personalized academic support, relying instead on static dashboards or periodic counseling.

Our Solution

ARC is a mobile-first, zero-hardware smart attendance and curriculum intelligence platform for higher education. It combines Bluetooth-based proximity detection, facial recognition with liveness verification, and a conversational AI academic companion that guides students throughout their academic journey.

Teachers’ smartphones function as BLE beacons, while students’ phones confirm classroom presence. Once attendance is verified, ARC’s AI roadmap engine and conversational AI assistant transform raw attendance and performance data into actionable academic insights and personalized guidance.

How It Works
1. Hybrid Attendance Verification

Teacher’s phone broadcasts a BLE signal.

Students’ devices detect proximity using BLE mesh logic and RSSI filtering, ensuring physical classroom presence.

A face recognition + liveness check verifies student identity and prevents proxy attendance.

Backend validation confirms attendance only when all signals match.

2. Conversational AI Academic Companion

Each student interacts with a chat-based conversational AI embedded within the app.

The AI understands the student’s attendance trends, academic performance, interests, and goals.

Students can ask natural-language questions such as:

“Why is my attendance dropping in this subject?”

“What should I focus on this semester to improve placements?”

“Create a weekly study plan based on my weak areas.”

The AI dynamically updates the student’s personalized academic and career roadmap based on real-time data.

3. AI-Driven Smart Curriculum

Attendance, assessment scores, and behavioral patterns feed into an agentic AI system.

The system continuously adapts learning paths, suggests resources, flags risks, and aligns recommendations with institutional rules and semester timelines.

Key Innovations & Novelty

Zero Hardware Attendance System using only smartphones

BLE Mesh + RSSI Filtering for location-accurate presence detection

Face Recognition with Liveness Verification to eliminate proxy marking

Conversational AI + Agentic Roadmap Engine for continuous academic guidance

Context-Aware AI that responds using real student data, not static rules

Overlay-Based Teacher Dashboard for real-time insights without workflow disruption

Tech Stack

Mobile App: Flutter

Bluetooth Layer: BLE Mesh, RSSI-based filtering

Face Recognition: ArcFace (512-D embeddings), liveness detection

Conversational AI & Roadmap Engine: LLM-powered agentic AI

Backend: Flask APIs, PostgreSQL

ML & Vision Pipelines: Powered using Google MediaPipe

Feasibility & Scalability

Uses proven, production-ready mobile technologies

Runs on standard Android and iOS smartphones

Average attendance verification time: < 10 seconds per student

Supports offline attendance logging with delayed sync

Battery-optimized BLE scanning

Encrypted biometric data storage with privacy-first design (DPDP/GDPR aligned)

Impact & Benefits

Saves 10–15 minutes per class, increasing effective teaching time

Ensures accurate, proxy-free attendance

Provides 24/7 conversational academic support to students

Enables personalized learning and career planning at scale

Improves institutional transparency and efficiency

Aligns with NEP 2020’s vision of personalized and experiential learning

Target Users & Stakeholders

Primary Customers: Colleges, universities, autonomous institutions

End Users: Students, teachers, academic administrators

Secondary Stakeholders: Parents, recruiters, educational boards, government bodies

Vision

ARC redefines attendance as a foundation for intelligent education systems. By combining hybrid attendance verification with a conversational AI academic companion, ARC ensures that every student not only shows up to class—but also receives continuous, personalized guidance to succeed academically and professionally.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges during development was debugging complex interactions across the frontend, backend, and AI-driven components simultaneously. Many issues only surfaced after full integration—such as API contract mismatches, inconsistent payload structures, state synchronization bugs, and edge cases during real-time interactions.

Another significant hurdle was testing and validating backend endpoints under real frontend conditions. Standard API testing alone was not always sufficient to replicate browser-level behavior, headers, CORS scenarios, and dynamic request flows.

To overcome this, we used Requestly to intercept, inspect, modify, and mock API requests and responses directly in the browser. This allowed us to debug endpoints in real time, validate request/response payloads, and simulate backend behavior while the frontend was still under active development.

In addition, we leveraged Kiro as part of our development workflow to debug issues, reason through complex logic, and rapidly prototype solutions. This helped us identify root causes faster and iterate on features more efficiently before committing to full implementations.

For the AI components, managing and testing different model behaviors was also a challenge. To address this, we used OpenRouter to route and experiment with multiple language models, and Gemini to validate responses, refine prompts, and improve reasoning quality. This setup made it easier to compare outputs, handle edge cases, and ensure consistent AI behavior across different scenarios.

Overall, combining real-time request debugging, assisted prototyping, and flexible AI model routing significantly reduced development friction and helped stabilize the system more quickly.

**Creative Use of Kiro**

From a technical standpoint, Kiro was the cornerstone of our system architecture and the primary reason the voice assistant remains stable, scalable, and context-aware under real usage. Kiro enabled us to model the assistant as an agentic workflow, clearly separating intent understanding, reasoning, action selection, and response generation, which drastically reduced state leakage and inconsistent behavior across conversations. It allowed us to prototype and validate complex logic—such as switching between roadmap planning, conversational guidance, and follow-up clarification—without hard-coding brittle flows. OpenRouter was used as the LLM orchestration layer to dynamically route prompts and maintain model flexibility, while Gemini handled high-throughput content and quiz generation, feeding structured outputs back into the agent state. ElevenLabs completed the pipeline with low-latency, high-fidelity speech synthesis. Technically, the key achievement is that Kiro unified these components into a single, deterministic agent loop, transforming a multi-model, multi-service stack into a maintainable, production-grade voice assistant rather than a fragile AI demo.

**Requestly**

Requestly was highly useful during development, particularly for debugging and validating a large number of backend endpoints across Spring Boot and Flask services. As the system evolved rapidly during the hackathon, managing and testing these endpoints efficiently became critical.

Requestly’s ability to intercept live frontend requests, rewrite URLs, headers, and request payloads, and mock API responses in real time allowed us to debug issues without repeatedly restarting or redeploying backend services. These features were especially helpful when testing authentication flows, AI-related endpoints, and handling CORS-related issues.

Overall, Requestly helped streamline our development workflow, reduced debugging time, and made it easier to maintain stable communication between the frontend and multiple backend services within tight hackathon timelines.

**ELeven Labs**

Arcy is a voice-first, AI-powered personalized learning assistant designed to function as a continuous learning companion rather than a traditional chatbot. The core user experience is built around ElevenLabs, enabling natural, expressive, human-like voice interaction that allows learners to engage conversationally instead of navigating rigid interfaces. This voice-driven approach significantly improves accessibility, engagement, and retention during extended learning sessions.

Behind the voice layer, Arcy’s conversational intelligence is powered by OpenRouter, which serves as the system’s central reasoning and model-routing layer. OpenRouter manages dialogue flow, preserves long-term conversational context, and dynamically selects the most suitable large language models for each task. This enables Arcy to deliver adaptive, goal-aligned responses that evolve with the learner’s progress, interests, and performance.

To handle complex behaviors—such as seamlessly switching between conversational mentoring, personalized roadmap generation, and step-by-step problem solving—Arcy employs an agentic AI workflow orchestrated through Kiro. This agentic architecture allows the system to decompose user intent, reason through multi-step decisions, and select the most appropriate actions before responding. The final output is then delivered through ElevenLabs, ensuring that even complex reasoning feels natural and conversational to the learner.

A key capability within Arcy is its Roadmap AI, which generates fully personalized learning paths tailored to each user’s goals, skill level, and pace. These roadmaps are not static; they continuously evolve through ongoing voice interactions. Learners can ask questions, refine objectives, request explanations, or pivot focus areas, and Arcy dynamically adjusts the roadmap in real time to reflect these changes.

By combining ElevenLabs for immersive voice interaction, OpenRouter as the primary intelligence and routing backbone, and Kiro for agentic decision-making, Arcy operates as an adaptive, context-aware learning companion. The result is a system that feels less like a tool and more like a personalized mentor—capable of guiding, responding, and evolving alongside the learner throughout their educational journey.

**Top Feedback**

Building our voice assistant genuinely felt smooth and enjoyable largely because of Kiro—it acted like a real thinking partner throughout the project, helping us prototype faster, debug complex flows, and make sense of how all the pieces fit together under tight hackathon timelines. We used OpenRouter as the core intelligence layer to manage our conversational AI and personalized learning roadmap, which gave us great flexibility to work with multiple models cleanly. **Gemini API**

Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite for Content, Quiz Generation, and Context-Aware Voice AI

We integrated Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite as a core model within our Roadmap AI to enable fast, scalable content generation and quiz creation tailored to each learner’s personalized learning path. Based on the roadmap structure, topic progression, and learner objectives, Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite generates structured explanations, learning material, and adaptive assessment questions aligned with the user’s current stage.

For continuous evaluation, Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite dynamically generates quizzes and follow-up questions whose difficulty and scope adjust according to learner performance. This allows the system to reinforce understanding progressively rather than relying on static, one-time assessments.

The generated content, quiz state, and learning context are then passed directly to our voice-based AI assistant, “Arcy,” which also runs on Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite. This ensures that Arcy remains fully context-aware, understanding what the learner has studied, what they are currently working on, and which concepts need clarification.

By running Arcy on Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite, the system achieves low-latency, real-time voice interactions while preserving conversational continuity across roadmap planning, content delivery, and assessment. Arcy can explain concepts, ask targeted questions, clarify doubts, and guide learners verbally in a way that is consistent with the roadmap AI’s outputs.

Overall, using Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite for both structured content generation and real-time conversational guidance enables a cohesive, responsive, and personalized learning experience, where planning, learning, assessment, and voice interaction are tightly integrated.

**The problem it solves**

# AI Threat Detection Project

## Project Description
I developed an **AI-based Threat Detection system** to identify and prevent cyber attacks in real time.  
The main goal of this project is to make existing security systems **smarter, faster, and safer** using Artificial Intelligence.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/80b9b2a72ac147bc8e5d0a31bec18a38/b5af3c9d-f34d-4d3d-ae6a-84d0336a5663.jpeg)

## What problem I am solving
Most traditional systems only check basic rules and fail to detect advanced or unusual attacks.  
They cannot clearly differentiate between a **legitimate user** and a **malicious attacker**.

Because of this:
- Accounts get hacked
- Sensitive data is exposed
- Security response is slow

## What my project does
My project continuously monitors user or system activity such as:
- Login attempts
- Failed authentications
- Location and device behavior
- Access patterns

Using AI models, the system analyzes this data and classifies activity as:
- Normal
- Suspicious
- High-risk threat

Based on the risk level, it triggers alerts or blocks access automatically.


## How this project helps people
- Reduces manual security monitoring
- Detects threats in real time
- Prevents unauthorized access
- Improves overall system security


## How it makes existing systems easier and safer
Instead of relying only on fixed rules, my system:
- Learns normal behavior patterns
- Adapts to new attack methods
- Responds instantly to threats

This reduces human error and increases protection.


## Technologies used
- **Frontend**: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
- **Backend**: FastAPI (Python)
- **AI/ML**: Machine learning models for threat detection
- **Alerts**: Real-time notifications

## Real-world use case
If a user usually logs in from one location and suddenly multiple failed login attempts occur from a different region,  
the system identifies it as a **high-risk threat** and immediately restricts access.

## Conclusion
This project demonstrates how AI can be used to strengthen cybersecurity by detecting threats early and responding automatically, making digital systems more reliable and secure.

**Challenges we ran into**

C

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/80b9b2a72ac147bc8e5d0a31bec18a38/61211184-bf11-440f-87cc-e36f8f0f1452.jpeg)hallenges We Ran Into
1. JavaScript `addEventListener` Null Error
One major issue we faced was the error:
> **Cannot read properties of null (reading 'addEventListener')**

This happened because the JavaScript code was trying to access HTML elements before the page was fully loaded.

**How we fixed it:**
- Ensured the script was loaded at the end of the HTML file  
  **or**
- Wrapped the JavaScript code inside `DOMContentLoaded`

This ensured the elements were available before attaching event listeners.

 2. Connecting Frontend with Backend (FastAPI)
Initially, the frontend could not properly communicate with the FastAPI backend.  
Requests were either failing or not returning responses.

**How we fixed it:**
- Verified API endpoints and request methods
- Enabled CORS in FastAPI
- Used proper JSON request and response formats

This allowed smooth communication between the website and the backend.

3. Handling False Positives in That Detection
At first, the AI model was marking normal login attempts as suspicious due to limited data.

**How we fixed it:**
- Adjusted the threshold values
- Improved feature selection (failed attempts, login frequency, location change)
- Tested with more realistic sample data

This reduced incorrect threat detection.

4. Real-Time Alert Triggering
Alerts were not triggering instantly when a high-risk threat was detected.

**How we fixed it:**
- Optimized the detection logic
- Triggered alerts immediately after risk classification
- Ensured the alert function was called only for high-risk cases

5. Managing Project Structure
As the project grew, files became harder to manage.

**How we fixed it:**
- Organized the project into clear folders:
  - `frontend`
  - `backend`
  - `model`
- Added proper naming conventions and documentation

What We Learned
These challenges helped us understand real-world development issues such as debugging, system integration, and improving AI reliability. Overcoming them made the project more stable, secure, and production-ready.

Our AI Threat Detection project uses ElevenLabs for **real-time voice alerts** when a high-risk threat is detected.  
Instead of only text notifications, the system generates **natural-sounding voice warnings**, helping admins respond faster.  
This improves accessibility, urgency, and real-world usability, aligning with ElevenLabs’ focus on advanced AI voice technology.

**Gemini API**

Our AI Threat Detection project uses Gemini API to intelligently analyze login and security behavior.  
Gemini helps understand patterns, explain why an activity is risky, and improve threat detection accuracy.  
This makes the system smarter than rule-based security and aligns with the Gemini track’s goal of building real-world, AI-powered solutions.

> See what you’re missing. Learn it together.

![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Room Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Room%20Database-333333?style=flat-square) ![Auth0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth0-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Students today face disengaging, unstructured study experiences that limit progress and retention. Existing tools provide only high-level scores, lacking actionable insights into concept-level weaknesses, which leads to inefficient revision and heightened exam stress. Additionally, peer collaboration is fragmented, with no effective way to coordinate, track, or measure joint learning. Our solution delivers a smart, social, and engaging platform that drives consistent study habits, connects
peers around shared learning goals, and offers personalized, concept-level feedback. This approach not only boosts motivation and efficiency but also addresses exam anxiety, positioning us to transform how students prepare and succeed.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Network Bridging: Localhost Disparity

The Challenge: Establishing a unified connection between a physical mobile device, a virtual emulator, and a local development server. Standard localhost (127.0.0.1) references are scoped to the local environment of the specific device, causing connection failures when the mobile app attempts to reach the host server.

The Resolution: I implemented a dynamic environment configuration strategy. By identifying the host machine’s local network IP (e.g., 192.168.x.x) for physical hardware and utilizing the specific Android loopback alias (10.0.2.2) for emulators, I ensured seamless API routing across all endpoints. I automated this process by creating a network utility script that detects the environment and injects the correct gateway address at runtime.

2. High-Stakes Proctoring & Focus Mode Restrictions

The Challenge: Enforcing academic integrity across different environments. The web environment is prone to "tab-hopping," while mobile operating systems (iOS/Android) strictly limit an app's ability to control user behavior outside its own sandbox.

The Resolution:

    Web Environment: I leveraged the Page Visibility API to monitor the visibilityState. Any attempt to switch tabs or minimize the window triggers an automated integrity flag in the proctoring dashboard.

    Mobile Focus Mode: Since mobile OS sandboxing prevents locking the user into an app, I utilized Lifecycle Observers. By monitoring onPause and onStop events, the system detects when a student exits the app and immediately issues a "Focus Lost" alert to the mentor, effectively discouraging unauthorized multitasking through real-time accountability.

**Gemini API**

Gemini API is used to dynamically generate questions adapted to the users' difficulties. The API is also used for our "GURU MODE", which is an attempt to empower the students to teach, learn and evaluate themselves by teaching an AI Agent Powered by Gemini using Feynman's technique.

**Best Use of Auth0**

Social Sign In using google for maximum security and real identification

> Turn Empty Trips into Guaranteed Revenue.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mapbox](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mapbox-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![mongoose](https://img.shields.io/badge/mongoose-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mapbox API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mapbox%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/20d0bfe38c454ba7a356e4d8a3bb216a/78487125-0dee-4ef3-b80d-9334532dd168.png)


**FreightIQ** is a web-platform designed to combat the logistics industry's "deadheading" crisis—where trucks return empty after deliveries, leading to wasted fuel and lost revenue. It serves as a digital bridge between shippers and drivers, using real-time connectivity to ensure vehicles are always moving with a load.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/20d0bfe38c454ba7a356e4d8a3bb216a/b8f43eae-7105-4c24-abbb-828385ccabc9.png)



**Key Utilities:**

* **Guaranteed Revenue:** The platform uses "Smart Matching" to identify and assign return loads to drivers, ensuring that both drivers and shippers retain the full value of the deal and minimize empty miles.
* **Operational Velocity:** By automating the dispatch process and prioritizing urgent loads, FreightIQ reduces idle time and speeds up the entire logistics workflow.
* **Ironclad Security (Digital Handshake):** To solve payment disputes and fraud, the system implements a "Digital Handshake." Shippers and Receivers scan QR codes at pickup and drop-off points to verify identity and instantly release payments, ensuring a trust-free, secure transaction.
* **Strategic Market Intelligence:** The platform provides pricing and demand visibility, empowering fleet owners to make strategic decisions based on data rather than intuition.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Real-Time Transaction Synchronization**
Implementing the "Digital Handshake" feature required instant communication between the driver's app and the shipper's dashboard. When a QR code is scanned, the system needs to update the shipment status immediately to release payments.
* **Solution:** We built a real-time socket architecture using `Socket.io` implementing live status updates (like Pickup or Drop-off) that is pushed instantly to all parties without requiring a page refresh.

**2. Adopting a Next-Gen Tech Stack (Bun & Astro)**
To ensure the platform is lightweight and high-performance, We chose to use **Bun** for the backend runtime and **Astro** for the frontend. While efficient, this newer stack posed integration challenges compared to traditional Node.js setups.
* **Solution:** We leveraged Bun's fast package manager and built-in TypeScript support to streamline development. For the frontend, we also utilized Astro's component architecture to build a highly responsive UI that integrates seamless forms for complex tasks like "Shipment Creation" and "Driver Onboarding".

**3. Complex State Management for Logistics**
Modeling the lifecycle of a shipment—from "Creation" to " acceptance," "Pickup," and "Proof of Delivery"—was complex due to the strict validation required at each step.
* **Solution:** We designed a robust data model in TypeScript that strictly defines the shipment states and user roles (Driver vs. Shipper). This ensures that valid state transitions (e.g., a driver cannot "deliver" a load before "picking it up") are enforced at the API level.

**Requestly**

Requestly fits in as a Backend API testing to verify and check if all server requests are working properly and without any software bugs and exploitation.

> AI-powered garment efficiency insights

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Jinja2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jinja2-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

GarmAI solves the problem of understanding and predicting productivity in garment manufacturing, where performance depends on many factors working together. In real production environments, supervisors and managers often estimate productivity based on experience or manual calculations, which can be inaccurate, time-consuming, and inconsistent. Important issues like high idle time, frequent style changes, or inefficient workforce allocation may not be noticed until productivity drops.

GarmAI makes this easier by using an AI model to analyze all key production inputs at once and predict productivity instantly. Instead of manually checking multiple variables, users can enter daily production details and get a clear productivity score along with a simple classification such as low, medium, or high. This helps managers quickly understand how well a production line is performing.

The application can be used for daily productivity monitoring, production planning, and decision-making. It allows users to test different scenarios, such as reducing idle time or adjusting incentives, and see how those changes might affect productivity before implementing them on the shop floor. By providing quick, data-driven insights, GarmAI reduces manual effort, improves accuracy, and supports better operational decisions in garment factories.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building GarmAI, one of the main challenges was handling data preprocessing consistently between the training phase and the web application. The machine learning model was trained using one-hot encoded categorical variables, and during early testing the app produced incorrect or failed predictions because the input feature order did not exactly match the model’s training features. This was resolved by saving the original feature list during training and reindexing the processed input data to that exact structure before making predictions.

Another major hurdle was managing template errors and layout inheritance in Flask using Jinja2. Issues such as defining the same block multiple times, missing variables like now(), and conflicting template logic caused runtime errors and page crashes. These problems were fixed by carefully organizing the base template, ensuring each block was defined only once, and passing all required variables explicitly from the backend.

Client-side behavior also introduced challenges, especially with form validation and autofill logic. At one point, the prediction form auto-filled values automatically without user interaction, which was not intended. This was corrected by separating autofill logic from page load and triggering it only through a dedicated button click event. Styling modern UI elements such as dropdowns, input focus states, and animated score indicators was another difficulty. Native browser styles caused unwanted white backgrounds and inconsistent behavior across elements. Custom CSS overrides were applied to ensure a consistent dark theme and smooth user experience.

Overall, these challenges helped improve the robustness of the application. By debugging step by step, aligning data pipelines, and refining both backend and frontend logic, the project evolved into a stable, user-friendly, and reliable AI-based productivity prediction system.

> Because you deserve to be Heard!!

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Speech API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Speech%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In today’s fast-moving digital world, many people work, study, and live in isolated environments — often spending long hours behind screens without emotional connection or support.
While virtual assistants exist, most of them feel robotic, emotionless, and disconnected from the user's mental state. They provide answers — but they don’t feel the user’s mood, stress, or energy.

As a result, people increasingly experience loneliness, lack of motivation, burnout, and emotional fatigue — especially students, remote workers, and individuals who spend a lot of time alone.

ROOMii solves this problem by creating an emotionally intelligent AI companion that doesn’t just process commands — it understands how you feel.

Everyone's individual character is saved and ROOMii is as same as YOU!! And the thing is IT changes according to people and people's Situations and Emotions!!

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c0051e54e58e4819addb4626f90d9271/686998fd-8adf-4fef-bbd5-60f755c2f7c3.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

While building ROOMii, I ran into quite a few unexpected challenges that really pushed me to think differently. Getting real-time emotion detection to work smoothly was tough at first — the camera feed kept lagging because the model was analyzing every frame. I fixed it by caching emotions for a few seconds, which made the performance much faster. Synchronizing AI replies with voice output was another struggle; ROOMii would sometimes interrupt itself or speak over previous messages. I restructured the backend so it waits for the AI’s full response before generating audio and added a stop button to instantly cancel playback if the user speaks again. These small details made ROOMii feel more natural and human.

Another major challenge was making the 3D model expressive and responsive. The model initially faced the wrong direction, and those text-style faces like ^_^ looked odd in 3D. I fixed this by reorienting the model, adding glowing eyes that change color with mood, and introducing breathing and idle animations for realism. I also dealt with voice API limits and local audio clutter — ROOMii now auto-deletes old files and falls back to backup voices if an API fails. Balancing AI logic, live emotion tracking, and smooth visuals wasn’t easy, but seeing ROOMii respond calmly, emotionally, and in real time made it all worth it.
We are still in devlopment phase, so accuracy will be increased soonn!!!

### 👩‍🏫 For Teachers

**Challenges we ran into**

### ⚠️ Challenges I Ran Into

- 🧠 **Building without a finalized AI model**  
  Since the project is currently a **prototype with demo data**, designing camera-based attendance without a trained model was challenging.  
  👉 I handled this by creating a **modular design**, so the real model can be plugged in later without changing the full system.

- 🧩 **Designing realistic flows using demo data**  
  Making the app feel real without live institute data required careful planning.  
  👉 I used **mock datasets** that closely represent real classrooms to validate the workflow and user experience.

- 🔐 **Role-based access for three user types**  
  Handling teachers, students, and parents in one system was complex even at the prototype stage.  
  👉 Solved it by clearly separating interfaces and permissions from the beginning.

- 🎮 **Gamification logic without production data**  
  Implementing streaks, coins, and leaderboards without real attendance trends was tricky.  
  👉 I focused on **logical rules and scalable reward systems** that can adapt once real data is available.

- 🚧 **Balancing scope within hackathon time**  
  Building features while keeping it demo-ready was a major hurdle.  
  👉 I prioritized **core functionality and UX**, leaving advanced AI optimization for future versions.

---

These challenges helped me focus on **clean architecture, scalability, and future readiness**, even at the prototype stage.

> Agentic AI Proactive Car Maintenance Feedback

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blender](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Car ownership today is reactive—we wait for a "Check Engine" light or a breakdown before taking action. Even when a warning appears, the cryptic OBD-II codes (like P0217) leave most drivers confused and anxious.

GLYTCH AutoSync transforms vehicle maintenance into a Proactive & Intelligent experience:

- Demystifies Diagnostics: Instantly translates complex engine codes into plain     English voice alerts and actionable advice using AI.

- Predicts the Future: Instead of guessing, our Neural Network analyzes vehicle age, mileage, and history to calculate the exact probability of failure before it happens.

- Automates the Boring Stuff: Detects a critical fault? The system automatically finds an open slot at the service center and books it for you instantly.

- Digital Twin Visibility: A real-time 3D visualization of the car lets users see their vehicle's status at a glance—turning dry data into an immersive command center.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a real-time system that listens, thinks, and predicts simultaneously wasn't easy. Here are the biggest hurdles we overcame:

1. The "Laggy" 3D Twin:

- Hurdle: Rendering a high-quality 3D car model alongside high-frequency WebSocket data updates caused the browser to freeze.

- Solution: We optimized the rendering pipeline by disabling expensive shadow calculations and implementing React.memo to prevent re-rendering the 3D canvas every time the RPM changed.

2. The Overconfident AI:

- Hurdle: Our initial Predictive Maintenance model was too good—it memorized the synthetic data and only outputted 0% or 100% risk, which isn't realistic.

- Solution: We rebuilt the neural network with a "softer" architecture, introducing Dropout layers and reducing neuron count to force the AI to learn general trends rather than hard rules.

- Dependency Hell (Keras vs. Transformers):

- Hurdle: Integrating the latest TensorFlow with HuggingFace transformers caused a version conflict that crashed the backend immediately.

- Solution: We identified the root cause (Keras 3 incompatibility) and implemented the tf-keras legacy bridge to allow both state-of-the-art libraries to coexist peacefully.
