### ORBITGUARD
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/orbitguard-3202) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/shanjaylr-art/ORBITGUARD) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/1cb8cfb7fe2342b6828b3396b831bf01) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> space debris collision avoider

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into
1. CelesTrak geo-blocking (data source failure)
Bug: TLE fetch from CelesTrak returned 403 on our deployment region. Without TLE data, nothing works.

Fix: Built a 3-tier fallback chain: CelesTrak → tle.ivanstanojevic.me API → offline bundled sample data. Added a data_source indicator in the UI so operators always know if they're looking at live or sample data.

2. scipy crash on Python 3.14
Bug: pip install scipy compiled successfully but crashed at import with a missing DLL error specific to Python 3.14.6.

Fix: Pinned scipy==1.16.2 (the last version with prebuilt wheels for 3.14). Two hours lost to diagnosing this — the error message was completely misleading.

3. WinError 10048 — port 8000 already in use
Bug: FastAPI refused to start because uvicorn didn't release the port on crash. Get-NetTCPConnection hung on this machine.

Fix: Used netstat -ano | Select-String ":8000" + taskkill /PID ... /F. Automated this into a one-liner for the dev loop.

4. Port 5173 stuck after Vite crash
Bug: Vite dev server left zombie node.exe processes. New npm run dev silently failed.

Fix: Get-Process node | Stop-Process -Force before every restart. Added to the dev script.

5. Chain-reaction timeout
Bug: The A→B→C→D cascade simulator timed out at 90s when screening 60 objects post-burn against each other.

Fix: Widened the maneuver search grid (step_s: 30, half_window_min: 4.0) and pre-filtered the "others" list to objects within 500km of the burn trajectory. Endpoint dropped from 90s+ to under 5s.

6. Orbital-intelligence agent debate timeout
Bug: The 5-agent hierarchy (Analyst → Physics → Risk → Strategist → Judge) took 18.7s due to redundant Monte Carlo calls.

Fix: Reduced Monte Carlo samples inside the debate from 10,000 to 4,000 (still statistically significant) and cached intermediate results. Down to 6s.

7. RL autopilot first-use delay
Bug: First engage of AI Autonomous Maneuver took 23 seconds (training 4000 Q-learning episodes on the fly).

Fix: Pre-warmed the RL policy at server startup. First engage now takes ~10ms. Training runs once, cached for the session.

8. Dashboard duplication after multi-page restructure
Bug: RiskPanel (Overview page) internally rendered 8 sub-panels that also had their own dedicated dashboard pages — every feature appeared twice.

Fix: Stripped RiskPanel to core stats + explainability + Monte Carlo only. Added 4 missing pages (Traffic Map, RL Spacecraft, Constellation, NLC Advisor) that were orphaned. Final audit: every panel mounts exactly once across 12 dashboard routes.

9. NumPy 2 compatibility (np.ptp removed)
Bug: np.ptp() was deprecated in NumPy 1.25 and removed in 2.0. Our discovery.py used it for feature-range normalization.

Fix: Replaced np.ptp(x) with np.max(x) - np.min(x). One-line fix, but took 20 minutes to find because the traceback was deep in the clustering pipeline.
-deployment error .forgot to read .env file and read api keys .
code latency.

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves
Space is getting crowded. Over 30,000 tracked debris objects orbit Earth, and a single collision creates thousands more fragments (Kessler Syndrome). Current collision-avoidance tools are:

Manual — operators stare at conjunction warning emails and decide "maneuver or wait" by gut feel
Single-object — they check one pair at a time, not the cascade effect across a constellation
Opaque — risk is a red/yellow/green light with no explanation of why
Reactive — you find out about a close approach 12-48 hours before TCA, with limited fuel budget left
ORBITGUARD automates and explains the entire pipeline:

Who	What they get
Satellite operators	Autonomous burn planning that respects fuel, thermal, and power constraints — with a full constraint-agent veto before any command is sent
Space agencies	Fleet-wide optimization: "which of my 50 satellites should burn?" instead of one-off decisions
Insurance / regulators	Explainable AI risk scores with Monte Carlo confidence intervals, not just a number
Researchers	Unsupervised discovery of dangerous orbital highways (DBSCAN + KDE + graph centrality) and chain-reaction simulators
Mission planners	7-day orbital weather forecasts, self-learning memory that remembers past conjunctions, and digital twins that model spacecraft health in real time
In short: it turns a reactive, manual, opaque process into a proactive, autonomous, explainable one — reducing the chance of creating more debris while protecting active assets.

### Arachnid
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/arachnid-ffa7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/crtl-freakssss/ARACHNID) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/NtM4ZZwJ5Co?si=7VHQ2pB_VXo9XY4n) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> Autonomous Search.Human-Saving Precision

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/pytest-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Getting the sensors to work correctly: We had to deal with multiple ultrasonic sensors sharing the same trigger while having separate echo lines, which required careful handling in the ESP32 firmware.
ESP32-to-ESP32 communication: Making the sensor ESP32 communicate reliably with the motor-controller ESP32 through UART took several iterations.
Hardware and software communication: Getting the physical rover to communicate with the ROS2 system and then with our backend was one of the biggest integration challenges.
Real-time sensor data: It wasn't enough for the sensors to work locally—we needed their readings to reach the dashboard reliably and in real time.
Controlling the motors from the dashboard: We had to connect the entire chain from a button/key press on the frontend all the way to the physical motors.
Safety: We needed to make sure that if communication is lost or an emergency stop is pressed, the rover doesn't continue moving accidentally.
Keeping everything synchronized: The frontend, backend, ROS2 layer, ESP32s, sensors, and motor drivers all had to work together without breaking the existing system

**The problem it solves**

Dangerous areas are unsafe for human rescuers
Sends a rover into collapsed, hazardous, or inaccessible areas instead of immediately sending people in.
Finding trapped or missing people is difficult
Uses onboard sensors/cameras and autonomous exploration capabilities to help detect and locate people.
Rescuers lack real-time information
Provides live sensor telemetry, rover status, battery information, and environmental awareness through the dashboard.
Manual rover operation is difficult in complex environments
Provides a centralized control interface with movement controls, mapping, navigation, and exploration functionality.
Poor visibility of the environment
Uses distance sensors and mapping/navigation capabilities to help the operator understand obstacles and surroundings.
Communication failures can make a rover dangerous
Includes connection monitoring, command timeouts, reconnection handling, and fail-safe behavior.
Emergency stopping is critical
Provides a dedicated E-STOP that can immediately stop rover movement.
Search-and-rescue teams need one unified interface
Combines:
Live telemetry
Mapping
Navigation
Exploration
Rover controls
Sensor data
Status/battery
Logs
Emergency stop

**Hardware**

ARACHNID is built as a hardware + software system, where the physical rover collects information and the software turns that information into something the operator can understand and control.
ESP32 #2 handles the sensors — 5 ultrasonic sensors and the ToF sensor collect distance information from the surroundings.
ESP32 #1 handles the motors through the BTS7960 motor drivers and controls the rover's movement.
The two ESP32 boards communicate through UART, allowing sensor/control data to move between the boards.
The hardware connects to the ROS2 layer, which acts as the communication bridge between the physical rover and the application.
The backend receives the real-time hardware data and sends commands to the rover.
The frontend dashboard displays sensor/rover information and allows the operator to control the rover.
A dedicated E-STOP and failsafe system ensures the motors stop when an emergency or communication failure occurs.

Team **Ctrl freaks** -- Nityashree Babu, Shreyas J B, Yagna Sanhit, Shivani Pallath

### ORCA Lite
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/orca-lite-e2b8) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://orca-lite-isro.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ISJAaC98X2k) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co)

> Safe Seas, Clear Decisions

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Coastal fishers often have to make important decisions using information scattered across different systems. PFZ maps may show where fish are likely to be found, but they do not always consider dangerous waves, strong winds, storms, or restricted maritime zones. At the same time, weather and safety alerts are provided separately, making it difficult for fishers to understand the overall risk before going to sea.

ORCA Lite solves this by bringing ocean, weather, satellite, and geospatial data together in one conversational system. It converts complex information into simple, safety-focused fishing and navigation advice in the local language. This helps fishers make better decisions, avoid hazardous waters, and stay within maritime boundaries.

**Challenges we ran into**

A major challenge was ensuring that ORCA Lite never gives unsafe advice in life-threatening situations. Instead of allowing the AI to make safety decisions, we use the LLM only to understand the user's request. A deterministic safety engine then checks official data against fixed safety thresholds, reducing the risk of AI hallucinations.

Another challenge was combining government datasets that use different formats. ORCA Lite uses specialized agents to collect ocean, weather, and boundary data, while a Fusion Engine standardizes this information based on the user's location and time before applying safety rules.

Since fishers may have little or no internet connectivity at sea, ORCA Lite also supports offline fallback data. However, outdated information is never treated as safe. If the cached data is too old, the system clearly shows “INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE” instead of making a guess.

Finally, ORCA Lite follows a strict Safety-First hierarchy: Warning → Geofence → Sea State → PFZ. If a cyclone warning or boundary violation is detected, the system immediately stops further analysis and displays “DO NOT GO”, ensuring that safety always comes before fishing opportunities.

> Smarter Crisis Response with AI

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![The Graph](https://img.shields.io/badge/The%20Graph-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

CrisisFlow AI is an intelligent emergency response platform that helps emergency teams make faster and safer decisions during crises.

It collects information from emergency reports, sensors, weather alerts, field updates, and other sources, then analyzes the incident to identify its type, severity, and escalation risk.

The system prioritizes multiple incidents, recommends the most suitable emergency resources, and calculates efficient routes using real-time road conditions such as traffic and blocked roads.

Instead of requiring operators to manually process large amounts of information, CrisisFlow AI provides a centralized dashboard with live incidents, resource availability, priority levels, recommended actions, routes, and decision explanations.

This helps reduce response delays, improve resource utilization, and support emergency operators in making informed decisions during rapidly changing situations.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges We Ran Into

One of the main challenges was connecting multiple components of the system into a single real-time emergency response workflow.

We had to handle communication between the frontend dashboard and the FastAPI backend while keeping incident data, resource information, priorities, and routing results synchronized.

Another challenge was designing the priority and resource allocation logic so that the system considers more than just distance. Incident severity, escalation risk, resource availability, and suitability also need to be considered.

We also faced deployment challenges while connecting the Vite frontend with the FastAPI backend. We solved this by separating the frontend and backend deployment and configuring the frontend to communicate with the deployed API through an environment variable.

Finally, we had to make the AI recommendations understandable to emergency operators. We addressed this by displaying the reasoning behind recommendations instead of presenting only a final decision.

**The problem it solves**

## 🚨 The Problem It Solves

### 🚌 Public Bus Travel Is Still Too Unpredictable

For millions of people, buses are an important part of everyday transportation. However, the experience of using public buses can often involve **waiting, guessing, and uncertainty**.

A passenger may know that a bus is *supposed* to arrive at a particular time, but they often don't know:

* 📍 Where the bus currently is
* ⏱️ When the bus will actually arrive
* 👥 How crowded the bus is
* 🛣️ Which available route is the best option
* 🔄 Whether changing to another route would save time
* 🚏 When they should get down at their destination
* 🛡️ How to share their journey with someone they trust when travelling alone

Traditional bus information systems are often based on **static routes and timetables**. These provide useful basic information, but they don't always reflect what is happening on the road **right now**.

This creates a simple but important problem:

> **Passengers have information about the bus, but not enough real-time intelligence to make better travel decisions.**

---

## 💡 How YatriGo Solves This

**YatriGo** is designed as an **AI-powered public transportation intelligence platform** that makes everyday bus travel more predictable, informed, and safer.

Instead of only answering:

> **"Which bus goes from A to B?"**

YatriGo aims to answer:

> **"Which bus should I take right now, where is it, when will it arrive, how crowded is it, and how can I travel safely?"**

The platform brings together **route information, live updates, passenger-generated crowd data, intelligent recommendations, and safety features** into one system.

---

## 🎯 What Can People Use YatriGo For?

### 📍 1. Know Where the Bus Is

Passengers don't have to depend only on a fixed timetable.

YatriGo is designed to provide **live bus-location information**, allowing users to understand where their bus currently is and how close it is to their stop.

This helps reduce the uncertainty of standing at a bus stop and wondering:

> *"Has my bus already passed, or is it still coming?"*

---

### ⏱️ 2. Get Better Arrival Estimates

A timetable tells you when a bus is *scheduled* to arrive.

YatriGo focuses on estimating when the bus is **actually likely to arrive**.

The intelligent layer is designed to eventually use information such as:

* 🚌 Current bus location
* 🛣️ Historical travel time
* 🕐 Time of day
* 🚦 Traffic conditions
* 📊 Previous journey patterns

This can make arrival estimates more useful than relying only on static schedules.

> **Goal:** Turn "Bus expected at 8:30" into "Bus is approximately X minutes away."

---

### 👥 3. Understand Bus Crowding

One of YatriGo's key ideas is **crowd intelligence**.

Passengers can provide lightweight reports about the current crowd level of their bus, such as:

* 🟢 Low
* 🟡 Medium
* 🔴 High

Instead of depending on a single passenger's report, the system can combine multiple reports to create a more useful picture of the current crowd situation.

Over time, this information can also become valuable data for developing **crowd prediction models**.

This means the long-term goal isn't only:

> **"How crowded is the bus now?"**

but also:

> **"How crowded is this bus likely to become?"**

---

### 🧭 4. Find a More Suitable Route

Sometimes the fastest route isn't necessarily the best route.

For example, one bus may be slightly faster but extremely crowded, while another may take a few extra minutes but provide a more comfortable journey.

YatriGo is designed to consider multiple factors when recommending routes, including:

* ⏱️ Travel time
* 👥 Crowd level
* 🔄 Number of transfers
* 🚶 Walking distance
* 📈 Route reliability

This allows the platform to move beyond simple route searching toward **intelligent journey recommendations**.

---

### 🚏 5. Avoid Missing Your Stop

When travelling on an unfamiliar route, passengers may not always know exactly when to get off.

YatriGo includes the concept of **stop alerts**, helping passengers know when their destination stop is approaching.

This can be particularly useful for:

* 🧑‍🎓 Students travelling to unfamiliar places
* 🧳 Visitors and tourists
* 🌙 People travelling in unfamiliar areas
* 🚌 Passengers using a new bus route

The goal is simple:

> **Less worrying about the route, more focus on the journey.**

---

### 🛡️ 6. Make Journeys Safer

Transportation isn't only about reaching the destination. **Safety during the journey matters too.**

YatriGo introduces a **Smart Safety Shield** designed around features such as:

* 🆘 SOS support
* 👨‍👩‍👧 Trusted-contact alerts
* 📍 Live trip sharing

This allows passengers to share their journey with someone they trust and provides an additional safety mechanism when travelling alone.

The broader objective is:

> **Secure Every Journey.**

---

### 📶 7. Keep Important Information Available During Poor Connectivity

Internet connectivity isn't guaranteed everywhere.

YatriGo is design

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🛠️ Challenges We Ran Into

Building YatriGo was not only about developing features. One of our biggest learnings was that **real-world transportation data is messy, unpredictable, and constantly changing**.

Here are some of the major challenges we faced while designing and developing the platform and how we approached them.

---

### 1. 📍 Handling Real-Time Location Data

One of the biggest challenges was dealing with bus location data.

In a real transportation environment, GPS data is not always perfectly accurate. A bus may appear slightly away from the actual road, or the location may jump because of GPS noise.

This becomes a problem because YatriGo depends on location information for features such as:

* Live bus tracking
* Estimated arrival time
* Distance from the next stop
* Stop alerts
* Route intelligence

#### 💡 How We Approached It

Instead of blindly trusting every GPS coordinate, our architecture is designed to process location information before using it for important decisions.

A future improvement we identified is **map matching**, where the GPS position is matched to the actual bus route.

This allows the system to understand:

> "The GPS says the bus is here, but which point on the actual bus route does that correspond to?"

This can make location-based features much more reliable.

---

### 2. 👥 Getting Reliable Crowd Data

Crowd information is one of YatriGo's most useful features, but it also creates an interesting problem:

> **How do we know whether a passenger's crowd report is accurate?**

For example, one passenger might report:

> "Low crowd"

while another passenger on the same bus might report:

> "High crowd"

There can be many reasons for this difference. They may be standing in different parts of the bus, or they may have different opinions about what "crowded" means.

#### 💡 How We Approached It

We decided that the system should **not depend on a single report**.

Instead, YatriGo can combine multiple reports and calculate an overall crowd estimate.

Our planned improvement is also to introduce a **user reputation or confidence score**.

Users who consistently provide reliable reports can have their reports given more weight.

So instead of:

**One user → One truth**

we move toward:

**Multiple users → Aggregated information → Confidence-based result**

This makes the system more resistant to incorrect or misleading reports.

---

### 3. 🐣 The Cold-Start Problem

This was one of the biggest conceptual challenges we identified.

YatriGo becomes more useful when more people use it because more users generate more transportation data.

But there is a problem:

> If there are not enough users, there isn't enough data.

And if there isn't enough useful data, new users may not find the platform valuable.

This creates a cycle:

**Few users → Less data → Less useful information → Fewer users**

#### 💡 How We Plan to Solve It

Our approach is to start small instead of trying to cover an entire city immediately.

We can initially focus on communities such as:

* Colleges
* Campuses
* Local commuter groups
* Frequent bus users

We also plan to introduce **gamification**.

For example, users could receive:

* Points
* Badges
* Contribution scores
* Recognition for useful reports

The idea is to encourage passengers to contribute small pieces of information that collectively become valuable transportation intelligence.

Our target feedback loop is:

**More Users → More Data → Better Intelligence → Better Experience → More Users**

---

### 4. ⚡ Handling Real-Time Updates

Another challenge was deciding how to deliver constantly changing bus information to users.

Bus locations and estimated arrival times can change frequently.

If the application only requests new information every few minutes, the user may see outdated data.

At the same time, continuously making new requests from every user can put unnecessary load on the server.

#### 💡 How We Approached It

For our real-time communication layer, we use **Server-Sent Events (SSE)**.

The basic idea is:

**Server → continuously sends updates → User's browser**

So when new information becomes available, the server can push it to the client instead of making the client repeatedly ask:

> "Anything new?"

This gives us a simpler way to provide live updates for things such as:

* Bus position
* ETA changes
* Crowd information
* Other journey updates

---

### 5. 📱 Battery Usage

Location-based applications can consume a lot of battery if they continuously request high-frequency GPS updates.

This is especially important for YatriGo because we don't want a passenger to gain better bus tracking but lose a significant amount of phone battery in the process.

#### 💡 How We Approached It

Our planned approach is **adaptive GPS sampling**.

Instead of requesting location information at maximum frequency all the time, the system can adjust how often it needs location updates.

For example:

* When movement is important → high

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges we ran into

One of the main challenges we faced while building Sancharam was bringing different travel-related requirements together into a single, simple user experience. Travel information can come from different sources and may vary in format, making it difficult to organize everything in a way that is easy for users to understand.

Another challenge was designing the application so that users could explore destinations without feeling overwhelmed by too much information. We had to carefully structure the interface and prioritize the most useful information.

We also faced challenges while integrating and testing different parts of the application. Some features did not work as expected during development, which required us to debug the implementation, identify the source of the issue, and test the solution multiple times.

We overcame these challenges by breaking the project into smaller modules, testing each feature individually, and continuously improving the user interface based on what worked best. This helped us build a more reliable and user-friendly travel experience while also improving our understanding of real-world application development.

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

Sancharam makes travel planning easier by bringing important travel information into one convenient platform. Instead of depending on multiple websites, social media posts, or scattered information, users can use the platform to discover destinations, explore places of interest, and plan their trips more efficiently.

It helps travellers make better-informed decisions by providing relevant information about destinations and making the overall travel-planning process simpler and more organized. This is especially useful for people who are travelling to an unfamiliar place and want to understand what they can explore before making their plans.

The platform aims to reduce the time and effort spent searching for travel information and provide a smoother experience from discovering a destination to planning a trip. It can also make travel more accessible to users who may not have extensive experience with trip planning.

Overall, Sancharam transforms travel planning from a fragmented process into a more convenient and user-friendly experience, helping people explore destinations with greater confidence.

> AI-powered, germ-free spatial kiosk software built

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mediapipe](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mediapipe-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Public touchscreens at fast-food restaurants, hospitals, and airports are major hygiene hazards, accumulating bacteria and germs from thousands of daily users. Upgrading them usually requires expensive infrared touchless hardware. TouchlessOS solves this by transforming standard monitors and webcams into touchless spatial interfaces using pure software, making public ordering safer, cleaner, and completely germ-free.

**Challenges we ran into**

During real-world user testing in high-traffic environments, we encountered the "crowd interference" challenge—where stray hand movements or background motion in public spaces could momentarily distract the vision tracking model. To solve this for production, we upgraded our model logic by restricting tracking to a strict single-hand session (maxNumHands: 1) and raising the confidence thresholds (minDetectionConfidence: 0.75) to filter out background noise, ensuring the spatial cursor locks only onto the active user.

Job seekers often struggle with resume feedback—traditional ATS tools are either locked behind paywalls, slow, or give generic advice. 

**Smart Resume Builder (SRB)** solves this by providing instant, zero-friction resume analysis without tedious account creation:

- **Constructive Roasts & Strengths:** Highlights weak phrasing, buzzwords, and vague descriptions alongside top resume strengths.
- **Action-Driven STAR Rewrites:** Automatically suggests high-impact, bullet point rewrites using action verbs and measurable metrics with one-click copy.
- **Universal Document Support:** Seamlessly parses PDF, DOCX, and raw text files up to 100MB.

### ARIA
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aria-fd2d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ankith-ux/ARIA) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/-8zRZk0RHbk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PEC%20HACKS%204.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pec-hacks.devfolio.co)

> Autonomous Research Intelligence Agent

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### **The problem it solves / What it does**

The modern academic research lifecycle is highly fragmented, manual, and prone to costly feedback loops. Researchers currently lose significant time switching between disconnected tools to discover literature, manually hand-code complex architectures, and wait months for peer review feedback only to face rejection over fundamental objections[cite: 1]. 

**ARIA (Autonomous Research Intelligence Agent)** solves this by providing a unified, closed-loop AI operating system that assists researchers through all three phases of the research lifecycle[cite: 1]:

#### 1. The Literature Scout & Interactive Chatbot (Explore)
Finding relevant literature and synthesizing it is traditionally a tedious process. 
* **Automated Paper Scouting:** ARIA features a paper scouter that integrates with the Semantic Scholar API and arXiv to automatically fetch relevant academic papers based on user queries[cite: 1].
* **Interactive Knowledge Chatbot:** Researchers can use an interactive chatbot to converse directly about the papers fetched from the keywords entered, instantly extracting insights and analyzing related work without manual reading[cite: 1]. 

#### 2. The Voice-Driven Architecture Co-Designer (Build)
Designing complex neural network topologies (like eDNA encoders) is traditionally a complex and manual process[cite: 2]. ARIA acts as a dynamic, voice-driven AI architecture builder (similar to "Friday" from Marvel) that automates design, multi-faceted validation, and code generation[cite: 2]:
* **Eliminates Manual Drafting:** Instead of hand-coding initial structures, users can simply speak their requirements, and the voice-driven Speech-to-Text (STT) system immediately passes the prompt to an Architect LLM to generate a valid structural blueprint[cite: 2].
* **Automates Deep Stress-Testing:** It prevents fundamental architectural flaws early through a multi-agent orchestration engine[cite: 2]. Designs are pushed through a Phase 1 "Quick Review" (Engineer, Feasibility, Skeptic agents) to catch immediate bottlenecks, followed by a Phase 2 "Deep Critique" where specialists (Physicist, Statistician, Optimizer) engage in a simulated debate to reach a Pareto Synthesis verdict[cite: 2].
* **Bridges the Gap Between Theory and Execution:** It dynamically visualizes the proposed neural network blocks (e.g., Attention, MLP) in an interactive component tree and simultaneously compiles the JSON blueprint into executable PyTorch `nn.Module` code on the fly[cite: 2].
* **Intuitive Feedback Loop:** It leverages ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech (TTS) using custom voice personas so researchers can listen to real-time, synthesized verdicts from the debate panel, making the architectural review process highly interactive[cite: 2].

#### 3. The AI Peer Review Engine (Review)
Months of research can be derailed by minor flaws discovered late in the actual peer review process. ARIA acts as a rigorous pre-submission auditor to bulletproof manuscripts:
* **Automated Scoring & Auditing:** The paper reviewer engine analyzes uploaded manuscripts and systematically scores various fields and academic aspects before the paper goes out for actual peer review[cite: 1].
* **Multi-Persona Debate Resolution:** It identifies potential weaknesses and minor flaws that could lead to rejection, utilizing AI agents to debate conflicting arguments and arrive at a synthesized score conclusion[cite: 1].
* **Actionable Improvements:** Rather than just acting as a gatekeeper, it provides concrete suggestions and improvements (including LaTeX diff patches), ensuring the manuscript is optimized to survive human peer review[cite: 1].

---

### **Conclusion**
By combining intelligent literature discovery, voice-driven architecture validation, and rigorous pre-submission peer review into a single platform, **ARIA eliminates manual bottlenecks and drastically compresses the research revision cycle**[cite: 1, 2]. It empowers researchers to build mathematically sound architectures faster, back them with solid literature, and submit flawless papers with confidence.

**Challenges we ran into**

### **Challenges we ran into**

Building a unified, multi-agent research operating system from scratch meant bridging the gap between several cutting-edge technologies. Orchestrating parallel LLM agents, maintaining stateful memory, and executing real-time voice synthesis introduced a host of unique hurdles:

**1. Real-Time "Thala" Voice Latency & Asynchronous Debates**
Our Voice-Driven Architecture Builder is designed to feel like a real-time conversation. However, chaining Speech-to-Text (STT), passing the prompt to the Architect LLM, running a multi-agent LangGraph workflow, and streaming the final verdict through the ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech (TTS) API created massive response latency[cite: 2]. To solve this, we decoupled the pipeline: we implemented a "Phase 1 Quick Review" that streams immediate verbal feedback while the heavy "Phase 2 Deep Critique" debate among specialist agents runs asynchronously in the background[cite: 2].

**2. Resolving Multi-Persona Hallucinations and Conflicts**
In our Paper Reviewer engine, we fan out manuscript evaluations to 6 parallel persona agents (Claims Auditor, Rigor Agent, Theorist, etc.)[cite: 1]. We quickly discovered that these agents would frequently disagree—for instance, the Theorist might approve a mathematical proof while another agent heavily penalized the feasibility of the same equation[cite: 1, 2]. To prevent contradictory feedback, we engineered a custom `DebateFlagsTool`[cite: 1]. This acts as a consensus protocol, forcing conflicting agents to resolve their differences in an arbitration round to reach a synthesized score before generating the final review letter[cite: 1].

**3. Multimodal PDF Ingestion and LaTeX Corruption**
For the Paper Scouter and Reviewer modules to understand academic papers, standard text extraction on two-column IEEE formats caused text to interleave, scrambling complex mathematical equations, tables, and citation structures[cite: 1]. Standard LLMs hallucinated fixes over this corrupted data[cite: 1]. We overcame this by building a multimodal ingestion pipeline that passes raw PDF binaries directly into Gemini, reconstructing the document into clean, semantic LaTeX so agents could evaluate the actual math and structure accurately.

**4. The Gemini API Key Migration (`AQ.` Prefix Validation Failure)**
When configuring our core reasoning models via the Gemini API, we hit an immediate authentication roadblock. Newly generated Gemini API keys started with an `AQ.` prefix rather than the traditional format. Our environment variables, existing SDK wrappers, and internal regex validators immediately flagged the key as a malformed or invalid string, completely blocking our API calls. We had to override the legacy regex validation layers in our codebase and manually configure the authorization headers to get the LLMs online.

---

### **Conclusion**
Overcoming these hurdles transformed ARIA from a collection of isolated API calls into a resilient, stateful AI operating system. Navigating API key format anomalies, managing real-time voice streaming latency, and engineering multi-agent consensus protocols ultimately resulted in a significantly more robust, production-ready hackathon submission.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

How we used it: We utilized the Google Gemini API as the core cognitive engine powering our multi-agent LangGraph orchestration. Because designing neural networks requires both vast domain knowledge and precise code generation, we divided Gemini's intelligence into three distinct, specialized agent roles:

1. The Research Paper Searcher (Theorists & Skeptics) To ensure our architectures are mathematically sound and physically viable, we mapped Gemini to specialized "Theorist" and "Skeptic" personas. These agents leverage Gemini's massive context window and reasoning capabilities to cross-reference the user's request against state-of-the-art research paradigms (like Attention mechanisms or Positional Embeddings), ensuring the proposed topology isn't just valid code, but actually makes sense from a deep learning research perspective.

2. The Builder (The Architect) We used Gemini as the primary Architect. When a user provides a high-level goal via speech or text, the Builder agent instantly parses the requirements and translates them into a highly structured JSON blueprint. Gemini's strong coding capabilities allow it to take abstract concepts and autonomously generate the correct, executable PyTorch nn.Module code on the fly, dynamically visualizing the component tree for the user. Its also the core Brain behind 7 agents running to test the architecture

3. The Reviewer Gemini is the core behind converting files to usage LaTex format

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

How we used it: We leveraged ElevenLabs (eleven_turbo_v2_5) to transform our multi-agent architecture from a static text interface into an immersive, real-time auditory experience. Instead of forcing the user to read through dense walls of text generated by multiple AI agents, we used ElevenLabs' ultra-low latency streaming TTS and STT to give our system a voice. We mapped custom voice personas to our specific AI agents using their Voice cloning platform to ensuring that when our system's narrator ("Thala(Dhoni)") reads out the final architectural verdict or explains a complex neural network topology, it sounds dynamic, natural, and distinctly authoritative. This audio-first feedback loop makes iterating on complex ML blueprints feel like a real conversation.

**Track Commons AI**

We used Trace Commons to transparently verify our AI-driven development process. Since ARIA relies heavily on complex agentic workflows, it was important to prove how we built it. We integrated the Trace Commons Contributor CLI to discover, locally redact, and securely submit the agent sessions (such as those from Claude Code and Gemini) that were used to plan, debug, and iterate on our codebase. By doing so, we generated a cryptographically signed JWT Attestation Token that serves as verifiable proof of our collaboration with AI agents. Furthermore, Trace Commons' local scrubbing ensured that all our API keys and sensitive project data were completely protected and stripped out before any telemetry left our local machines.

**Best Use of Actian Vector Database**

### Actian VectorAI: The Semantic Memory of ARIA

**1. Role in the Pipeline**
Actian VectorAI powers our Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine. Our SCHOLAR agent fetches academic papers, converts their abstracts into mathematical embeddings (using SentenceTransformers), and stores them as vectors. When a user queries a topic, Actian performs a rapid Cosine Distance search (`client.points.search()`) to fetch the most contextually relevant papers.

**2. Why It's Critical**
Without a vector database, we would have to rely on flawed keyword matching or overwhelm our LLM's context window by feeding it every paper at once. Actian acts as our system's "semantic memory." It instantly isolates only the top 5 most relevant abstracts to feed into Gemini 3.6 Flash, ensuring highly accurate and hallucination-free synthesis.

**3. Why It's the Perfect Fit**
- **Blazing Fast Similarity Search:** Highly optimized for vector operations, retrieving relevant abstracts in milliseconds before LLM handoff.
- **Massive Scalability:** Easily handles scaling from dozens of papers to indexes of millions without choking.
- **Developer Velocity:** Quick local deployment via Docker paired with a clean, intuitive Python SDK made it the perfect, frictionless solution for rapid hackathon iteration.

### NeuroLearn AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/neuro-learn-94cf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/renu7483/Neuro-Learn.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PEC%20HACKS%204.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pec-hacks.devfolio.co)

> Beyond Scores, Towards Understanding

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

NeuroLearn solves the problem of one-size-fits-all learning by identifying what each student is struggling with and providing personalized support.

Students often receive the same questions and learning materials regardless of their individual misconceptions or performance. NeuroLearn uses a Rule Engine to identify learning gaps, creates a student learning profile, and uses an Adaptive Learning Strategy to decide what the student needs next.

Students can also upload large learning materials, which are processed using RAG, chunking, embeddings, and Actian VectorAI DB. The system retrieves only the most relevant content and uses Gemini to provide grounded explanations and personalized practice questions.

For teachers, NeuroLearn provides misconception insights, student progress analytics, and targeted MCQ generation, helping them identify learning gaps and create more effective assessments.

In short: NeuroLearn turns assessment results into a continuous cycle of diagnosis → personalization → remediation → practice → re-evaluation, making learning more personalized for students and more actionable for teachers.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest challenges was handling large learning materials efficiently. Initially, the PDF upload limits were too restrictive, and sending complete documents to an AI model would be slow and expensive.

We solved this by building a RAG pipeline with page-wise extraction, structure-aware chunking, embeddings, and Actian VectorAI DB. Instead of sending the entire PDF to Gemini, we retrieve only the most relevant Top-K chunks using student_id and document_id metadata filtering.

Another challenge was maintaining student-specific learning data securely. We added student and document ownership checks at both the API and vector-retrieval levels so that one student cannot retrieve another student's learning material.

We also faced challenges in keeping the system personalized without making diagnosis dependent on AI guesses. We therefore kept the Rule Engine as the deterministic authority for misconception diagnosis and learning decisions, while using Gemini mainly for grounded explanations and question generation.

Finally, we tested the system extensively for offline failures, duplicate questions, large-file boundaries, and backward compatibility, resulting in 190/190 automated tests passing.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

NeuroLearn uses the Gemini API as the intelligent generation layer of our adaptive learning platform. After the Rule Engine identifies a student's misconceptions and learning needs, NeuroLearn retrieves only the most relevant content from the student's uploaded materials using RAG, chunking, embeddings, Actian VectorAI, metadata filtering, and Top-K retrieval. Gemini then uses this grounded context to generate personalized explanations, worked examples, hints, and practice MCQs.

This makes Gemini useful beyond simple chatbot responses: it adapts the generated learning content to each student's diagnosed misconception and difficulty level while grounding answers in their own study materials. Gemini also supports teachers by generating targeted MCQs based on topic, learning objective, misconception, and difficulty.

The Rule Engine remains responsible for diagnosis, mastery, and learning decisions, while Gemini focuses on high-quality, personalized educational content generation. This combination makes the system more explainable, reliable, and useful for both students and teachers.

**Best Use of Actian Vector Database**

NeuroLearn uses Actian VectorAI DB as the semantic retrieval layer for its personalized learning system. Students can upload large learning materials, which are processed through page-wise extraction → structure-aware chunking → embeddings → Actian VectorAI DB.

When a student asks a question, NeuroLearn does not send the entire PDF to Gemini. Instead, Actian VectorAI performs fast semantic Top-K retrieval and returns only the most relevant educational chunks. We also apply metadata filtering using student_id and document_id, ensuring that students can retrieve only their own learning materials.

The retrieved evidence is then passed to Gemini to generate grounded explanations, worked examples, and personalized MCQs with page/section citations.

This makes Actian VectorAI especially valuable for large educational documents, fast semantic search, personalized RAG, and secure multi-student isolation, while reducing the amount of data sent to the LLM.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MySQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ollama](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ollama-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### 🧠 1. Vision Model Output Parsing & Edge Latency
* **The Hurdle**: Running multimodal vision models (`llava:7b`) for plant disease analysis presented high response latencies and non-deterministic JSON formatting (e.g., models outputting markdown wrappers or `<think>` tags instead of strict JSON).
* **The Solution**: We engineered a robust 3-tiered response extraction pipeline with regex fallbacks (`extractJSON`) to sanitize LLM outputs. Additionally, we implemented a zero-downtime offline fallback engine (`plantHealthFallback.js`) to guarantee instantaneous, non-blocking UI feedback.

### 🛰️ 2. Fusing Geospatial & Environmental Data Streams
* **The Hurdle**: Normalizing multi-source datasets (SoilGrids v2, Open-Meteo microclimate telemetry, and satellite NDVI indices) into a single, cohesive prompt context for LLM reasoning without exceeding token limits.
* **The Solution**: Built a lightweight context compressor (`fieldContext.js`) and unified PHP `AIOrchestrator` engine that aggregates raw telemetry into concise token representations before feeding the AI prompt pipeline.

### 🎨 3. Maintaining High-FPS Spatial UI with Ambient Motion
* **The Hurdle**: Combining dynamic background video loops with complex glassmorphic UI elements and live map layers caused GPU rendering lag on low-power devices.
* **The Solution**: Built an optimized HTML5 Canvas engine (*Living Firefly Field Emerald Swarm*) leveraging `requestAnimationFrame` and CSS hardware acceleration, maintaining a smooth 60 FPS spatial visual experience.

**The problem it solves**

🌾 The Problem
Smallholder farmers in climate-vulnerable regions face two severe structural crises:
1. **Uncertain Crop Health & Delayed Advisory**: Lacking immediate access to agricultural experts, farmers struggle to identify plant diseases early, leading to crop losses up to 40% annually.
2. **Opaque & Delayed Crop Insurance Claims**: Traditional crop insurance validation (e.g., PMFBY) requires tedious manual field inspections, taking months to process payouts during critical drought or flood distress.

---

### 🚀 What People Can Use AgriVision For

**1. AI-Driven Field Digital Twin & GIS Mapping**
* **Geo-Fenced Plot Intelligence**: Farmers and agronomists can map interactive polygon farm boundaries to track real-time soil chemistry (SoilGrids API), moisture index, and hyper-local microclimates.

**2. Instant Multimodal Plant Disease Diagnosis**
* **Snap & Diagnose**: Farmers snap a photo of damaged leaves/crops. Our vision AI instantly identifies crop species, diagnoses diseases, rates severity levels, and prescribes localized organic & chemical remedies in 6 regional languages (*Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Kannada, English*).

**3. Automated Parametric Crop Insurance Engine (FarmClaim)**
* **Objective Loss Settlement**: Insurers and field officers can generate automated loss assessments. Our parametric algorithm fuses satellite-derived NDVI vegetation health (55% weight), rainfall deficits (30%), and heat stress (15%) to validate claim payouts in seconds instead of months.

**4. Context-Aware Advisory & Market Intelligence**
* **Krishi Saarthi AI Companion**: An AI advisor powered by field context (current weather, soil type, crop stage) that delivers tailored farming bullet-points, crop rotation suggestions, and real-time mandi price trends.

**Best Use of Render**

AI & Machine Learning Track / Sustainability & Climate-Tech / Open Innovation

### FinGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finguard-b0ac) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Black-and-Yellow/finguard.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PEC%20HACKS%204.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pec-hacks.devfolio.co)

> Financial Bodyguard

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

UPI is instant and irreversible. That's the whole problem.

India lost ₹22,495 crore to cyber fraud in 2025. UPI scams alone took ₹1,750 crore in FY 2025-26, up 31%. By the time someone realises they've been tricked, the money has already moved through several mule accounts across state lines.

Every safety feature that exists today fires after you've paid. FinGuard is a pre-authorisation safety layer — it reads the payment request before any UPI app opens.

What people actually use it for:

Before paying a stranger. A seller sends a UPI ID over WhatsApp. Paste it into FinGuard and see whether the network has ever met that address, how long it's been known, and what the address itself gives away — before you deal with them.
When someone is on the phone telling you to pay. FinGuard notices a call is in progress and that AnyDesk is installed, and treats that pairing as the digital-arrest setup it is.
When you're told money is coming to you. Say "I was promised a refund" and FinGuard checks that belief against what the request actually does. If the request debits you, it says STOP — this request sends money above everything else.
When a QR claims to be a bank. sbi-refund@okaxis grades D on address structure alone, with no history required.
After the money is gone. A prepared incident report, the cybercrime portal, the 1930 helpline, and a first-hour countdown — because the golden hour decides recovery.
What makes it different: most such tools claim to "block fraud." FinGuard states exactly what it can and cannot see. No bank connection. No NPCI access. It cannot block or reverse anything. It publishes its entire scoring policy and says outright that the numbers are deterministic intervention values, not statistically calibrated

**Challenges we ran into**

# The CIBIL problem — a score with no data to score
The judges asked for a credit-score equivalent for a UPI ID. NPCI publishes nothing per-address, so the literal version is impossible for anyone outside a bank.
The breakthrough was realising CIBIL isn't a regulator reading the banking system — it's a bureau holding what its members contribute. That construction is copyable. Our network is the membership; every safety check is one contributed observation.But a bureau with no members reports nothing, so we added a fifth pillar that needs no network at all: the address text itself. That's 30 of 100 points available on an address nobody has ever checked — which is why a judge can invent a scam address on stage and get a D from an empty database.

# Our warning kept changing its mind
We built a feature to spot suspicious payment addresses. It worked — but then we noticed an honest seller got flagged on the second check and cleared on the third. Same address, different answer.
The reason was that checking an address adds to its record, so we were partly reacting to our own checks. We made the rule stricter so a single check can't tip the result, and wrote a test that checks the same address ten times in a row and fails if the answer ever changes.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

to use the help of gemini api to explain to common people about the risk of the fraud payments they are about to do

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

From the research earlier in this build:

Only 22% of Indian seniors fully understand UPI; 68% are afraid of scams
Cybercrime against seniors rose 86% in two years
Digital-arrest scams work by keeping the victim on a call for hours
Right now FinGuard's verdict is English text on a screen. A panicking 70-year-old, mid-scam-call, will not read a signal breakdown.

**Best Use of Vultr**

Everything runs on our laptop. That means:

The APK has the API URL compiled in, so every network change forces a rebuild
Venue Wi-Fi changes your IP → demo dies
You cannot demo the network effect, which is your strongest moment — three judges scanning the same QR and watching REACH tick up needs one shared server, not localhost
Release builds refuse plain HTTP by design, so you can only ever ship a debug APK

> Context Aware AI Travel Orchestration System

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced while building Journey360 was making AI-generated travel information reliable enough for real-world usage. Although LLMs are powerful at reasoning and generating itineraries, they can sometimes produce incomplete or malformed outputs. To overcome this, we implemented structured validation and a stack-based JSON repair mechanism that detects incomplete structures, repairs them, and validates the final response before it is used by the application.

Another major challenge was dealing with inconsistent or incorrect location data from external APIs and AI-generated results. An incorrect coordinate could potentially direct a traveler to the wrong location. We addressed this by implementing a multi-level geocoding fallback mechanism along with a post-generation coordinate verification process, ensuring that locations are validated before being used for navigation and itinerary generation.

Budget reliability was another important hurdle. We realized that allowing an AI model to directly calculate the final travel cost could result in inaccurate totals. Therefore, we separated AI reasoning from financial computation. The AI can recommend activities and reason about travel options, while the final cost is calculated deterministically from itemized expenses, making the budget more dependable.

We also faced challenges with external API failures, rate limits and temporary service interruptions because Journey360 depends on multiple real-time travel data sources. To make the application resilient, we introduced caching, retry mechanisms with exponential backoff and a multi-model fallback strategy. This ensures that a temporary failure in one service does not unnecessarily interrupt the entire travel experience.

The most important challenge was not simply collecting information, but making information from different sources work together as one coherent travel decision. Weather, local news, safety alerts, maps, places, budgets, user preferences and itineraries all provide different pieces of information. We addressed this by building Journey360 around a shared travel context, allowing the system to combine validated real-time information with the traveler's personal journey before generating recommendations.

Our biggest learning was that building reliable AI is not just about using a powerful model. It is about engineering everything around the model—validation, grounding, deterministic computation, error recovery and intelligent fallbacks—so that AI can be trusted in real-world situations.

**The problem it solves**

Travelers today have access to countless apps for navigation, weather, news, budgeting, translation and trip planning, but these services are often fragmented. When conditions change, travelers must manually connect information from different sources and decide what to do next—creating confusion, wasted time and avoidable safety risks, especially in unfamiliar cities.

Journey360, aligned with SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities, addresses this gap by creating an intelligent, context-aware travel companion that brings critical travel information together and helps travelers make better decisions throughout their journey.

The platform combines AI-powered itinerary planning, real-time safety alerts, local news and alerts, weather conditions, route and navigation assistance, budget awareness, local recommendations, multilingual assistance and adaptive itinerary management. Instead of simply displaying information, Journey360 uses the traveler's location, itinerary, preferences, budget and real-world conditions to understand how a change may affect the journey and recommend an appropriate action.

Its Journey Impact Analyzer further enables travelers to ask “What if?” before changing their plans—such as “What if I leave two hours late?”, “What if I add another destination?” or “What if the weather changes?” The system evaluates the potential impact on time, cost, route, safety and existing activities, helping users understand trade-offs before making a decision.

By bringing these capabilities together, Journey360 aims to make urban travel safer, more accessible, better informed and more resilient, while reducing the need for travelers to constantly switch between disconnected applications.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/af0bf0a781f04be093b572fa14545f54/974ef6d5-a24c-428a-abac-4297926c84a2.png)

**Best Use of Actian Vector Database**

Journey360 uses Actian VectorAI DB as a core intelligence layer rather than as a secondary data store. We use 384-dimensional vector embeddings and cosine similarity to transform unstructured travel intent into meaningful semantic results. User queries such as “misty tea estates with hiking and serene lakes” are converted into embeddings and matched against our indexed destination data to power semantic discovery. More importantly, every AI-generated itinerary can be embedded and indexed in our trips_index and itinerary_places collections, allowing Journey360's RAG-based travel assistant to retrieve relevant past itineraries, places and local context when making recommendations. We also apply vector similarity to our Scam Radar, where submitted fare feedback is semantically matched with existing transit routes to support local price calibration. Thus, Actian VectorAI DB is not simply storing vectors—it connects semantic search, RAG, personalization and community intelligence into a unified travel intelligence layer. This enables Journey360 to move beyond keyword-based travel search toward context-aware, continuously improving travel recommendations.

Problem It Solves

Many women face difficulties accessing sanitary pads due to limited availability, distance, affordability, and social stigma. At the same time, plastic waste is often improperly discarded and remains underutilized.

The collected plastic can further support sustainable, women-led reuse and recycling initiatives, helping create a circular and potentially self-sustaining model.

Nizhali ultimately aims to improve menstrual hygiene accessibility, promote responsible plastic waste management, and empower rural women through technology and sustainable livelihood opportunities.

**Best Use of Actian Vector Database**

Actian VectorAI aligns directly with the Nizhali Reverse Vending Machine (RVM) architecture by acting as a high-speed, local-first "memory bank" for real-time visual classification. Instead of relying on static, monolithic object-detection models that require hours of GPU retraining whenever new product packaging or bottle brands are introduced, Nizhali offloads semantic recognition directly to Actian VectorAI. Raw camera frames are converted on the fly into 512-dimensional OpenAI CLIP embeddings, allowing Actian to execute Cosine Nearest-Neighbor ($K$-NN) similarity searches over gRPC in under 20 milliseconds. Operating as a lightweight Docker container, Actian VectorAI enables instant multi-modal retrieval across normalized image and text space directly on edge hardware. This empowers Nizhali to ingest new waste items dynamically without model retraining, validating waste types and triggering automated eco-token dispense actions with minimal latency.

> Your goals. Your plan. Smarter investing.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

Building the platform involved several technical challenges as we evolved it from a basic fund-listing application into a **data-driven, goal-based recommendation system**.

### 1. From Alphabetical to Meaningful Recommendations

The initial system returned funds alphabetically. We introduced a **peer-relative scoring engine** that ranks funds using measurable performance and risk metrics.

### 2. Building a Reliable Scoring System

Fund quality is evaluated using multiple metrics, including **CAGR, volatility, maximum drawdown, Sharpe, Sortino, benchmark performance, and consistency**. Missing data is handled through dynamic weight adjustment.

### 3. Separating Score from Data Confidence

We separated **recommendation score** from **data confidence**, ensuring funds with insufficient or unreliable data do not receive misleading recommendations.

### 4. Benchmark Integration

Implementing **Alpha, Beta, R², and rolling consistency** required integrating benchmark data, category mappings, historical observations, and date alignment.

### 5. Tax-Aware Planning

Tax considerations were integrated without allowing tax benefits to distort fund-quality rankings. The system considers factors such as **ELSS, Section 80C, investment horizon, liquidity, and risk**.

### 6. Making Recommendations Interactive

Instead of immediately producing a final allocation, the system is designed to let users **review their strategy and consider alternatives** such as increasing investment, extending the horizon, or adjusting risk.

### 7. Reliable Data Synchronization

We implemented **scheduled data refreshes, database-backed locking, and sync-status tracking** to prevent duplicate synchronization and monitor ingestion failures.

### 8. Testing and Stability

We encountered test-isolation issues caused by shared refresh state. These were resolved with explicit state-reset mechanisms and test fixtures.

### 9. Preserving Existing Functionality

The new recommendation, scoring, tax, and strategy layers were added **modularly without breaking the existing application**, with the full test suite passing after integration.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Choosing the right mutual fund is often confusing because a fund with high historical returns is not necessarily the right choice for a particular financial goal. Users need to consider their goal, investment horizon, risk tolerance, required investment, tax considerations, and the quality of the underlying fund data—all at the same time.

Our platform solves this by turning mutual fund selection into a goal-based, data-driven, and personalized investment planning process.

Users can:

Define a financial goal and target amount.
Specify their investment horizon, risk level, and investment capacity.
Check whether their goal is realistically achievable.
Explore suitable investment strategies and asset allocations.
Understand potential tax-optimization opportunities before finalizing the strategy.
Compare mutual funds using quantitative metrics such as CAGR, volatility, maximum drawdown, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, and benchmark-relative metrics.
Receive funds ranked using a deterministic recommendation score, rather than alphabetical or arbitrary ordering.
See a separate data-confidence level so they understand how reliable the analysis is.
Incorporate personal investment preferences without changing the underlying fund-quality assessment.
Understand why a particular fund or strategy was recommended.

The platform is designed to make the process more transparent:

Financial Goal → Feasibility → Strategy → Tax Review → Preferences → Fund Analysis → Confidence Assessment → Ranking → Personalized Recommendation

The project also includes a mobile application version, allowing users to access the same goal-based investment experience from a mobile device. The APK will be provided through a Google Drive link.
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1O0oQl23zT3-AHnbejrjePueXfSDUqC5w/view?usp=sharing](url)

In short: the platform helps users answer not just "Which mutual funds are available?", but "Which funds are most suitable for my goal, how reliable is that recommendation, and why?"

**Best Use of Render**

Our project is a goal-based mutual fund investment planning platform that combines financial goals, risk profiling, tax awareness, real-time fund data, quantitative analytics, and deterministic fund recommendations.

Render is the production backend layer of the application. We deploy our FastAPI backend on Render and expose the APIs consumed by both our web application and mobile application. The backend handles goal creation, strategy generation, mutual-fund discovery, NAV data ingestion, performance analytics, recommendation scoring, data-confidence evaluation, and tax-aware planning.

A key part of the system is keeping the mutual-fund universe and NAV information updated. We designed a synchronization pipeline with database-backed locking, sync-status tracking, failure handling, and automated scheduled refreshes. Our GitHub Actions workflow can trigger the deployed Render API for scheduled data synchronization, allowing us to keep the data pipeline automated without requiring a continuously running worker.

Render therefore serves as the bridge between our development code and a publicly accessible, continuously usable investment-planning service. It allows the same backend logic to power our web experience and Android mobile application while keeping the architecture modular and scalable.

**Best Use of n8n**

**n8n acts as the automation and intelligence layer of our investment platform.** Instead of putting every notification and AI-related task inside the FastAPI backend, we use n8n to orchestrate these processes independently.

The workflow starts with a **Schedule Trigger**, which periodically initiates the process. n8n then sends an **HTTP request to our FastAPI server**, which provides the latest goal information such as the user's email, goal name, target amount, current amount, and progress. The data is passed to an **AI Agent**, which interprets the goal progress and generates a personalized notification. n8n then checks its **Data Table** to determine whether that milestone has already been notified, preventing duplicate emails. If it is a new milestone, another **AI Agent** prepares the final email content, and **Gmail sends the notification to the user**. Finally, n8n stores the notified milestone in the Data Table.

### In simple terms:

**FastAPI → provides the data**
**n8n → manages the workflow**
**AI Agents → add intelligence and personalization**
**Gmail → communicates with the user**
**Data Table → prevents duplicate notifications**

This approach keeps the main application clean while allowing us to **automate, personalize, and extend notification workflows without changing the core FastAPI application every time.**

**Best Use of Gemini API**

Our project uses the Gemini API as an intelligent decision and communication layer rather than just a chatbot. Gemini analyzes users’ financial goals and progress data, identifies meaningful milestone events, and generates personalized, motivating notifications based on each user’s situation. It is integrated into our n8n automation workflow, where Gemini processes the data received from our FastAPI backend and produces structured email content such as the subject and message. This allows our application to automatically transform raw financial data into human-friendly, personalized guidance, demonstrating a practical use of generative AI in financial goal management.

**The problem it solves**

Students often struggle to find the right teammates for hackathons and projects because they don't know who has complementary skills, interests, or roles. Elevora solves this by intelligently matching students based on their skills, interests, preferred roles, and project/hackathon interests, using a swipe-based interface to make team formation quick and intuitive.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into
Frontend–backend connectivity: Initially, the deployed frontend was trying to connect to localhost, which only works on the developer's computer and caused network errors for the deployed website.
Backend deployment: We had to deploy the FastAPI backend separately so the frontend could communicate with a publicly accessible API.
Authentication integration: Connecting the login/signup flow with the FastAPI authentication endpoints and JWT-based authentication required careful handling of tokens and user IDs.
Database integration: We integrated the real student database with the team-matching system instead of relying on mock student data.
Matching algorithm: Designing a deterministic compatibility algorithm required combining shared skills, interests, hackathon interests, complementary roles, complementary skills, and college information.
Swipe persistence: We initially had swipe actions only on the frontend, then implemented backend persistence so Interested/Pass actions are stored and previously swiped students are excluded.
Pagination: The matching system had to support loading recommendations continuously instead of being limited to the first 10 students.
Authentication & authorization: We added checks to prevent users from accessing another student's recommendations or submitting swipes on behalf of another user.
Testing and deployment: Backend tests passed successfully, while frontend deployment required additional debugging because the local and deployed environments behaved differently.
Time constraints: Integrating and testing the complete system close to the submission deadline required prioritizing the core login, dashboard, database, and student-team matching functionality.
