### LaunchTown
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/launchtown-7d22) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/perfect7613/launchtown) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://launchtown-seven.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Push%20to%20Prod%20Hackathon:%20Building%20at%20the%20Frontier-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pushtoprod-india.devfolio.co)

> Rehearse your launch with a living synthetic town.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyPDF2](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyPDF2-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Convex](https://img.shields.io/badge/Convex-333333?style=flat-square) ![claude](https://img.shields.io/badge/claude-333333?style=flat-square) ![bolna](https://img.shields.io/badge/bolna-333333?style=flat-square) ![Claude Agent SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Agent%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://launchtown-seven.vercel.app/

**How you are solving it?**

## A causal launch rehearsal, not an aggregate score

LaunchTown turns any public product URL into a living 2D market. Claude first constructs a structured product model. Eight seeded residents then act through a deterministic policy using need, awareness, curiosity, social proof, distrust, and expected friction. Conversations become structured influence events; relationship strength and social susceptibility determine the state change. When a resident crosses a visit threshold, a browser journey is built from their own traits, memories, and hearsay. The result becomes a first-hand `productExperience` memory that can change the next conversation.

> We built a causal simulation loop where website experience becomes memory, memory becomes social influence, and social influence changes subsequent real-browser behavior. Claude interprets meaning; our simulation engine owns causality.

The flagship cascade makes that claim visible. Priya finds Ledgerly's early bank-access request uncomfortable and warns Rohan. His trust falls but curiosity rises. His browser context includes Priya's warning, so he investigates the security page first. The strong security documentation restores trust; he then tells Meera, changing her state.

Every transition is inspectable. The town shows activity and funnel state; the three-tab resident inspector exposes **Mind** (state and sourced beliefs), **Browser** (objective, live view when available, or the last completed journey), and **Social** (relationships, conversation effects, and the causal arrow to a triggered visit). Follow Resident tracks the cascade automatically. A validated cached-journey fallback keeps the same persistence and result-interpretation boundary available if a browser provider fails during a live demo.

Founders can then interview a resident by voice. Bolna places a consented, rate-limited outbound call to a fixed masked destination with bounded live resident context; browser Web Call is available as a fallback. When the simulation completes, a read-only Claude Agent SDK workflow reconciles influence events, browser runs, resident states, and memories into an evidence-grounded Launch Report with top frictions, belief propagation, resident outcomes, and three concrete website fixes. The report agent has no simulation write tool, and its output must pass a JSON schema before it reaches the UI.

**What is the problem your project solves?**

## Founders can rehearse pitches—but not launches

Behavioral product feedback arrives too late. Analytics tools such as PostHog and Amplitude explain what real users did only **after** a product is live. The alternative—recruiting users for interviews and usability studies—is slow and expensive. Before launch, founders cannot see how a website experience becomes a belief, how that belief spreads through word of mouth, or how social context changes the next person's behavior.

**LaunchTown lets founders rehearse a website launch with a living synthetic population.** Paste a URL and eight residents with different needs, trust thresholds, price sensitivity, technical fluency, memories, and relationships evaluate it, talk to one another, and change what they do next.

This is not a conversion-forecasting or calibration claim. LaunchTown is a pre-production simulation environment for discovering plausible user journeys, social effects, and product failures while there is still time to fix them. The impact is a faster, inspectable feedback loop: founders can trace not only *what* happened, but *why one experience changed the next person's journey*.

**How Did You Use Claude?**

Claude is a core runtime dependency, not a chat layer added on top.

1. **Product understanding:** Claude analyzes any submitted public website into a validated Product Model containing facts, personas, promises, pricing, calls to action, objections, and likely friction. This grounds every resident in the same real product.
2. **Resident cognition, dialogue, and reflection:** residents retrieve semantically relevant memories, use Claude to generate in-character dialogue, summarize completed conversations from their own perspective, and reflect on accumulated first-hand experiences and hearsay.
3. **Social influence extraction:** after a conversation, Claude returns a validated semantic event—awareness, curiosity, and trust signals; transferred beliefs with confidence and source; and a behavioral suggestion.
4. **Resident-specific browsing:** Claude-guided browser journeys use a resident's goals, traits, memories, and social context. Returned pages, friction, outcomes, and evidence must pass schema validation before deterministic reducers can apply any state update.
5. **Founder-ready Launch Reports:** a scoped Claude Agent SDK session must use four read-only tools—resident states, influence events, browser runs, and memories—to assemble an evidence-linked report. The agent has no simulation write tool, and the report is validated against a strict schema before display, copy, or Markdown download.
6. **Causal separation:** Claude never writes simulation state. Deterministic code applies each signal as `signal × relationshipStrength × socialSusceptibility`, clamps it, records an auditable influence event, and uses a fixed visit-policy sigmoid to decide subsequent behavior.

Remove Claude and there is no product model, meaningful resident cognition, conversation, semantic word of mouth, guided website journey, or evidence-grounded Launch Report. We use a separate embedding model only to create vectors for memory retrieval because Anthropic does not provide an embedding model; it performs no generative reasoning.

### Saarthi AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/saarthi-ai-4498) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mikelord007/Saarthi-AI) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/144051c0-f346-4d21-834a-eb9fb8ef867b) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/yPPrIhvW2II) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Push%20to%20Prod%20Hackathon:%20Building%20at%20the%20Frontier-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pushtoprod-india.devfolio.co)

> Speak a task, Saarthi taps through your phone

![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anthropic](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anthropic-333333?style=flat-square) ![claude](https://img.shields.io/badge/claude-333333?style=flat-square) ![SarvamAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/SarvamAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![AgenticAI](https://img.shields.io/badge/AgenticAI-333333?style=flat-square) ![JetpackCompose](https://img.shields.io/badge/JetpackCompose-333333?style=flat-square) ![AccessibilityService](https://img.shields.io/badge/AccessibilityService-333333?style=flat-square)

**How you are solving it?**

**Architecture**

- `SaarthiAccessibilityService` + `ScreenPerception` walk the live accessibility tree and compress it into plain text (`PerceptionResult`/`NodeText`) an LLM can reason over.
- `AgentLoop` feeds that perception plus the user's spoken task to Claude (`ClaudeClient`) via an 11-tool schema (`AgentTool`) — tap, type, scroll, swipe, open-app, and more — in a perceive → decide → act loop.
- `ActionExecutor` carries out whatever Claude decides, gated by `IrreversibleActionGuard`, which forces a hand-back confirmation screen before any action that can't be undone.
- `ChatRouter` classifies every incoming message as chat-vs-task *before* AgentLoop ever runs, so an offhand remark can't accidentally trigger a device takeover.
- Voice loop: `AudioRecorder` + Sarvam's streaming STT (with VAD auto-stop) capture speech; streaming TTS narrates the agent's steps starting from the first audio chunk instead of waiting for the full line to render.
- The whole UI and narration is localized into 11 languages, so the experience — not just button labels — matches the user's language.
- Three entry points (long-press home via `SaarthiInteractionSession`, the system ASSIST intent, and typed in-app chat) all funnel into the same `AgentLoop`, so a takeover works identically everywhere.

**Disclosure on prior work:** This project is based out of a prior project Manu did for a prior hackathon - Sarvam Hack but it is *shell only* — static screens (onboarding, home, history, settings, the assist overlay/hand-back UI), navigation, and design tokens, with no real functionality behind any of it. Every piece of actual intelligence — the accessibility perception layer, the Claude-driven agent loop, the voice pipeline, ChatRouter, irreversible-action guarding, and the 11-language localization — was built during the 5-hour hackathon window itself.

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://github.com/mikelord007/Saarthi-AI

**What is the problem your project solves?**

Millions of smartphone users in India are locked out of full participation in the app economy — not because they lack a phone, but because most apps assume screen literacy: small tap targets, dense text, flows written in English, multi-step forms. Existing voice assistants (Google Assistant, Siri) can open an app or set a timer, but they can't actually **operate** an arbitrary app for someone — they can't fill a form, navigate a confirmation dialog, or read out what's currently on screen in the user's own language.

**Saarthi AI** closes that gap. It's a voice-first Android agent that can:
- **See** the screen through Android's Accessibility API
- **Understand** a spoken task in the user's own language (11 Indian languages supported)
- **Act**: either read the screen aloud, or literally tap/scroll/type through the app on the user's behalf — narrating every step *before* taking it, and pausing for explicit confirmation before anything irreversible (payments, deletions, sending messages)

It's aimed at users for whom the smartphone UI itself is the barrier — low-literacy users, elderly users, and anyone more comfortable speaking a task aloud than hunting through menus.

**How Did You Use Claude?**

Claude is the decision-making core of the agent loop, not a bolt-on feature:

- **`ClaudeClient`** sends Claude the current screen's perceived text plus the user's task, using a custom 11-tool schema (`AgentTool`) that models real UI actions — tap-by-text, tap-by-coordinates, type, scroll, swipe, open app, go back, wait, and more.
- Claude runs in a **perceive → decide → act loop** (`AgentLoop`): after every action, the screen is re-perceived and fed back to Claude so it adjusts to what actually happened rather than executing a static plan.
- **`ChatRouter`** is a separate, lightweight Claude call (Haiku 4.5) that classifies each incoming message as chat-vs-task and resolves ambiguous replies (e.g. a bare "yes" confirming something said earlier) before anything reaches the main agent loop — so Claude decides *whether* to act, not just *how*.
- The main agent loop runs at effort:high with adaptive thinking enabled, since screen-navigation decisions (which of several near-identical buttons to tap, whether a dialog is a confirmation or a distraction) benefit from deliberation.
- Claude is also responsible for respecting the irreversible-action guard: it's prompted to flag actions that need explicit user confirmation before `IrreversibleActionGuard` hands control back to the user.

In short: Claude is the thing actually looking at the phone screen and deciding what to tap next — the rest of the app is perception, execution, and voice I/O built around that core loop.

### Slopfolio - AI artifacts Provenance feature
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/slopfolio-b187) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/salmanneedsajob/notary-mcp) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://slopfolio.com/@salmanneedsajob/posts-that-remember-how-they-were-published) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/4jkj4wDTY-Y) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Push%20to%20Prod%20Hackathon:%20Building%20at%20the%20Frontier-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pushtoprod-india.devfolio.co)

> The work and how you made it, at one URL

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OAuth](https://img.shields.io/badge/OAuth-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Playwright](https://img.shields.io/badge/Playwright-333333?style=flat-square)

**How you are solving it?**

## What Slopfolio is

Slopfolio gives every piece of AI-assisted work a permanent URL carrying both the artifact and a `process.log` — tools, iterations, time, a self-reported %AI split, the best dead end. Each page stands on its own as a process log of the artifact: a stranger can land on it cold and understand what was made and how. It is a live invite-only alpha at slopfolio.com with real members posting real work.

## Prior work, disclosed

Slopfolio has been in development for about a month before this hackathon. The post page, profiles, explore feed, compose, auth, the database schema and its row-level security, comments, likes, follows and notifications were all built before today and are already live. Everything below is the hackathon work.

## Where it was yesterday: the paste-back workflow

Until today, getting the process into Slopfolio was manual. You copy a prompt out of Slopfolio, paste it into your own AI chat at the end of a working session, the model writes a structured summary of what just happened, and you paste that back — where a versioned parser turns it into the process log. Honest, but every word of it passes through human hands. The page *says* how the work was made; nothing about the page can prove it.

## What shipped today: a provenance layer

**The AI that did the work can now file the report itself.** Slopfolio runs an MCP server, so an agent like Claude connects over OAuth, prepares a draft from the session it was actually part of, and publishes it — with preparing and publishing as two separate, separately-approved steps, so a human stays in the loop. Until this morning, connecting a client took five founder-only steps (create an OAuth app, capture a one-time secret, hand-insert an audience row, edit an env allowlist, redeploy). Those five steps are now zero: any member can connect their own AI.

**And the site can prove which path a post took.** A post published through the MCP server carries a `witnessed` mark on its page. That mark cannot be produced from the compose form, and it cannot be claimed by a client either: it is enforced at the database layer by column-level grants — the column appears in no client insert or update grant at all, so no request an author or an agent can make will set it. Provenance is derived from the write path, not asserted by the writer. Four new permission tests pin exactly that.

**Why this is significant.** The self-reported half of the process log ("60% AI") stays self-reported — that's honesty. But *witnessed* is a different kind of claim: the agent that made the work was present at the publish, and the platform can vouch for it structurally. As more of everyone's output becomes agent-made, "this process log was filed by the AI that did the work" versus "this was typed into a form" is the difference between a record and a claim — and Slopfolio can now tell them apart, unforgeably.

**One more fix on the way: the writing itself.** Agent-written summaries read like insider notes in the usual model register. Both paths — the paste prompt and the MCP server's instructions — now carry the same explicit writing rules (name the stranger reading it, ban the slop register), with a test asserting every rule appears on both paths so they can't drift apart.

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://slopfolio.com/@salmanneedsajob/posts-that-remember-how-they-were-published

**How Did You Use Claude?**

Three ways, and the third is the interesting one.

**Claude built it.** Effectively all of Slopfolio was written with Claude Code — Opus 5 for engineering (schema, RLS, the versioned paste parser, the MCP server, every migration) and Fable 5 for copy and creative passes, with an explicit switch between the two. The project runs on a set of standing instruction files and custom skills that gate every schema change, deploy, and user-facing copy change on my approval before anything happens.

**Claude is a user of it.** The MCP server exists so that Claude can be a first-class client of the product: it authenticates over OAuth, prepares a post from a real working session, and publishes it. The posts on the site carrying the `witnessed` mark were published by Claude through that path — they were not typed into the compose form.

**Claude's own writing was one of the bugs.** The process summaries Claude generated read like insider notes, so part of today's work was giving both the paste prompt and the MCP server's instructions the same explicit rules about who they are writing for and how to write plainly.

Worth saying plainly: I am not a developer. Slopfolio is a product I designed and directed. Claude wrote the code.

**What is the problem your project solves?**

Everyone is building with AI now. Very little of it ever gets seen.

Most AI-assisted projects end their life on localhost. They work, they taught their maker something real, and they never go anywhere — sometimes because there's no obvious place to put them, often because of a quieter hesitation: *is this worth showing if AI did a lot of it?* So the work stays private, and the thing that would actually be valuable to other people — how it was made, what was tried, what failed — disappears with it.

Slopfolio is a home for that work. You get a portfolio page for yourself and a permanent URL for each project, and every post carries a `process.log` alongside the artifact: the tools, the iterations, the time it took, an honest self-reported %AI split, and the best dead end. The process is presented as something other people can consume and learn from — a short case study, not a screenshot with a link.

### qs-GO
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/qsgo-69f2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Len3hq/qs-go) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Port%20Mortem%202026%20--%20Code%20Resurrection%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://portmortem.devfolio.co)

> query string parser

![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every Go web server uses `net/url` for query strings. It does flat key-value pairs. That's it. No nested objects (`a[b][c]=d`), no array notation (`a[]=1&a[]=2`), no depth control, no charset handling. The only way to get full query string parsing in Go is to embed a JavaScript runtime — until now. qs-go gives Go services the same battle-tested query string parser that Node.js has depended on for a decade, as a native library with a 5ms cold-start binary.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Go's zero-value problem vs JavaScript's 'undefined'.** In JS, 'typeof opts.depth === 'undefined'" cleanly distinguishes "not set" from "set to 0." In Go, the zero value for int is 0 — there's no way to tell if the user explicitly passed 0 or didn't set the field. This caused silent option overwrites where 'arrayLimit: 0' or 'depth: 0' from the test suite got reset to defaults. Solved with a 'MarkUserProvided()' sentinel method and a heuristic for bare struct literals. Still imperfect — documented as Decision #18.

**2. JavaScript 'null' vs 'undefined' — both map to Go 'nil'.** JS sparse arrays use 'undefined' holes ('[, 'b']') while explicit nulls are 'null'. Go represents both as 'nil' in slices. This meant 'compact()' was deleting explicit null values along with sparse holes. Solved by introducing a 'Null' sentinel type with a custom json.Marshaler to output JSON null while keeping Go nil for sparse holes.

**3. Map ordering — Go maps are randomized, JS objects preserve insertion order.** Merge results depend on processing order when keys collide (e.g., a=1&a[]=2). Sorted keys produced wrong element ordering in 6 tests. Solved by tracking insertion order in 'parseValues()' with a separate key slice.

> I ported parsimonious, Python PEG parser in RUST

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

The hard part of this hackathon isn't writing a port — it's proving the
port behaves like the original. I picked parsimonious because its test
suite asserts exact parse trees and exact error messages, giving me an
unambiguous oracle. The biggest technical challenges were the original's
self-hosted bootstrap (which deadlocks when re-implemented naively in
Rust), a packrat cache-key collision, and matching Python's
"most-rightward-progress" error reporting byte-for-byte. The differential
fuzzer comparing both engines is the submission's centerpiece: 60
seconds, zero divergences, oracle enabled.

**The problem it solves**

# parsimonious-rs — Python → Rust (Track D)

A complete, idiomatic Rust port of parsimonious, the pure-Python PEG parser
library (~1,500 lines). The port reproduces the original's *observable
behavior* — identical parse trees, identical error messages, identical
edge-case handling — while shipping as a standalone binary with zero
`unsafe` blocks and no Python runtime.

## Why parsimonious
A PEG parser is the ideal port target: recursive, memoized, benchmarkable,
and rich in edge cases (left recursion, forward references, exact error
reporting). It has a real test suite (unittest + pytest) that asserts exact
tree shapes and exact error strings — the perfect oracle for parity.

## What we proved
- **Test parity:** 20/20 adapter tests pass — the original Python test
  cases re-pointed at the Rust API. The original test suite is preserved
  verbatim in `tests/original/`, hashed at kickoff, byte-for-byte
  unmodified. No test edits to make the port green.
- **Differential fuzzing:** a harness generates random PEG grammars +
  inputs and parses each with BOTH engines (Rust port vs. real Python
  parsimonious installed via pip), comparing accept/reject decisions.
  Result: 188 iterations over 60 continuous seconds, Python oracle
  enabled, **zero divergences** (`fuzz/log.txt`).
- **Zero `unsafe`:** the entire crate is safe Rust — no `unsafe`, no `any`,
  no escape hatches.
- **Honest benchmarks:** cold start median 734 µs (p99 7.3 ms), hot parse
  median 323 µs, methodology fully documented (`bench/methodology.md`).

## Key architectural decisions (DECISIONS.md, 12 documented)
1. **Lazy tree materialization** — compact match summaries cached; Node
   trees built on demand (biggest memory win, structurally identical).
2. **Hand-written grammar compiler** — no self-hosted bootstrap (avoids
   the original's fragile recursive init).
3. **Left-recursion sentinel** — packrat `InProgress` state mirrors
   Python's `IN_PROGRESS` object; same LeftRecursionError, no hang.

## One-command build
```bash
cargo build --release
# or: docker build -t parsimonious-rs .

### Payless
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/payless-0992) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/tpriyank596-cmd/payless) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/b1CakvSDzJ4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co)

> Compare. Shop. Shop smarter

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Playwright](https://img.shields.io/badge/Playwright-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Fragile DOMs: Instamart (and similar apps) change selectors often — we centralized them in selectors.py and added fallback selector chains.
When CSS alone failed, we added vision mode: screenshot the search results and let an LLM pick the right product card.
Multi-platform browser state: each app needs its own Chromium profile and login; switching platforms meant headed windows and session checks before every run.
Offer parsing: coupon text is messy and inconsistent — we combined DOM scraping with LLM parsing to pick the best eligible offer without applying invalid codes.
Bill accuracy: a platform only “wins” if we read a real post-coupon To Pay; partial carts or missing totals are marked failed instead of fake comparisons.
Prava wallet + passkeys: embedded card enrollment required HTTPS in dev and a custom Permissions-Policy header for the collect iframe.
Async orchestration: Playwright, WebSockets, and optional CrewAI tasks had to stay in sync without blocking the FastAPI event loop — we routed browser work through dedicated workers with strict “never pay” guardrails.

**The problem it solves**

Quick-commerce apps rarely show the same price for the same basket — coupons, delivery fees, and stock differ by platform.
Manually rebuilding your list on Instamart, Zepto, and Blinkit takes time and mental load every week.
PayLess automates that grind: you describe what you need once, and it runs the same list sequentially on each app.
It applies the best eligible offer on each cart and compares real To Pay totals, not headline discounts.
Runs stream live progress over WebSocket so you can see search, cart, and offer steps as they happen.
Persistent browser profiles mean you log in once per platform, not on every comparison.
Frequent items and session memory make repeat shops faster.
Because nothing is auto-ordered, it’s safe for price-checking before you choose where to buy.
Ideal for households optimizing weekly groceries, roommates splitting runs, or anyone tired of app-hopping for a fair deal.

> A browser-based financial civilization idle game

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![BatchFile](https://img.shields.io/badge/BatchFile-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

One of the biggest problems Prosperity Empire addresses is the lack of engaging ways to learn economics and finance. Many students learn concepts such as inflation, investing, supply and demand, diversification, and monetary policy through textbooks or lectures, which can feel abstract and disconnected from real-world applications. Prosperity Empire transforms these concepts into interactive systems where players experience economic growth, market fluctuations, and financial decision-making firsthand. By learning through gameplay rather than memorization, players gain a deeper understanding of how economic systems function and how different decisions can impact long-term outcomes.

Another problem the game solves is the disconnect between education and entertainment. Educational software is often viewed as informative but not engaging, while traditional games are engaging but rarely teach meaningful academic concepts. Prosperity Empire bridges this gap by embedding educational content directly into core gameplay systems. Players are rewarded for learning through the Academy and Codex systems, while simultaneously applying that knowledge through investments, policy decisions, resource management, and economic planning. This creates an environment where learning becomes a natural part of progression rather than a separate activity.

The game also addresses the lack of accessible opportunities for people to explore complex financial and economic systems without real-world consequences. Concepts such as stock markets, commodities, foreign exchange, government policy, and technological investment can be intimidating for beginners. Prosperity Empire provides a risk-free environment where players can experiment with strategies, observe market behavior, and learn from mistakes without financial repercussions. By simulating the challenges and tradeoffs faced by businesses, investors, and governments, the game helps players develop analytical thinking, long-term planning skills, and financial literacy that can be valuable far beyond the game itself.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges I faced was balancing complexity with accessibility. I wanted the game to feel deep enough to simulate meaningful economic systems while still remaining understandable and enjoyable for new players. Many mechanics, such as inflation, production scaling, market volatility, population growth, and policy balancing, required extensive tuning and testing.

Performance optimization was another major challenge. Since the game constantly updates dozens of systems simultaneously, including passive resource generation, population simulation, financial markets, event timers, AI calculations, and the live 3D city, optimization became critical. I had to carefully organize update loops, reduce unnecessary calculations, and improve rendering efficiency to keep the game running smoothly.

Balancing progression was also difficult because every system was interconnected. Small changes to resource generation or technology bonuses could dramatically affect the pacing of the entire game. Creating meaningful progression without making the game too slow or too fast required many rounds of iteration and testing.

Another challenge was designing the educational systems in a way that felt integrated rather than forced. I wanted players to genuinely enjoy learning economics and finance concepts instead of feeling like they were reading textbook material. Creating hundreds of accurate and engaging questions and encyclopedia entries required extensive research and refinement.

### Areapulse
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/areapulse-d1cf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/shoyo-shashwat/Areapulse) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://areapulse-1.onrender.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeStorm%202026%20#2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codestorm-week2-2026.devfolio.co)

> Citizen complaints into actionable intelligence

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gunicorn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gunicorn-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges We Ran Into**

**AI-Generated Fake Reports**— As AI image generators became widely accessible, we realised bad actors could submit synthetic photos of potholes and garbage that do not exist. A convincing AI-generated pothole image looks identical to a real one to the naked eye. We built a multi-layer defence inside the **Groq Llama-4-Scout vision pipeline** that detects unnatural lighting, repeated pixel patterns, missing real-world context, and digital artifacts typical of generated images. Every flagged image is logged separately in a **spam_issues collection** for audit before it ever enters the main database.

**Rate Limiting and System Flooding** — During testing, automated scripts flooded the report endpoint with hundreds of fake submissions per minute. We built a per-user rate limiting system that tracks submission frequency and automatically blocks users who exceed thresholds. Combined with AI spam detection, this creates a two-layer shield — spam caught by AI, flooding caught by rate limiter — so neither fake content nor volume attacks can pollute the database.

**Firebase Quota Exhaustion** — Firebase free tier ran out within hours during live testing. We engineered a 5-minute TTL read cache that reduced daily reads from 2,880 to 288. Added graceful 429 handlingthat serves from in-memory seed data and queues writes in background threads. Users never see an error even when quota is fully exhausted.

**Duplicate Detection at Scale**— Calculating Haversine distance between every incoming report and all existing issues was computationally expensive as the database grew. We bounded the search to a 50m radius and 7-day window to keep response times fast without missing real duplicates. Multiple citizens reporting the same pothole now strengthen one issue instead of creating noise

**WhatsApp EXIF GPS Extraction** — WhatsApp strips EXIF metadata on some devices before sending images. We built fallback logic— if GPS is missing from the photo, the bot asks the user to share a location pin. If they do not share one, it defaults to area centroid coordinates derived from reverse geocoding via Nominatim.

**Neon Postgres Connection Drops**— Render free tier and Neon serverless pooler reject persistent connection pools and drop SSL connections under load. We replaced pooling with **per-request fresh connections** using a context manager that opens, commits, and closes cleanly even on errors — with auto-retry logic on transient SSL drops so no query fails silently.

**AR Camera Latency**— Getting computer vision classification under 5 seconds on a mobile browser was harder than expected. Raw camera photos were 3 to 5MB. Sending that to Groq caused consistent timeouts. We added client-side image compression to under 500KB before the API call, bringing classification time down to under 3 seconds on average mobile connections.

**SLA Auto-Escalation Under Load** — Running SLA checks on every issue during every API call caused database overload during high traffic. We capped auto-escalations at** 5 per request**to protect the database connection pool, ensuring the feed always returns even if some escalations are deferred to the next polling cycle.

**The problem it solves**

India files over 40 million civic complaints every year. Almost none get resolved. The system fails at every level.

Citizens — face government portals with 15-field forms, ward numbers, captchas, and OTPs. Most abandon the page halfway. Those who complete it wait two months and hear nothing. No status updates. No accountability. No feedback loop. They file once and never again.

Government Officers — receive thousands of unsorted complaints daily. No intelligent prioritisation. No duplicate detection. No SLA enforcement. A critical sewage overflow sits in the same queue as a noise complaint. Officers manually sort everything. Critical issues get buried. Response times stretch into months.

NGOs — willing to deploy resources for civic improvement but have zero access to structured ground-level data. They cannot see which areas have the most unresolved issues, which issue types government is ignoring, or where their intervention would create the highest impact. They operate completely blind.

The core problem is a broken feedback loop between three stakeholders — citizens, government, and NGOs — with no shared platform, no automation, no accountability, and no transparency.

AreaPulse fixes all three simultaneously.

> JUST CODE

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many beginners struggle to learn programming because they need to remember complex syntax and language-specific rules before they can even start building projects. This makes coding intimidating and slows down the learning process.

Our tool solves this problem by allowing users to communicate in natural language and instantly convert their ideas into code in their chosen programming language. For example, a user can type a simple sentence like "print hello" or describe a task, and the system generates the corresponding code automatically.

The platform also includes a chatbot interface, making coding more interactive and beginner-friendly. Users can experiment with programming concepts without worrying about syntax errors or language barriers.

This tool can be used by students, beginners, self-learners, educators, and anyone who wants to learn or prototype code faster. It reduces the time spent memorizing syntax and helps users focus on understanding programming logic and problem-solving.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges while building this project was converting natural language input into accurate programming code across different programming languages. The same user request can have different syntax in HTML, JavaScript, C++, and other languages, making consistent code generation difficult.

Another challenge was designing a chatbot experience that felt simple and intuitive while still generating useful code outputs. We had to ensure that users could easily switch between programming languages and receive code in the correct format.

We also faced issues with handling ambiguous user inputs. Sometimes users provided incomplete instructions, which resulted in unclear code generation. To address this, we improved the prompt structure and added logic to better interpret user intent before generating code.

Throughout development, we continuously tested the platform with different prompts, identified errors, refined the workflow, and improved the overall user experience. These challenges helped us build a more reliable and user-friendly coding assistant.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Many students and job seekers struggle with creating strong resumes, identifying the skills required for their target roles, and preparing effectively for interviews. They often rely on multiple websites and resources, which makes the process time-consuming and confusing.

CareerPilot AI solves this problem by providing an all-in-one AI-powered career assistance platform.

### How it helps users

* Analyzes resumes and provides a score along with strengths, weaknesses, missing skills, and improvement suggestions.
* Generates role-specific interview questions to help users practice and prepare confidently.
* Identifies skill gaps and creates personalized learning roadmaps for career growth.
* Saves time by combining multiple career development tools into a single platform.
* Provides instant AI-powered guidance without requiring professional career coaching.

### Impact

CareerPilot AI makes career preparation more accessible, faster, and personalized for students, freshers, and professionals looking to improve their job readiness and career growth.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

While building CareerPilot AI, I faced several technical and design challenges.

### 1. Gemini API Rate Limits & Availability

One of the biggest challenges was handling Gemini API rate limits and occasional high-demand errors (503 Service Unavailable). Sometimes the AI features worked perfectly, but requests would fail during peak usage.

**Solution:**
I improved error handling in the application and displayed user-friendly messages instead of raw API errors. I also optimized prompts to reduce unnecessary API requests.

### 2. UI/UX Improvements

Initially, the generated AI responses were difficult to read because long text blocks appeared unstructured and the interface felt visually cluttered.

**Solution:**
I redesigned the UI, improved spacing, typography, result containers, and added copy/clear functionality to make the experience cleaner and easier to use.

### 3. React Component Integration

Managing navigation and keeping all pages (Resume Analyzer, Interview Prep, and Skill Gap Analysis) connected properly through React Router required multiple iterations.

**Solution:**
I refactored the component structure and improved routing to ensure smooth navigation across the application.

### 4. Deployment Issues

Deploying the project and configuring environment variables for Gemini API on the hosting platform required careful setup.

**Solution:**
I configured environment variables correctly, tested production builds locally, and successfully deployed the application using Vercel.

### Key Learning

This project helped me gain hands-on experience with React, API integration, prompt engineering, error handling, deployment workflows, and building AI-powered web applications.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern users often rely on multiple applications to manage their daily workflow. Tasks, notes, documents, AI assistants, search tools, and productivity utilities are usually scattered across different platforms, resulting in constant context switching and reduced productivity.

JARVIS Web OS solves this problem by providing a unified AI-powered workspace where users can access essential productivity tools from a single interface. Instead of opening multiple applications, users can manage tasks, organize notes, interact with an AI assistant, search information, and access important utilities within one intelligent platform.

The system improves efficiency by reducing distractions, simplifying workflow management, and delivering AI-powered insights that help users stay organized and focused. With its futuristic interface and integrated productivity features, JARVIS Web OS creates a seamless and engaging web experience designed for students, developers, professionals, and productivity-focused users.

Key Benefits:

* Centralized productivity workspace
* Reduced application switching
* AI-powered assistance and insights
* Faster task and information management
* Improved focus and workflow organization
* Modern and intuitive user experience

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was designing a futuristic operating-system-like interface while keeping the application responsive and easy to navigate. As the number of features increased, maintaining a clean user experience became difficult.

Another challenge was managing data flow between different modules such as the AI assistant, productivity dashboard, notes, and document management system. Ensuring that all components worked together seamlessly required careful state management and modular architecture.

Performance optimization was also a hurdle. Some UI animations and dashboard components initially caused slower page rendering. This was resolved by optimizing component rendering, reducing unnecessary updates, and improving the overall application structure.

To overcome these challenges, the project was developed using a modular approach, continuous testing, and iterative UI improvements. Breaking the application into reusable components made debugging easier and significantly improved maintainability and scalability.

Ashutosh Choudhary

### 3D-Models
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/doodle-storyteller-da48) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://claude.ai/share/1ae29466-323a-431f-9c74-d3590b54a06b) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeStorm%202026%20#2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codestorm-week2-2026.devfolio.co)

> From scribble to sculpture

![CSS3](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vanilla JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vanilla%20JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square) ![Claude (Sonnet 4.6)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20(Sonnet%204.6)-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I ran into

Getting the AI to return strictly structured data. Since the 3D scene is built programmatically, even one malformed value (a missing field, a string where a number should be) could crash the render. I solved this by writing a sanitizer that validates and clamps every shape's size, position, and color before it's ever added to the 3D scene — so a weird AI response degrades gracefully instead of breaking the page.
Library version conflicts. Three.js's controls and export tools are separate add-on scripts that must match the core library's version exactly, or they fail silently. I pinned every script to the same Three.js version to fix this.
Making the doodle-to-shape mapping feel natural. Doodles are messy and abstract, but 3D primitives are precise. I tuned the AI prompt to interpret loosely and playfully rather than literally, so even rough sketches produce a fun result instead of nothing at all.

**The problem it solves**

Most people can sketch an idea in seconds but have no CAD skills to turn it into an actual 3D shape — modeling software has a steep learning curve and isn't built for quick "what if" ideas. Doodle to 3D removes that barrier entirely: draw a rough doodle, and it's instantly interpreted into a real, rotatable 3D model you can inspect, zoom, and even download as a .gltf/.obj file. Useful for:

Quickly prototyping a product or character concept before committing to real CAD work
Helping students or hobbyists visualize 2D ideas in 3D space without learning Blender/Fusion360
Game devs or makers blocking out rough concept assets in seconds
Anyone who just wants to see their doodle "come alive" as an object they can spin around

AADITHYA SUJA

> Forensic Intelligence for the AI Era.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

# ⚙️ Challenges We Ran Into

Developing TruthGuard AI involved solving several engineering challenges beyond simply integrating AI models.

## 🧠 Reducing AI Hallucinations

One of our primary objectives was ensuring factual reliability.

Instead of allowing an LLM to generate answers independently, we engineered a **real-time evidence grounding pipeline** that collects contextual information from multiple trusted sources before AI inference. This significantly reduced hallucinations while improving factual consistency.

---

## 🌐 Building a Reliable Search Infrastructure

Search providers frequently return inconsistent results or enforce rate limits.

To overcome this, we implemented:

* Parallel search execution
* Intelligent fallback mechanisms
* URL normalization
* Duplicate result elimination
* Context ranking based on relevance

This architecture ensures comprehensive evidence retrieval even when individual providers fail.

---

## ⚡ Balancing Speed with Accuracy

Delivering comprehensive verification without sacrificing responsiveness was another major challenge.

We addressed this by designing a **dual-LLM architecture**:

* **Groq Llama 3.3**

  * Handles ultra-fast real-time verification.

* **Google Gemini**

  * Performs advanced reasoning, multimodal analysis, and fallback processing for complex investigations.

This hybrid approach provides both low latency and high analytical quality.

---

## 📊 Presenting Complex Results Intuitively

Raw forensic data can easily overwhelm users.

We redesigned the reporting experience to include:

* Interactive confidence visualizations
* Structured forensic breakdowns
* Evidence summaries
* Source citations
* Four-state verdict classification
* Clear reasoning behind every decision

The goal was not only to provide a verdict, but to make every conclusion **transparent, explainable, and trustworthy**.

---

## 🚀 Outcome

The final system delivers a scalable, resilient, and transparent verification pipeline capable of analyzing multiple forms of digital deception while maintaining a fast, intuitive user experience suitable for both technical and non-technical users.

**The problem it solves**

# 🛡️ The Problem it Solves

TruthGuard AI is an **AI-powered forensic intelligence platform** engineered to combat the growing epidemic of **digital misinformation, AI-generated deception, and online fraud**.

Modern AI assistants often generate responses without verifying their factual accuracy, while traditional fact-checking platforms require users to manually investigate multiple sources. TruthGuard AI eliminates this friction by combining **real-time evidence aggregation** with **multi-model AI reasoning**, delivering transparent and evidence-backed verification within seconds.

## Key Capabilities

* **📰 Fake News Verification**

  * Validates viral claims against real-time web sources, Wikipedia, and trusted fact-checking databases.

* **🖼️ AI Image Forensics**

  * Detects AI-generated or manipulated images through visual artifact and forensic analysis.

* **🎤 Deepfake Voice Detection**

  * Identifies synthetic speech by analyzing pitch, frequency, and spectral characteristics.

* **💼 Fraudulent Job Detection**

  * Flags suspicious job postings by evaluating salary anomalies, domain legitimacy, urgency patterns, and scam indicators.

* **🔬 Research Verification**

  * Assesses scientific claims by examining citations, methodology, sample sizes, and publication credibility.

* **🕵️ Behavioral Fraud Analysis**

  * Detects suspicious interactions using behavioral biometrics such as typing dynamics and mouse movement patterns.

* **🌦️ Weather Validation**

  * Cross-verifies weather claims against live meteorological data.

## Why TruthGuard AI?

Unlike conventional AI assistants, TruthGuard AI **does not rely solely on language models**. Every claim is validated using a **multi-source evidence pipeline**, combining:

* Parallel web search aggregation
* Wikipedia knowledge retrieval
* Google Fact Check API
* Trusted fact-checking organizations
* Dual-LLM verification architecture

Each investigation produces:

* ✅ Structured Verdict *(Real, Fake, Partially True, or Unverified)*
* 📊 Confidence Score
* 📚 Supporting Evidence
* 🔗 Source Attribution
* 🧠 Transparent Reasoning

By transforming fragmented verification workflows into a single intelligent platform, TruthGuard AI empowers journalists, researchers, students, organizations, and everyday users to confidently distinguish fact from fabrication in an increasingly AI-driven digital landscape.

Team **Nova** -- [Thuyavan M](https://github.com/Thuyavan28/), [Akash S](https://github.com/akashS-18), [Lokesh A](https://github.com/itslokeshx/)

> Smart Services for the Brilliant and Broke

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Bootstrap](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bootstrap-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chart.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chart.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Database deletions: One of the trickiest bugs was that deleting a service listing would completely crash the app. Because order history requires a service ID, deleting a listing left orphaned orders stranded, causing SQL integrity errors. The fix was setting up SQLAlchemy relationship cascades so that deleting a service listing automatically cleans up all associated orders, classroom sessions, and chat logs in one go without breaking the database.

**The problem it solves**

Being a college student usually means balancing a tight budget with a stressful workload. Standard part-time jobs rarely fit around lectures, and commercial study help websites charge monthly subscriptions that students simply can't afford.

"***Please use name- admin and password- AdminPassword123! to see the full website with admin panel*****"

Broke Geniuses solves this by creating a hyper-local campus economy. It lets students make quick money on their own terms by listing any service their peers might need—whether that’s tutoring, resume reviews, custom study notes, or even physical errands like picking up library printouts and binding documents.

For academic gigs, it removes the hassle of post-session studying. A built-in AI monitor logs the session transcript and automatically compiles structured study notes, summaries, and interactive revision quizzes. The platform charges a flat ₹100 fee to unlock these materials, creating a direct monetization model.

Normally, these kinds of student transactions are messy and unorganized happening over scattered WhatsApp groups, and email threads. Broke Geniuses brings everything together into a clean, unified dashboard where messages, collaborative classrooms, shared files, and payments are managed in one trustworthy place.

> Safe. Smart. Social. Travel.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

TravelBuddy solves the problem faced by solo travelers who struggle to find trustworthy travel companions with similar interests, budgets, and destinations.

Many people cancel or avoid trips because they don't have a compatible travel partner. Existing platforms mainly focus on booking hotels and transportation but do not help users connect with like-minded travelers.

TravelBuddy allows users to create a travel profile, specify their destination, budget, travel duration, and preferences. The platform intelligently matches users with compatible travel partners. Once matched, users can securely chat within the application before planning their trip together.

The platform makes solo travel safer, more affordable, and more enjoyable by helping people build trusted travel connections.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f80ef69254084d068b56ccffcaa50682/eed8e892-1a5f-4350-aebf-0daef2c037a1.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f80ef69254084d068b56ccffcaa50682/f9e0dcdb-4fc8-4af5-9f43-2964ebb3cfc5.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f80ef69254084d068b56ccffcaa50682/562dd0b3-3614-42bb-a1ef-638936c194d8.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/f80ef69254084d068b56ccffcaa50682/78bddfd7-6230-4dd3-b8c8-3af640b0b33e.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building TravelBuddy involved several technical challenges.

One of the biggest challenges was implementing real-time user matching based on travel preferences while ensuring correct profile retrieval from the database.

Another major challenge was deploying the application. We faced issues with MongoDB Atlas connectivity, DNS resolution, backend deployment on Render, frontend deployment on Vercel, CORS configuration, API integration, and route handling.

We also encountered problems while implementing the chat system, especially due to inconsistent field names between the frontend and backend models, which caused message delivery failures. After carefully debugging the APIs, updating the database schema, and synchronizing both frontend and backend, we resolved the issue.

Despite these challenges, we successfully built a fully functional travel partner matching platform with profile management, secure authentication, matching, and an integrated chat system.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Millions of students miss out on scholarships every year—not because they are ineligible, but because they never discover the opportunities that match their profile. Scholarship information is often scattered across multiple websites, shared through word of mouth, or buried in lengthy eligibility criteria. This makes the process confusing, time-consuming, and discouraging, especially for students from underserved communities.

ScholarSathi solves this problem by bringing scholarship discovery into one platform. Students simply enter their details, and the platform identifies scholarships that match their eligibility. Instead of manually searching dozens of websites and reading complex criteria, they can instantly discover relevant opportunities, view complete details, and register through a simple, user-friendly interface.

By making scholarship discovery effortless, personalized, and accessible, ScholarSathi helps ensure that deserving students don't miss life-changing educational opportunities simply because they were unaware of them.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was designing the scholarship eligibility logic. Every scholarship has different eligibility criteria such as family income, category, gender, age, and academic level. Ensuring that the platform accurately matches students with scholarships based on their profile required careful planning of the database structure and backend filtering logic.
I also integrated an SMS notification system to notify students after registration. Setting up the SMS service and ensuring that notifications were triggered at the right time required additional testing and debugging.
Overall, these challenges helped me build a platform that is reliable, easy to use, and focused on making scholarship discovery effortless for students.

### Smart URL Threat Detection for Secure Browsing
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/smart-url-threat-detection-for-secure-browsing-9e04) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/varshan-4068/URL-Based-Cyber-Attack-Detection-System) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeStorm%202026%20#2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codestorm-week2-2026.devfolio.co)

> Automated trust. Algorithmic safety.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The rapid increase in phishing websites and URL-based cyberattacks has made it difficult for users to identify malicious websites before visiting them.

Existing blacklist-based security solutions cannot effectively detect newly created or zero-day malicious URLs.

Browser warnings often provide little explanation, making it difficult for users to understand the actual security risk.

The proposed system intercepts URLs using a browser extension and performs an instant local allow list check to reduce unnecessary analysis.

The main objective of this project is to deliver a fast, accurate, privacy-preserving, and explainable URL threat detection system that enhances secure web browsing through a hybrid rule-based and machine learning approach.

For unknown URLs, the system extracts lexical, structural, and domain-based features without collecting sensitive user data or browsing content.

A lightweight rule engine detects common attack patterns such as SQL Injection, XSS, SSRF, Open Redirects, Path Traversal, and phishing indicators in real time.

An XGBoost machine learning model further analyses suspicious URLs to improve detection accuracy and reduce false positives.

High-risk URLs undergo DNS, WHOIS, and reputation analysis before generating a final security score and threat classification.

The system provides clear, human-readable explanations along with appropriate browser warnings to help users make informed decisions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Faced
Dataset Quality: Obtaining a balanced and up-to-date dataset containing both legitimate and malicious URLs.
Feature Engineering: Identifying URL features that effectively distinguish malicious websites from legitimate ones.
False Positives & False Negatives: Reducing incorrect classifications while maintaining high detection accuracy.
Zero-Day Threats: Detecting newly created malicious URLs that are not present in existing blacklists.
Real-Time Performance: Ensuring URL analysis is fast enough without affecting the user's browsing experience.
Privacy Preservation: Performing analysis without collecting or exposing users' browsing data.
Browser Integration: Seamlessly integrating the machine learning model with the browser extension for real-time detection.

Team **Binary Breakers** -- [Thennarasu N](https://github.com/thennarasu-n), [Alfred Joseph](https://github.com/alfredjoseph0405-commits), [Sirivarshan K](https://github.com/varshan-4068/), [VISHAL M](https://github.com/vishalm2007123), [LEKSHME BALAJE R](https://github.com/balaje-16), Manoj A

### NexBuild
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nexbuild-37ab) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://6a6bd8c6d6dfed7824b3670a--genuine-beignet-0ae496.netlify.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeStorm%202026%20#2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codestorm-week2-2026.devfolio.co)

> AI-powered planning for smarter construction.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google GenAI SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20GenAI%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

1. Turning AI-generated ideas into usable architecture :-

-One of our biggest challenges was getting an AI model to generate architectural concepts that could be translated into consistent 2D and 3D representations.
-Simply asking an AI model to generate a house often resulted in generic or repetitive rectangular structures.
-We addressed this by moving towards a structured architecture:
[User Requirements → AI Design Specification → Validation → 2D Blueprint + 3D Model]
-Instead of allowing the AI to directly generate arbitrary geometry, the AI produces structured architectural information that our application can interpret.

---

2. Keeping the blueprint and 3D model consistent :-

-Another challenge was ensuring that the generated blueprint and 3D house represent the same design.
-We designed the system around a shared structured design specification so that the same architectural information can drive both:
  a) 2D floor-plan generation
  b) 3D architectural massing
-This helps prevent the blueprint and 3D visualisation from becoming two unrelated outputs.

---

3. Making construction calculations reliable :-

-We did not want an LLM to freely invent construction costs, quantities, or mathematical calculations.
-Therefore, we separated AI interpretation from deterministic construction calculations.
-The AI handles design reasoning and recommendations, while the calculation engine handles construction mathematics using explicit assumptions and inputs.
-This makes the system more transparent and gives us a path to replace demo assumptions with verified regional construction data.

---

4. AI API security :-

-We also had to solve the problem of securely integrating Gemini without exposing the API key in the browser.
-NexBuild uses a server-side API proxy so that the Gemini API key remains in environment variables and is never placed in client-side `VITE_` variables.

---

5. Generating designs dynamically

-Creating multiple meaningful architectural concepts instead of repeatedly displaying the same model was another challenge.
-We introduced structured design generation with unique design specifications and generation states so that concepts can eventually be regenerated, compared, saved, and revisited.

---

6. Building a useful prototype while keeping the architecture extensible :-

-Because construction estimation depends heavily on regional rates, standards, and building practices, we avoided presenting demo assumptions as authoritative construction data.
-The architecture therefore includes a future retrieval layer for verified sources such as CPWD and BIS data, allowing the prototype to evolve towards a more reliable construction intelligence platform.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem

Building a home is one of the biggest financial decisions people make, yet the planning process is often based on rough estimates, scattered information, and heavy dependence on contractors.

Homeowners commonly struggle with:

- Unclear construction cost estimates
- Unexpected budget overruns
- Difficulty estimating material quantities
- Poor visibility into labour and construction timelines
- Difficulty comparing materials and design alternatives
- Limited understanding of how architectural decisions affect cost
- No simple way to visualise a proposed home before construction begins

# Our Solution

"NexBuild" is an AI-powered construction co-pilot designed to help homeowners plan and understand their construction project before breaking ground.

Users can provide project details such as plot size, location, floors, rooms, budget, construction quality, and design preferences. NexBuild combines AI-assisted architectural planning with deterministic construction calculations to provide:

- Construction cost estimation
- Material quantity and cost estimation
- Budget allocation
- Labour and timeline estimation
- AI-powered cost optimisation suggestions
- Alternative design concepts
- 2D blueprint generation
- Interactive 3D home visualisation
- Project-aware AI assistance
- Scenario-based planning and comparison

The goal is to turn the traditional process of "estimate → guess → build" into:

"Plan → Visualise → Estimate → Optimise → Build."

NexBuild is designed to help homeowners make better-informed decisions earlier, when changes are significantly easier and less expensive to make.

### AgriNova
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agrinova-1d14) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/MdAfxoT2f2M?feature=shared) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeStorm%202026%20#2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codestorm-week2-2026.devfolio.co)

> Smart Farming. Sustainable Future.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Artificial Intelligence](https://img.shields.io/badge/Artificial%20Intelligence-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was integrating multiple features into a single, seamless platform. Combining AI-based crop disease detection, weather services, farm finance management, government schemes, multilingual support, and drone-assisted precision spraying required careful system design and API integration.

Another challenge was obtaining a diverse and high-quality dataset for training the crop disease detection model. We addressed this by using publicly available agricultural datasets, preprocessing the images, and optimizing the model to improve prediction accuracy.

Designing an interface that would be simple enough for farmers with different levels of digital literacy was also challenging. We overcame this by adopting a clean, intuitive UI and incorporating support for 22 regional languages to improve accessibility.

Finally, ensuring that the platform remained scalable and modular was a key focus. We designed the architecture so that future technologies such as IoT sensors, satellite imagery, and advanced drone automation can be integrated without major changes to the existing system.

**The problem it solves**

Farmers often struggle with delayed crop disease detection, excessive pesticide usage, unpredictable weather, rising cultivation costs, and limited access to reliable agricultural information. Existing digital solutions are fragmented, requiring farmers to use multiple applications for different needs, which makes decision-making difficult and time-consuming.

AgriNova addresses these challenges by providing a single AI-powered platform that enables early crop disease detection, personalized treatment recommendations, weather intelligence, drone-based precision pesticide spraying, farm finance management, government scheme discovery, and agricultural news. By bringing these services together, it helps farmers make faster, data-driven decisions, reduce crop losses, optimize resource usage, lower cultivation costs, and adopt more sustainable farming practices.

> AI FIR Assistant for Smart Case Analysis.

![MEAN STACK](https://img.shields.io/badge/MEAN%20STACK-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

#Challenges We Ran Into ---
Building an AI-assisted FIR decision support system involved several technical and domain-specific challenges.
1. Mapping complaints to legal sections
Victim statements are often written in free-form language with incomplete details. Accurately identifying the cybercrime category and suggesting relevant BNS and IT Act sections required careful prompt engineering and rule validation to reduce incorrect recommendations.
2. Handling incomplete complaint data
Many complaints lacked critical information such as bank account details, transaction IDs, timestamps, or communication evidence. We solved this by adding a *Missing Facts* module that identifies absent information before report generation.
3. Generating actionable outputs
Instead of returning only a crime classification, we wanted the system to produce outputs useful for police officers. We designed additional modules for:
- Suggested FIR sections
- Evidence checklist
- Immediate actions
- Case caveats
- Downloadable investigation report
 4. Balancing AI with legal reliability
LLMs can occasionally hallucinate or overgeneralize legal advice. To address this, we positioned the application as a **decision-support tool**, included confidence indicators, and added clear disclaimers that all suggested legal sections must be verified by the Investigating Officer.
5. Creating an intuitive interface
The application had to remain simple enough for quick complaint intake while presenting a large amount of legal information. We redesigned the UI multiple times to organize the workflow into **Overview → Intake → Analysis → FIR Sections**, making the results easier to review.
6. Report generation
Generating a clean, printable report containing the complaint summary, classification, legal sections, evidence checklist, and recommendations required careful formatting to ensure consistency and readability.

**The problem it solves**

#The Problem It Solves ---
Law enforcement officers often receive cybercrime complaints in unstructured, natural language. Converting these victim statements into a legally accurate FIR is time-consuming and requires identifying the correct crime category, applicable legal sections, missing information, and required evidence.

FIR Assistant streamlines this process by using AI to analyze complaint narratives and generate structured decision support. It helps officers:

- Classify cybercrime complaints into the appropriate category.
- Suggest relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Information Technology (IT) Act.
- Highlight missing facts required for a complete FIR.
- Generate an evidence collection checklist.
- Recommend immediate actions for investigators and victims.
- Produce a downloadable case assessment report.

By reducing manual effort and improving consistency, the system enables faster complaint intake, better documentation, and more informed decision-making. It is designed as a decision-support tool to assist investigators—not replace legal judgment—with all suggested sections requiring verification by the investigating officer.
