### BhoomiSense
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bhoomisense-0108) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://bhoomi-sense.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MicroCraft%20--%20ArcNight-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://microcarft-arcnight.devfolio.co)

> Turning Satellite Intelligence to Farmer Decisions

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Router-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building BhoomiSense required us to integrate multiple independent data systems into a seamless experience.

One of our biggest challenges was combining satellite imagery, weather information, and market intelligence into a single advisory that remained accurate, understandable, and actionable. Each data source used different formats, update frequencies, and levels of granularity, which made real-time data fusion difficult.

Working with geospatial data introduced additional complexity. Generating NDVI-based crop health insights, rendering field overlays on interactive maps, and supporting custom field polygons required significant experimentation and optimization to maintain performance and usability.

Another challenge was designing an interface suitable for both technical reviewers and real farmers. We wanted to avoid overwhelming users with charts and raw metrics while still exposing the intelligence generated by the platform. This led us to redesign several components and focus on concise AI-generated action plans, visual indicators, and multilingual voice guidance.

We also faced challenges in creating a smooth user journey across multiple modules including crop health analytics, yield prediction, crop diagnostics, planning, and market intelligence. Ensuring consistency in design, navigation, and data flow across the platform required continuous iteration.

Other Technical issues:
## 1. The Leaflet `removeChild` crash

The hardest bug in the project. When navigating between pages, React unmounted and remounted the `MapLayer` component. Leaflet's internal DOM tree doesn't survive React unmount cycles — every navigation triggered a `NotFoundError: Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node'` that crashed the entire app into the ErrorBoundary.

**Fix:** We moved `MapLayer` out of the route tree entirely, rendering it once at the `App` level and never unmounting it. Visibility is controlled via CSS `visibility: hidden` and `pointer-events: none` — Leaflet never knows the page changed.

## 2. NDVI always returning 0.55

The Sentinel-2 STAC API query was failing silently — the cloud-cover filter was too strict for many Indian locations, returning zero features. Every call hit the catch block and returned our hardcoded fallback of `Array(144).fill(0.55)`.

**Fix 1:** Added a missing `centerNDVI` variable that was referenced but never defined, causing a `ReferenceError` that bypassed the real data path.

**Fix 2:** Rewrote the fallback to generate realistic spatially-varied NDVI from a deterministic seed based on `lat × lon`, so every pin location now produces a unique, physically plausible field grid even when satellite data is unavailable.

## 3. GSAP ScrollTrigger vs Lenis scroll conflict

The cinematic landing scroll worked perfectly with a mouse scrollbar but was completely non-functional with a trackpad or keyboard. The `ScrollTrigger` pin was fighting Lenis smooth-scroll, which was intercepting scroll events before GSAP could receive them.

**Fix:** Disabled Lenis entirely on the `/` route. ScrollTrigger owns the landing page scroll exclusively. On all other pages, Lenis runs normally.

## 4. Text-to-speech failing silently

The TTS button appeared to work — it triggered the `synth.speak()` call — but produced no audio. Chrome requires a small gap after `synth.cancel()` before a new utterance can be queued. Calling speak immediately after cancel was silently dropped.

**Fix:** Added a 50ms `setTimeout` between cancel and the next `speak()` call. We also added proper voice loading via the `voiceschanged` event (voices are loaded asynchronously in most browsers) and set the correct BCP-47 language tag (`hi-IN`, `mr-IN`, `pa-IN`, `ta-IN`) on the utterance so the correct voice is selected.

## 5. Vite proxy not configured

All `/api/*` calls returned 404 in development because Vite's dev server didn't know to forward them to the Express backend on port 5000. This only manifested after we moved the backend to a separate process.

**Fix:** Added a `proxy` configuration to `vite.config.js` forwarding all `/api` traffic to `http://localhost:5000`.

Through multiple development cycles, testing sessions, and UI refinements, we were able to transform a collection of complex agricultural datasets into a unified decision-support system that feels intuitive, responsive, and impactful.

**The problem it solves**

India has 120 million smallholder farmers. ISRO and NASA publish thousands of satellite datasets covering every farm in the country — 10-metre resolution crop health imagery, soil moisture readings, rainfall forecasts, pest outbreak signatures. All of it is free. None of it reaches a farmer.

The data sits behind research portals built for scientists, not growers. A farmer in Bihar has no way to know that his field's NDVI dropped to 0.31 last Tuesday — which means severe crop stress — or that a pest outbreak signature appeared in the north-east quadrant of his plot.

**BhoomiSense is the last-mile translation layer.**

Drop a pin anywhere on a live satellite map of India. In 8 seconds you get:

- **NDVI crop health grid** — a 12×12 colour-coded overlay on your field from real Sentinel-2 imagery, showing which patches are healthy, stressed, or at risk
- **AI-generated 3-day action plan** — specific instructions for today, tomorrow, and day 3 based on fused satellite + NASA POWER soil moisture + live Mandi market prices
- **Voice readout in 5 languages** — Hindi, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil, English via Web Speech API
- **180-day season planner** — a drag-scrollable crop calendar generated by Mistral AI, anchored to real historical NASA rainfall data for the exact location
- **AI yield predictor** — predicts tons/hectare based on live NDVI + moisture + temperature, with an interactive What-If slider (change irrigation level, see yield change instantly)
- **Crop Doctor** — upload a leaf photo, get AI disease diagnosis with treatment steps and urgency tags
- **Market intelligence** — live Mandi prices, 7-day price chart, sell-window calendar, and a live profit calculator

**Who uses it:**
- Smallholder farmers who can't afford agronomic consultants (₹0 cost)
- Agricultural extension officers who can cover more ground with data-backed visits
- Agri-fintech platforms that need field-level crop health for loan underwriting
- State agriculture departments monitoring district-level crop stress at scale

### SpaceTracker
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/spacefarer-bb16) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MicroCraft%20--%20ArcNight-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://microcarft-arcnight.devfolio.co)

> Your natural gateway to the stars.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![POSTGIS](https://img.shields.io/badge/POSTGIS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Overcoming API Outages with Autonomous Fallbacks
The Hurdle: During heavy synchronization cycles against remote aerospace endpoints, the system would periodically stall or reject queries if rate limits were reached or service degradation occurred. This created dangerous gaps in our relational local telemetry charts.
The Solution: We engineered a lazy-loading architecture inside our backend data engine (tle.service.ts). Instead of relying exclusively on batch crons, the application tracks the relative expiration state of local entries. If a user queries an asset and the local records are missing or older than a specific threshold, the application executes an on-demand micro-fetch hook directly to public alternative streams like CelesTrak, ensuring continuous operational availability.

2. Resolving Strict Union Types across AI SDK Providers
The Hurdle: While building out our polymorphic AI orchestration wrapper, we introduced a major compilation bug where TypeScript consistently threw TS2339 errors: "Property 'function' does not exist on type 'ChatCompletionMessageToolCall'". This was caused by modern changes to LLM vendor libraries splitting automated payloads into strict discriminating unions (distinguishing standard function definitions from alternative developer-centric options).
The Solution: We decoupled and reinforced our provider integration layer (e.g., inside openai.provider.ts and groq.provider.ts). By implementing a precise type guard architecture that explicitly evaluates tc.type === 'function' before mapping array arrays, we successfully narrowed the compiler's inference, satisfying the engine's strict structural requirements while maintaining pristine execution security.

3. Namespace Typing Imbalances between Cloned Packages
The Hurdle: While mirroring the internal OpenAI tooling schemas into our high-speed Groq endpoint layer, TypeScript surfaced a TS2694 compilation error stating that the Groq chat namespace had no exported member named ChatCompletionCreateParamsNonStreaming.
The Solution: Rather than applying blind type coercion, we analyzed the structural export layout of the underlying vendor sdk, mapping it directly to the native Groq.Chat.CompletionCreateParams interface type parameters. This satisfied the specific package parameters and cleared our production compiler pipeline.

**The problem it solves**

Managing and interpreting space debris and satellite data is a massive technical challenge. Traditional aerospace tracking databases rely heavily on complex, raw Two-Line Element (TLE) coordinate streams that are difficult for developers, researchers, and everyday enthusiasts to visualize or dynamically manipulate. Furthermore, single data registries often experience missing information, regional bottlenecks, or system downtime.

SpaceTracker simplifies orbital logistics through several key real-time enhancements:

Dynamic Visualization over Static Logs: By converting mathematical line arrays into live rendering calculations, it renders a high-fidelity 3D digital twin of the Earth. Users can visually monitor ground tracks, shadows, and paths instantly without performing manual propagation calculations.

Automated Data Continuity: Instead of relying on a fragile single-source configuration, SpaceTracker sets up an intelligent multi-registry data retrieval layer. If the primary telemetry provider faces downtime or contains stale history, the system automatically redirects and extracts real-time updates from alternative providers to keep information current.

Bridging Aerospace Telemetry with Natural Language: Rather than forcing users to write database query overrides to locate space entities, an autonomous AI assistant acts as a natural language compiler. Users can ask complex contextual questions (e.g., forecasting next-pass parameters over precise tracking positions), and the system dynamically intercepts the intent and executes proper programmatic backend tools.

Team **HackOff** -- Vedant Jadhav, [Akshit Singh](https://github.com/akshit369-rgb), [Swastik Basu](https://github.com/SPBasu-win), Rishi Raj Chowdhury

### Overshare
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/overshare-a9e5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/lucario-1-7/Overshare) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MicroCraft%20--%20ArcNight-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://microcarft-arcnight.devfolio.co)

> Turn your digital footprints into useful insights!

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced was designing a system that could combine outputs from multiple independent components—face detection, OCR, PII extraction, metadata analysis, and digital-footprint discovery—without creating a tightly coupled and difficult-to-maintain codebase. Early on, each module produced data in a different format, making it difficult to correlate findings and generate meaningful risk assessments. To solve this, we introduced a standardized Signal schema that every component outputs to, regardless of the underlying model or technology. This allowed us to build the exposure graph, risk engine, attack-path generation, and recommendation system on top of a common representation, making the platform significantly more modular, extensible, and reliable while also simplifying debugging and future feature additions.

**The problem it solves**

People share photos, screenshots, usernames, and personal information online every day without realizing how much can be inferred from them.

A single post may seem harmless, but attackers rarely look at information in isolation. They combine small clues from multiple sources to build a much larger profile of a person.

This can lead to:

 Targeted phishing attacks
 Doxxing and privacy leaks
 Social engineering attacks
 Identity exposure
 Workplace information leaks
 Location tracking and stalking risks
 Oversharing across multiple platforms

The Gap in Existing Solutions

Most existing privacy tools only tell users what information is visible.

Overshare helps users understand what becomes possible when that information is connected together.

### Areapulse
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/areapulse-f28f) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://areapulse-a1k2.onrender.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeStorm%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codestorm-week1-2026.devfolio.co)

> A Smart civic-issue tracking and resolution system

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gunicorn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gunicorn-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Urban civic issues — potholes, garbage overflow, broken streetlights, water leaks — go unreported or unresolved for weeks because reporting is friction-heavy and there's no accountability loop between citizens and government authorities.

AreaPulse fixes this with a full-stack civic intelligence platform:

- **AR Camera Scanner** — Point your phone at any civic issue; Groq Llama-4 Vision auto-detects, classifies, and draws a bounding box over it in real time
- **WhatsApp Bot** — Send a photo to our Twilio number; AI files the report with zero app install required
- **Live Map** — FR24-style real-time map of all issues across Delhi with severity markers, SLA timers, and crowd escalation
- **Government Dashboard** — Officers see only their department's issues, sorted by SLA breach urgency, with one-click status updates and automatic WhatsApp pings to citizens
- **AI Complaint Drafting** — Groq generates formal complaint letters to the right Delhi authority (MCD, DJB, PWD, BSES) in English or Hindi
- **Spam & Duplicate Detection** — AI filters joke/test submissions; geographic radius deduplication merges nearby reports automatically
- **Public Stats** — Anonymous resolution rates, SLA breach rates, and department performance visible to all citizens

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **AR bounding box accuracy** — Llama-4-Scout returns normalized 0-100 bbox coordinates, but mapping these onto a live video canvas with correct aspect ratio took significant trial and error, especially on phones with different aspect ratios.

2. **Groq JSON reliability** — Vision models occasionally return malformed JSON or wrap output in markdown fences. We built a multi-stage extractor (direct parse → strip fences → regex fallback) to handle every case gracefully.

3. **WhatsApp media download** — Twilio CDN requires HTTP Basic Auth to download message attachments; standard `urllib` without auth returns 401 silently. Switched to `requests` with explicit `auth=(SID, TOKEN)` to fix this.

4. **Camera access on mobile** — iOS Safari requires HTTPS strictly; plain HTTP silently blocks `getUserMedia`. We had to document ngrok tunneling for local phone testing and ensure Render deploys used HTTPS.

Team **Nexons** -- [Shashwat Shukla](https://github.com/shoyo-shashwat), [garv chopra](https://github.com/GarvChopra)

> Oralia is an AI 3D globe preserving global legends

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![GraphQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/GraphQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mediapipe](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mediapipe-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web-Speech-API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web--Speech--API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Glob.gl](https://img.shields.io/badge/Glob.gl-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges & How I Solved Them

One of the biggest hurdles was making the AI-generated experience feel consistent and meaningful instead of random or disconnected.

Because Oralia combines:

* AI-generated storytelling,
* an interactive 3D globe,
* narration,
* and user-submitted cultural stories,

it was difficult to keep the experience coherent across different countries and story types. Early versions often produced outputs that felt too generic, repetitive, or disconnected from the cultural context.

Another challenge was working with AI-assisted development tools. Since parts of the interface and structure were generated iteratively through prompting, small prompt changes could unexpectedly affect layouts, styling, or functionality. Managing this required constant refinement and careful testing.

I solved these issues by:

* breaking the project into smaller modular components,
* refining prompts incrementally instead of changing everything at once,
* creating a clearer structure for how stories are processed,
* and adding stronger constraints to guide the AI toward more culturally grounded outputs.

I also simplified some planned features to focus on delivering a polished core experience rather than trying to build too many systems at once during the hackathon timeline.

Through this process, I learned that building with AI is less about pressing a button and more about direction, iteration, testing, and continuously shaping the final experience.

**The problem it solves**

## What People Can Use Oralia For

### Cultural Discovery

Users can explore myths, folklore, traditions, and oral histories from countries around the world through an interactive 3D globe. Instead of reading fragmented articles online, users experience stories in a more immersive and engaging way.

### Preserving Endangered Oral Traditions

Many local legends and spoken histories disappear over time because they are never digitally documented. Oralia helps preserve these cultural memories by allowing communities to contribute stories that become part of a living global archive.

### Education & Learning

Students, teachers, and researchers can use Oralia as an interactive learning tool for history, geography, anthropology, and cultural studies. Complex cultural information becomes easier to understand through AI-enhanced narration and storytelling.

### Multilingual Storytelling

AI can help translate and adapt stories into multiple languages, making local traditions accessible to a global audience while reducing language barriers.

### Easier Cultural Contribution

Traditionally, documenting oral history requires writing, editing, archiving, and publishing knowledge manually. Oralia simplifies this process:

1. Users submit a story or tradition.
2. AI refines and structures the narrative.
3. The story becomes an immersive experience with narration and visuals.

This lowers the barrier for communities to preserve and share their heritage digitally.

### Tourism & Cultural Exploration

Travelers can use Oralia to discover legends, traditions, and historical context connected to places before visiting them, creating deeper cultural understanding beyond standard travel guides.

### Safer Long-Term Digital Preservation

Oral traditions are vulnerable to being forgotten when older generations pass away or when records are lost. By storing stories digitally, Oralia creates a more durable and accessible preservation system that can continue growing over time.

### Community-Driven Global Archive

Unlike static encyclopedias, Oralia allows people from different cultures to continuously contribute stories, making the platform evolve into a collaborative map of human culture and identity.

### AI-Assisted Story Enhancement

Instead of replacing human stories, AI helps:

* organize narratives,
* improve readability,
* generate narration,
* create immersive presentation formats,
* and make stories easier for younger generations to engage with.

This helps transform traditional storytelling into a modern interactive experience without losing its cultural meaning.

> Smarter Contracts. Safer Decisions.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTTP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTTP%20server-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Netlify](https://img.shields.io/badge/Netlify-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced while building ContractCompass was integrating AI-powered contract analysis at scale. Most advanced legal document analysis models require access to premium AI APIs, which operate on a token-based pricing system. During development, we frequently encountered token limitations and API usage costs when processing lengthy contracts, as legal documents often contain thousands of words. This made testing and debugging difficult because even small changes required additional API calls.

To overcome this challenge, we optimized our prompts to reduce token consumption, implemented document chunking to process large contracts in smaller sections, and added caching mechanisms to avoid repeated API requests for the same content. We also developed fallback handling for API rate limits and token exhaustion, ensuring that users receive meaningful feedback instead of application errors. These improvements significantly reduced costs, improved response times, and made the platform more reliable when analyzing large legal documents.

**The problem it solves**

ContractCompass addresses the challenge of understanding and reviewing legal contracts efficiently. Legal agreements are often lengthy, complex, and filled with technical language that can be difficult for individuals and businesses to interpret. Manually reviewing contracts requires significant time, expertise, and financial resources, while important risks, unfavorable clauses, or compliance issues may be overlooked. ContractCompass uses artificial intelligence to analyze contracts instantly, helping users identify potential risks, check legal compliance, understand contract terms in simple language, and receive suggestions for clause improvements. By automating the contract review process, it reduces the time, cost, and effort involved in legal analysis while enabling users to make more informed decisions with greater confidence.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/studyhelix-c068) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://studyhelix.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/nKpuuFjhyJ8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-CodeStorm%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://codestorm-week1-2026.devfolio.co)

> Study Smarter, Achieve Better

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Study Helix tackles a major pain point for students: managing their academic journey effectively. Students struggle with:

• **Scattered study resources**: Notes, schedules, and materials are all over the place
• **Lack of personalized guidance**: Generic study methods don't work for everyone
• **Time management**: Balancing multiple subjects and deadlines is overwhelming
• **Learning gaps**: Students don't know where they're falling behind until it's too late

Study Helix unifies everything into one AI-powered platform where students can:

✅ Plan their studies intelligently with AI-suggested schedules
✅ Get personalized tutoring from an AI tutor 24/7
✅ Track progress through analytics and insights
✅ Upload and organize study materials
✅ Boost productivity with built-in tools

The result? Students study smarter, not harder, and see measurable improvement in their academic performance.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Study Helix came with several technical and UX hurdles:

**Authentication & State Management**: Implementing secure login with localStorage was tricky - we had to balance security with simplicity for a web app. We overcame this by using proper data serialization and validation.

**AI Integration Complexity**: Integrating AI tutor functionality without a backend initially seemed impossible. We solved this by designing a modular architecture that could easily connect to AI APIs later while maintaining offline functionality.

**Responsive Design Across Devices**: Getting the sidebar navigation and dashboard to work smoothly on mobile and desktop required extensive media query testing and responsive redesign. We fixed this by using flexible CSS grid layouts and testing on multiple devices.

**Data Persistence**: Managing user sessions and study data across page refreshes was complex. We implemented a robust localStorage system with error handling and JSON serialization to ensure data consistency.

**Performance Optimization**: The app had to load quickly even with multiple pages and features. We optimized by lazy-loading components, minimizing CSS, and structuring JavaScript efficiently.

These challenges taught us the importance of scalable architecture from the start! 🚀

> Turn boring logs into a living 3D battlefield.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Reactstrap](https://img.shields.io/badge/Reactstrap-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

The Core Challenge

Cybersecurity teams are drowning in data.

Every day, organizations generate billions of security events — firewall logs, intrusion attempts, traffic anomalies, vulnerability scans. Traditional security dashboards present this data as endless tables of IP addresses, static charts and graphs, text-heavy log files, and overwhelming spreadsheets.

The result? Critical threats get buried in noise. Security analysts suffer from alert fatigue. Decision-makers can't quickly grasp the severity of attacks.

How SentinelX Solves This

Instant Visual Threat Assessment

Instead of reading through thousands of log entries, security teams can see threats as 3D terrain where critical attacks appear as towering red spikes, understand severity at a glance through color-coded visualization (Cyan = Safe, Amber = Warning, Red = Critical), and identify patterns spatially as distributed attacks create wave patterns across the terrain.

Use Case: A SOC analyst uploads a DDoS attack log. Instead of parsing JSON, they instantly see a violent red landscape with camera shake effects — immediate understanding that this is a critical incident requiring emergency response.

Real-Time Incident Response

Traditional tools require opening multiple dashboards, cross-referencing data sources, manual threat correlation, and time-consuming analysis.

SentinelX enables drag-and-drop log analysis where you can upload any JSON security log in seconds, AI-powered insights with automatic threat classification and confidence scores, actionable recommendations with immediate next steps based on threat level, and simulation testing to test DDoS and vulnerability scenarios before they happen.

Use Case: During a live security incident, an analyst drags the latest threat intelligence feed into SentinelX. The terrain morphs in real-time, AI provides a 96% confidence assessment, and recommends isolating compromised nodes — all within 3 seconds.

Executive Communication

The Problem: CISOs struggle to communicate cyber risk to non-technical executives and board members.

SentinelX makes it easy through cinematic presentations showing live threat landscapes in board meetings, no technical jargon with visual metaphors anyone can understand, confidence metrics with clear percentage-based risk scores, and before/after comparisons by uploading baseline vs. attack logs to show impact.

Use Case: A CISO presents quarterly security posture. Instead of PowerPoint slides, they upload Q1 logs (calm cyan terrain) vs. Q2 breach attempt (violent red spikes). The board immediately understands the severity and approves increased security budget.

Security Training and Education

Perfect for cybersecurity bootcamps where students visualize attack patterns, red team exercises to simulate attacks and see defensive responses, incident response drills to practice with realistic threat scenarios, and security awareness training so non-technical staff understand cyber threats.

Use Case: A university cybersecurity course uses SentinelX to teach students about DDoS attacks. Students upload different attack vectors (SYN flood, UDP flood, HTTP flood) and watch how each creates unique terrain patterns — making abstract concepts tangible.

Threat Intelligence Analysis

Traditional Approach: Parse threat feeds manually, correlate indicators of compromise, assess severity through spreadsheets, and generate reports over hours or days.

SentinelX Approach: Upload threat intelligence JSON for instant visualization, compare multiple feeds by uploading sequentially to see evolution, use pattern recognition where spatial clustering reveals coordinated attacks, and export insights to share visual reports with stakeholders.

Use Case: A threat intelligence analyst receives feeds from 5 different sources about a new botnet. They upload each feed to SentinelX, watching the terrain build up. Overlapping spike patterns reveal the botnet's true scale — 12,000+ compromised nodes across 47 countries.

Who Benefits?

Security Operations Centers (SOCs) get faster triage of security alerts, reduced mean time to detect, and lower analyst burnout from alert fatigue.

Incident Response Teams benefit from rapid threat assessment during active breaches, clear communication with stakeholders, and simulation of attack scenarios.

CISOs and Security Leaders gain executive-friendly risk visualization, board presentation material, and budget justification through impact demonstration.

Penetration Testers and Red Teams can visualize attack effectiveness, demonstrate vulnerabilities to clients, and create compelling security reports.

Educators and Students have an interactive learning tool for hands-on threat analysis and portfolio-worthy projects.

Compliance and Audit Teams get visual evidence of security posture, historical threat analysis, and regulatory reporting support.

Measurable Impact

Time to Assess Threat: Traditional tools take 15-30 minutes, SentinelX take

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

Building SentinelX was an intense journey with several critical technical hurdles that pushed my understanding of React, Three.js, and performance optimization. Here are the major challenges I faced and how I solved them.

Performance Bottleneck with 400 Individual Mesh Components

The Initial Problem:
My first approach was to render each terrain block as a separate mesh component using array.map(). With 400 blocks (20x20 grid), each with its own geometry, material, and animation logic, the frame rate dropped to 15-20 FPS. The React reconciliation process was re-rendering components on every frame, causing massive performance degradation.

The Breakthrough:
I switched to instanced rendering using Three.js InstancedMesh. Instead of 400 separate meshes, I created a single mesh with 400 instances. Each instance shares the same geometry and material but has its own transformation matrix. This reduced draw calls from 400 to 1 and brought the frame rate back to a stable 60 FPS.

Implementation Details:
I used useFrame to update all 400 instance matrices in a single loop, storing height values in a Float32Array for efficient memory access. The color updates also use setColorAt() to modify instance colors without creating new materials.

Key Lesson: When dealing with repetitive 3D objects, always use instancing. Individual components don't scale.

File Upload Component Not Responding to Clicks

The Initial Problem:
Users couldn't upload JSON files. The file input was completely unresponsive. I had positioned an invisible input element with opacity: 0 over a styled div, but clicks weren't registering. The z-index layering was fighting with Framer Motion's transform properties and the glassmorphism backdrop-filter effects.

Debugging Process:
I added console.log statements to the onChange handler — nothing fired. I checked the browser dev tools and saw the input was being rendered but had zero dimensions. The parent container's pointer-events were interfering with the input's click area.

The Solution:
I completely redesigned the upload component using a semantic HTML label element wrapping a hidden input. This approach uses the browser's native label-for-input association, which is more reliable than z-index tricks. I also added three upload methods: click to browse, drag-and-drop on the sidebar button, and drag-and-drop anywhere on the screen with a full-screen overlay.

Code Change:
Changed from div with absolute positioned input to label with display: none input. Added onDragOver, onDragLeave, and onDrop handlers at the root div level to capture files dropped anywhere on the application.

Key Lesson: Don't fight the browser. Use semantic HTML and native behaviors instead of CSS hacks.

Terrain Animating Before User Interaction

The Initial Problem:
The 3D terrain was constantly animating with sine wave patterns even when no data was loaded. This made the application feel like it was showing fake data rather than being a true data visualization tool. Judges would see movement and assume it was just a demo, not a functional analysis tool.

The Design Flaw:
My useFrame loop was calculating animated heights for all blocks regardless of whether the user had uploaded any data or clicked any buttons. The terrain was essentially running a screensaver mode.

The Solution:
I introduced a hasInteracted state that starts as false. The terrain renders as a completely flat, static grid (height = 0.5) until the user uploads a JSON file, clicks a threat level button, or triggers a simulation. Only after interaction does the terrain come alive with dynamic animations based on the actual threat state.

Implementation:
Added hasInteracted prop to ThreatTopography component. Modified the useFrame loop to check if (hasInteracted) before applying sine wave calculations. Set hasInteracted to true in handleFileUpload, handleUpdateState, and handleSimulation functions.

Key Lesson: Data visualizations should be silent until they have data to show. Static states communicate "waiting for input" better than random animations.

Camera Shake Effect Causing Motion Sickness

The Initial Problem:
When users uploaded critical threat files or triggered the DDoS simulation, the camera shake was too aggressive. The random offset values were too large and the shake lasted too long, causing disorientation and making the UI unusable during critical moments.

User Feedback:
During testing, I noticed the shake made it impossible to read the AI insights panel or click buttons. The effect was supposed to convey urgency but instead created frustration.

The Solution:
I implemented a smooth damping system using THREE.MathUtils.lerp() to gradually reduce the shake intensity over 1.2 seconds. I also reduced the shake magnitude from 2.0 to 1.0 for critical states and 0.45 for warning states. The camera position lerps back to the original position with a factor of 0.08, creating a smooth recovery.

Technical Implementation:
Created a shake

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Most digital learning and examination platforms depend on stable internet connectivity and centralized servers. In schools, colleges, remote areas, large campuses, or emergency situations, poor connectivity can disrupt exams, classroom communication, and resource sharing.

Our solution uses a **Decentralized P2P Mesh Network** that allows devices to communicate directly without internet access. This creates a reliable offline learning environment where teachers and students remain connected.

### What Can It Be Used For?

* **Offline Examinations:** Conduct and manage exams without internet dependency.
* **Digital Classrooms:** Share announcements, notes, assignments, and learning materials in real time.
* **Collaborative Learning:** Enable peer-to-peer communication and resource sharing among students.
* **Remote & Rural Education:** Support educational activities in areas with limited or no internet access.
* **Emergency Connectivity:** Maintain classroom operations during network outages.

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier

* Eliminates the need for internet during exams and classroom sessions.
* Reduces dependence on centralized servers and network infrastructure.
* Provides reliable communication through decentralized peer-to-peer connections.
* Enables secure distribution of exam papers and collection of responses.
* Ensures uninterrupted learning and assessment in challenging connectivity environments.

**Result:** A secure, scalable, and internet-independent platform for modern education.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenge 1: The "Android Permission Hell" (API 31+ & 33+ Compatibility)
*   **The Hurdle:** 
    Google’s Nearby Connections API is incredibly powerful, but it requires a strict set of runtime permissions to operate offline: standard Bluetooth, Bluetooth Admin, Fine/Coarse Location, BLE Scan, BLE Connect, BLE Advertise, and Nearby Wi-Fi Devices (introduced in Android 13). 
    
    Attempting to request these one by one using standard Flutter permission packages resulted in a terrible user experience—showing up to 5 consecutive system dialog prompts. If a user took too long to click "Allow" or clicked outside a prompt, the connection engine would immediately timeout, resulting in failed discovery.
*   **The Solution:** 
    We bypassed standard Flutter plugins for permission handling and built a custom native Android **Platform Channel (`MethodChannel('meshexam/permissions')`)**. On startup, the app makes a single call to native Kotlin/Java code that groups all required location, Bluetooth, and nearby device permissions into one unified native permission request dialog. This increased connection success rates dramatically and smoothed out the setup workflow.

---

### Challenge 2: Infinite Packet Looping (Network Flooding) in Mesh Relays
*   **The Hurdle:** 
    Since the application uses a peer-to-peer (P2P) mesh model where every student node acts as a relay for others, broadcasting a packet (e.g., a teacher sending a new exam question) created circular routing loops. Node A would relay the question to Node B, B would relay to C, and C would relay it back to A, causing an infinite packet storm that saturated the local offline bandwidth and quickly crashed the app.
*   **The Solution:** 
    We implemented a robust **Payload Deduplication & Hop-Limiting (TTL)** system in the custom `MeshRouter`:
    *   **Deduplication Set:** Every message generated is assigned a unique, signed UUID. Each node maintains a high-speed memory cache (`seenMessageIds`). If an incoming payload’s ID is already present in this set, it is immediately discarded and not relayed.
    *   **Hop Count Limiter:** A `hopCount` field is embedded in every network frame. If a packet has hopped more than 10 times (`hopCount >= 10`), it is automatically dropped to prevent runaway packets.

---

### Challenge 3: Dynamic Network Churn & Eventual Consistency (Auto-Syncing)
*   **The Hurdle:** 
    In a physical room, students' device signals fluctuate, or they might temporarily turn off Bluetooth/Wi-Fi, causing nodes to leave and rejoin the mesh dynamically (churn). If a student was temporarily out of range when the teacher sent an exam question, they would completely miss that question even after returning to the mesh.
*   **The Solution:** 
    We developed two complementary systems to ensure the mesh network remains self-healing and eventually consistent:
    *   **Reconnection Sync Engine:** We implemented `_syncExistingMessagesToNewPeer()`. The moment a connection is established with a peer (either for the first time or after a disconnect), the node automatically crawls its local Hive database and replays all stored exam events and questions directly to the newly joined peer.
    *   **Dynamic Topology Timers:** To prevent stale nodes from cluttering the live interactive Network Visualizer, the `MeshRouter` broadcasts neighborhood mappings every 3 seconds. Concurrently, a background cleanup timer runs every 8 seconds, automatically purging any node not heard from within 15 seconds, ensuring the topology map reflects the live physical state of the classroom.

**Open Innovation**

**MeshExam (AetherNet)** is a textbook fit for the **Open Innovation Track** because it takes a highly advanced networking concept (Decentralized Ad-Hoc Mesh Networking) and democratizes it to solve a massive, real-world educational disparity. 

Here is how the project aligns with the core pillars of Open Innovation:

---

### 1. Solving a Global Infrastructure & Digital Divide Problem
Traditional educational technology (EdTech) platforms—like Google Classroom, Moodle, or Canvas—fundamentally assume that users have constant, high-speed internet access. This assumption excludes billions of students in rural areas, developing nations, disaster zones, or schools with severely restricted budgets.
*   **The Innovation:** MeshExam flips this paradigm. By creating a **100% offline, zero-cost digital examination environment**, it ensures that any classroom in the world can conduct modern, secure, and instant digital testing using only the smartphones already in the room.

---

### 2. Paradigm Shift: Infrastructure-Less, Collaborative Edge Computing
Instead of relying on costly, centralized servers (like AWS, Azure, or Firebase) which represent single points of failure and ongoing operational costs, MeshExam relies on the concept of **collaborative edge infrastructure**.
*   **The Innovation:** The devices themselves *are* the network. The more students that enter the room, the stronger, wider, and more resilient the network becomes. If a device goes offline or a student steps out of range, the network automatically self-heals and routes around the gap. This introduces an entirely new way of thinking about building decentralized mobile software.

---

### 3. Open-Source Blueprint for "Offline-First" P2P Applications
While MeshExam is currently tailored for classroom examinations, the core modules we built are highly abstract and highly reusable:
*   **`MeshRouter`**: A dynamic mobile ad-hoc routing protocol built on top of standard consumer hardware protocols.
*   **`SyncEngine`**: An offline eventual consistency event-sourcing model.
*   **`CryptoUtils`**: Decentralized validation to prevent payload tampering in a local environment.
*   **The Innovation:** This project acts as an open-source blueprint for developers worldwide to build other localized, offline applications—such as post-disaster messaging apps, remote research polling, or local decentralized gaming.

---

### 4. Cryptographic Trust in a Zero-Trust, Zero-Internet Environment
Establishing trust and security online is easy with third-party authentication servers (OAuth, SSL certificates). In a pure offline mesh network, the environment is inherently "zero-trust" because anyone can inject fake data.
*   **The Innovation:** By building standard cryptographic integrity (SHA-256 signing) and packet deduplication directly into local client transactions, we proved that high-stakes, secure events (like school examinations) can be run with complete data integrity and auditability—entirely offline.

> stop leaking secrets and start deploying safely

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSX](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSX-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Vaultify is a proxy-based secret isolation layer for AI applications deployed on platforms like Vercel, Netlify, and Railway.
Instead of storing real API keys in environment variables, Vaultify replaces them with proxy tokens. The real keys remain securely stored in Vaultify's vault and never reach the deployment platform.
Every request is validated, logged, and forwarded by Vaultify, which injects the real API key server-side. If a token is compromised, it can be revoked instantly without redeploying the application.
 Key Benefits
* Prevents exposure of real API keys on deployment platforms
* Eliminates the need to share sensitive `.env` files
* Supports instant key rotation and token revocation
* Provides audit logs and usage tracking for every API call
* Reduces credential breaches from major incidents to quick, manageable fixes
 Vaultify turns a credential breach from a crisis into a one-click fix.

**Challenges we ran into**

Proxy Request Handling
Forwarded requests were being malformed due to header modifications and buffered streaming responses. Fixed by preserving upstream headers and piping streams directly.

Production Decryption Failures
AES-256 decryption worked locally but failed in production because the encryption key contained a trailing newline, causing authentication failures. Resolved by normalizing the key before use.

Token Validation Race Conditions
Concurrent requests occasionally bypassed rate-limit checks, causing valid tokens to be rejected. Fixed by combining validation and counter updates into a single atomic database operation.

Most issues appeared to be security problems but were actually reliability problems. For a security proxy, reliability is part of security.

**Open Innovation**

Vaultify addresses a universal problem faced by developers and organizations: securing API keys and secrets in modern cloud deployments.

The solution is platform-agnostic and can be integrated into AI applications, SaaS products, developer tools, enterprise systems, and startup projects. By providing a simple way to isolate and protect credentials, Vaultify improves security for a wide range of industries and use cases.

Its broad applicability, scalability, and potential for adoption across different ecosystems make it a strong fit for the Open Innovation track.

**The problem it solves**

Traditional logistics systems mainly optimize delivery routes based on distance or time, which ignores business realities like profitability and payment risk.

This leads to:

High-risk COD deliveries being prioritized incorrectly
Increased delivery losses due to failed payments
Inefficient resource allocation
Lower overall profit per route
💡 PayRoute AI solves this by:

Instead of just minimizing distance, it introduces a profit-aware intelligence layer that considers:

Payment success probability
Order value
Customer reliability
Distance impact

This ensures logistics decisions are financially optimized, not just operationally optimized.

🧠 What users can use it for:
Logistics company decision-making
Delivery prioritization systems
Risk-aware dispatch planning
Business profitability analysis per route
Smart warehouse-to-customer optimization

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Normalization Problem

One major issue was combining distance, order value, and probability into a single scoring system because they were on completely different scales.

✔️ Solution:
Implemented min-max normalization so all values were scaled between 0 and 1 before calculating the Priority Score.

2. Realistic Risk Simulation

Creating believable payment success probability without using real ML data was tricky.

✔️ Solution:
Designed a hybrid heuristic model using:

Payment type (COD vs Prepaid)
Customer reliability score
Randomized noise factor for realism
3. Before vs After Comparison Logic

Initially, results were confusing because both views used the same sorting logic.

✔️ Solution:
Separated logic clearly:

BEFORE → Sorted by distance
AFTER → Sorted by Priority Score

This made the optimization impact visually obvious.

4. UI Clarity for Complex Metrics

Showing risk, revenue, and scoring together made the UI cluttered.

✔️ Solution:
Used:

Color-coded risk indicators
KPI cards
Section-based dashboard layout

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Building is no longer the bottleneck — AI has made shipping an MVP a matter of days. But that speed has exposed a more fundamental problem: most founders are building the wrong thing, or the right thing at the wrong time. The ideation phase is broken. You're either chasing trends, guessing on gut feel, or spending hours manually trawling Reddit, Hacker News, and Product Hunt trying to spot something real. The signals are everywhere, buried in frustrated comments, recurring complaint threads, and niche blog posts — but extracting a structured opportunity from raw noise is slow, inconsistent, and mostly guesswork.

OpHunt fixes the front end of the founder pipeline. Paste any URL, a Reddit thread where people are venting, a Product Hunt launch with frustrated comments, a blog post about a niche problem, and OpHunt reads it, extracts the unmet need hiding inside it, and hands you a structured brief: the gap, the target user, the MVP scope, and a path to your first 100 customers.

Beyond the URL analyzer, OpHunt runs a live idea feed, monitoring Reddit, HN, Product Hunt, and tech news 24/7 across six categories (AI Tools, Dev Tools, B2B SaaS, Fintech, Health Tech, Consumer Apps). Founders can browse free teasers and unlock a full $1 report when something clicks. So instead of stumbling on opportunities by accident, founders get a curated stream of validated signals they can act on — before writing a single line of code.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest technical headache was the deployment pipeline. The project went through multiple build configurations, React/Vite, then a pure static HTML version, and the deploy system kept rejecting builds as "default Locus starters" even when the actual OpHunt content was fully written and in the file. The container environment was also blocking npm from forking child processes (exit 126), which killed every React build attempt.

The fix was a patch fix from Locus team.

The second challenge was payments. Stripe doesn't support Nigerian accounts, which is where I'm building from. The workaround was Lemon Squeezy, they act as the merchant of record, so my customers pay them (via their Stripe account), and they pay me out via PayPal. No Nigerian Stripe account needed anywhere in the chain.

**Using LocusFounder to Build a Business!**

OpHunt wasn't just built with Locus, it was built as a business from day one using Locus as the operating system.

Locus handled the full stack: brand identity (cream canvas, Fraunces type, claymation card design), landing page, full-stack app with AI-powered URL analysis and a blurred report unlock flow, CRM, and outreach infrastructure. Every decision, pricing model, ICP, market thesis, was captured and iterated inside Locus.

The meta-irony is intentional: OpHunt helps founders find ideas worth building, and it was itself built by a founder using an AI agent to go from idea to deployed product. Locus is the reason this went from a concept to a live, paying product in days rather than months. The agent wrote the code, managed the deploys, debugged the payment integration, and kept the brand consistent across every surface. That's the track in one sentence: Locus didn't assist the build, it was the build team.

> A real-time cash dashboard for LocusFounder.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The real problem with tools like LocusFounder is that they make launching a business too easy, which leaves the human owner completely overwhelmed. 

If you use an AI agent to spin up three different shops at once, you suddenly have money moving in three different directions. You have tech bills, product costs, and marketing expenses scattered everywhere. You end up jumping between browser tabs, staring at raw code logs, and guessing your actual profit. You can't even answer the most basic question: "Did I actually make money today, or am I going broke?"

This project solves that exact human headache. It is a simple, visual command center that pulls all the confusing data from your different AI storefronts and translates it into clear, honest numbers on a single dark-mode screen. It does the messy financial math for you automatically—factoring in specific ad costs and product margins—so you can see exactly how much cash is hitting your bank account at a single glance. It turns autonomous machine chaos into peace of mind for the founder.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The Serverless Cold-Start Problem (Data Resetting)
Because this application is deployed as a serverless application on Vercel, standard global variables in Node.js tend to completely wipe out and reset whenever the server goes idle or experiences a "cold start." This meant our 900+ historical seed transactions would vanish randomly. I solved this by securely binding the in-memory ledger array directly to the Node.js global context object, forcing the database state to persist seamlessly across hot reloads and live API requests.

2. Heavy Library Bloat vs. Performance
I wanted the dashboard charts to look incredibly smooth and premium, but standard React graphing libraries are heavily bloated, slow down page load speeds, and are notoriously frustrating to style in dark mode. To keep the application lightning-fast, I chose to avoid external charting libraries entirely. Instead, I manually programmed custom mathematical coordinate calculators that map the transaction data streams straight into raw, native browser SVG vector paths. This kept the page performance close to 100% while allowing for instant fluid animations when switching storefront views.

3. Handling "Division by Zero" Crashes
When an operator switches to a brand-new storefront tenant that has zero transactions recorded yet, standard financial formulas will try to divide by zero, resulting in "NaN" (Not a Number) errors that can instantly crash the entire user interface. I had to write strict defensive validation layers across all mathematical data hooks to guarantee that if a store has zero sales, the cards gracefully fall back to displaying 0% or $0 rather than breaking the UI.

**Using LocusFounder to Build a Business!**

This project is built explicitly to support and scale businesses created via LocusFounder. 

Instead of just launching a single standalone storefront, my project serves as an Executive Portfolio Console designed for an operator who uses LocusFounder to run multiple autonomous business lines simultaneously (such as e-commerce, digital products, and consulting services). 

It maps directly into the track by listening to live transaction streams from the Locus Checkout engine via a secure serverless webhook (`/api/locus-ledger`). It automatically aggregates the data, calculates business-specific product costs (COGS) and marketing channel spend (like Google Ads vs. Apollo cold email costs), and turns raw machine logs into a single, beautifully visualized screen. It directly solves the administrative mess of running multiple AI-driven businesses, giving the human owner total financial clarity over their entire Locus portfolio at a single glance.

### agentleash
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agentleash-82c4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/MukundaKatta/agentleash) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/agentleash/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Locus'%20Paygentic%20Hackathon%20--%20#4-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://paygentic-week4.devfolio.co)

> Python safety harness for AI agents that touch mon

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents that touch money (pay-per-API calls, autonomous purchases, on-chain bots) are starting to ship in production, but the safety primitives haven't caught up. A small bug or a malicious prompt can drain a Stripe key, fan out unbounded paid LLM calls, or post to a wrong endpoint before anyone notices.

agentleash is a single Python context manager that puts a leash on each agent run:

- USD-per-run + per-call caps (token-budget-py under the hood; agent halts cleanly when cap hits)
- Egress allowlist (wildcard hostnames; e.g. *.stripe.com only)
- Optional tool-arg JSON Schema gate so bad args never reach the side-effectful function
- Append-only JSONL audit log; tool args are sha256-hashed by default so PII / secrets never land on disk

It's the dollars-side companion to birddog (egress side, also today) and pairs with agentvet / agentsnap / agenttrace.

**Challenges we ran into**

Three things ate the most time.

1. **token-budget-py API mismatch.** Tests kept failing on `BudgetPool` having no `usd_used` attribute. Fix was calling `.snapshot().usd_used` instead of reading state directly. Once I read the lib's source the API was obvious; lesson was to drop into the dep's code earlier, not later.

2. **PII in audit logs.** First version dumped tool args verbatim into the JSONL, which means a Stripe customer ID or a personal email lands in plaintext on disk. Switched to sha256-hashing each arg by default so the audit trail still proves a call happened without leaking content.

3. **Where to halt.** A naive cap check at the start of `tool()` misses the fact that the LLM has already produced output costing tokens. Moved the budget check to after the LLM call returns but before the side-effectful tool runs, so the agent halts at the latest safe point - the network/payment side-effect doesn't happen, but you don't lose the LLM output you already paid for.

**Using LocusFounder to Build a Business!**

Paygentic agents are LLM-driven workers that move money - the second a model hallucinates a billing endpoint or fans out a paid loop, the bill goes up fast. agentleash is the Python guardrail that sits inside the agent run: every tool call goes through usd_cap + call_cap + egress allowlist + optional JSON Schema arg gate, and lands in an append-only audit log (tool args sha256-hashed, no PII). It's the production safety primitive a LocusFounder-built paygentic business needs day one, not month six.

### Manoli
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trololilo-611a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/joalavedra/weather-cli) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co)

> get a quote from prediction market for your asset

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional insurance is slow, opaque, and limited to standardized products. Anyone who wants to hedge a specific real-world risk — a missed flight, a bad harvest, a geopolitical event, a volatile crypto price — has no easy way to do it.

Insurance broker solves this by turning Polymarket's deep prediction-market liquidity into an instant, chat-driven hedging desk:

- **Describe your risk in plain language.** The LLM finds the right Polymarket market for your event.
- **Get a precise quote.** The broker computes the correct YES/NO position size against your dollar exposure, including expected ROI and cost.
- **Place the trade in one click.** After explicit confirmation, it submits the on-chain order through the Polymarket CLOB — no trading UI, no manual position sizing.

In short: it converts any insurable event into an executed, on-chain hedge in seconds.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Mapping free-text risk descriptions to Polymarket markets**
Users describe risks in natural language (e.g. "I'm worried about a Bitcoin crash"). The hardest part was building a reliable routing layer that maps these descriptions to actual Polymarket market slugs across categories — weather, politics, crypto, sports, entertainment — and gracefully tells the user when no matching market exists.

**2. Correct hedge sizing math**
Computing the right YES/NO share quantity to fully offset a user's dollar exposure (not just buy an arbitrary amount) required careful `computeHedge` / `quoteFromMarket` logic accounting for current market prices and implied probabilities.

**3. Safe on-chain trading flow**
The trading flow spans wallet creation, USDC + MATIC funding, one-time CLOB approvals on Polygon, and finally order placement — all while never placing an order without explicit user confirmation in chat. Getting the state machine right and recovering gracefully from partial states (e.g. wallet funded but approvals not run) was tricky.

**4. Streaming tool calls with real-time UI state**
Integrating the AI SDK's streaming responses with live wallet/trade state updates in the Next.js UI — keeping the chat reactive while tool calls run asynchronously — required careful coordination between server actions and client components.

> Futarchy analyst

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# 🛡️ The Problem It Solves

Demo: https://share.descript.com/view/pnsbObRikUV

### The Challenge: Information Chaos & Adversarial Markets
Traders and participants in futarchic decision markets (such as **Umia**, **MetaDAO**, and **Polymarket**) operate in a high-stakes, high-noise environment. Currently, making an informed decision requires manually tracking scattered signals across Telegram, X (Twitter), Discord, GitHub activity, and on-chain movements. 

This fragmented landscape leads to critical failures:
* **High Cognitive Load:** Participants spend hours cross-referencing data, leading to slow and inefficient decision-making.
* **Vulnerability to Manipulation:** Markets are often swayed by coordinated misinformation and "pump-and-dump" schemes disguised as community consensus.
* **Inefficient Capital Allocation:** Poor information quality results in mispriced risks in high-stakes governance and prediction markets.

---

### The Solution: Umia Analyst Agent
The **Umia Analyst Agent** is an autonomous AI research analyst designed to turn chaotic data into actionable, auditable intelligence. It operates as a continuous intelligence layer that:

* **Smart Ingestion & Weighting:** Automatically classifies signals from multiple sources using a credibility-weighted model (**Verifiable** / **Partial** / **Manipulable**).
* **Adversarial Synthesis:** Generates structured Bull and Bear cases with direct citations, ensuring every claim is backed by evidence.
* **Anti-Manipulation Shield:** Actively flags coordinated manipulation attempts by cross-referencing social hype with on-chain reality.
* **Skin in the Game:** Beyond mere reporting, the agent publishes structured trading memos, takes its own positions, and maintains a public, transparent PnL track record.

---

### 🚀 Key Benefits
| **For Traders** | **For Protocols** | **For the Ecosystem** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Reduces research time from hours to seconds. | Improves the quality of governance decisions. | Enhances market efficiency and liquidity. |
| Minimizes exposure to social engineering. | Attracts informed capital via clear reporting. | Reduces the success rate of malicious actors. |
| Provides an auditable trail of logic for every trade. | Hardens the futarchy mechanism against "noise." | Sets a new standard for AI-driven financial transparency. |

**The Umia Analyst Agent doesn't just provide data—it provides the "Signal" necessary to navigate the "Noise" of decentralized governance.**

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges WE Ran Into

Building the **Umia Analyst Agent** presented several unique technical and conceptual hurdles. Our goal was to move beyond simple "AI wrappers" and build a resilient, institutional-grade engineering system.

### 1. Adversarial Information Filtering
The biggest challenge was creating a system that doesn't just aggregate data but actively resists manipulation. In futarchic markets, we found that social signals (Telegram/X) are often heavily manipulated by proposal authors to create "fake consensus."
* **The Solution:** We implemented a **Source Classification Layer**. We assigned deterministic weights to data: verifiable sources (on-chain transactions, GitHub commits) are weighted at `1.0`, while manipulable social channels are strictly capped at `0.3`.

### 2. Ensuring Agentic Reliability
Standard LLM prompts often suffer from "hallucinations" or "groupthink." In a financial context, we couldn't risk the agent making biased or "hallucinated" trading recommendations.
* **The Solution:** We utilized a **LangGraph-based multi-node architecture**. By separating the pipeline into distinct stages—Source Classification, Synthesis, and Position-taking—and adding an autonomous **Self-Reviewer** node (the "Advocatus Diaboli"), we forced the agent to argue against its own conclusions before finalizing a memo.

### 3. Domain Shift & Architecture Repurposing
We started with a robust pipeline designed for corporate credit underwriting and had to transform it into a DeFi intelligence tool within 48 hours. Mapping "banking risk" to "governance risk" required a total overhaul of the business logic.
* **The Solution:** We maintained the underlying "plumbing" (deterministic logic gates, audit trails, and versioned skills) while completely swapping the domain layers. This allowed us to preserve institutional-grade reliability while moving at hackathon speed.

### 4. Data Ingestion Latency
Scraping decentralized forums and GitHub activity in real-time is computationally expensive and prone to rate limits.
* **The Solution:** We developed a dual-mode ingestion system. For the demo, we use a high-fidelity mock-market layer based on historical MetaDAO proposals, while the production environment is designed to utilize Apify actors for fresh signal ingestion.

### 5. Ecosystem Early-Stage Adaptation (The MetaDAO Bridge)
Since Umia’s native decision markets are currently in their earliest stages, we faced a "cold start" problem regarding live data for testing our agent's predictive accuracy.
* **The Solution:** We chose to stress-test our agent on **MetaDAO** (the pioneer of futarchy). This is a strategic advantage: by proving our agent can navigate the most adversarial and "noisy" established market in the space, we ensure it will be the most robust and battle-tested analyst the moment Umia’s mainnet markets go live. We aren't just building for a sandbox; we are building for the open ocean.

**Network Economy**

We built Mochifi — an autonomous research analyst that makes futarchic decision markets function the way they were designed to. Today, governance markets suffer from thin liquidity and uninformed traders: social signals are manipulated, on-chain data is unread, and most token holders vote blind. Our agent ingests every signal — GitHub commits, on-chain wallet flows, Telegram, X — classifies each source by verifiability, and publishes an institutional-grade trading memo with a YES/NO/ABSTAIN position scaled by confidence. It then tracks its own realized PnL as markets resolve. We're not building another DAO dashboard. We're building the Bloomberg Terminal that makes decentralized governance economically rational.

**Future Society**

Futarchy only works if the people trading in governance markets actually understand what they're trading. We built the infrastructure that makes this possible. Our agent implements adversarial information filtering — verifiable on-chain data is weighted at 1.0, manipulable social signals are capped at 0.3 — and forces itself to argue against its own conclusions through an autonomous Self-Reviewer node before publishing any memo. The result is a system where governance decisions get priced on facts, not coordinated shilling. We believe this is what the next generation of community-driven organizations needs: not just a voting mechanism, but an intelligence layer that makes every vote worth casting.

**Best Agentic Venture**

# 🤖 Why Umia Analyst Agent is the Ultimate Agentic Venture

Our project is a perfect embodiment of an **Agentic Venture** on Umia. We haven't just built a tool; we have launched an autonomous economic entity that operates, earns, and scales natively within the Umia ecosystem.

### 🧠 Autonomous Intelligence Layer
The core of our venture is an **AI Agent** that acts as a real-time intelligence layer for traders in Umia’s resolution markets. 
* **Continuous Monitoring:** The agent autonomously tracks all open proposals, aggregating data from Discord, Telegram, X (Twitter), and on-chain activity (with a focus on Uniswap V4 pools).
* **Actionable Output:** It delivers structured “Memos” that help traders bypass information asymmetry, making the entire Umia ecosystem more efficient and liquid.

### 💎 Economic Alignment & Tokenomics
We have designed a sustainable, deflationary business model that directly benefits the Umia community and token holders:
* **Revenue Loop:** Our subscription and pay-per-memo services run natively on Umia’s token rails.
* **Deflationary Pressure:** **20% of all revenue generated by the agent is automatically burned**, creating a powerful feedback loop that increases scarcity and drives long-term value for token holders.

### 🏛️ A True On-Chain Organization
We operate as a fully sovereign digital entity. By utilizing the **MetaLex BORG** legal wrapper, we transform from a "project" into a **True Agentic Venture**:
* **Autonomous Governance:** We are an autonomous economic entity governed by our own token and resolution markets.
* **Native Infrastructure:** From treasury management to service delivery, every part of our business model is built to leverage Umia’s non-custodial vaults and settlement layers.

---

> **The Bottom Line:** We don’t just participate in Umia — we enhance the entire protocol. By turning chaotic information into a monetizable, deflationary service layer, we provide the essential "Signal" that allows Agentic Ventures on Umia to thrive.
