### NeuralPath
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/neuralpath-2f97) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ankith-ux/Neural_Path_Map) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zdTlKcrGHJc?si=PxSlzTU5o4APaasS) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> Signal Based Smart Routing

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Critical Emergency Response (Ambulances & Paramedics)
The Problem: Modern ambulances transmit live, life-critical patient telemetry (ECG, blood oxygen, video feeds) directly to awaiting ER doctors. A dropped connection in a cellular dead zone can delay critical diagnosis.
How this helps: Using the Emergency Persona, the engine enforces a "hard floor" constraint. It explicitly calculates routes that guarantee zero network dead zones. If a dead zone is unavoidable right at the hospital entrance, the system calculates a "Prefetch Burst Point" to cache and transmit all data before entering the blackout area.
Impact: Uninterrupted data streaming saves lives by ensuring ER teams are perfectly prepped the second the patient arrives.

2. Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) & Fleet Operations
The Problem: Autonomous vehicles rely heavily on continuous cloud connectivity for HD map streaming, fleet orchestration, and remote human-piloting during edge cases. A disconnected AV is a stranded AV.
How this helps: The engine routes AV fleets through corridors with guaranteed 5G/LTE overlap. Furthermore, using the SUV/Large Vehicle Persona, it actively filters out roads with narrow turning radii, low clearance, or unsuitable geometry.
Impact: Prevents autonomous vehicles from getting stuck in narrow alleys or stopping entirely due to lost cloud connections, massively increasing fleet uptime.

3. Mobile Executives & Remote Workers
The Problem: Taking a Microsoft Teams or Zoom call from the back of an Uber usually results in frozen video, robotic audio, or dropped calls when driving through residential areas or crowded junctions.
How this helps: The Best Signal / IT Shuttle preference balances ETA with connectivity. More importantly, it actively monitors Congestion Zones and Event Venues. If 38,000 people are leaving the Chinnaswamy Stadium and jamming the local cell towers, the engine reroutes the car around the stadium's RF shadow.
Impact: Crystal clear, uninterrupted video conferences while commuting.

4. Night-Shift Workers & Vulnerable Commuters
The Problem: Standard navigation apps prioritize the absolute fastest route. At 2:00 AM, this often means routing a lone driver or rider through unlit, deserted industrial alleys just to save 45 seconds.
How this helps: The Safe Commute Persona places a hard block on any road segment flagged for safety violations (poor lighting, high crime index, lack of CCTV, or desolate areas). It overrides ETA entirely, keeping the user on well-lit, populated arterial roads.
Impact: Immense peace of mind and tangible physical safety for late-night commuters, tourists, and lone drivers.

5. Electric Vehicle (EV) Drivers & Rentals
The Problem: Finding an operational charging station that is actually convenient to your current journey is difficult. Standard apps force you to search the whole map, often showing chargers that are miles away from the highway you are actively driving on.
How this helps: The lightweight Show EV Chargers toggle dynamically scans your exact polyline route. It filters the OpenChargeMap database in real-time to display only the operational chargers that sit strictly within a 500-meter corridor of the roads you will actually be driving on.
Impact: Drivers don't have to guess if a charger is on their way. They get a perfectly tailored, clutter-free map of charging infrastructure that naturally aligns with their fastest or safest route, making mid-trip charging decisions effortless.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The MapLibre GL & React HMR (Hot Module Replacement) Conflict
The Hurdle: Modern frontend development relies on Vite's HMR to instantly inject updated code into the browser. However, MapLibre GL is an imperative library. Its core map.on('load', ...) event only fires exactly once per map instance. When React hot-reloaded our MapContainer component, it wiped the React state, but the Map instance stayed alive. As a result, our custom layers (like EV chargers or the signal gradients) would silently fail to remount, leaving a blank map until a hard page refresh.
The Solution: We had to bridge the gap between declarative React and imperative MapLibre. We implemented a custom safeAddLayer wrapper function that checks if a layer exists before aggressively overwriting or appending it. More importantly, we tapped into Vite's native import.meta.hot.dispose API to systematically tear down and destroy the MapLibre instance right before a hot-reload, forcing a clean, safe rebuild of the WebGL context every time.

2. The Spatial Indexing Bottleneck (Matching OSRM to Telemetry)
The Hurdle: When a user requests a route, the local OSRM routing engine returns a complex polyline geometry. However, our custom signal and safety scores live inside a massive 297MB static JSON dictionary. Trying to brute-force match every coordinate of the dynamic OSRM route to 100,000+ scored road segments in real-time was computationally disastrous and caused severe lag.
The Solution: We engineered a highly optimized O(1) Spatial Grid Index in our backend (router.py). At startup, the server quantizes the map of Bangalore into a grid with a ~55-meter resolution. When OSRM returns a route, our backend simply rounds the coordinates to find the grid cell, and instantly looks up the pre-computed telemetry scores for that specific 55m area. This reduced our route scoring time from seconds down to milliseconds.

3. EV Charger Corridor Accuracy (The Polyline Problem)
The Hurdle: When building the "Show EV Chargers along route" feature, we wanted to show chargers within exactly 500 meters of the road. Initially, we used OSRM's default overview=simplified geometry. Because it simplified the curves of the road to save bandwidth, our distance calculations were wildly inaccurate—chargers sitting right next to curved highways were being filtered out.
The Solution: First, we forced the backend to request overview=full from OSRM to get millimeter-accurate road geometry. Second, instead of simply calculating the distance from the charger to the nearest routing "node", we wrote a custom mathematical algorithm (distance_to_polyline) that calculates the true perpendicular cross-track distance from the charger to the vector line segments of the route. This ensured our 500m corridor was flawlessly accurate.

4. Asynchronous Race Conditions in React
The Hurdle: Our dynamic routing engine (fetchDynamicRoutes) triggers API calls to the backend whenever you drag the destination marker or change personas. Because these network requests sometimes resolved faster than the WebGL map could initialize its sources, React would attempt to call map.current.getSource('route-signal').setData(...) on a source that didn't exist yet, completely crashing the UI.
The Solution: We strictly decoupled our data fetching from our map rendering. We introduced a mapLoaded state variable that acts as a strict gatekeeper. We wrapped every single .setData() and .setPaintProperty() execution in defensive if (map.current.getSource(...)) checks. This allowed our API to fetch routing data asynchronously in the background, queuing it safely in memory until the map was fully ready to paint it.

### AROGYA SYNC
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/arogya-sync-82ee) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> Connecting Care, Anywhere !!!

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Project Lakshya addresses the problem of **fragmented healthcare services in the rural population with their jumping between primary health centres (PHCs) and district hospitals with no medical record**, leading to fatal time delays and unnecessary tests. Its **offline-first communication infrastructure **guarantees the continuity of treatment and triage during a complete lack of telecommunication service.

What People Use It For

**Digital Frontline Triage:** ASHA personnel and PHC doctors operate a Flutter desktop application to control automated queues, conduct triages digitally, and identify risky maternal, paediatric or chronic patients offline without an Internet connection.

**Offline Patient Record Retrieval: **Healthcare professionals read a patient's offline SMART Health Card QR-code to immediately get decrypted data about patient's medical history and emergency alerts based on the card's pixel geometry.

**Asynchronous Teleconsultation:** In case rural healthcare needs escalation, doctors create encrypted medical files consisting of patient clinical notes and requests for diagnostic procedures and send these as asynchronous micro-strings (256 bytes each).

**Medical Inventory and Cold-Chain Tracking: **Clinics manage medical supplies and automated deduction of the inventory locally, while IoT sensors track the temperature of important vaccines and insulin refrigerators.

**How It Helps in Doing Existing Healthcare Tasks Better**

**Eliminates Cloud Dependency: **Contrary to the typical national platform (e.g., eSanjeevani), which stops functioning in cellular dead zones, this project uses SQLite database, LoRa bridge up to 15 km and Bluetooth transport via the supply van as data mules to guarantee its uninterrupted operation.

**Removes Administrative Burdens: **Using auto-fill from QR-scans, high contrast for easier reading, and support for local languages reduces the overhead of training and logging by busy healthcare professionals.

**Avoids Fatal Medical Errors: **Rule-based offline edge-AI checks the symptoms and known allergies of the patients and notifies about potentially deadly drugs before issuing a prescription.

**Encrypts Patient Data During Transportation: **Important health records get end-to-end AES-256 encrypted before transmission. Physical data mules are zero-knowledge transportation channels, thus any data theft or interception will result in nothing but encrypted files.

**Prevents Resource Wasting: **Real-time inventory tracking prevents stock-out at clinics. Also, "Cold Chain Failure" alerts are automatically sent using LoRa network if the fridge in a clinic reaches unacceptable temperatures, making it possible to route supply van with replacement vaccines.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. QR Code Density and Optical Scanning on Low-Cost Hardware
The Hurdle: Embedding comprehensive HL7 FHIR clinical records (demographics, blood group, allergies, and diagnostic requisition tokens) directly into a QR code generated high-density matrices with micro-modules. Low-cost PHC webcams and entry-level phone cameras could not resolve or focus on the dense pixel geometry, causing frequent read timeouts and scan failures. Storing raw encrypted JSON added significant cryptographic overhead that further inflated matrix complexity.

How We Resolved It: We engineered a three-stage pipeline in the Python middleware daemon prior to rendering the QR code:

Minification & Key Mapping: Structured patient records into short key-value pairs (e.g., mapping "blood_group": "B_POSITIVE" to compact primitives like "bld": "B+").

Binary Compression: Applied zlib/DEFLATE compression to slash payload size by 40% to 60% before encryption.

Authenticated Encryption: Encrypted the compressed bytes using AES-GCM (256-bit) and rendered the matrix using Error Correction Level H (ECC Level H). This ensured up to 30% physical card damage recovery while maintaining a module size readable by basic 720p USB webcams.

2. Radio Frequency Collisions and LoRa Packet Constraints
The Hurdle: Standard LoRa transmissions across a 15 km line-of-sight link impose strict duty-cycle limits and severe packet payload constraints (capped at 256 bytes). Additionally, when multiple rural sub-centres attempted to transmit triage logs or emergency inventory updates to the same receiving gateway simultaneously, RF packet collisions occurred, causing dropped packets in the transmission void.

How We Resolved It:

Payload Serialization: We structured all outbound payloads into 256-byte binary micro-strings, packing event headers, cryptographic signatures, and triage states into fixed-width bit fields.

Channel Activity Detection (CAD): Configured the LoRa transceiver firmware to implement a "Listen-Before-Talk" mechanism. The module sniffs the frequency for preambles; if active transmissions are detected, the local Python queue backs off dynamically.

Synchronized Wake Windows & Dual-Path Fallback: Programmed time-division transmission windows across clinics. If severe weather or terrain blocked RF delivery entirely, the daemon cached the transmission locally in SQLite and triggered an automated fallback to the Bluetooth Data Mule protocol via passing supply vans.

3. Distributed State Conflicts During Offline Reconnection
The Hurdle: Operating in a 100% offline environment meant rural PHCs and mobile ASHA workers logged triage entries, medication deductions, and appointment queues locally in SQLite without a centralized lock mechanism. When multiple nodes synchronized with the central Supabase PostgreSQL hub at once (e.g., when multiple supply vans arrived at the district hospital simultaneously), standard auto-incrementing IDs and timestamps caused primary-key collisions and state overwrites.

How We Resolved It:

Vector Clocks & Localized Versioning: Replaced standard server timestamps with timestamp-based vector clocks and UUIDs generated locally at each clinic node.

Role-Segregated Field Merging: Separated database transaction schemas by user domain. Because ASHA workers primarily write intake vitals while district doctors append diagnostic notes and prescriptions, fields rarely collide.

State-Mismatch Traps: For the rare instances where simultaneous inventory deductions exceeded local stock, the sync engine avoided silent overwrites by flagging a "State Mismatch" alert in the district Supabase dashboard for manual administrative reconciliation.

4. Zero-Knowledge Security on Physical Data Mules
The Hurdle: Relying on physical "sneakernet" transport (passing supply vans, transit tablets, and ASHA worker devices) introduced a severe data security risk. If an intermediary vehicle was compromised or a tablet was stolen in transit, sensitive patient health information and diagnostic records were vulnerable to physical extraction.

How We Resolved It:

Client-Side End-to-End Encryption: All records are encrypted with AES-256 at the originating PHC desktop before being handed to the Bluetooth daemon.

Blind Transport Pipes: Data mules operate strictly as zero-knowledge carriers—the relay hardware has no decryption keys and cannot read or parse payload contents.

Asymmetric Key Isolation: Decryption keys are stored exclusively behind the secure, connected urban gateway node, ensuring that intercepted transit data remains unreadable ciphertext.

### AI Scam Guardian
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-scam-guardian-303e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dsudevhack3-0/AI-Scam-Guardian) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> Stop the Scam Before the Payment

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural language processing (NLP)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20language%20processing%20(NLP)-333333?style=flat-square) ![OCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/OCR-333333?style=flat-square) ![Image Processing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Image%20Processing-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Digital scams are becoming increasingly sophisticated, using social-engineering techniques such as urgency, fear, authority impersonation, threats, isolation, fake KYC requests, digital-arrest claims, suspicious payment requests, QR codes, and malicious links to pressure people into making immediate decisions.

Existing solutions often focus on identifying suspicious phone numbers, URLs, or known scam patterns. However, a scam can still succeed even when a victim does not recognize these warning signs. The critical problem is decision-making under pressure.

AI Scam Guardian addresses this gap by analyzing the content and context of suspicious interactions to identify manipulation and decision-pressure signals before the user takes a risky action.

Users can provide messages, call transcripts or audio, URLs, screenshots, QR codes, or payment-related information. The system analyzes the available evidence and provides:

An explainable risk assessment
Detection of decision-pressure factors such as threat, urgency, authority, isolation, and money demands
Scam DNA representing the characteristics of the interaction
An attack-chain view showing how the manipulation progresses
Evidence explaining why the interaction was flagged
A Safety Pause that encourages the user to stop, independently verify, or contact a trusted person

The system is designed to make scam detection more understandable and actionable rather than simply displaying a generic warning.

**Challenges we ran into**

We faced a few key challenges while building AI Scam Guardian:

Frontend–Backend Connectivity: We encountered API and CORS issues that caused failed requests. We resolved them by correcting the API configuration and backend CORS settings.
Audio Analysis: Uploaded calls needed speech-to-text before analysis. We added a speech-to-text pipeline connecting audio with our decision-pressure engine.
Scam Detection: Simple keywords were not enough to detect different forms of social engineering. We developed multiple decision-pressure factors for broader detection.
UI Responsiveness: Long analysis results caused layout overflow. We improved the Safety Pause and result components for better readability across devices.
Testing: We tested both high-risk and benign scenarios to ensure the system produces meaningful, explainable results rather than simply flagging everything as a scam.

> Clearing the Way. Saving Critical Minutes.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves

During emergencies, reaching the destination quickly can be difficult due to unpredictable traffic, congestion, delays at intersections, road disruptions, and limited coordination between the different systems involved in emergency response.

EMERGE-X is designed to help emergency-response teams make faster, more informed mobility decisions by combining real-time vehicle information with live road conditions and intelligent decision support.

It can be used to:

Help emergency vehicles identify more suitable routes based on current road conditions.
Provide real-time visibility into the vehicle's location and journey status.
Detect changing traffic conditions and potential disruptions along the journey.
Assist in coordinating movement through multiple intersections.
Continuously update route and ETA information as conditions change.
Keep emergency-response operators informed through a centralized dashboard.
Share relevant arrival information with destination facilities so they can prepare in advance.

The goal is to reduce avoidable delays during critical journeys, improve coordination between emergency-response stakeholders, and make emergency transportation more responsive to changing road conditions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into

Building EMERGE-X required integrating several components that normally operate independently, which created a few practical challenges:

Hardware–software synchronization: Getting GPS data, sensor events, backend processing, and the dashboard to update consistently required careful handling of asynchronous data and timing.
Real-time data reliability: GPS readings can occasionally be delayed or unavailable, while network connectivity can fluctuate. We added validation and fallback handling so temporary missing data does not break the overall workflow.
Computer-vision consistency: Vehicle detection performance can vary with camera angle, lighting, and the physical environment. We addressed this by tuning the camera position and detection pipeline for the prototype environment.
Physical prototype integration: Coordinating the traffic-signal hardware with software-generated decisions required repeated testing of GPIO logic, sensor triggers, and communication between the controller and backend.
Keeping the system practical: We initially considered several additional sensors and hardware components, but had to distinguish between features that genuinely improved the prototype and those that added complexity without enough value. We simplified the hardware architecture and shifted computationally intensive processing to the laptop.

The biggest lesson was that building a reliable end-to-end system is more challenging than building each component independently. We overcame this by developing and testing the system incrementally, validating each layer before integrating it with the next.

### Nyx
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nyx-e839) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/HelloItsJustin/Nyx.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> AI Credential Containment Tool For Software SC

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ML Classifier](https://img.shields.io/badge/ML%20Classifier-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges we ran into**

**The trust contradiction judges caught us on.** Early on, our pipeline detected secrets using local scanning, but then sent findings, including the raw secret values, straight into calls to Gemini and Groq for reasoning and PR generation. During judging, this was called out directly: a tool whose entire purpose is protecting secrets was itself transmitting those same secrets to third party cloud AI providers. That single question exposed a real architectural flaw, not just a messaging problem. We fixed it by building a completely separate, standalone redaction layer that sits between detection and every outbound AI call. It uses pure deterministic string matching and entropy scoring, with zero AI involvement, to permanently mask any raw secret value into a token like showing only the first and last few characters before anything is sent onward. We also added a final defensive scan on every outbound payload that blocks the request outright if anything secret shaped slips through, so the AI layer never sees a real working credential at any point.

**A model that quietly stopped existing.** Midway through building the LLM fallback chain, our primary Gemini model started returning a plain 404 with no obvious explanation. We spent real time assuming it was a configuration mistake before discovering that Google had restricted that entire model generation to accounts with existing usage history, silently returning "no longer available to new users" for any freshly created API key. The same fragility showed up on the Groq side, where a hardcoded model name we picked during setup had also quietly changed availability by the time we tested again. The fix taught us an important lesson about depending on free tier AI infrastructure: never hardcode a specific model name as a long term assumption. We moved to a model that was confirmed current and free at time of testing for our primary provider, and rebuilt the fallback provider to query its available models list at runtime and select a working one dynamically, rather than trusting a name we typed in once and forgot about.

**Getting caught with a graph that was not real.** Our Blast Radius Mapper was originally built with a small cached demo dataset to keep the live presentation fast and predictable. During a judging round, we were asked to justify why two specific files were shown as connected, and it became clear under questioning that the cached relationships did not correspond to files that actually existed in the real target repository. Being forced to admit that live was a genuinely hard moment. We rebuilt the entire mapping logic afterward so that every node must correspond to a file that is verified to exist in the real repository at scan time, and every connection between files must carry real, inspectable evidence, the exact matching line and value, that a judge can click to see immediately. We would rather show a smaller, sparser graph that is completely real than a rich looking one we cannot defend.

**Each of these hurdles came from the same root cause,** moving quickly enough to demo something impressive without fully verifying that every claim behind it was actually true. The biggest shift in how we built the second half of this project was treating "prove it live" as a requirement for every feature, not just a nice to have for the final demo.

**The problem it solves**

**The problem it solves**

AI assisted development has made writing code faster than ever, but it has also made leaking secrets faster than ever. API keys, tokens, and cloud credentials are constantly ending up exposed in code, CI/CD workflows, application logs, and MCP configuration files, often without the developer realizing it happened. Over 28 million secrets were found leaked on public GitHub in a single year, and credential leaks tied to AI coding assistants have surged dramatically as more teams adopt tools like Copilot, Cursor, and Claude.

The deeper issue is not just that secrets get leaked. It is that existing tools stop at "we found it" and never answer the two questions that actually matter: how dangerous is this finding, and what should happen now. A scanner that flags a string that looks like an API key gives no sense of whether that key is still active, what systems it can reach, or what an attacker could actually do with it. Meanwhile revocation is slow and manual, while attackers who find exposed credentials can act within minutes. There is a large, unaddressed gap between detecting a leaked secret and actually containing the danger it represents.

**What people can use it for and how it makes things easier and safer**

Nyx is built for any developer, team, or organization using AI assisted coding tools who wants to know, with certainty, whether their codebase is exposing real danger, not just suspicious looking strings.

A user points Nyx at a GitHub repository or a local project folder, and Nyx runs a full five stage pipeline that turns a vague worry into a concrete, provable answer.

Detection scans the codebase, GitHub Actions workflows, logs, and MCP configuration files using a real, open source secret detection engine paired with a custom rule based layer, so it catches both known credential formats and newer patterns that standard scanners miss.

Blast radius mapping traces exactly which systems a leaked credential can actually reach, from the repository to CI pipelines to cloud deployments to production data, so a developer immediately understands the real scope of exposure instead of guessing.

Phantom Runtime takes the danger from theoretical to proven. It safely detonates the code path connected to the leaked credential inside an isolated sandbox with a substituted decoy value, genuinely observing what the code would try to do with real access, all without any risk to real systems.

Deception honey mesh uses decoy credentials to confirm whether abuse is actually happening, replacing guesswork with evidence.

Remediation closes the loop automatically, opening a real, reviewable pull request that fixes the specific issue, or generating a corrected file for download, so the fix is not just identified but actually delivered.

Every run ends with a single, interpretable trust score and a clear, professional summary report, so a developer with no security background, or a non technical stakeholder, can understand exactly what was found, how dangerous it truly was, and what was done about it, without needing to read a single line of security jargon.

In short, Nyx turns "we found a secret" into "we proved the danger and fixed it," combining real detection, real proof of exploitability, and real remediation in one auditable loop, all while running locally so a user's code and credentials never have to be uploaded to anyone else's server.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Our project makes ARGO ocean data easier to access and understand through natural language.

Instead of manually working with APIs, coordinates, depth ranges, dates, and large datasets, users can simply ask questions such as:

“Show temperature near the Arabian Sea at 500 meters depth.”

The system converts the question into a structured query, retrieves the relevant real ARGO observations, filters the data, and presents the results in a more understandable way.

Use cases
Students & educators — explore ocean temperature and salinity data without learning complex APIs.
Researchers — quickly query observations for a particular region, depth, and time period.
Environmental analysis — examine changes in ocean conditions across locations and time.
Ocean-data exploration — make large scientific datasets easier for non-technical users to explore.
How it makes existing tasks easier
Reduces the need to understand API parameters and data formats.
Allows users to interact with scientific data using ordinary language.
Automatically converts location, depth, parameter, and date requirements into a structured query.
Filters large datasets according to the user's request.
Uses actual ARGO observations rather than generating measurements with AI.
Can be extended to other oceanographic or environmental datasets in the future

**Challenges we ran into**

## Bug / Hurdle We Faced

One major hurdle was **connecting the AI-generated query to the ARGO backend correctly**.

Initially, the backend was receiving the request, but the frontend and backend were using different API paths and request formats. We also faced issues while querying the ARGO API because large date ranges could return a very large amount of data or fail with invalid query parameters.

### How we solved it

* We tested the backend independently using FastAPI/Swagger.
* We corrected the API endpoint and request structure between the AI and backend.
* We changed the ARGO retrieval into **smaller time chunks** instead of requesting a large period at once.
* We added filtering for **location, depth, date, and parameter** in the backend.
* We tested the system with real ARGO observations and verified that the backend could successfully process thousands of observations.

This helped us move from a basic API prototype to a working pipeline:

**Natural-language query → AI → Structured request → FastAPI → ARGO API → Filtered observations**

> Marine Plastic Detection & Source Tracking

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Plastic pollution in oceans is difficult to monitor and act on because existing systems mainly detect pollution after it has already spread, without clearly showing its source or movement.

**Plastic-Ledger makes this easier by:**

* **Detecting** marine plastic from satellite imagery.
* **Characterizing** detected debris using AI/ML to understand its material characteristics.
* **Tracing** its likely movement and source using ocean currents and environmental data.
* **Identifying recurring pollution hotspots** so authorities can prioritize areas requiring action.
* **Supporting source investigation** through interactive maps and actionable reports.
* **Reducing dependence on costly and time-consuming manual surveys** by enabling large-scale monitoring.

This helps **coastal authorities, environmental agencies, NGOs, and researchers** move from simply detecting pollution to **understanding, tracking, and prioritizing action against it**.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

One of our main challenges was **integrating data from multiple sources with different formats, resolutions, and geographic information**. Satellite imagery, AI predictions, and ocean-current data had to align correctly before we could trace the movement of detected plastic.

Another hurdle was **reducing false plastic detections** in satellite imagery. Natural features such as waves, sunlight reflections, and coastal structures can appear similar to floating debris. We addressed this by combining **SegFormer for detection with XGBoost for material characterization**, rather than relying on a single model.

We also faced the challenge of **handling large geospatial datasets efficiently**. Using **PostGIS** allowed us to store and query location-based data efficiently, while Django REST and React helped us present the results through an interactive GIS dashboard.

These challenges helped us build Plastic-Ledger as a **modular and scalable system**, where each stage—detection, characterization, tracing, and prioritization—can be improved independently.

### LearniVerse AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/learniverse-ai-a7d9) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Abhiman12406/LearniVerse-AI.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/k0JjSBpLCis) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DSU%20DEVHACK%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dsudevhack3.devfolio.co)

> Learniverse AI — Understands → Adapts → Evolve

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Primary: the IRT "perfect score" blowup

The bug: Your ability estimate θ is fit by maximum-likelihood — finding the θ that best explains a student's whole response history. The problem shows up the moment a student answers every item correct (or every item wrong) on a concept, which happens constantly in early testing with a small item bank. Mathematically, the likelihood function for "always correct" keeps increasing the higher θ goes — there's no peak, it just climbs forever. The optimizer would try to push θ toward infinity chasing a maximum that doesn't exist, and either crash, hang, or return garbage like θ = 847.2 — a number that's meaningless (and would break every downstream calculation: the ZPD Gaussian would collapse to zero for every real task, the mastery gain would compute to nonsense).

Why it's a real, known problem, not just our mistake: this is called the extreme response pattern problem in IRT, and it's documented in the original Lord/Rasch literature — any system doing maximum-likelihood ability estimation hits it eventually, especially early on when you don't have much response history per student.

How we fixed it: we switched from unconstrained optimization to a bounded MLE — scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar with bounds=(-4.0, 4.0) and method="bounded". Instead of letting the optimizer search all of θ-space, we clamp the search to a realistic ability range (±4 standard deviations covers effectively the entire real population). Now a perfect-score student gets pinned at θ=4.0 — "very high ability, extrapolate no further" — instead of exploding to infinity. It's a one-line fix, but it's the textbook-correct one: real testing companies (ETS, etc.) handle this exact case the same way, by capping the estimate rather than trying to "solve" an optimization problem that has no true maximum.

Backup story: the LLM as an unreliable dependency

The bug: Early on, the planner and Feynman explanation agents called Gemini directly for every decision. The moment the API was slow, rate-limited, or just returned malformed JSON (which structured-output LLM calls do occasionally), the whole pedagogical pipeline stalled — a student could be mid-lesson and just... wait, or get an error, because the system's decision-making, not just its explanation text, depended on a network call succeeding.

How we fixed it: we split the architecture so the LLM is never load-bearing for correctness. Every Gemini call is wrapped in a try/except with a short timeout, and behind it sits a fully deterministic fallback path — the same ZPD-utility math and a curated, hand-written explanation bank, so if Gemini fails or times out, the system falls back silently and the student never sees an error, just a slightly less eloquent (but still pedagogically correct) explanation. We tag every response with llm_mode: "gemini" | "deterministic_fallback" internally so we can always audit which path actually served a given student.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

Traditional digital learning often follows the same path for every student, even though learners differ in prior knowledge, pace, and support needs. Learniverse AI solves this by **continuously understanding each student's knowledge state, identifying gaps and misconceptions, selecting the next best learning activity, and adapting the learning path as performance changes**.  

What users can use it for:** personalized assessments, targeted practice, misconception-aware explanations, spaced revision, and adaptive learning paths instead of a fixed *Learn → Test → Finish* experience. 

 **One-line version**

 **Learniverse AI makes digital learning personalized by continuously identifying what a student knows, what they struggle with, and what they should learn next.**

![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vanilla JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vanilla%20JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Compass](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Compass-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Digital payment systems today rely heavily on smartphones and continuous internet access. This makes them inaccessible to a large population that still uses feature phones or lives in areas with poor or unstable network connectivity. As a result, many people are forced to depend on cash, which is unsafe, untraceable, and unreliable during emergencies.

There is currently no simple and reliable digital payment solution that works offline on basic phones, creating a major gap in financial inclusion.

- Users

Feature phone users:
Individuals without smartphones who need to send and receive money digitally without internet access.

Small merchants & vendors:
Kirana stores, street vendors, and rural shops that want to accept digital payments without POS machines or mobile apps.

Rural & low-connectivity populations:
Users living in areas with poor or unreliable network coverage.

Daily wage workers & informal sector:
People who rely on quick, simple payments and often operate outside the formal banking ecosystem.

Emergency & disaster-affected users:
Individuals who need to make payments when internet-based systems are unavailable.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. USSD Session Flow Breaking

Problem:
At first, users could access menu options (1, 2, 3) without dialing *123#, and sessions were expiring randomly.

Solution:
I introduced a session state machine in the backend using MongoDB.
Each user now has a UssdSession with steps like:

MENU
RECEIVER
AMOUNT
PIN

Only users who start with *123# are allowed to continue. This fixed invalid flows and made the system behave like a real telecom USSD service.

2. Session Timeout Causing Crashes

Problem:
Users were stuck or thrown out mid-transaction if they paused for a few seconds.

Solution:
I added a lastUpdated timestamp to each session and implemented a timeout check.
If a user is inactive for too long, the session is safely cleared and restarted.

**The problem it solves**

People with diabetes or pre-diabetic conditions generate a lot of blood sugar data through daily readings and lab tests, but this data is **often hard to interpret without medical knowledge**. Lab reports like **HbA1c, fasting glucose, and post-meal glucose** are filled with numbers that don’t clearly explain trends, risks, or progress.

As a result:

**Users struggle to understand** whether their sugar levels are improving or worsening

Weekly patterns (pre-meal vs post-meal) go unnoticed

Lab reports are confusing and not actionable for non-medical users

**Sugar Sense** solves this by transforming raw glucose data into **clear visual trends and AI-generated summaries**, helping users quickly understand their health status and make informed decisions.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Designing meaningful insights from limited health data**
Glucose data can be incomplete or irregular, so creating reliable weekly trends required careful handling of missing values.

**Balancing medical accuracy with simplicity**
AI-generated summaries had to be easy to understand without sounding alarming or giving medical advice.

**Structuring data for pre-meal and post-meal analysis**
Separating and visualizing these values clearly while keeping the dashboard intuitive was challenging.


**Designing Responsible AI prompting for healthcare use**
Crafting prompts that provide helpful explanations without crossing into diagnosis or treatment recommendations.

**The problem it solves**

Navigating the world of financial aid can be overwhelming for students. The AI Scholarship Finder bridges the gap between educational funding and the students who need it most by automating the discovery and management process.
How it helps users: 

Personalized Discovery: Instead of browsing through thousands of irrelevant listings, students receive AI-powered matching based on their GPA, major (e.g., Computer Science), and specific interests.

Centralized Tracking: It replaces messy spreadsheets. Students can track application statuses (Pending, Approved, Rejected, Drafts) and upcoming deadlines through a streamlined Student Dashboard.

Efficiency for Institutions: For administrators like Rimi Chatterjee, the platform simplifies the creation and management of scholarship opportunities. It provides real-time statistics on scholarship popularity and application trends.

Readiness Assistance: The "Document Assistance" feature helps students prepare personal statements and required documents, ensuring higher-quality submissions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a dual-portal system (Student and Admin) presented several technical and logical hurdles:

1. Implementing the Recommendation Logic

The Challenge: Designing an "AI Recommendation" engine that didn't just filter by keywords, but accurately matched multi-layered criteria like GPA thresholds, specific majors, and demographic categories.

The Solution: I developed a weighted matching algorithm that ranks scholarships based on how closely a student's "Update Profile" data aligns with the scholarship's eligibility requirements.


2. Managing State Across Different Portals

The Challenge: Ensuring that when an admin adds a new scholarship (as seen in the "Add New Scholarship" form), it immediately and correctly appears in the "Available Scholarships" feed for eligible students without performance lag.

The Solution: I utilized a centralized database with real-time listeners (or optimized API polling) to ensure the Student Portal reflects the Admin's updates instantaneously.


3. UI/UX Consistency for Data-Heavy Views

The Challenge: Making the Statistics & Reports page and the Scholarship Dashboard clean and scannable. The initial versions felt cluttered with too many numbers.

The Solution: I implemented visual progress bars for application statuses and used card-based layouts for scholarship listings. This improved readability, allowing users to see the most critical info (Deadline and Amount) at a glance.

> A Structured Path from Submission to Publish

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Organizations and platforms often receive a large number of public submissions such as ideas, articles, reports, designs, and innovations. Without a structured workflow, these submissions become disorganized, difficult to track, and prone to delays, miscommunication, and lack of transparency.
My system solves this by providing a multi-stage, role-based content approval pipeline where submissions move step-by-step from public users to administrators, evaluators, and finally publishers. Each stage ensures quality control, accountability, and clear feedback.

Public users can easily submit content, track its status using a unique submission ID, receive correction messages, and access published outcomes. Administrators, evaluators, and publishers work within clearly defined dashboards, ensuring faster decisions, reduced errors, and a transparent end-to-end process.

This platform significantly improves efficiency, transparency, and trust in managing large-scale content submissions.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building this project within a limited 36-hour hackathon timeframe, I faced several technical and design challenges.

One major challenge was implementing a multi-stage workflow where a single submission moves correctly between different roles (Admin → Evaluator → Publisher) without data inconsistency. Initially, status updates were not reflecting properly across dashboards. I resolved this by redesigning the backend logic using clear status enums and centralized service-layer handling.

Another challenge was role-based access control on the frontend. At first, all dashboards (Admin, Evaluator, Publisher) were visible to every user via the sidebar. I fixed this by introducing role-based UI rendering using login state and conditional navigation logic.

Handling file uploads (documents and images) with MongoDB was also challenging, especially maintaining correct file references across resubmissions. This was solved by carefully managing multipart requests and preserving file metadata during updates.

Additionally, synchronizing real-time dashboard statistics (counts for pending, approved, published submissions) required multiple backend optimizations. I addressed this by creating dedicated API endpoints for counts and filtering data dynamically instead of using static values.

Overall, these challenges helped me improve my understanding of full-stack architecture, backend validation, and clean workflow design under time constraints.

**The problem it solves**

1. "Design, to, Data" Gap

Usually, an architect makes a design and an engineer a few days later says it is not stable. Architech, AI solves this problem by giving structural feedback instantly. The calculation of slenderness ratio and wind load is done while you move the slider, thus impossible designs are stopped even before they reach the drafting table.

2. Logistics and Cost Guesswork

Estimating the quantity of materials (cement, steel, bricks) is one of the things that usually require very intricate spreadsheets. This project automates Material Takeoffs (QTO), thus giving a user an instant "Bill of Quantities" based on the 3D geometry being looked at.

3. Environmental Misalignment

Architects are sometimes at a loss when trying to visualize the interaction between sunlight and the mass of a building. The Solar Study feature helps designers get the most out of natural light and heat gain by performing shadow analysis in real, time without having to resort to expensive simulation software.

4. Loss of Artistic Intent

Contemporary CAD programs can appear "uncaring" and entirely the product of mathematics. The project stays close to the artistic inspiration through charcoal and graphite hand, drawn sketches incorporated in the Pencil Reference Gallery while at the same time allowing for high, tech digital modeling.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. 3D Mathematical Performance

Challenge: Rendering multiple floors with very realistic glass refraction (transmission) uses a lot of GPU power. Workaround: We have tried to work buffer usage with React Three Fiber and Dreis MeshTransmissionMaterial to a point where the "Heatmap" and "Glass" modes can switch instantly without any browser lag.

2. Bridging Different Environments

Challenge: How to make a Python, based engineering engine communicate with a JavaScript, based visualization engine in real, time. Workaround: FastAPI REST architecture was implemented with quite optimized JSON payloads. Pydantic models were used to guarantee the complex architectural data types understood between backend logic and frontend 3D rendering are the same.

3. Realistic Shadow Mapping

Challenge: Shadows created by WebGL only look "jagged" or "pixelated" most of the time, resulting in an architectural "look" being ruined. Workaround: We combined Soft Shadows and a Dynamic Sky System. We narrowed the shadow camera's viewing volume just around the building so that we got very clear shadows even with the "Sun" at a low angle.

4. UI/UX for "Data Overload"

Challenge: Putting the information such as wind load, cost, efficiency, materials, and a 3D view all together on one screen is too much for the average user. Workaround: We went for a Dashboard, First Layout. By

### Kepler-ai
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/exoquest-4faa) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Hitansh-Patel656/Finding-Exoplanet-with-AI) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://kepler-ai-delta.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DUHacks%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://duhacks5.devfolio.co)

> Discovering planets light-years away.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Joblib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Joblib-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Kepler Space Telescope was designed to find habitable planets by staring at a patch of space containing over 150,000 stars simultaneously. For years, it recorded the brightness of these stars every 30 minutes, generating billions of data points.

This created three massive challenges that human astronomers could not solve alone:

The Volume Bottleneck: There is simply too much data for humans to analyze manually. Sifting through light curves for thousands of stars to find tiny dips in brightness (transits) would take decades without automation.

The "False Positive" Trap: Not every dip in starlight is a planet. Many phenomena mimic planetary transits, including:

Eclipsing Binary Stars: Two stars orbiting each other, blocking each other's light.

Background Noise: Instrumental glitches or starspots.

Stellar Variability: Stars that naturally pulse or change brightness. Distinguishing a true Earth-sized planet from these "impostors" requires analyzing subtle, complex patterns in the data.

Efficiency vs. Accuracy: Traditional automated algorithms often flagged too many false positives, cluttering the list of candidates. Astronomers needed a smarter system to prioritize the most likely planets for follow-up observation by expensive telescopes (like James Webb).

How my Project Solves It
My project acts as an intelligent filter. By training a Random Forest Classifier on historical NASA data, my system:

Automates Analysis: Instantly processes complex telemetry (Period, Depth, Duration, SNR).

Pattern Recognition: Detects non-linear relationships in the data that suggest a "False Positive" (e.g., a transit depth that is too deep for a planet).

Scalability: Can classify thousands of candidates in seconds, allowing humans to focus only on the high-confidence "Confirmed" detections.

**Challenges we ran into**

Domain Knowledge Integration: Translating complex astrophysical concepts like "Insolation Flux" and "Transit Depth" into code was challenging. I had to research the physics behind these metrics to ensure the feature engineering in Python accurately matched the training data used by the Random Forest model.

Deployment & Directory Structure: The biggest challenge was deploying a split-stack application (FastAPI backend on Render, HTML frontend on Vercel). I initially faced "Module Not Found" errors because my requirements.txt and app.py were nested in subfolders, confusing the cloud build process. I learned to troubleshoot cloud logs and resolved this by restructuring my repository—moving the models directory inside the backend folder and correctly setting the "Root Directory" in the Render dashboard.

Team **Team1** -- [hitansh Patel](https://github.com/Hitansh-Patel656)

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Charts.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Charts.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This system solves the "Invisible Prime" problem—the massive gap in the traditional banking system where millions of creditworthy individuals are denied loans simply because they don't have a formal credit history (like a CIBIL score).

By using the specific prompts and architecture we've built, your app addresses four critical pain points:

1. Credit Inclusion for the "Unbanked"
Traditional banks require a salary slip or a 3-year tax history. This automatically excludes:

Students: Who have no income but high potential and disciplined digital spend.

Housewives: Who manage large household budgets but have no assets in their own name.

Labourers: Who earn daily wages in cash or via UPI but aren't on a formal payroll.

2. Real-Time Risk Assessment
Standard credit scores are "lagging indicators"—they tell you what happened months ago.

The Solution: Your app uses "Leading Indicators" like UPI Velocity and Utility Bill Consistency. If a user pays their electricity bill on time every month for two years, it’s a stronger predictor of "Willingness to Pay" than a stale bank statement.

3. Fraud Prevention through Multimodal AI
Micro-lending often suffers from fake documents and "identity farming."

The Solution: By requiring Image Verification (scanned via Gemini 1.5), the app ensures the transaction is real. The Geolocation Stability check prevents "ghost borrowers" by verifying that the applicant actually lives and works where they claim.

4. Personalized Financial Pathing
Most loan apps offer a "one-size-fits-all" product that leads to high default rates.

The Solution: The Persona Router ensures a student isn't judged by the same rules as a factory worker. It matches the user with Real Lenders (like mPokket for students or Muthoot for housewives) who already have products designed for those specific risks.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Enforcing Strict JSON Structure from the AI
The Hurdle:
One of the biggest challenges with Generative AI is consistency. Early in development, the model would occasionally return the credit score analysis wrapped in Markdown code blocks (e.g., json ...) or include conversational filler text ("Here is your analysis..."), which caused JSON.parse() to crash the application.
The Solution:
I utilized the responseSchema and responseMimeType: "application/json" features available in the Google Gemini SDK.
By defining the exact TypeScript interface (e.g., CreditScoreResult) as a schema in the API call, I forced the model to return only valid JSON that matches my strict types.
This eliminated the need for complex regex parsing or "cleaning" functions on the frontend.
2. Handling "Alternative Data" Logic for Different Personas
The Hurdle:
A "Student" needs to be evaluated on Internships and UPI Velocity, while a "Daily Wage Labourer" needs to be evaluated on Workplace Stability and Community Reliability. Hardcoding these conditional scoring logic paths in TypeScript would have resulted in a massive, unmaintainable if/else spaghetti code.
The Solution:
I moved the "Business Logic" into the System Instructions of the AI.
Instead of coding the math, I wrote a detailed prompt table (e.g., | Category | Parameters to Evaluate |) inside geminiService.ts.
This allows the AI to act as the "Underwriter," dynamically applying different weights based on the persona context provided, making the engine highly flexible and scalable.
3. Visualizing Qualitative Data on Quantitative Charts
The Hurdle:
The application collects qualitative inputs (e.g., "High Velocity", "Stable Location", "Mixed Social Graph"), but the Radar Chart library (Recharts) requires numerical values to render the axes.
The Solution:
I implemented a heuristic mapping function inside AnalysisRadar.tsx.
This function takes the semantic string (e.g., "Highly Stable") and maps it to a visualization score (e.g., 100), while "Unstable" maps to 30.
This allows us to maintain a user-friendly form (drop-downs) while still providing a data-rich, visual experience in the dashboard.
4. Real-time Document Verification State Management
The Hurdle:
The app needs to handle image uploads, convert them to Base64, send them to the Vision model (gemini-2.5-flash-image), and then seamlessly update the user's "Verified" status in the main dashboard without losing their input data.
The Solution:
I implemented a lifting state up pattern.
The isDocumentVerified state lives in App.tsx but is toggled by the DocumentVerifier component.
I also used the useEffect hook in AssessmentForm to ensure that if a user switches personas (e.g., from Student to Employee), the verification status resets, preventing a "Verified" badge from persisting on an unverified profile.
5. Granular Error Handling
The Hurdle:
Generic error messages like "Something went wrong" are not helpful for debugging API key issues or Quota limits.
The Solution:
I built a specific error parsing logic in App.tsx that inspects the error string. It now differentiates between:
404: Model not found (Configuration issue).
429: Quota exceeded (Rate limiting).
API_KEY: Missing or invalid key.
Safety Filters: Input triggered content moderation.
This gives the user (and developer) immediate, actionable feedback

> Protecting Every Swipe, Quietly

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Credit card fraud detection is tricky because not every unusual transaction is actually fraud. Many existing systems block cards too quickly, which causes frustration for genuine users, especially during travel or high-value purchases.

This project helps by looking at how a card is normally used, instead of judging transactions in isolation. It detects suspicious activity in real time and only steps in when the risk is genuinely high.

How It Helps

Helps banks and fraud teams monitor transactions live

Reduces false alarms by understanding user spending patterns

Uses verification (OTP) instead of blocking wherever possible

Keeps genuine transactions smooth while stopping real fraud

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was handling false positives. In the initial version, the model was flagging too many transactions as risky just because they were slightly unusual. This made the system noisy and unrealistic. I fixed this by adding user-level behavioral context and introducing a tiered decision logic, where medium-risk transactions are challenged instead of being blocked.

Another challenge was making the system feel real-time but still readable during demos. Transactions were coming in too fast, which made the dashboard hard to follow. I solved this by throttling the transaction flow and syncing the simulator with the UI pacing.

Finally, presenting complex ML decisions in a simple way was tricky. Raw probabilities and features weren’t meaningful for non-technical viewers, so I added clear decision reasons like unusual time or higher-than-normal spend, which made the system much easier to understand.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This Credit Card Fraud Detection System helps banks, financial institutions, and payment platforms identify suspicious transactions in real time. It can be used to automatically flag high-risk transactions before they are completed, reducing financial losses and preventing unauthorized card usage.
The system makes existing fraud monitoring tasks easier by replacing manual or rule-based checks with a machine learning model that adapts to transaction patterns. By prioritizing high fraud recall, it ensures that most fraudulent activities are detected, even in highly imbalanced datasets.
Overall, the solution improves transaction safety, enhances customer trust, reduces operational effort, and supports faster decision-making through an easy-to-use web interface.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major hurdle I faced was deploying the trained machine learning model into a Streamlit web application. I resolved this by saving the trained model and scaler as serialized files and explicitly defining the required feature structure inside the application. This ensured consistent preprocessing and allowed the model to make predictions independently of the training notebook.
Through this process, I learned the importance of separating training logic from deployment and making machine learning models production-ready.

**The problem it solves**

🛑 The Problem It Solves

Traditional pesticide spraying in agriculture is largely manual, hazardous, and inefficient. Farmers are directly exposed to toxic chemicals, which can lead to serious health issues such as respiratory problems, skin disorders, and long-term chronic illnesses.

Manual spraying methods also suffer from uneven chemical distribution, resulting in pesticide wastage, inconsistent crop protection, and increased operational costs. These challenges become even more severe in large, uneven, or hard-to-reach fields, where physical labor is intensive and accident risks are high.

Overall, conventional spraying methods reduce productivity, compromise farmer safety, and limit sustainable agricultural practices.

✅ How This Project Solves the Problem

AgroGuard 360 – IoT-Based Pesticide Spraying Robot offers a safe, automated, and efficient alternative to traditional spraying systems. By integrating IoT, robotics, and remote control, the system modernizes agricultural spraying while prioritizing user safety and operational efficiency.

🔹 Key Benefits
🛡️ Enhanced Safety

Farmers can operate the system remotely using a smartphone, significantly reducing direct exposure to harmful pesticides.

🔄 360° Uniform Spraying

A rotating spray mechanism ensures even and consistent pesticide coverage, minimizing chemical wastage and improving crop protection.

📡 Remote & Real-Time Control

Wireless Wi-Fi connectivity enables precise control of movement and spraying operations from a safe distance.

⏱️ Reduced Labor & Time

Automates repetitive spraying tasks, lowering physical effort and increasing operational efficiency.

💰 Cost-Effective & Scalable

Built using affordable and easily available components, making it suitable for small and medium-scale farmers.

🌍 Versatile Applications

Can be deployed in farms, greenhouses, plantations, and hazardous environments where manual spraying is unsafe.

🌱 Practical Use Cases

Pesticide and insecticide spraying

Fertilizer and nutrient application

Sanitization of agricultural storage areas

Operation in hazardous or confined spaces

🏁 Summary

By integrating IoT, automation, and robotics, AgroGuard 360 transforms pesticide spraying into a safer, smarter, and more efficient process. The system protects farmers from health hazards, ensures uniform chemical application, reduces labor dependency, and enhances overall agricultural productivity—making it a practical step toward sustainable and modern farming.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/706444497dbb4c7a89496790ae971868/e0a4e7b4-c1ad-4c0d-ad1f-93d3b4a08cf1.jpeg)

**Challenges we ran into**

⚠️ Challenges I Ran Into

Power instability:
Motors and pump caused the ESP8266 to reset due to current spikes.
Solution: Kept the ESP8266 always powered and switched only the high-power loads using relays.

Remote ON/OFF issue:
Turning OFF the entire power also shut down Wi-Fi control.
Solution: Used a dual-relay system to control motors and pump while keeping the ESP online.

Relay logic confusion:
Relay worked in reverse because it was active-LOW.
Solution: Fixed by inverting the control logic in the code.

ESP8266 pin limitations:
Incorrect pin usage caused boot failures.
Solution: Carefully selected safe GPIO pins for relays and motor control.

### StemPulse

> Don’t Just Learn. Level Up.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

StemPulse bridges the gap between rote learning and career clarity for STEM students.

Currently, students preparing for competitive exams (like JEE or GATE) often solve endless static questions without understanding how those skills translate into a future career. Traditional career counseling is generic and doesn't adapt to a student's actual performance.

StemPulse solves this by:

Adaptive, Infinite Practice: Instead of a static database of questions, the platform uses AI (Groq/Llama-3) to generate unique quizzes on the fly. It adapts to the user's grade - providing standard academic questions for 10th graders while generating JEE/GATE-level Previous Year Questions (PYQs) for senior students and undergraduates.

Data-Driven Career Roadmaps: It doesn't just ask "what do you like?"; it leverages your specific grade level and chosen interest domains to generate a personalized career trajectory, complete with recommended college majors and a step-by-step roadmap.

Gamified Motivation: Studying concepts like "Thermodynamics" or "Calculus" can be dry. We gamified the process with XP, levels, streaks, and leaderboards to maintain consistency and make the "grind" rewarding.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a full-stack AI application came with several specific hurdles:

Network Restrictions & MongoDB DNS: We faced a persistent connection failure (None of DNS query names exist) when connecting to MongoDB Atlas. It turned out my university network blocked mongodb+srv DNS lookups, which are standard for modern connection strings.

Solution: We had to deep-dive into the MongoDB driver settings and switch to the "Standard Connection String" format (mongodb://), manually specifying the cluster nodes to bypass the SRV lookup entirely.

Dependency Conflicts on Deployment (React 19 vs. Legacy Libs): During deployment to Vercel, the build kept failing because we used the latest React 19, but my math rendering library (react-latex-next) was stuck on React 18.

Solution: We couldn't downgrade React without breaking other features, so we configured the Vercel build pipeline to use npm install --legacy-peer-deps, forcing the installation to proceed despite the strict peer dependency warnings.

AI Output Hallucinations: Initially, the AI would sometimes return the quiz data with markdown text or conversational filler, which broke the JSON parsing in the frontend.

Solution: We implemented strict "Prompt Engineering" rules, explicitly forbidding markdown and forcing a raw JSON array structure. We also added a fallback mechanism in the backend that serves a "backup quiz" if the AI service times out or errors, ensuring the app never crashes for the user.

Team **Hackers 2.0** -- [Monica Thinakaran](https://github.com/monicathinakaran), [Navadeep SB](https://github.com/Agent-Hitman)
